232 Corner Café is a fine little cafe that enjoys a good laugh, great sandwiches and lots of coffee. When I first stopped by last year, it seemed as if there had been something going on. However, for many of us, it was all too easy. Loss to many. But something changed...the owners recognized the significance of the space, and decided to re-open Ron's establishment. In 2011, Ron Roper, who had previously owned LaBelle, came in with several different offers. Not to be disappointed, I was greeted by a new owners' team, who took over a three level brick apartment with a view to The new owners, Ron and Irma, opened on October 12th. The chairs are still there. It's just that Ron still has the crowbar over the bar, and he's still proud to have those things on top of the As you might suspect, everything is kept within the limits of the original concept, and the restaurant is staffed by the same staff. One of my favorite breakfasts was the bacon, eggs, and syrup pizza—or "frigelty" as it turned out at my table A new batch of pancakes sat on a plate, which was a great addition. The oats were slightly sweetened before rising to the point at which they became nearly raw. I had another coffee, and it was a welcome addition. The owners are family run, and Ron is a man that is very proud to be a part of it. The service here is much improved, and the food is much better. Just for one visit; it will change your life.

Located in this very large multi-story condo complex off of the main drag in the South Loop, this establishment is typical. I had heard the food was good and the prices were a bit cheaper. The service is good, and is really friendly. I had to pay a few dollars more than normal, to eat in. I ordered chicken nuggets with a side of fried rice. It had wonton soup, though with a bit of fresh chicken on top. I noticed there was little oil and even less vegetables, which would have been the case for any Chinese version I've had. The wonton soup was a bit too tender for my taste, but again not my favourites. The Porkfried Rice was a mix of traditional fried rice and the kind served in restaurants around the same time. The chicken wasn't as juicy as most I would find elsewhere (including many Chinese) and wasn't even mungry enough to be memorable. The general was quite moist and well done. The menu prices reflect that the general tso's chicken is available only by request. The Chicken Chow Mein was good, though it did take a while longer to be served. A bit pricey, maybe not that great of a deal for a Chinese takeout.

Despite my last trip to Chinatown being rather uninspired, last week our family and I took our first trip to Hong Kong Star Noodle House. Normally Chinese restaurants in the area are quite glamorized. The restaurant was nice to go to at an hour after a busy lunch hour and they had a good selection of chow fun and some sort of Then, there is the excellent friendly wait staff (which was even more impressive), whose dishes were all outstanding, and that seemed to be quite the description I did not expect great things from this noodle house due to my familiarity with Hong Kong noodles, but it did not appear as if the food Hot & Sour Soup is a sweet broth with some sour sauce added. The whole bowl was topped off with a light drizzle of soy sauce. A thin pan of broth brought this soup to the table. The soup had some finely ground vegetables, tender, chewy tofu and plenty of vegetables. It was a large bowl, but enough to sit in and sip all day. The soup had a sweet, warm acid that added great depth of flavor and texture to the broth. The temperature dropped quickly from high of 93.5 °F (161 °C) to about 78.9 °F (22.4 °C Second great was the Beef Chow Fun, which came with a nice layer of mixed vegetables, beans and meat filling. I asked to keep the cheese and onion on the side because it was the standard sauce for clam chow fun in Hong Kong. I love when it is marinated in flavorful orange sauce before being grilled. The broth was very thick, reminiscent of soup. At the end of the lunch I was asked if I wanted my order to be brought to my table. You get to choose your own table at the sushi bar located on the 2nd floor on the third floor. The restaurant had a pleasant and casual atmosphere, with well-marked interior decor. There are numerous Chinese restaurants in this area and this one was near my office this afternoon.

Core Creek State Park is in the center of Tyler's urban center. It was created in 2004 and has a name that is a bit out of place, but still very well thought out and very pleasant. The park has a basketball court, a swimming pool with a hot tub and showers, a playground with a swing set, baseball fields You can access the park by boat, or you can come to the lake directly from the shore. There are kayaks/canoes for those brave enough – but remember – you may fall off. There is also a pond in the lake and a tennis court, and you can rent a life jacket and beach shoes if that sounds like Besides this, Core Creek Park offers a wide variety of opportunities for outdoor recreation. When it is windy, fishing is not permitted on the lake, but there is a good boat ramp to rent and rent a boat for a Some of the spots, like the kids' play structures, or where the adults come to gather, are accessed by trails which are open to the public. So come out and enjoy this lovely park.

There is certainly plenty to do in the historic districts of Tacony. This historic area, once known as Tacony, can still be a swath of old-fashioned townships, old-fashioned Just by wandering the streets, you may see an old farm that you remember decades ago with the large shed on the ground, and have heard stories of the The old days have come back, the town is still working, and you get to know fellow locals who work here on a long-term basis. The place that I visited the most is the old Greek diner, at 219 Main St, on Broadway which had been open for 65 years. With the help of a friend of his (I think he ate there the second time he was here), I wandered outside, and The diner has been on site since 1942, including the old dining room, a big enough for 6 tables and a space from which you can seat That's what I was told. For people who love to sit at the table, you have an experience to take home from the meal. The diner is a place of kinship, even among the neighborhood's locals. It's just that when you eat there, you want to sit down and drink some coffee and watch the waitresses talk about what they see The menu seems to be fairly standard, and has a fairly high percentage of Greek dishes on the menu. I chose a plate of traditional home-style eggs & hash for my breakfast station, a mixture of vegetables from my kitchen garden. The first two eggs were topped with a smear of feta cheese, and the second two eggs had a savory-rich mix I found myself wishing my heart was in Greek as I ate it. Suggested seating for this was at 9, but, we took my tequila shots with my iPad. The eggs came out perfectly warm. The egg was boiled very well, and very slightly sweet, and the Greek Omelet was one of the best I've had in a long I had lunch at Athenian, as it had been established for over 50 years, and it seemed as if the business had had a bad reception A few questions of what I was eating and how it was made, helped me to make the decision of giving this place a try. The restaurant is at 1245 Torresdale Avenue, and it was busy. A very unique neighborhood with not much going on, but all of that makes the experience worth it.

Since my injury with arthritis in my feet, I have been dealing with the repercussions. I came in on Sunday afternoon for my first Tai-Na massage in a while, but even at that point a massage therapist was not what So this weekend, I was told to allow the hands to touch in different directions to release the pressure and strains that I believe have been attached to the spinal I had the opportunity to get the full treatment. My therapist, Lily, was able to work some tense muscle fibers by placing them under great stress. My forearms were unmolested and massaged into a rhythmic "sweat dance." I watched her carefully go into my lower back, then my upper chest, and then my upper body. My body was literally rocking while my masseuse massaged it. She then began to move the hips out of their "downside" configurations and in to the "up" position. She massaged my hips, back, ankle, and shoulders to loosen them up and reduce pain, and to get the full effect. She used all the body parts to do this, so we worked incredibly hard to release the pain. A massage in the form of a Chinese massage will truly deliver these results. We sat down after a long wait to be checked, and the masseuse was immediately available. She was professional; she was thorough about what she wanted and what she wasn't going to replace. My lumbar spine feels less strainful and feels restored. Service and prices are highly recommended. I like my massage, but I don't want to go back there every weekend, because I don't want the same results.

We decided to stay for dinner this evening (Dec 6th) during the Chicago Bears home game. As we left the city, the Polish language sign at the entrance gave us a hint of what we were looking for. Not by much.The place looks like a large, somewhat unfriendly place to sit in a row, but still close enough to get in there quickly The parking lot was not large enough for the four of us, and an un-level side door made entry difficult. They are open seven days a week, but the atmosphere was somewhat unfriendly. Upon arrival, we were immediately struck by the uniform, and familiar, atmosphere of most East European restaurants. After an hour or so, a nice warm color would be needed. The menu suggested that the restaurant was offering what might be a new creation, based on an idea that not every item was the same. We ordered the soup, and the latkes (pierogis) and sausages (chorizo). The chicken was fresh, piping hot and thick and hot with sauces, fried with onions and the arugula was nicely crisp. The chicken was well-done and perfectly moisturized in a simple tomato soup. It was soup with two thick boiled bones made into broth with a generous amount of carrots, a fried egg, a penne Onions were thick and nicely simmered. The green onions lacked an earthy flavor and were mild. We could only see the soup from a mile away. The sauce was thin, but not cloying. The sides were breaded well, and slightly a crunch. The Chicken Parmesan Special offered was a chicken breast. We ordered a bowl of Cream of Leeks and cream sauce (Chelsea sauce) with the Chicken. Soup was very satisfying, very light in texture and flavor, but without any over-powering flavors or spices. I don't know if this is considered "tender", but it had a nice moist, tender chicken. The Chicken came with a delicious sauce, fresh herb-wrapped potatoes, and a simple sweet potato. Our server wasn't too friendly, but was efficient, patient with us and our table, and well-staffed. The two young people waiting on us didn't ask anyone to be kind to us, although I'd rather have this man there than in the store. Unfortunately, this is not a way to make a restaurant more profitable. On our way out, we noticed that they had gone dark. Besides, quality of food was excellent. Very tasty and a little too short on the cheese.

In general, how a restaurant compares to most other places is one of a number of factors that matters. At the end of the day, there's only you. Sometimes I can't help but feel myself drawn to a place that is just romantic to me. Some of these places have the ingredients to do it, others just need "touching" to allow me to enjoy it. If you are a visitor to a place, just be willing to stay a bit longer in order to fully appreciate the experience, but for me that I had this experience at Coffee Cup Café on my last trip to Charlotte. After seeing what other reviews were saying of this place, I stopped in and learned that it was not just a burger place, but a hot breakfast I had read that on the Google map, the place was a little off of Queens. Coffee Cup Café was an intimate space with some small tables, one at the entrance, but two in back. From the corner to the back there were two open kitchen areas, plus the usual "cafe" area. Those are the only things keeping this place fresh, despite the fact that it had just been a year since the last time I was here. Using the small camera I took a few images. When I entered the coffee house it was obvious the sign was for Mamma. Having only been here a few times, I asked why. She had a strong, strong, sultry voice: "Stay, Mam, you got my coffee." I was warmly welcomed. She was just a regular. Coffee Cup Café is a family owned business, and the staff came with her. She said she had been running uptown for at least three years when her mother died, and then moved back down to this small town. I felt like I was sitting in our own neighborhood. A few more minutes passed and it became a comfortable, casual place with a good menu, and good coffee. A nice mix of eggs, bacon, and fresh veggies. A burger cooked to my specifications, and really hot, with a hefty side of cheese. The decor was warm and relaxing. Beth was really friendly and easy going. But the atmosphere? It was warm, welcoming, and comfortable. It took me a few minutes to figure out where I was, but in the end, I was very comfortable, and could not imagine giving up my time One afternoon I am back up and running, and I can't stop thinking of the good friend, Beth, who I am going to pass on a What do you think?

My last breakfast of the night was in New York. The Violetwood Café is a small independent breakfast place near the intersection of Haines and Van Horn Road. There are tables and chairs available, but they are still tucked away behind a brick wall. That said, the restaurant is really small, with only 14 seats for service and about 20 tables for food. I ordered the Coffee Ricotta Cheese Muffin, Bacon Sandwich, and two breakfast offerings - the coffee was awesome - but I found the menu All of the hot dishes had fresh berries, onions and a wonderful seasoning called Fenugreek. The first item I tried on the menu was the Belgian Waffle with a piece of French Bread as a side. I really did enjoy the scramble, which was very tasty but the cheese was just too heavy. The coffee was a bit weak, but the service was very good. The breakfast is not too bad, but definitely not a bad place to hang out.

I went to Snack-Snack, when it opened in the 1990s. Despite not ordering in, I was able to get a server there to explain the menu and order with great service. I stopped by to say hello after the last one in Bucks County had gone to the store. My favorite Mexican food bar, FireGirl, is on Street Road around the corner from the Hotel San Angelo. This is not something I would recommend, but I think they are good enough to open a new location in the same strip mall. I was a bit disappointed to find FireGirl very small, but we had a good time. All of the Mexican items on display were the traditional Mexican favorites - Chicken Flautas with guacamole, Spicy Peach Marg In the middle of the room was a small plastic basket that had three fillings, one for each person. We ordered the Fried Flautas which were called El Fucha, a small basket filled with two tortillas stuffed around a hot pepper They were cooked properly (which we assumed at the time). The small plastic basket filled with Flautas came with either one or two pepperoni pieces, the filling was smothered with cheese We took these to go, and to wait for a side of chips, and then a little salsa and a beer. FireGirl is friendly and helpful, welcoming and hospitable (no-smoking) just as much as a Mexican The presentation of the menu would have made it far more interesting. If I get to this place early in the morning or on a weekend, we will probably pop in to this FireGirl restaurant and pick out

Freddy's Bistro is located in the old building in the corner of 2nd and 6th Streets. The original facade was covered in brick which made the place feel like you were in Roman times. It was built in the early 1900s, and originally was owned by Fred & Judy Connell, who worked the squaw in the basement before We ventured in late Tuesday evening after my wife left me the morning before. The restaurant seats 25 in a large room, but it varies. The place had live singers playing throughout, and the bar was filled up with a crowd of about 25 or more people. We got an 8pm start, but in spite of the empty pub, the food still was good. After we had ordered, the three items to go, but no alcohol, were brought to our table. This Calamari was marinated in a light olive oil and added panko, but still good. The pizza was a medium crust, with an Italian taste, and the marghadrita sauce was thick and rich, no taste cloying. I had one bite, so I tried the one on the bottom, and found it to be soggy even without the sauce. It was quite filling. The Margharita Pie was like an old pizza pie with a side of sauce. Both were satisfying.The burgers were good too, but the fries just weren't as thick as I liked. Hopefully I'll have to return soon. A long time favorite! For me, I hope they stick to their menu and stay as close to the neighborhood as possible.

Now open for business on Fridays 10-3. As the name implies, if you want fried rice, Chinese food, or something else, this is not the place for you. I went to Wild Ginger for lunch around lunch time with a friend and a co-worker to sample their tapas. So we sat at a lovely booth in the heart of the dining room, facing a bright green counter, decorated with fresh Thai art prints, The menu is very well executed, and my boyfriend and I got the "Dirty Thai" with crab cakes, fish in the tank, and A slightly darker decor would be a welcome relief to some, but I think I'd rather drive out to the river. Here I was, ready to eat in front of all the tourists, and then be the one to eat them; but as there were only four dishes I ordered the Pho (watercress) soup, which looked the only thing on the menu that was Thai. The Szechuan Beef was the star. At the server's suggestion I called it, "Tom Kar, lemongrass/ coconut milk soup." The restaurant was busy, but the service was good. They made the soup to look like Thai, but the noodles had a green tinge! The Pad Kee Mao was similar; just got a little better than Tom Kar. One bite and I wasn't sure if it was the lemongrass or the coconut milk. I turned it back down, but to no avail. Later I re-used the red chili pepper. He did not mention the red chili pepper. At least it didn't taste like it. I ordered my Szechuan Beef. The beef portion was large, the chicken less-than-tender, but we enjoyed the vegetables and chicken well enough. I knew the red pepper was a spicy fusion, before they added the beef and the Rice won't match up with traditional tastes. It added a little extra heat just to the protein itself, or so I suspected. The chicken was also dry and the skin was mushy. No, that's not "New Hope Thai," but it does explain how it translates. The name could be based upon charred ginger in a spicy sauce with fresh Thai veggies to accompany the meat. Don't get me wrong, I love Thai food, and this is a good restaurant to go to if you are looking for it.

I was driving down the Old Freeway when I was stopped at this small breakfast restaurant, known as Seams on the Boulevard, off of Route No. 55., about 40 miles to the south of the city center in Eastchester, NY. I arrived at 2:56 pm. The waitress is nice and friendly and the menu is full of interesting choices. The burger sandwich was an excellent piece of meat on a large wheat roll. It's a small, but flavorful portion. The pulled pork & hot dog sandwich was good. The sandwich was also pretty filling with a few extra pieces of turkey, fresh cranberries, and green onions, with a side of fries I asked for a ranch dressing, because the ones I have in NJ, don't have ranch dressing. Next were the sides I would order again, the Chicken Salad on Rye bread, which was plenty of chicken and tastiness and enough vegetables Also, the salad was a good, large quantity, not much extra fat. Nice idea..I didn't come to the restaurant today because I was looking for a place to hangout but my mate recommended it to me

We ordered six different types of dishes, and were both equally delectable. We went in with our expectations about what we were going to eat and what to expect. There was a kind of explosion in the air, with a sense of pyrotechnic fire, but not in the way you might expect to The meat was fresh, but very flavorful, with a complex, nutty flavor. The chicken was tender and warm, almost as thin as a knife blade, but held its crispness and freshness at the same time. We couldn't believe how good such a good meal was! And what a wonderful experience! Not only was the menu extremely fresh, but it was also well thought out, with all the great choices to cater to your needs. For the price, this could be the next best Szechuan diner in town. We definitely made a return trip to Pin Wei. While the dining table and servers didn't let us leave when they left, we were rewarded. A perfect start to the weekend! It was great to see what such great restaurant is working toward this day. We finished the meal in one piece - no complaints - and are already writing a review in our restaurant blog, I mean - I love them I would love to tell you the name, Pin Yun and Yong Hek Yee. The dinner was wonderful, however, it wasn't enough to enjoy the experience. A treat that should go straight to your freezer. A great meal!!!! So glad we enjoyed Szechuan Szechuan. They serve all of these at this restaurant! This is a restaurant that has become more of a family tradition than a restaurant; for most, as we ate, we were entice The rest of the plates were made up of fresh corn, topped with an intense, garlicky mixture that was just as intense and intense as the beef  We ended the evening with this: Chinese Blue Shrimp with Garlic, Thai Basil, Garlic, Basil and Szechua Peppers. Sickness.. The meatballs were perfectly medium, not even the slightly spicy hot chilies could compare. After one bite, there was a very numbing feeling in the back of the throat and in the behind of the eyes. The food was extremely fast, with the entrees arriving on time and very filling. For your next Szechuani chili bash, bring your lunch in hand and try not to do everything in your power to forget the chili. Great food and service. Pin Wei Chinese Restaurant was awesome! All the more enjoyable for me. Pin Wei is a true Szechuan restaurant here in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania. At this point, I felt very numb, a little like I had been electrocuted that night. With our steamed longhots, a spicy, yet very mild sauce, was added.

After having read my new friend Jim's blog about the brewery in Nedlandsville, it was time to give it a try. I had been passing by the Puddlers Row taproom at the corner of Main and Grand in South Austin a few years ago when the concept of My friends said it was a good place to make a drink when I was there in 2006. I've been meaning to finally try some of their beers for a while now. It's a perfect place to unwind and hangout with friends. One was just sitting at the table, with the counter covered in a few scraps of wood on top. It's a beautiful old industrial city, with a cute vibe, and a great food truck. One of our server's assistants suggested the bottled beer, but we had already ordered it. The beer was a few years older than what I'm used to, and all seemed tan. The ESB was a pretty big, almost hazy, beer and the brewery was quite busy in between regular drafts. Very interesting to see the different styles, and I enjoyed each of them. Puddlers Row ESB, which had a nice grassy smell, was great. The Glasping Saddles was an English brown ale with some dark chocolate malt flavor, dark cocoa, and a very roasted and very mal ), and Viking Funeral (that little sour in that pilsner?). Somewhat a letdown though. The app was my favorite. They brought out the Brussel sprouts topped with a creamy, rich sauce on arugula bread. Very tender and tasty. The brisket was seasoned well with salt and pepper. The tacos were served with anchovies, pico de gallo, and polenta. They were so good! The Harvest Salad was huge. I didn't like the sprouts. Both were incredibly fresh. The beer list was a solid mix of beers from around the world, and I would like to find more to try. The food was excellent, too. Had the burger, and the fries were solid.

The fact that a bagel is so small and fresh, doesn't necessarily describe the overall quality of the product. Some may find them to be fine, others are less enthused. One thing is certain; a bagel cannot be overserved. All Star, in the heart of the San Francisco Bay Area is a one stop shop for that. 21. After driving through the local shopping center for a little while, I stopped in. The experience was pleasant. The cashier and associate were all friendly and helpful. The portions were huge, but I got a free bag at the end. The shop was a good deal. I was really pleased when I arrived home to find it ready (and in a good shape) to enjoy. The bread sliced in half, and had a very flat, sticky crust. It was not an unaffected bite, not one that dragged down the bar or didn't seem to have as much flavor. In a small corner of Sobeys, I found the original Antonio's Italian Garden Restaurant. This is the restored one of a hundred, with a new kitchen. It's a large kitchen setup that includes multiple ovens, and some big wood burners with a little kitchen area sat near the front Each booth offers a variety of Mexican entrees; their lunch offerings range from chicken and rice, to rice and beans. As a Guatemaltec, we had the honor of trying many of the delicacies on the menu: chicken, steak, fish, There is also a full bar, and a couple of televisions on the side. I ordered the Chicken Tortilla and Pineapple Juice for $10. The Pechuga Empanizada did not come with rice, but did come with a bowl of black beans. My pechuga was very large for its space and the texture was really great, combining soft and tender, but light and tasty. The chicken was soft, juicy, and moist. The beans were steamed and the rice was cooked in a pan on the stovetop. The beans were cooked to a thick consistency, served over a soft white tortilla. Pechuga Empanizada was a good mixture of protein and flavor and had some tender chicken (though not a lot), but it also If you have kids, you'll be rewarded with a generous serving of sour cream and beans. I was impressed with the service- all from the waiter to the host and manager. And I will venture out to visit it again soon! La Chapinita is open on weekdays from 4 to 6, with weekend hours.

What I liked about Fat Jack's was the food. That was a fact, and, in the end, that was a blessing, too. First, we could get the full kitchen staffed for all meals except a side order, and the kitchen was ready when we left. I was able to get a reasonable burger with half a pound of ground beef. I've recently spent some time at Number One Chinese Restaurant in Chengdu. It originally opened in 1958, and has served the area ever since. A large restaurant with a small indoor bar, the food is average. A large, old-world facade with bright red painted windows makes it attractive and inviting. I stopped in a while ago for lunch. By the time I got to this place, there were still a couple of tables left, and I was greeted with a friendly smile, who We ordered a half order, which cost $5.40. In response, I ordered the Chicken in Garlic Sauce. It was a red plate topped with a mashed chicken with carrot, egg, bell pepper, radish, black beans and greens. The soup was a thick layer of broth, with a little water added at the end. The chicken and rice were very thick, both of which were very salty. The dressing was light, not thick. The rice was cooked perfectly, though the texture and flavor of the meat wasggy with the grease. After a few bites, it got old, and I got sneezing all over. After lunch, we headed to the corner of Broadway, Broad Street and East Broad Street. There were a few pieces of meat that were very cold, but they were still tasty and there was enough left over to go on a salad. In the back of the restaurant were posters of "the best Chinese food", which was hung over by the workers and customers. It was still good enough to eat. So far I haven't experienced the same great service again. It's an interesting concept, but I didn't find it very good.

Having just had a quick lunch at El Barrio Cantina & Tequila Bar, I was a little wary. Walk in the door and you can be sure that this restaurant looks up in awe. Everything was beautiful.. except for the bar, which is the least interesting building in the mall. Very dark woods. Fresh Mexican beans and rice. Some of the tables were empty, but they were busy for the whole night. The food was tasty. Fried chicken for the old man. The main dish.A chicken and cheese flute filled with fried Chicken, cheese & pepper. A molcajete plate for me. Meatballs, chicken and chicken egg roll for stepmother. Nothing special.The food was solid - nothing special. That was the case with the burrito. There was more of a fish flavor. We left with a little bit of salt on the inside of our pockets. Chicken was not impressive. Small sauce.I could have used more mayo and less seasoning. Flautas looked like little stuffed chicken cutlets topped with fried eggs, cheese, ham and a dollop of rancho He wolfed down two pieces. I asked if it was a bit hard for him to chew the shell with all the stuffing inside. My son ordered the shrimp to go with it. The flautas weren't good. The beans were great, but overpriced and didn't come with a side of rice, guacamole or beans on the Our meals came with a pitcher of bar strength tequila, which was quite good. "La Hacienda" is a Mexican-style restaurant in The Forum Shopping Center, with a fairly busy front entrance. The restaurant creates a somewhat fun atmosphere that isreminiscent of a Latin American town, where an adult may walk in, get one cab ride, This place also has a somewhat loud and colorful mural (see photo). However, I was a mixed bag on my tastes. However, given the somewhat less than stellar chile flavor and decor of many Mexican joints, I would still recommend La Hacienda as a local The menu is relatively well-rounded - a few specialty items available for a limited time, such as Chicken Adobado, and a My first course was the Pork Patties- a very thin Pork Plate topped with ham, cheese, and guacamole We each ordered the Carne Asada, Fried Fish with Salsa, and Salsa En Blanco with Shrimp and Clam You would want to see what kind of sauce was served, and if necessary, add more heat to make it taste better. The Chicken was quite tasty and moist, but the Mexican spices a bit too much. A small portion of the Mexicali Icecream was available to share with my companions, and it was excellent. The Chicken exhibited enough texture and flavor, which I did not find lacking. However, I definitely felt the Chicken was a little dry. The enchiladas had good flavor and had a good presentation to go along with the Chicken. The Rice was too wilty and not very fragrant. There were many small improvements to the taste. I think I would like to see more people dining there.

The owners were very knowledgeable about coffee, and my favorite thing about Lavazza was the artisan coffee. The building is tiny, containing only a few tables, and the interior seems bright, but not invitingly cozy. It's a bit smaller and more crowded than I'd have expected, since it was a Friday night. Forget the huge French toast (that may have seemed like a good start to a morning at breakfast), a good breakfast was lacking. I picked out the chicken, bacon, egg and Gruyère (which seems to be the official word for breakfast). I tried their new Nicaraguan coffee. The coffee was very rich and flavorful, and I enjoyed every drop. Later on, the bloated milk spread stayed in mycup. In fact, the coffee was good, the flavor had been added by the waiter, and the heat was a nice compliment. She asked if we could have the coffee in another bowl. It did tinge with the alcohol (which is to be expected when you're talking about java, not a chocolate drink, ion With the meal, I did feel a bit dissatisfied with the service. The sausage came out perfectly hot. I'm sure there were lots of different versions in the kitchen, but it was pretty much the same as my brekkie sandwich. One of those times when I look at a restaurant and consider whether or not it will go the distance from a fast food joint. I also had three steamed cookies and some mini fruit cola, and did notice the cashier was asking me to tip at the end of my meal I ordered out from the menu and headed home. The meal, in my opinion, was nothing special, but good enough to make me give it another try. The decor was too minimal, not very exciting but not bad.

The chicken and egg roll combos here were average. The front is just a tad bit too dirty, and it's about as good as it gets outside. When my father was driving, we wanted to find a physical for my two sons. By this time, my 10-year old would have been in his second year at junior high, and so we had to get a physical exam before you could Because of the long waiting times at most hospitals, I asked for a local doctor's appointment for an exam for a young female driving applicant and  If I could find an urgent care facility at least a few miles from work, could I use their services? It's difficult to find a better, far better looking shop that serves pizza. This business started out as a local deli in the middle of Rome called Pisce, but has been transformed into a family business. This new addition to our local Italian food scene opens in early April. But it's their own little business, with the support of their husbands, Sal and Sal Jr. Now, that little pizza hut that was in the shop was a ghost town, as we've all noticed with all the old Italian houses and Cafe The owners set about renovating it to give it a more modern look, with modern appliances. This is not just a typical "come to Napolitan" pizza joint. This oven is well worth the time it takes to cook your own pie. The pizzas were lovely and they made me feel like an artist waiting to be presented to the table. There was also a small plate of veal cutlets and salami, and a piece of red pizza sauce mixed with clementine on We were happy.. At the table, Pasquale brought us the pie. The entire pie seemed to descend from the oven, with the steam streaming off, and coming out just before that white and red steam poured down on all the The toppings were arranged in a large hive oven on the second floor of the establishment. It was this crust that the bakery uses for the creation of the pie that it gets its name. The Italians have found this unique flavoring to be a perfect blend of "New York City" pizza, with home-baked taste. I was very impressed with the bread and crust, and particularly the presentation of this pie. What does not fit on a Siciliana Pie? It is like a fresh, thick, southwestern tomato and pepper pizza, with just the right amount of sour cream, basil, pine nuts The pizza was delicious. I'll be back. The crust is soggy (in theory); soggy when it has been left to bake forever (until you use a spatula). As an aside: This particular pie has an Italian flavor that does really hit the spot. I'm going to order another. Also for your convenience, the staff here is very friendly, as long as you can make your way to the front door. I was giddy. So far, so good. But to be fair, it's a bit of a challenge. The oven is very warm, and when the hot crust is cooking, the edges are golden brown, but they are still soft and moist.

I didn't like sushi but I did like the decor. The fish is fresh and fresh, the vegetables are crisp and cooked to perfection, and the service is first to go, and last to eat. The quality of the fish is impressive, even while its preparation and presentation must not be subjugated to a more practical atmosphere. As with any entomology and art form, the environment matters because you are either at the market or occupying a seating area to  And, while Akiko makes sure that each fish is fully cooked when you are presented with your plate, the food is also expertly presented to the table in One may be thinking, "Do I like Japanese food?" I wish a place with a beautiful view of a skyline would be the place to enjoy a hearty meal. Why sit around while your food is being cooked? To me, this is the perfect setting for a perfect meal.

Originally the store was for the locals; the locals wanted a local grocery store. After a while the original owner had to give up for the benefit of his family’s children and moved to a smaller facility that offered a better With the loss of the grocery store as a whole it had a difficult time keeping up with the rest of the market for several years after that. The best way to describe The Coffee Bar at this time is to quote from the name. I discovered Dulce Pizzeria last night while having a late night meal at a friend's wedding. The day we decided to go out, I was running late and I was headed straight to the pizzeria at my destination. The next day at work, I set out to find a pizza place that would satiate my vegetarian food addiction. Even for an hour and a half before, Dulce Pizza was looking surprisingly average. I was greeted by someone who smiled, took my order, and then disappeared. It had a strange, gritty feel to it. In my mind, it was obvious the kitchen had been covered in oil and grease. I tried not to eat anything unless the place was busy and I felt that a pizza was my only opportunity. The waitress offered no discount but she seemed to notice that they were taking orders quickly. My food came out when it should have. The salad arrived with the chicken, eggs, greens, and a side of shaved Parmesan cheese, thrown into a plastic The salad was very nice, though a touch overly sourdoughy and a little lacking in taste. It came with a nice crisp crunch to the edges of the leaves that a bit of dressing would have saved. Then was the chicken tenders, which were soaked in sauce for hours and weeks with the olive oil/soy sauce and cooked until a The melanzone was nice and warm but the sauce was incredibly intense. I was amazed by the food's mellowness which went from the skin to the top. And no salt. No pepper. It felt like what I expected. I feel really sick of all the red sauce's! How could a pizza that did not smell so good be so good? Even a little. It was not too bad, but it was not good. However, I found myself lingering on the food for just a moment. What I thought was a good pizza ended up as a better sized pizza that was much too little. You'll have to admit, when I first tasted the sauce, the eggplant felt a little lumpy, but after slathering it It could only have been a sauce. I didn't know about this place. I was glad with what I had. For a moment I thought it might have been roasted in some kind of brown sugar before being plated, but I was pleasantly surprised. It was as if the Chef had been to Italy a few times and was familiar with the local recipes and ingredients. My stomach was aching from the richness and mouthfeel of the sauce and the crust was well done.

It was wonderful to meet someone who was willing make my life a little easier. Been to this friend's many times and never been disappointed, which was the case as it was the first time I had one here. The fresh fruit, fresh bread and the friendly greeting from the counter was a welcome relief. I wish I could eat there every day. Trentini's Kitchen has been in business in our area and has been serving a very good selection of Italian and southern American food for years. Its Italian Italian menu includes several new and exciting offerings over the last year or so. The restaurant is casual and bright, with a well stocked bar and a high ceiling. On the other side of the room, there is a small kitchen with an excellent selection of ingredients, but it's hard for me to make up my We selected a pizza that was made with volcanic cheese. The pizza itself seemed to have been cooked in a pot of oven at some point, and the sauce was delicious (try not to oversalt) with We pushed the pizza into the oven and it smelled wonderful with all of the spices and seasonings packed into the crust. But it had some very heavy mozza cheese, a small amount of fresh tomato sauce, and a few sprinkles of pepperoni. But... no... this was a tomato pie. At least this was our first try at the pizzas, as they made it all the way to our table. Unfortunately, the pie got heavy, and we could only eat half, which made it difficult to maneuver around the plate. This made it particularly difficult to enjoy the meal when finished. This pizza, however, had a very mild tomato flavor, and the pie itself was excellent. While we finished the pizza, it was slightly cold, which was a significant surprise given how quickly the restaurant opened in the early '90s. It will be sure to reappear on our next visit.

Cheeseboro's is an up and coming diner based out of a restaurant at the New River Market in the North Hills, Indiana. If it wasn't for the fact that the owner took on a new lease, that building would be vacant. They don't take orders. It is just as your food gets prepared, so it's always fresh. There is an almost identical kitchen (one of what had been left from earlier use) that is primarily used for making sandwiches. The fact that their orders are placed so close to each other, does tend to speed up the processing and quality even further. There are several tables set to sit out in the back area. The menu is extensive, and the food is pretty good. The food is really good. Cheeseboro's provides high quality food here, and I was able to get myself a big meal and take a few minutes to take a The menu is not very elaborate, but it doesn't seem to make sense. The bread was really good, as was the fish loaf. That's why I ordered it along with a French onion soup (made by the waitress herself). A lot of people, including the manager, had opted at the time to substitute brisket for the fish, but it really was enough for one What I really didn't understand was the onion collar and the side of chowder. I could barely put anything there. The restaurant is small, mainly filled with pies, but the quality is good. With the lunch I had, I ordered to go. The whiting sandwiches came in pretty big containers. Also, much better than a bag of brown dog slaw. The side of iced tea was excellent. So, four to go. The salad had been cooked in a pressure cooker for a while and was perfectly fresh. The other side dishes included an iced tea cocktail, which was a pleasant sipper. "Best of": "Spicy", "Bold": "Sad", "Too Good," "Edgy," " The food here is delicious, and it works. And hey, if you go with your wife there, you can get two free sandwiches.

Very nice and charming place in downtown Phoenix. Is everyone in awe of this venue? When I look back at the menus and menus at restaurant chain establishments, they are all a hoot. It is now a charming family bar where the decor is charming enough and the decor is as unique as the patrons who visit the place. Like a museum, it has wonderful history, and is more than a place to sit and take in the view, but also an experience to explore. The outdoor space is also spectacular. It's a fun place to spend time with the dogs, a comfortable comfortable place to catch up on work, or simply have a nice dinner This is one of the reasons we like this place so much. I don't think the eats and drinks are as good, because a couple days of sitting in the restaurant doesn't really take long. But the sausage was undercooked, and the eggs were extremely runny. Some of them was a little too soft and not all that chewy. What we could have done should have been more. The only other complaint I had was that the coffee was too strong, and the burgers got so greasy that the sausage fell soft, and was flavor However, the food and atmosphere were a lot better, and definitely worth the price. The menu was a little limited, and most of the menu items are from an Indian and Chinese-style menu. The kids were well fed, and enjoyed being outside, albeit to a limited extent.

To the animals, I could only imagine the glee of an entire animal from a close-up that he would be excited to walk around. It brought to mind the science of natural history when my children were young. That was his fantasy too. I learned a lot, both in terms of science and philosophy. Some of it is actually true, but has been discounted. The tavern is located at 97 Easton Road in Plumsteadville, and is a nice addition to this neighborhood. As if to further confirm that it was not a shady spot in town as was once claimed, Devil's Acre Tavern has in In fact, the first time we visited for lunch on a Saturday in the spring, the restaurant was empty. During Happy Hour we sampled the happy hour menu. We had a selection of drinks to try (trying to find the right one for the restaurant). At first my stepdaughter and I didn't really like the soup, but our companions agreed it was good. There's a good selection of dishes at lower prices, and for most people I would probably choose to make the apps at a later time. And good enough for two of us. They were very good for the price and a great starter to an otherwise fantastic meal. They weren't ok, but I tried to taste the potato pierogi before ordering. The dough was mushy, and a little oily, and had the same chewiness of an onion soup. Some people complained about the crust not beingggy, but they felt like it just had a weird texture. In all, our waitress was extremely friendly, and our server provided great customer service. The chicken breast and onion soup were excellent, but the BBQ buns were very dry. Did not like the red onion slaw, it was a littleggy. I love to eat here and find a good location where you can watch the food preparation. I also liked the soup as it did have a bit of a kick to it. They were fantastic!. Had an awesome dining experience at Devil's Acre Tavern, great bar and great service! Just needs some good food and more HH.

I got this coupon from an uncles and aunts Facebook page, so we figured we'd stop at Pizza Hut to purchase a pizza for It wasn't too busy, but they needed one more pie, so ordered one of three to go. We wanted to get a crusty whole pie pizza, with the cheese layer on top of our slice. We were too hungry and couldn't even finish the rest. The crust wasggy and oil dripped from the bottom. So we could taste the cheese that had been used for the pizza, and then lifted the slice with both hands. We began to eat it and we thought it was good. The crust was very good, cooked in an airy oven that also smoked. It was an unappetizing experience. We were also disappointed by the lack of chicken bouillon, a piece of bbq chicken, and a piece of ham.

Chuck has a huge selection of organic and local ingredients, as well as a large selection of flowers and a variety of products. He has grew up living in the South (near San Francisco), and his garden and produce are from around the world, including many small gardeners in It is a small shop, about about half of what I would consider a grocer's shop. I recently moved from Oregon and need more than a box of jars of kale or neems. I don't think that this is a problem in most cases, mainly because it is very expensive and often varies amongst sources. As part of the move to a small city like Ntown in the summer, I thought, "We will be able to buy some food here." But of course, if I don't take advantage of this location it isn't helpful at all. All the staff are young, clean and friendly, and they welcome you with open arms. My next visit may have to be the day after my anniversary, because that is a day for us to pay tribute after all. Here, the shop is so tiny it feels like he has just stepped in the back door! We used to ahem, keep the front window open, as we always did after the rain, but this year, it makes a big impression on Despite the name, you can't get too many of it. I enjoy it, and I look forward to seeing it all year round, even when you aren't looking out the window.

When I first went in, we were seated outside. An inviting bar.It has a French touch, but the menu does not. A variety of wine and beer selections. Full bar of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beers. I ordered a simple Short Sleeve of French Toast. Ordered this morning and decided to try their French toast with four wedges of buttery Carolina toast. This was ordered at 8 am and the toast was delivered in 10 minutes. As quickly as we ordered it they took their time deciding between the short stack or the two large wedges next to the French Toast. I tried it once at a time, but it was too thin and tooggy. The serving plate had the wrong side up. Their batter had just dipped and no burnt skin. I have never used a kitchen knife to help a French Toast. The topping was too cold, not a good thing. This wasn’t my first chance at French Toast but it certainly wasn’t my last. A tad disappointed. Perhaps we'll try again next time. What does it take to get a quality food truck?

In the summer, we visited a restaurant in Chattanooga for our first trip to Laos. We stopped by for lunch while our car was parked outside to avoid the heat of the morning's arrivals. Our waitress got us a few items for a small charge without any problems. She asked for our name, order and the location; we had no idea what we ordered, so she asked we order at the front. The food arrived as we left. She then set the table, brought water and a friendly waitress sat down to take our order and answer questions. We were ready for the burgers and the hot noodles, having done away with the fried Chicken Na soup at the previous restaurant. The Homemade Laotian Sausage was warmly salted and flavored with a mild seasoning that added a fresh flavor and the sausage was It seemed like a hot sausage with a hint of garlic. Nam Khao Salad had a thick, warm salad base with iceberg lettuce, carrot, radishes and beets on Drunken eggs were warm, the hot was tangy and the egg was very tender, but at the same time was still quite sweet. It was good, but our bill showed a little too generous for our tastes. The Service was very prompt, but it was not one of the crowded service I wanted. When all of our sandwiches arrived to go, the meal was just as good as if we ordered in restaurant.

A convenient place to order, eat and socialize, with good prices to match. The large outdoor grilling area is spacious which is a great way to view the food being prepared, even if the hot water gets overflowing  No bad seats at the tables. We tried the traditional Hibachi and the Tempura Box which were acceptable, but the quality of the meat is just average to average. The staff is pleasant as is the food, but they are unable to accommodate a large family or busy lunch rush. The hotter than usual food isn't enjoyable either. Overall, I am not an immigrant from Japan and do not feel drawn to this cuisine. The Hibachi food is ok as with other Japanese fast food joints nearby. A few of the items offered on the kabeku (watered down Japanese versions of their restaurant menus) are not terrible, but not great My friend from out of town came here as well, and was impressed by the decor. The rolls were dry, perhaps because they were brought out in advance. I hope to go back and try to order a new roll, but not too often just because it is good. Ota is a solid, but not exceptional, experience with a variety of options. I would recommend the regular Hibachi to go places like Meizu, or Watanabe, though.

I was expecting a vegan "hot dog" with a sweet lemon glaze sprinkled on top. I figured the fact that there are plenty of vegan options for breakfast, that a vegan menu included pancakes, and that they were vegan made it even If this is what happened to the original ingredients (which I'm still waiting for) then that is definitely what I blame... well, and they were definitely Although Turning Point has not yet opened, its concept is already in place, and it was etiquette to go in for a drink. The interior is a great mix of clean, simple, but hip, and decorated in what looks like the style of a small village. There is lots of table seating, and this is not a restaurant where you will receive a waiter directing the customers. At the outset, the ambiance was nothing more than a whimpering old college campus-looking parking garage. It was a tad overpriced, but the coffee was fantastic and didn't leave me feeling cheated. And, it's not like I was expecting it to be better than any other Pancake House on the block, either. After eating my breakfast, my coffee, and the lunches I had there, I wished I had stayed longer. Turning Point is already making a big splash in Newtown after getting the franchise opened in the Village @ Newtown Shopping Center. I am not sure if this area will be a success, or a failure (okay, I'm just a bit of a ), a new wave of local food outlets is coming to Newtown in two or three years. At this point, the taverns are really the exceptions, and people don't seem to have a choice. Regardless, the mall is starting to feel like a good one in the short term. I wish them the best on this challenge.

In my youth I had a passion to drink coffee. That's where the coffee comes in and is the reason I keep my morning mug full! However, there are a few places in Florida that offer superior quality of raw coffees. One of them is The Crock n' Coffee Co., home to the world's finest coffee beans. They are also very responsive to my needs and shipments on a regular basis. As you can see in the pictures to the right, the beans are already roasted and ready to pour out into the tea kettle. After 10 minutes we sent in our order. It was my birthday the week before and it must have been a busy time. They were delivering to us from South Africa so I had a special treat. I have always enjoyed the Ethiopian beans more than the Bee's Knees blend. It was time to pay them a visit. To my surprise on arrival at the shop, the Ethiopian Natural Kembata grade 1 had a unique aroma to it that I had to pay attention You know you are into something special when you snort it when it comes to quality, flavor and aromas. It possessed an elegance that I have rarely seen in so many coffee drinks. As my first sip, I can't say enough about the flavor, the texture, and the balance of flavors coming through. Well, actually it was quite a pleasant surprise. After setting up for the day's brew, cooled the cup under a faucet, added a cup of cold water and a couple Then it was off to the cafe, and the apex in the mug took the time of day to settle into place. I couldn't believe I had a real cup of coffee in my hand, the sensation of the ground coffee settling into my hands and then floating away This is the kind of coffee you can only dream of drinking. When we opened it, the bitterness became too strong to compete with what was going on, so we tucked it all into a small coffeebag

Service seemed a bit out-dated, but there is some originality and decoration. The setting was a bit odd... very casual. With no seating, that was the best fit for my small chowder plate. The food was nice, but I figured that because the food was prepared with a wooden board and a steamer oven, most items may age somewhat The vegetables and chicken dishes came with a lot of extra sauce, like it was the third day of Ramadan - which means it was a I ordered a chicken dish, which came with a mix of potatoes, carrots, green beans, peas, and rice on the side. A few of the dishes I didn't want were a little too spicy, so the khubbati dish had it covered in a very The place was packed with locals and it was all of the people I saw, so I didn't mind the lack of advertising. The portions were generous so most were enough for two. The customer service is great. And what happens next when you run out of food?! There is something about the air of freshness that I do not particularly like in many Indian restaurants, and this one delivers on both counts. The food was excellent, as was the service.

The beautiful, modernly run, and family run coffee bar in the middle of the Upper Valley, on the corner of Route 32 and I-90. In fact, it is the only coffee establishment in the city to offer an organic option, in addition to the traditional cafeteria coffee. The decor is clean and simple. They give you a small cup to sip from, and the coffee is encased in a beautiful glass container, adorned with chocolate sprinkle Coffee has a robust dark chocolate taste, and a perfect amount of licorice. The coffee was warm, deep and nutty. Perfect..so good. Saffrony, blackberry, and chocolate, complemented by notes of dried rose petals, a beautiful sweet honey, and a pleasant acid Perfect milk.The coffee's flavor was not fad-like, but was fresh by definition. Perfectly roasted. It was a pleasure to spend the last 45 minutes as she pours a second delicious cup. Best of all, there is no milk. The flavor is fresh, dark and dense all morning. The filtered coffee is a little too sweet, but there's a deep, subtle flavor. There were plenty of things to do, but as for me, the wait for the first cup of coffee was worth the wait. It is a must-try item if you plan to go to Chicago; the local coffeehouse is one stop between here and the airport. No place like Ray's in Stamford would appeal to just anyone who is interested in coffee or has tasted coffee at their local cafeteria or So be sure to bring your favorite camera!

I first met Lily in 2006 when she was a waitress at the popular Dutch Market. I got to know her during my visit, just as I had with everyone else. If you have a chocolate addiction, Lily has a little spot for you too. Like most people, I am very picky about my chocolate, so I opted for the unisex variety of chocolates. It is the soft, dense leather goods that beckon you and your eye is drawn to the chocolate & peanut butter cups.The boxes in the display But really the atmosphere sets the scene in the shop. She has a little notebook to the left of the shelves in case she forgets to take notes. Take a bite from the various treats and ask for the expert advice. The chocolate and the treats are everything you could imagine on the way up from Reece's. I bought 2 shards of milk chocolate: a jar of peanut butter and a jar of chocolate covered peanuts, so I  A half pound of her peanut butter cups was enough to fill me almost empty, and Lily topped them off with a bag of milk chocolate with Or at least in the picture I'm wearing, would I want a chocolate bath? I probably wouldn't try the buckeyes any more... Or how many customers the quality of your chocolates could you have had at Reece's? I guess I'll have to eat the full box. There is a price to support local, independent business, that carries a soul so rich it's hard to go back. I mean, come visit. I will be back soon!

Luckily I decided to try my hand at being a better student again. It is fairly old but has a surprisingly good restaurant concept. Fortunately, the restaurant was open. The servers' manners are so friendly that I was quickly given the hint that I had visited with her previously. She was quick and took great care of me. She was a willing host; I was just starting my shift, but she suggested a three cheeseburger with fries. Adrianna sneered and made a little comment about how good them tasted, but he didn't know if I wanted And I said, yup. No worries, I might order one of those as a side if I wanted to. There was a good balance of burgers and potatoes, with the fries a tad over the top. Luckily, I got a bite of my burger, which was a medium, almost lukewarm patty (not a I enjoyed the ketchup, but the cheese was way too salty to be liked any more than a ketchup. I wanted a little meat to make my buns crispy. I won't deny the first half of the food as good, as this is a small joint, and the food is good. I had a burger for lunch, and enjoyed, as the restaurant told me, the flavor of beef might make a comeback during the summer. However, I found that by the time I got home, I was  exhausted and hungry. I felt really  hungry for some sort of protein fix, so I turned in the request form for a burger at the same restaurant. I just couldn't quite do anything to change that. It was a pretty nice evening, but I would have loved a more thorough review. I'll say that I'm definitely going to avoid this place again next time. How much more would I be willing to pay?

After a long road trip, and a quick visit to the old Elgin Chicken Shack, I headed up Broad Street and dropped into the location I was visiting from Montreal after being back in town a while. They opened in 2011, and have come out with new style and feel. If you are looking for a good, fast and tender fried chicken around town, take a look. Popeye's is conveniently positioned between the two large parking lots that run by the place. The chicken itself was very tougher than standard chicken, though not raw. The chicken was thick and tough. Very hard.Fast to bite. Their wings were moist and tender though quite dry. And had the guacamole. The sides were very good, with fresh peas, tomatoes and corn. Great place for a quick post-work meal. Popeye's has a lot of space in the shop but you will be able to find a spot to sit and enjoy your meal. I gave it three stars without a question because it was definitely worth it.

This was located next door to Tao Thai, right next to the Vietnam Army Academy. As it happened, I ordered the Banh Mi, and the Drunken Noodles. Why the poor quality? Why don't they have that kind of thing in stock or what are they trying to tell their customers? As if it was a secret that they can no longer get it, they did a good job in trying. The coconut was slightly sour, with no tang in the taste. Then the Drunken Noodles went down the same path as the soup. I was so hungry I had to have the Banh Mi. I ordered the spicy hot wings and there was a tiny amount of spicier steaming sauce on the bottom instead of the usual noodle-based It was just barely pleasant. When I asked for a beer, no suprise. Forget everything you've ever heard of Thai restaurants, as these were definitely not Thai. Unfortunately for Vietnamese restaurants like Pho & More, the lack of Thai flavour, the unfocused menu and attitude, and the lack of customer satisfaction, are If they have it, they should have it because these dishes fall into the category of "spicy." I am no expert on Vietnamese cuisine, but know that Thai kitchens tend to be really good in Thai cuisine. But I've just got to know who the real cook is. If you're looking for something to eat in the area, I think you should look elsewhere. Go check out some of the places out in Vietnam!

River Horse provides a typical American neighborhood hangout. I was so pleased to try this place. The name (applebee's) reminds me of all those other chain restaurants on Route 66. I had seen the menu before and knew it had to be good, but the decor was not over the top. I was driving from Boston to the Pittsburgh area on a Friday night, so I decided to drop by. With so many options at the restaurant that don't require me to be anywhere near the bar, I decided to check out the local area. There was a bit of an in-front smokin' in the corner of the bar and parking lot. We made our way by way of the lobby to the bar. An friendly server took my order off the table,  explaining that the beer offered was "Fallouts" (also a great gif!) We got to chit chat about music and where there was a good atmosphere. You will find the beer on taps right next to my table. Kate placed it on the back seat, so I could take the beer home. When I asked the staff if they had any food, they were kind, and suggested two food items. My order came out to be a "burger." We had one bite too many and wished we only had a few more. I think the cheese sauce did a good job of contrasting and moistening the dish. I was not a fan of this dish, and it isn't that I couldn't do it at home since it isn't  Their large portion is relatively large for the price of a burger. The burger cost over $5 which is an excellent value. Applebee's also provided a nice menu selection with a couple of salads and a side of chips and salsa, and they even offered

The menu at Brooklyn Bagels includes two variants of the classic Boston Style (alongside three other Bagel Houses), the one at Brooklyn's The latter refers to the original ingredients that are used in a variety of flavors, and is commonly associated with the name of an ethnic group. In terms of what the two words mean, ostensibly the latter means that the bags are fresh. One of the bagel houses I frequent, however, is also a fairly reliable source for my signature Brooklyn style bagel. The bagel is tasty all the way through and the toppings are rich, tender and rich. The food is deliciously prepared, and the waitress is prompt and clean. Manhattan Bagels is a chain, but it is certainly a franchise. Definitely a worthy addition to the regular bagels list, and a must after breakfast. With a side of coffee-a-holics in the background, and its delicious breakfast, there is no reason not to enjoy it.

If you are looking for fresh meat you should head to the Harrisburg, New Jersey location of HBH Deli. Unlike the chain whose logo is rather obscure, I have found a number of them in Tyler Park, NJ. A nice selection of food is available in the Tyler Park location, and is usually fairly inexpensive. I've ordered many meals here and I really like the bread and sandwich. I have been impressed by their sandwiches. I love how the sandwiches are made in small lots, so they are really fresh without having to wait any longer than the typical HBH shop, and I like The cashier is very nice and does a good job in registering, delivering and ating the food, but I have had to explain to him Because most of the sandwiches don't have sides (unless you ask for them), they are probably not worth a visit. There is one in the Valley Road section that I do not recall (not only is it less busy, but that is less quiet). It has been very good but in a short time the prices have gone up. It also has a good location, but is more than 30 minutes from the subway.

I know about that time when we need to go with ourselves to an emergency room when we have a minor chest infection and are trying to regain some sense Most of us know better than to get injured in the hospital, eat at the table and smoke and over a cup of coffee. Jefferson Medical Center is not any more a place where you feel disoriented. I have seen the best medical center in the country. The hospital has a comfortable environment. The staff is professional and caring, and most therapists are dedicated to helping each patient. Being a patient of the hospital is an important consideration for me: for the patient’s peace of mind, and the patients’ health. You won't be disappointed. If you are looking for a good atmosphere and patient interaction go there. And, as with all hospitals, they are as good as they come.

"King of Diners" The place has everything right. I first went back about a year ago while I was in the area, and recently found the menu quite good. I got there about 7:00 p.m., was seated at a booth, then made my way inside. The menu has a variety of items, including a selection of soups and wraps. I chose to have the Chicken Salad, and chicken soup. The soup was very thick. I liked the Fries too though, so a few stars for that! The Fries were well seasoned, but also had some heat from the sauce. I ended up with 3 pieces of chicken salad with 3 rounds of fries on one side. The service was also good. The menu was quite well-organized and easy to digest. It was very clean, and I enjoy dining in restaurants that stay clean. I don't know who it is, but I enjoyed it, and I am looking forward to returning soon. I will definitely return and give them another go.

Tina's coffee has become more of a regular and the service is very good. At the lunch hour today, our server, Tina, was excellent. I love the quality, and I think it's a great value for breakfast. After all, I am the customer. I like this place. In-progress.

The food is authentic and excellent. The coffee is great. The chocolate is so-so. The pizza is a good size, with a good sauce. The drinks are not very unique too which is nice. I love it..I don't hate it. A friend of mine got the same donut from an outside window. I go there, sometimes.

I did not stop off at California Tortilla, but the food tastes good. They have a lot going on but don't just put the usual chicken, corn, ricotta and cheese. Their roasted meat teddies, quesadillas, and enchiladas are very good, also. The place has a lot of Spanish speakers, and it was busy on a Saturday night at 5 p.m. but this place was very busy If you are looking for something to eat that's fast and authentic, but also serves good grub, then California Tortilla has  It came with two salsas to choose from. The Pineapple and Bee Sting sauces were excellent. There aren't too many hot sauces on the menu, but they were well-balanced and balanced. It's a wonderful combination. It included the hot sauce and a tiny little pitcher of the Honey sauce to go with it. At the same time, the Chicken Quesadilla was absolutely delicious and very filling. If you like a good meal with tons of sauce, this is your place.

This is a great place to eat on an early Friday morning at Newington Street. I was there for the first time to have a good lunch with Bambino and his friends. The entire place is very attractive! I was not impressed. In the middle of the kitchen is the Server with her head held high and with her gaze fixed on the customers. I had the luscious Argentine Lamb Bourdouin with olive butter and red and green cheeses. I ordered the Salsa and the Home Made Bread Basket and the Basil and Olive Oil Soups with Tomato, Herbs, Onion I enjoyed the Turkey Breast with the Olive Oil & Ricotta Alfredo. The thick, rich flavor of the olive oil kept me all afternoon. And, when I tasted the bread, cheese, meat and tomato sauce – I found myself in over my head. I had the Rigatoni a la Scaloppine (Francoise), a skewer of an Oven baked dish While it was quite a feast, I did not experience a real sense of appreciation for the chef who made it. I really enjoyed the meal, and the service was good. In addition, I can’t forget to mention how generous the meal was.

I was quite surprised to find a casual Vietnamese House outside of City Hall. I found it by accident near SF Airport, probably to take advantage of there being someplace similar to it nearby - I had known about this place from The menu was simple, and presented a pretty basic meal. is a small private table that can be booked for groups of eight or more. As with all Asian joint in the greater Boston area, I was a bit put off by the lack of Vietnamese choices, but we decided to give it  Almost immediately the server opened his door to the left and glared blankly at me. I guess you should have given it two tries at a time. The Spring Rolls were good. Just as described.As usual, the bread rolled up (even though the bottom half could have used a coating.) They came with a few small cut outs of lemongrass, which complemented the rolls nicely. The portion was large enough, but not thrice overflowing. It was a rather complex soup, but not at all overly soupy. The egg on top was good. Sadly, the Pho Phail was the worst of the three. Felt like the meat was overdone. I know there really aren't other choices (at least here in SF) for the Pho, but I was forced to order the Beef The cutlet was chewy, with more skin than meat. The egg noodles were not cooked at all, but more like under cooked egg noodles. I ended up with a bowl of cold broth and more than two inches of meat. I didn't try the other dishes, but will be back for a tidbit.

Lee's is a nice local cafe on the corner of Park and Le Moy street. One might expect the restaurant to be just like another Vietnamese café & bistro - a breakfast, lunch and dinner area. You can still see the redstone-clad roofline of our home, but just beyond the awning, you can see a red brick wall. The food is prepared quickly and is clearly visible when you walk through the dining room. The menu is easy to find and the portions of the dishes are substantial, even if a big portion. The service is quick and friendly, with a small staff, and a big menu. The place feels quite modern - and that's a plus for the modern day space. The outdoor space is huge, with a good patio if you like to take a break, and the coffee has a light Belgian stein It felt like we were lining up for an overpriced diner offering a runner up to Pho Tai. It was, but for the price - we expect a better meal. The Summer Roll was a little tooggy and the flavor of the sauce not very pleasant. Well, the shrimp - a great contrast to the plain white roll. However, the Pho Tai came through with flavor and a slightly overwhelming slurp. The slurp was thick and too sweet: more acid than sweet. The tea was served on the side of the pho with a few frothy ice cubes and an egg. The BBQ Pork Banh Mi was just as good for a cheaper price, and just as tender. But it was soggy, and did not have much flavor to it. That is true that they use the regular baguette that they have at Pho Ha. The price for the three dishes ($3); the rice tea (a good substitute for the local fruit juices); Pho Tai (the chicken-p And, like Pho Ha? A little overpriced for the quality and quantity of the food and service. It is only the quality of the menu that really matters.

Typically we find the best of the best when it comes to sportswear and clothing for the common man: baseball and basketball. As I am at the hospital undergoing surgery for my son, the need has always been for a store that sells quality youth basketball gear, and Dick This is a retailer who does it really, really well. The price is reasonable and the discount card cards are good. There is a large portion of the selection for children, as well as Nike and other well known brands. Our daughters Nikes were only $19.99 each, and so were they in two sets. The shoes, however, lasted approximately six runs and I'm happy to let you know they are almost ready for Christmas. With this purchase I am a bit confident that I will become a regular wearer of Dick's and get the best price every time. Dick's Sporting Goods is open Mon. through Thurs., 10am - 5pm, and Fri. 10 am - 3pm

My favorite restaurant is Olive Garden. I had two of our kids bring their mother over this Memorial Day weekend for some light Italian cuisine. My son (my father) has to deal with a limited amount of food on regular meals, with some of it being extra chicken. My daughter likes pizza, and loves her pizza with cheese and veggies. I also want to eat with the kids, but also for my husband and our pet. I am a low-calorie omnivore, and I needed something to fill my belly. The dinner was at 7:30 and we had lunch in-between our reservations. So we headed to Olive Garden on Tuesday evening from noon to 2pm. My mother ordered two salad bowls and two Breadsticks. Ordered the unlimited salad, breadsticks and chicken wings (with a side of sauce) on the "Light" menu. The Salad was well-dressed, though the ingredients didn't really wilt. It was still warm, but with a light taste. On a Tuesday, we were able to have a casual dinner without complaints and to have "a salad" or salad and breadstick, not both The other two dishes came quickly. After tasting it for a little while I agreed that it didn't have the right flavor and that the garlic was not as bad as I remembered. They added the threw with the garlic and the tomatoes. The onions were good, the Spinach too, but the garlic dressing was too light and too sweet. I could have easily made off with a little more salt before the chicken was done cooking. As most Italian Restaurants attempt to woo customers with big portions, I was fairly pleased with my experience. Will Olive Garden be my new go to restaurant? No.The Salad was delicious, but the Chicken was good, but they made it a little dry after the Garlic Rosemary sauce was added However, one of the salad sides that my family was expecting to share with us was the Chicken Soup. I was looking forward to the wings, but at that point I didn't think any of my friends would go for it. There is not much of a better option on the menu.

Yes..Is this a good gas station? If you live in either the East or the West side, this station is well away from other gas stations. I have no problem getting the price I need by myself during the week. The pumps are clean and there are a few good cars parked in the parking lot. Also, the price is good, so much so that I keep going when I am traveling.

I was quite pleased with the experience of my breakfast at Cafe Istanbul. It was on the upper floor area below the Morrisville Saloon/Gala Bar. I found it by looking around for signage. The restaurant used to have a Turkish-ish feel, which still exists. It's nice and casual, with a nice layout. My first breakfast, a nice cheeseburger with a pickled onion, tomato and pickle relish. Just like I had at home. Made with a fresh batch, and very similar to a French toast with a lot of butter. Perfectly cooked, fresh eggs. I tried a few different dishes for my dinner, and one of the waitresses had a chicken naan. This is an important item. The menu offered a few choices of sandwiches and other items, which was great. The location is just a few blocks from the Trenton airport. If you take a few seats at the bar, the menu features a very strong Turkish feel to it that will make you want to stay for the rest Despite the "cheap" price, the food is great, and the service was excellent. Service could use a little fresh tang with a sprig of kale. This would enhance the entire experience. Also, perhaps improve the quality of the fried chicken, instead of the generic plain old chicken.
