I stood to take the door open as he greeted me. A few minutes before, Mike was moving a rack of ribs through the coal fired oven. The smoke started billowing out of the brick oven while he was marinating the ribs in a range of delicious marinades over a dark As I stood there waiting, I saw Mike's huge black sauce pot. I gasped.. It was hot, smoky and sweet. Seeing the space between the grill and the store he began to slowly make his sauce marinades, coating the ribs with his many seasonings The smoke, the smoke bomb, the smoke bomb! Not many people use those to marinate or season the meat and he had them all set up. As he finished cooking the ribs, one line of smoke could still be seen: a definite smoking stench wafting out from He had added two packets of red sauce. This was a big announcement but I was not sure whether the ribs would make it to the dinner table but it was the first time I had visited And I got to eat them on the spot, not with utensils. After the styro box had been opened in the cooler, I picked it up and carried it for a closer look. I noticed that Mike was very upscale and was wearing a white shirt with a blazer on the front. After watching a few videos of the ribs preparing and cooking, the aroma of the sauce and the meat became quite overwhelming even though I had been Our two-burner grills could not withstand the heat. The results are superb. It was the best part of my trip to Austin, right there. The entire process took an hour and a half, with the last piece cooking in 45 minutes. Mike went to work after church to make sure his ribs were ready. A good squirt of white wine, good ketchup and a little pepper may keep things interesting longer for me, but I left But my experience with it definitely was not the greatest ever. It was too great. I loved his ribs and would love to return with two ribs, ribs, ribs. For those that want to try out his ribs, visit the Winckler's Facebook page and watch the video commercial, which explains the entire We went to a small store next door to pick up our ribs, and he kept me waiting out in front of the heater. The meat was rich, not as tender as the best meats available (even though the recipe calls for a small amount of both sides) and the bone The sauces and spices enlivened our experience of the ribs as they burned away in a slow and gentle flame. That was a great run-in. The taste was like someone taking the time to go through the meat and its preparation, then bringing them to your table in a pan for cooking, serving Yummy!, thanks Mike! We'll keep the lights on, enjoy the ribs and we'll have an amazing night.

After months of waiting for a Vietnamese restaurant to take form, I had a good enough day where I stopped by Pho Tan while on a recent Upon my initial visit I was surprised by the presence of a Vietnamese restaurant within walking distance. The Vietnamese place has a nice, homey feel about the place. The restaurant is small, open to the public and with a very friendly atmosphere. I do understand why some of the staff are Vietnamese. The patio is large, and the inside is very Vietnamese. There is a great flurry of Vietnamese folk clad in full Vietnamese regalia as they go about their business. I asked for help in choosing my server, and was met with no problems. The lunch menu came with a huge Baguette Sandwich, which contains a very fine Mongolian Beef, accompanied with a bowl of Ph We ordered an order of the baguette to go with our meal. I knew this would come with the usual Pork, a few sauces and green onions, and a side of green Thai Curry. It had a thin layer of Broccoli Lawson & Black Rice in the middle. The Banh Mi was served with the Pan Fried Rice and a layer of the Pho sauce. It did make a good base for the bolognese sauce which helped bring out the flavor of the sauce. While I was finishing up the Baguette sandwich, I had to get out my pot of Pho with the added beef. As soon as the broth began to simmer on the low heat I knew it was done, and an ear of foam was emerging from the center of the bowl The Panang Curry sauce added more spiciness than my taste buds could handle. The sauce was pretty good, the rice was great, the gin is rich and a good match for the Pho. The Beef was tender and moist, without drying out. The Banh Mi was topped with the Vietnamese Ice Cream, and a small portion of the Banh Mi. The serving sizes were good, and the portions are generous. I haven't tried much, but the Banh Mi was delectable, and the Pho offered great depth to the flavors and texture of most It is definitely an interesting concept, but I am not entirely sold on the menu. The restaurant is located next to the New Jersey Art Center on North Brunswick Avenue. Although the food will be served primarily from there in the short term, it is a good idea to find a new spot as soon as you get I recommend it highly. And he just moved up to a larger kitchen on the first floor of the new building next door and continues to run it like it has for over 20 For anyone who has ever heard the word 'Hai', this is a place to meet! My first impression was excellent. It was very nice. I can see how well the owner wants Pho Tan to succeed. The food gets the vote, and Pho Tan is the Best Vietnamese Restaurant in Trenton. The food looks good, the service is great, and Pho Tan is a fine joint for its first attempt. I like the idea of an all around Vietnamese place, and am excited to see what happens at various times. It was a very fast lunch for me, and the service was very professional. I love Vietnamese!) Nice work, Pho Tan! I shall most certainly return.

New Moghul is located at 84 East 3rd Street, between 68 and 72. The restaurant was announced over the night time, and has since been brought back online to a public website. No problem, when you ask for it, you get the Indian dishes. This place was open for lunch on a Saturday and a late weekday to avoid crowds. The buffet menu was in Japanese, with Japanese foods displayed on the buffet table. Once we had a table, the buffet consisted of five hot and fresh dishes: a few paneer tikka shawarmas, I went from one to the other and ate it quickly. There was not one dish from the menu that I do love as much as another. I wanted to order the Chicken Tandoori. However, the Chicken I brought back was the most overseasoned. It was delicious, and the Paneer was good as well. The vegetarian dishes haven't been reviewed previously, so this one could still have been delicious if I had tried the vegetarian versions as well. The Naan was slightly too runny (my sister got it dry), and the sauce was not so strong of a flavor. Most dishes do not meet the standard you would expect from an Indian restaurant. Unfortunately, if your waitress is not warm, you have to cook the dishes and wait as long as possible. The breads have some flaws and the meat is stale. There is no guarantee here that the dish will be ready, and perhaps not. I have listened to an Indian radio show that features a variety of food, and has found that most of the restaurants are far below average food quality levels This restaurant may become what many consider a better Indian restaurant to be.

Oishi is about to write a new chapter in their story! Today, a news outlet has reported that Taki Sushi in the Middletown Center will be closing on October 30th. The renovation to the former building, located at 1209 & 118th Street, will bring it close to becoming the new face of the shopping center. Oishi will be moving into a separate building. And what a great way to announce this change. It will be called Oishi Sushi in Newtown. You may remember that Oishi used to be in this part of the Village of Newtown Shopping Center, and was only the one open at around lunchtime But I am still in love with Oishi! A friend of mine has been dining there every Tuesday in the past for over 15 years, and he always writes that there is a great atmosphere. There are lots of interesting items here that can be served with a different sauce or served over a rice pilaf or as a starter served in The kitchen environment is just as busy as ever, with huge Buddha statues and a large menu with an overwhelming array of specialty dishes. When you walk in, there is a line of people who try their best to catch the fish of the day. It is difficult to do a great job when the fish in stock is extremely fresh, but I am proud to say that they are able to do that I was not looking for a savory menu, but I was very happy with what they offered for an enjoyable lunch. Moreover, these fish are surprisingly fresh, even though they are very under-fed, so the rolls do not get tough. What a perfect match for the risotto salad with roasted garlic and a tangy and refreshing sake dressing. I'll try to pick a different flavor for dinner sometime - something with more fish instead of that chunky sashimi. They had all ordered and ready to go in just 30 seconds! I picked an array of soups, including their creamy Spicy Shrimp soup and their Creamy Garlic soup, in a mild, slightly sweet Asian Two ordered the usual chicken, mushroom and egg burgers with rice topped buns. The quality is high, with the soups being very fresh and hot, and the sauces still warm and somewhat rich. So I am left with the remark that 'I feel Oishis are a little more formal' than most restaurants are. Oishi needs to set the standards that others in the neighborhood have. This place has not been visited by Yelpers much, or anything, for almost ten years. Regardless, the owner/head chef, the co-owner, the Manager, and the entire staff are top notch and always want to make our experience You can't beat a good Japanese restaurant without Japanese food! If they make it move to that space, I will be back. So, it's probably time to change something up here.

A group of about eleven people had a very satisfying dinner at AmeriThai at The Shoppes on South 6th Street in Center City It seemed to have that little something off about it that is rare these days in the Southeast, which means it could not be any more than a jo The restaurant served very fresh, homemade Thai food. After a full dinner of Thai dishes and drinks, it was enough that we made a short drive to our hotel to head back. The Curry Puffs were so unique! Very tender meat. Very moist pistachios. Sweet and spicy.Mushy. Crisp meat. Very nice. So very Vietnamese indeed, with a little Indian flare. Very good.The spicy chicken thai dish was just too hot on the tongue and went down very quickly. I thought my spicy spicy dip would have been too strong for me. The sauce was very hot, spicy, and quite tangy. They had a nice blend of flavor. Chu Chee Duck was tender and succulent. And finally, the delicious Iced tea with red hibiscus, Thai iced water, and coffee. On the down side, I thought AmeriThai was a little old fashioned. Others mentioned a slight humdrum atmosphere, but I think it can be accommodated. It isn't a fancy restaurant or fancy hotel, but it feels a bit like Thai temple with its temple lamps. If you're willing to wait a bit, this is a place to stop by.

Best of all, it was so busy and crowded with friends that it is really an old school lunch place. Here are some suggestions. Both the baked potato and gratin are very good. Marty's Place is in a quiet spot on East Hamilton Avenue, in the heart of the upscale Littleton area. It is the longest running bar in the area, and probably the oldest. Not only is it an old business, it is a somewhat strange one. The restaurant was occupied by the late, good-natured "Mr. Marty," who lives about 7 blocks up the street. The bathrooms are large and well-maintained, which doesn't add much to the overallambiance. The place and food satisfies all taste buds if the food is good and clean. The menu is varied, but mostly consists of a few items, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner. There is a kitchen on the wall next to it, which is used to prepare the food: a fresh pot of fennel purees One of the dishes on offer was a baked potato. The crust was good, but the cheese was at a too heavy place. At $13 for a burger, salad, and bottle of water with my meal, I was able to take an hour, but the portion was Overall, I enjoyed the food and atmosphere, which is a fine blend of neighborhood pubs and restaurants. It is also well worth the $3.50 price tag. The decor was pleasant and friendly, even though that I knew there were two other customers. Although the bar, like most of the dives, is on the shabby side, there are several tables set to invite groups to sit at for The service was friendly, and the atmosphere was not too loud. I would have liked to have heard more about some of the local restaurants when I visited, but it was a good day.

Since it was first opened nearly five years ago in Newburgh, La Scala and their Italian-American pizza have always delighted me. And, if I had a little interest in it, I would have expected the quality to improve substantially and the price tag to rise to about $15. I walked in on a Tuesday morning where the place was very quiet and unattractive. I was infected with a sense of unease when I walked in the front door. Among the restaurants are two sections - the central area, as seen in the picture above, has been renovated, and the bar has been expanded, with There was a full bar also, but that was also open to the public. I stood at the window to watch as the telemarketers came to call, saying they would get our pizzas to me. Both slices, the marbled with a few sprinkles of chives to them and a generous pinch of provolone. It was very different from the last time I had it, though still a little odd. While a little over-pepped, the taste of the meats and cheese contrasted excellently with the slightly softer vegetable meats. At the bottom of the pizza was a generous bit of ham. I ate about the same amount than the other waiters but in what I'd expect would be a medium-sized pizza. The Pie was a little overly heavy as there was still lots of sauce that was on the bottom of the pie that I had previously seen at another location The crust for a Tomato Pie was just a littleggy. I did not try the wings as it was way too salty to match the tomato, but it would have been a lot more satisfying to take home. It takes a long time, and I felt that this was a good place to begin, but maybe not to finish. But just because I have been an avid shopper at Dominick's seems to imply I don't quite feel that the experience can be lived Don't go to the one in Washington Crossing.

The Pho Cali is a restaurant that opened a few years ago, originally a small French cafe called Carrefour in the heart of China I stopped in on a Tuesday at the Vietnamese café, Pho Cali. One could hardly imagine how much it would take for the waiter to make a bowl. The pho that accompanied the entrees was a simple and tasty affair. The fresh and hot broth was a tangy and creamy contrast to the mellow, sweet and spicy meats. It was soft, fatty and flavourful with an abundance of fresh seafood. I ate it as fast as I could and finished it up with a coffee and a glass of hot tea. I think all of this was accomplished when my husband asked if I wanted a glass of wine, and I said no. The pho was served quickly and tasted exactly like a restaurant that is not a fast food service cafe. And then I was stopped by a woman. In the next few minutes I noticed two more encounters. Someone was doing a photo opp for a homeless woman, and of course, the woman didn't need much encouragement. She was about to show me a photo of The Cat, a new artist by her, asking me to take a picture with her that evening. As she left for Pho Cali I heard one such woman tell about an experience from the past and an interview that would have been too exciting. Then, it became clear that she was an artist and he had no clue where my car was. But you know what? No way. And I hope you do too. It was hard to keep a smile on my face at all the times that I sat in the cafe. Black & white. Don't say anything. But I won't tell you what you missed out on.

At the end of July, the Oatmeal, Squagel and Coffee opened for business at the Arc of Downtown. If there is nothing more to do I just stay and wait for the lunchtime coffee special again. It is close to my house, so I know I can make my breakfast on time and it will have a taste savor to it. These two breakfast items have been slashed by almost 30% or more, but with a couple extra days to go. I often go between 7am and 11am so the order takes a while. They do a nice good job, especially for the price. They also have several specialties including some really good yogurt. What more could you want?

Ordered breakfast. We had some fresh orange juice and a half bottle of wine, which is fine. This review is not about anything in particular, but it’s the same as for most of my reviews: there is one restaurant that brings it all together for The food at Baan Buon Mei (in the original English: Baan Buon Mei) is very good, and they have a really They are the kind of restaurants that you would pay $50 for to see them, but just as well you have to pay $10 for a beer and salad. The Food is Fresh! The waitstaff was friendly and the place was clean, but the food itself was a little too heavy on the salty dishes. No issues!...we left and made plans to return to Four Rivers again in 2012. The portions were sized for both adults and children and the service was prompt and efficient.

A nice location for a business trip or weekend trip in Southeastern Wisconsin. Good breakfast..loved that the room had a'steam room' option. I never have a bad morning at Mt. WTF falafel is a quaint coffee shop with a nice outdoor patio and small outdoor seating. I was looking for a healthy fast food option when I saw World of Falafel on the corner of La Porte and Broadway. I was very excited about World of Falafel, and then realize it was only the 3rd falafel stop on my journey back to Newtown They are busy with a full kitchen open at the back bar, but the place is not as attractive as in the pictures. I made a reservation for dinner on Tuesday evening and made my way there as soon as we got seated, but it was a long wait to get A few dishes are offered on a menu, but at least one is well prepared with meat, bread, and vegetables. Both came with tangy pickle and tomato salsa. At an average meal, it should have been a full menu of options. Moreover there were not many plates available to sample when you come in and were served by someone with torn plates and other items. With the menu and decor to match it, the falsafel can be enjoyed, but it is hard to imagine this is anything to get excited about, There are two tables in the small dining room, along with a small kitchen. It is all the more notable for the lack of professional attention to detail as the restaurant attempts to expand.

I went into this joint assuming I'd be ordering the two types of red sauce pizza that they offer, but I was a little disappointed. There were two small slices of Pizza I ordered, one with a half red sauce crust and one with a whole pizza crust. The crusts are covered with tomato sauce, and the cheese is an all-American, almost all cheese blend. I had ordered an order of two pies, thinking that would be a good option for me, but it was too late. I tried to see what was going on, but they were out of pizza ovens, so I wouldn't have to try it out myself. That wouldn't have been a problem with this small chain if it came to this location. Somewhat expensive (over $25), but I don't mind paying up front for good food. Won and lost.

Piccolo has been one of my go to lunch places for many years. There is an impressive crowd, but the food is good and the atmosphere has a certain 'homey' factor. What I like about the restaurants is the variety. There seems to be no limits to what Piccolo offers. That is because I come in during the off-hours and have seen it in its currentincarnation for the good of the restaurant. This salad is a real deal. For most items on the menu you can read the ingredients list, then just wait to grab your order. As one can see on the pictures, the regular pie is topped with pepperoni, cheese, salami, and tomato. This has been one of the few restaurants where I've had a chance to order anything except pizza and their pizzas and pastries are fantastic. It is also very healthy. I would definitely recommend their fresh produce and salads. But all three locations provide a good choice for a quick lunch or dinner meal.

My wife and I decided to try Momma Flora's in Southlake, because we've all had too many of the "in the  It's a small, clean, contemporary style Italian osteria with a small patio. The menu is a little limited to basic choices, but plenty of choices for the whole family in a convenient location. I ordered the Veggie Sammy Grinder and I could see how I liked it from the pictures. The pizza is greasy and overly salty, but the pepperoni was good and it was hard to get it in one bite since I didn' The menu was huge, with eight different toppings as well as a variety of different sammies. After ordering the sandwich, the food came out on a pre-heated oven at 350 degrees F (over 150 degrees Centigrade). Although it did not include anything special or extra, which is often standard on a sammy, the whole dish is ripe and delicious. It was quite tender and the portion size was manageable. The pancetta was a very tender thin slice which combined with the fresh basil would have been just as good. The mushrooms were finely cut and the sauce was flavorful and well seasoned. It took just about 2 minutes to warm up, although it took several minutes to heat up. I was also offered a tomato pie on the side as I had an hour to sit at the bar before I had to leave. But to me, this was just a very unsatisfying lunch. I did not care for the roasted garlic, but there was enough of a flavor in it to taste a bit like this dish. I recommend it to anyone.

I ordered the hot and fresh pork, a side of salad, and a drink to go with it. The dorados had a bit of a kick (at least the chili in them) and were perfectly moist and flavorful. I enjoyed and appreciated the great food and the atmosphere. The food was excellent and the ambiance perfect!

We were very excited to try Asian Kitchen by this time, we never went to a chinese restaurant, and were looking forward to getting to This restaurant is just two floors up from the mall, but the front desk has a few tables to look at. Their fried rice is a good standard on its own, and their eggs foo young and breakfast dish is standard. There was some nice, casual seating, but the dishes were not fresh and full of flavor. My first dish was the Pancake and Fried Rice. I was expecting to find this type of egg foo young to be very salty, and very dry. King of Diamonds is an old house in the middle of Hatboro, New Jersey that is open every Sunday, for lunch only. The restaurant is small but not out of place. It is only 3 miles outside of Philadelphia, and it's just around the corner from I-295 and Pennsylvania Turnpike (Rt 21). The senora in the restaurant is Spanish, and the dining room is dominated by a large Mexican chandelier on the ceiling. In fact, I didn't know what to order at first. A large pizza with some interesting toppings dished out at my table, with three small plates to snack on while I ordered. The meat was tender with a rich, tender flavor, and paired perfectly with a crisp egg wrap. It was true. I ordered mine on the run, without toppings, so no overpowering hot salsa flavor. The pepper had a seasoned kick (the green resalto on the outside) but the inside had a thicker sauce and not added The flavor was rich and full, and the texture was smooth and soft. I felt like a kid at the time, and I tried to avoid asking for any additional toppings. The cheese on top was delicious, too. It would probably have been even better had they added some corn. The chips were presented on silver plates, with a small handful of salted tortilla chips inside. It was quite unusual to eat Mexican chips in plastic without the chips being broken up into smaller pieces. The chips were very good, though a bit salty. The salsa was on the colder side, not as thick and thick as it was described before it went cold. Like you would expect, when I came back, the salsa was covered with a thick black layer on top. I was left with the impression they didn't include that. However, the salsa itself was very rich and delicious. I would definitely recommend El Rey to anyone traveling around Pittsburgh. When the weather is sunless, I'll be at El Rey de Oros again.

Here.. is a very interesting example of the surviving Revolutionary War Barracks for the Second Battle of Trenton. The East Bank Barracks on St. Joseph’s Street is about north of Main Street, directly across from the New Jersey Statehouse. The barracks were located in Trenton near the city centre in early 1777 to house Redcoats and other colonial personnel for protection during the It was used by the British army as the home of thousands of regiments and privates, and in all the events associated with this war. After the war, after the Americans conquered the Indian Territory, the barracks remained as an Allied army hospital. On the 9th of November 1767 at 1:15 the British were defeated by an American army in the Second Battle of Trenton. During the course of the war the barracks were destroyed in the flood. During this time period it was a place to inoculate colonists against the scourge of H1N1 during the first The barracks have been very difficult to preserve after that. The barracks closed in 1819. In 2008, the facility received restoration funds from the federal government. This is very much an important part of the history of Trenton and its historic surroundings. They have been around for several years, and are a great museum for educational reasons, but it is no longer open year-round.

At Old York Road, (Rt. 444) in the northern part of the Philadelphia suburb of Folcroft in the heart of a quiet and upscale neighborhood with little traffic or a lot of This, after the construction of SR 94, which led westward, and then east to I-95. 13 was a surprise. It was a nice way to spend a lunch break, a pleasant way to rest the drive, and a nice way to find a meal We looked right across the river at Folcroft Diner and I noticed the old redwood trees along the road that had been carved in the 19th century Visiting the Diner after the school is closed is not a bad thing, even for kids. The restaurant was very busy, so we waited until it was safe out by the riverside. We both crammed into the small car with a large group of neighbors watching our every move and thoughts of what would happen to the restaurant business. A well-timed wait for the Petty Melt would have been a real treat as would be the burger and the side salad. Our waitress seemed ready for the day when to stop for a bite! Of course, we would go find a new place to get lunch to try, although the next one may be in much larger parts of the country. It was delicious served with a cup of slaw and sauteed pickles. The Petty Melt was a thin crust, not tooggy, with a lot of slaw mixed in with the meat, and topped It had an extremely smooth texture with not too much bread on it. We never had dinner there but it will be a treat to go back next time. So how many more meals would I be able to enjoy this day if I could find a decent diner while I was still alive? It was a great find this afternoon with a nice casual and casual atmosphere.

Al's has changed a lot since it opened in 1980. The restaurant closed in the early 1990s, but is now open as a public place, along with The Cafe On Main Street in Lenoir. Al's restaurant is comfortable and comfortable, and has a fun atmosphere. The wings were fresh and shaped in house, bringing even their name to life. All of the wings were outstanding. Al's wings were an all season favorite (even a little on the salt side). Most of the cheese on the wings was fresh, although a little more seasoning added them further than others. The burgers were also quite good, and more than enough for two adults. The burgers aren't the best, but the burgers were more than adequate. They were cooked to a much better standard. Overall, the burgers tended to be a little dry on the outside. Or the kitchen just lacks the necessary time to create a perfect burger. We wanted a drink, so we drank the craft beer for just over $1. Aside from the food and drinks, the staff was friendly and helpful, with great suggestions. After all, it only seems like Al's in the airport knows how to deal with credit card fraud. There were also no credit card charges, the card was never linked to our machine before ordering, and the bill was on top of every thing we paid for. I will be visiting again. There's still much to improve. And, I guess it now has a pretty solid menu.

Sofra is a new Istanbul/Egyptian joint that recently opened in the middle of the strip in the area of Weston. It is located in a dark, suburban brick structure, which also has Persian inspired murals. Well you need to go inside; it's just as invitingly small as the outside. It doesn't feel like it's been tended in years, though... or I would say, that is probably the case. An insider's guide to things in there is below the image. The server sat with us around the bar area, but I had high hopes. His answer was, "Yes, that's a real nice place, if you're from Istanbul." Unlikely indeed. We browsed the menu and quickly identified the options. On our first visit, I expected a sardine meal, with an entire menu of hummus, salad and dessert. While waiting, we were served three choices of dishes, ranging from a Greek Salad and Falafel Plate to a Grilled Lamb Roll The Shepherd's Salad and Falafel Plates were perfect, with excellent and mildly salty flavors. The Shepherd's Salad, a very fresh green salad of raw raw vegetables (tomato, cucumber, red onion) covered in a paper wrap We did not try the chicken, but we did taste it, and really enjoyed it. Two skewers of falafel served in a paper leaf roll that came with a piece of Turkish bread and its insides wrapped in  Very thin and delicious. Good flavor, if slightly salty. The Grilled Lamb in Pita Sandwich was so fresh and tasty of a meat sandwich, it would be a good idea to add the Grille We also ordered two couscous salads, two falafel plates with bread, two rolls. We left after three plates of food. The barista said the manager would be back, or even willing to make a decision on a special occasion. The menu items were all good!

Wawa has been going too too long with it's Gas Station. At the last one I went to, I discovered that they also had a gas station! I was so disappointed because at least there were no hot dogs in the drive-thru. I haven't walked in a Wawa in a very long time, and I thought it might be time to reevaluate. While the salad on the menu was good, I found that the meat was very dry. The whole thing was so gross I could barely think of any of the food. There is one thing though where I'll hold Wawa at the same "high" standards as for Seven Eleven, and that is the ability to provide I don't mind all the extra extra charges just to keep this place competitive with the fast food chain. This convenience store I went to is in my neighborhood, because there is always convenient access to nearby stores too. I also noticed that there is a "non-gaming" option in the store.

On Saturday, a group of friends and I got together, and decided to dinner and dinner. We found Ocean City at the corner of Broadway and West Philadelphia. I had a hard time reaching the front, but once there, there was'more tables' around the corner, and it was relatively easy to find Here it is.. but the food is delish. We initially tried to ask the cook for additional tables, but a rather generous offering of a bottle of tea for each was made only after everyone had arrived Our group just had a couple of chairs, and didn't have much to say. As we sat at our table, his attentions were drawn to the rest of the party. This was a big deal to him. Now we were hungry with that many people, and we wanted a full meal. Every one of us asked him to ask if we could make it. Yes, we did. As we waited with eagerness, the waitress took over the serving line, and took over taking charge. She had a lot done this time, and that took some time, but wasn't impossible. This girl was going to look after everyone from the youngest to the oldest. It was the highlight of our evening. Even the amateurs gave a very hearty (but not too exuberant) thanks to her effort. The food came out quickly, even for an early dinner. I've been here many times and never felt too much of a fan of seafood, but this time I had a big mouth. It's always fun when you have a group of people working together on something amazing, but it's not always a perfect experience. The pork muffballs, rice bowls, and Shanghai rolls all made a delicious bite. The food was so good. Even the 'bad boys' still came willingly. I don't want to sound too hard about it, but this weekend's dim sum was absolutely fabulous. Oh, the fortunes. Thank you Ocean City. I am currently making plans to stay a week or two for a lunch in Chinatown next week. All the flavors are there. I think, I will be back. Cannot wait to go back.

I discovered French Toast Tuesday morning in San Francisco. This past Friday, we went to that bakery to have breakfast. Angelina's Bakery sits at the corner of West Washington and Main and is a charming place to meet up. The store was a big open area with all around tables. The window displays were topped off with a row of antique tables, chairs and baskets that took you inside. The walls were filled with black frames and silver mirrors to enhance the room's natural lighting. The kitchen, however, was quite empty. I stopped by while in town to find out what was available, as this was one of the few places in the city to serve French toast. I noticed that the menu was pretty clear, and I knew nothing was wrong. It made all the difference for me. My meal started out good, after several minutes of sitting. I noticed some streaks of cream cheese in the center of the thin sandwich, but didn't notice any sprinkles on top of the slice. I noticed a huge drop of sugar on the butter on me. And it's not just me who thought that. While the waitress looked around, while others were finishing their dishes, I sat with a glass of wine in my hand. It was not too bad. The bread was golden brown, and moist. Then I placed it on the grill to cook the outside for 30 seconds. It was too sweet to make it edible, and the resulting batter was a bit dry, tasteless and a little overdone. I haven't had French toast this bad in the last 40 years. There were a few spots of dripping on the inside of the bread, and the top half was a dry charred mess. What I needed was some water to keep this one from swimming in liquid for hours. And so it continues. I guess it is to be expected if you work in a keg shop. You've gotten better - I could see something on Angelina's website, then make the same choice on a chain of bakeries I've got my eyes on the breakfast sandwich too.

I went to a Thai restaurant for lunch yesterday, where I was not disappointed at all. I love the Korean and Chinese selections, but the selection of fresh Vietnamese dishes is especially interesting. I am so glad to be able to pick up produce where I can, just as I was able to pick up food that I was driving home.

This old fashioned-style cafe has been around since the late 1960's. Their decor is a pleasant mix of old European, American, and Spanish antiques, and the owners are a bit of a mix of both. The bakery has two ovens, serving a wide range of dough types, and a wide variety of fresh baked goods. The front counter is big enough for a table, but also big enough for an outdoor dining table with a glass-fronted patio. The place was filled up to capacity; there were more than 30 tables and a few tables of tables and chairs. Maybe I can't decide what to have with breakfast. I have no idea what special meals they offer. My waitress had a good eye since I had arrived late, but no reservation. We ordered our sandwiches by the glass. This is not your usual American bakery; every day there is bread being baked on a hot-grill in the kitchen. After 15 minutes of sitting and waiting (literally for me) I decided to try one of the sandwiches that was offered. They serve bread with their own cheeses, but also sell a variety of non-dairy choices. I settled on a simple sausage patty and fried egg sandwich. It was a basic, burger with a few pieces of meat and an egg on top. The sandwich was still small, with only one slice of bread to fill its gap. The green sauce did not enhance the sandwich at all and instead had an overpowering, peppery sweetness. This was a good breakfast with some nice bread and coffee, but the price was about the same as elsewhere...I may eat at their new cafe for What I couldn't stand was the coffee and I had to find another quick food (like a lattes) option for their Sunday F.U. but hey, it was free, so hey, buy one in the end.

Home Depot and Lowe's would give you more choice if they could find a place to put the merchandise they sell. At their larger locations in Jersey and Pennsylvania, they don't compete with the big boxes that are more common in the area. Until recently, NHH had a lot of vintage hardware to choose from, but many of these are used, from old hardware or discontinued items. They are both small, independent stores. Smith's Ace and Newtown hardware have come under fire for the same reasons: a lack of competition, and lack of customer loyalty. However, Ace has its positives. Both stores operate on state and federal taxes, which are two important things to consider. There are good reasons to shop in a corporate warehouse like Ace. If your preference was towards the small-business experience, Newtown Hardware could be your new retail store. Ace is locally owned and operated. It's the type of company that was built by a group of people, on a small farm in the Middle Lebanese town of It also gives back to the community, so, they're more likely to be community anchored. If you don't want to go through the hassle of finding an old hardware store, go to S&S Ace on Route 30.

Eagle Bakery & Cafe is a place to look past the usual downtown atmosphere and consider dining at. They keep prices reasonable for all three meals for the price of a small dinner. It has a brick and concrete roof with a painted metal entry, and is the official Diner of the Warminster Home Owners Association. It is also quite quaintly decorated. After leaving the drive, I was waiting until 11 o'clock for a table. The entrance was a pleasant 15-minute walk along the narrow back road. It was almost cold, so I put on a coat and turned on the TV and watched a bit of a movie with the kids. I also saw a little bakery on the floor, and the store manager was super helpful. At the diner, there are several options for dinner. The menu had no meat, fish or vegetables, but instead offered both main dishes and a salad bar. The salad bar was mainly populated with mostly fresh romaine, yellow onion, bell pepper, white pepper, chives and other vegetables. For my salad, I ordered the following. The salad was a mixed greens trio with a lot of dressing on one plate. It gave me a good taste of the breads, including the feta cheese and red pepper flakes. The meatloaf was almost the same size as the sandwich I have at the diner, but served on this large slice and two mashed potatoes The meat was cooked really well; tender, but a little tough overall. My mashed potatoes, thick and rich, were tasty. I ate my whole plate, but I didn't finish off the mashed potatoes, and I didn't even take the sides. That's always the problem, with this town. They were also just under two inches wide. I'm still hoping for a better meal. The salad bar was very good, too.

Jo J- Jo's ice cream shop at the corner of 12th and Alder, just outside of downtown Indianapolis. The original ice cream shack is no longer operating; its original location has been bought over by friends of my now long-deceased late brother Tom The slick old-style exterior. The old fashioned faces of the sleazy, old lady workers. The smell of salty, sweet treats, and the fun of the sand-dune skimpy ice cream machine in motion. The gentle sound of the ice cream truck machinery on the air conditioning, your feet pumping as it speeds through the warm summer night. The adolescent looking women, as they eat on the counter. I just got back from a day long vacation in Italy. In addition to their ice cream and ice cream toppings, Jo-Jo also has a beautiful outdoor patio overlooking the water that flows. It's made simple and fun again. My mouth glistened to your sweet words. These scoops filled my heart while I was eating ice cream. It was clear that Jo-Jo's does know how to treat their customers, not just because they need a scoop...but also because they care I was so glad I stayed; I wish it were for me. I will be back. Pure joy..of ice cream.

During the week, we visited our long running stop on the Main Street Market. Riverfront Market is open from May to September. It was designed by architecture students at Wilmington’s American Enterprise Institute. The area is rich in history and has been transformed into a well known dining destination for Wilmington families. There are several locations for food court businesses: Mexican food, Mexican food and Italian restaurant. Many places have a full menu: Mexican, Thai, Asian and Vietnamese. After finishing my dinner, there was nothing left for the night. The riverfront itself looks a refurbished warehouse with several vacant lots on the banks of the river. The Mexican house was open to the public at 12PM and I was able to try both their food and a drink at 1PM. The vendors are efficient, and offer great deals (ranging from 2 for $40 to $39). My visit brought back a feeling that it was not only empty but a little bit more attractive and than usual.

It goes without saying, that your next stop should be a place whose name is already on your radar screen. If you ever feel like taking the short drive out for a visit, take a look at this picture of us in an old rusting ram For those of you who haven’t heard, the farm is known as the home of the pigs. I have the pig-like version — her name is Kien, her abode is on the other side. One of our last visits to Ross Mill Farm was just before Christmas. A dog walks over the grass, looking at itself from a pigs’ perspective, while eating, playing and drinking. They are all beautiful, though, as well as completely safe and healthy. There is room for them to grow up, to play and to be more intelligent. You can relax with a cup of coffee, take a walk on the trails, or even visit your local pet eagle. Visit their web site and enquire about adoption, or donate to support this wonderful project. This is one pig rescue, not just a farm. And, the pigs were too cute!

In the early evening hours of our trip to Mt. Holly, the highway was slow and unsteady. I am on the road for a conference a couple weeks later, and stayed in an outlaws motel with a family; it was The entrance was obvious, with a full wall of windows. However, for me, the best thing about this new venue was the servers, I was greeted very warmly, with an excellent view of the tables Green, Texas..

UPDATE: APRIL 19, 2017 - I had lunch at Golden Dragon (formerly known as Golden Dragon Chinese Grille) in Westgate. Like all the other Chinese take out joints, it seems to be mostly a take-out joint. They hired three young men, four of whom are all working the registers. They're a little out of place at first, especially since the menu isn't even that extensive. This house serves fried rice and rice porridge, and the chicken flavor is fresh. My first order, which was Pork Egg Foo Young, cost me $5. It appears the chicken broth is diluted before being baked. The chicken was meaty. One cup size of this rice would come up to 10 cups, all though you wouldn't get the full 5 bowls of fried rice. This was the version that I found from around two decades back. The chicken was just average. While most Chinese restaurants are full of menus, this one leaves the customers wanting to eat in. The only other thing I saw was the cashier having to do two rounds to have the food delivered. Just a few people trying to get in front of the counter. You need to get on the moving to eat, and get it served on a plastic tray. I'm not sure how that will be taken care of and if the kitchen can actually deliver to my address, at lunch the next morning. Also, nice if you want to grab a quick lunch at the market. Golden Dragon is the second of the three in a long line of Chinese restaurants and takes order all the time. My last trip, they had me order the Shrimp and Garlic Soup, and a variety of chicken and pork dish. After a quick scan on a menu, I decided to go with it. It didn't have a huge taste, but the hot & sour element was definitely present. Very tasty, and I'm not a fan of most of the soups, so my biggest criticism was that some of the tofu was tough I can't say enough about the chicken. It was a true take out restaurant, with clean lines and the tastiest and tastiest chicken. They have a great little display of the sauces they're making. I wish I wasn't in this area so often for Chinese dishes, as I'd be left with just soup. I can't wait to go back to Golden Dragon, but I'm still not getting all the meat from that hot & sour soup back The chicken was tender, a little salty, but the sauce was tanish and not too salty, though not too much. Both dishes are highly recommended, with the soup being great and the chicken great.

I am glad I stopped by the new Bakery & Deli in my neighborhood. They already have that going for them. We were lucky - that was about all they had left. The menu is very diverse, with the main ingredients for the meal being from fresh local farms. It was an easy walk to the restaurant, so this was not as hard as it seems. If the reviews were forgoing that dessert, then this meal was a definite letdown. Upon first glance, the chicken was slightly tough, but that could have been addressed with better flour and eggs. The beef was perfectly cooked with tender tender meat and tender enough veggies that they were held together. It was good, but overheated, and dominated by the gravy. It does a good job of balancing the two main courses. The roasted carrots were a mixed bag with a few bits of crust and the baked beans were tender, not tooggy. It was pretty good, though the meat was heavy, even with all the sauce on top and it was hard. Some texture to the crab Cake, but still plenty of crab meat to absorb any additional broth or seasonings. The bottom meat was fine, too, but there needed more bread. My only complaint was the carrot cake. The only thing I was not as satisfied with was the carrot cake. I've had better. By the time I put my order together, however, it was an entire slice of old cardboard cake sitting on the table. That slice was a pale cake, with a thin cream filling that just tasted like marmalade. Instead, the cake was soft and chewy, lacking the subtle flavoring that a great carrot cake should have. So, I had to resist the reselling when I finally ate it. But it was good enough to not mind the taste. That was just my experience with the dessert. After all, what are you waiting for? Southern Comforts seems to get it just right.

Best Greek Restaurant in downtown Atlanta. This new shop has been making delicious food available for years and is well worth the drive down North Union Street. The coffee is outstanding and the menu changes weekly. The bread was moist, and the warm butter for toast was almost too rich. There was hardly any bread crust (it was not even made of anything but a buttery batter that would have been impossible to shape). The bread was toasted with butter and topped with a cream sour cream/butter mixture, sugar/vanilla mixture/creame I added a small knob of butter (the kind that makes a small, buttery cup) then sank it onto the toast and pressed The texture and the flavor of the bread really were intoxicating. The server and kitchen were always pleasant and helpful. I also took advantage of the live music on the tableside that stayed music without being as loud as one can hear in a restaurant with tables. The atmosphere was very casual and the servers gave very good service during meals. We would definitely recommend Liv & Charlie! They put the time in and do a great job making each meal.

I started my day early on January 2nd and got in the car to the lab where my nefarious tumor was doing a bit of  It was already late for lunchtime, but I was still looking for a place to eat. Until that is if the other two trucks were open. At the food truck, they had a small open kitchen in front of the truck that looks cozy enough for a lunch date. The operator was friendly and helpful, explaining the process on my phone. The sandwich was just as ready as it was sitting on the table, not a full order at first. A lot of the meat was on the plate, the rest under the halved slices of roast pork. They let me sample the hot pork until it was almost at room temperature. I picked up my lunch and walked to the grill before I could pick it up. It was a little on the salty side, but perfectly delicious! The flavor was almost non-existent but it had some garlic and a sweet hint of cheese. And the meat was tender and cooked perfectly, with a sweet smokey flavor that brought the whole mouth to a smile. And because I only had about 15 minutes, the whole thing was a little burnt. My little girl loved it.

Barry & Co. has been located in the Old Market area of Chicago for a while. It doesn't have a huge selection, but it does have an interesting past and a good beer selection. Although we were getting ready to head to the Markets, my friend and I went for breakfast, so I didn't want to go in the afternoon because There was a small menu in the window but no cake choices. I decided to buy a big bundle of apple cakes and an apple wedge for my morning drink. When my stomach woke up and I noticed that a few pieces were still left in the kubboodle bag, I tried to force myself to go I also couldn't give away how wonderful the apple/rosemary buttercream pie really is, so I did have to stop at one. The Cupcakes however were still tasty. The Apple Cake was pretty gross (I even tried taking it to a McDonald's for myself).

I was about the town to see about seeing Greenstream in Greensburg, MN. We entered the restaurant by luck of the draw, at 12:54 pm, and within 15 minutes the place was packed with patrons; the menu was well No doubt they make great smoothies, but they are a little more expensive. There are also options for your child to choose from, but I took advantage of their snobby friendlyness. One of the best things about Greenstraw is that the drinks are poured through a straw. My son said he tried several of the mixed drinks. It was a sweet nutty mash, with a little hint of orange and pink (It was like a green tea l a straw)...Yum! The berries kept the berry taste, along with the sweetness, but the whole thing was still very refreshing after a couple of days. Young man ordered a Blackberries Mud, consisting of Almond Milk, Banana Juice, Strawberries, Raspberries, Green The fruitier blend was smooth and light, though not too much of the fruit itself. The food was well prepared and well served, along with a large plate of fruit salad with fresh-cut banana and mango. I am pleased that the smoothies are not too protein wealthy, and tasted really good. I hope that Greenstraw is on the Newtown scene soon as they have opened there new location in the North End. The menu also has a selection of salad, wraps, sandwiches and a variety of sweets. I think I'll check back soon and post some of my findings. It is still too soon to know if Greenstraw will be operating at the same time as the other place on East Sycamore. Greenstraw Smoothies is located at 522 Sycamore Street in Newtown (NJ).

Today I visited La Villa's, as a family of four. This was made using traditional bread, the thin crust. They were cooked perfectly, there were no dry marks on the surface, and the crust was crusty and perfectly crisp. There were two big apps to share with one of us. At lunch, they delivered their specialty salads with good selections and they were also offering hot salads. I noticed a slightly different side salad this past weekend. The other app specials of the day were their chicken marsala, and their swiss roll. The Veggie Pasta was also lacking. The only complaint is that it seems that they do not always have the same quality of pizza. If the pizza is as good as it is, it will be hard to find elsewhere to eat. Have you tried La Villa's?

This morning I was out in Pittsburgh for breakfast, and discovered a cafe called, The Lodge. The restaurant was very busy that morning, so everyone appeared to be busy. One of the servers called me out on my presence, asking if I wanted anything off of the menu, and he had me order a small selection Her suggestions was endless, even though I'd probably have to try out a few before I gave up. In that moment, I decided to try my hand at something new. There were two pieces of bacon, two slices of white, two pieces of black, and all three of them were hot. They gave me two free slices of sourdough since we had been in town for several days prior to my birthday. I enjoyed the fresh cut bread, and the deliciousness of the sausages. Just as the bread had finished cooking, a huge serving of pork sausage came into play. I was immediately asked if I wanted a beer. I think I will be back. Also, I asked the waitress about their brewing process, and she said she knows everything about it. You can check out their website here.

On a nice, warm, dry Saturday afternoon, while out and about walking the neighborhood there were a couple pizza places on my mind. Instead I decided to head over to Adriana's to have a nice restaurant dinner, so I came home the night before to find the restaurant open! Just to check, I went there at 10:20pm on a Tuesday night, but there are no servers at the counter. I ordered a Chicken Pannini, cheese and fried potatoes, which came up quickly, and the waitress checked to make sure the food was The menu came out of a salad bar, and I had ordered the sandwich. As the waiter approached I could appreciate the vibe. My first experience at Adriana's was not the best I've ever had, but the food was a few points above average, and the atmosphere The sandwich was good, but lacked depth. The breading was smooth, and flavorful. The chicken was a bit tough, the pannini itself soft but firm. The Spinach was very good, but the Provalone was just a little too acidic. It tasted incredibly salty, with no taste of the pizza itself at all. The Provolone had a nice crisp crust and didn't taste fishy or "fishy" like the previous reviewers have mentioned. I went back the next day to make something else and didn't find anyone to help me decide what to order. The service wasn't the speed that you would expect from an Italian chain, but was well prepared! Also, if you are looking for a good salad to go with your pizza, they have it all, but they often run out of fresh vegetables.

The sticky Wicket Grilled Sandwich Bar is the location for burgers, hot dogs, and their infamous “Bunker Fried Chicken It is located in a old outbuilding, so it has a lot of original furnishings. A spot in the middle of the town in New Hope is known for its pleasant weather. This Italian cuisine is made with fresh Italian ingredients and the menu is generous. It is a great place to enjoy a casual lunch with friends, with a perfect environment to enjoy our mornings together. From the outside we could see the rolling hills of New Hope as well as the grass at the back, overlooking the nearby teepee and The lunch I ordered was simply a grilled snack, with a simple side of salad and a salad that included a side of arug The Panini was thin, light and a light texture, with great balance between the protein and the white rice. The side salad was prepared in a traditional Mexican way, with fresh tomatoes and fresh onions. Weinrich's Bakery serves a wide variety of cakes and sweets as well as a few coffee shops. If you need a little bit of everything in one go, it is a good drive to find. This bakery has a very nice feel inside, featuring all types of food and the latest fad trends. The counters are in the entry, which, thanks to small tables, is rather easy to get a good view of the entire collection of pastries, The bakery itself offers a variety of items in a small variety of flavors, to appeal to adults and children alike. As all of my past visits, my first was here on July 19th, 2010. Let me tell you first that I tasted the lemonade. That said, the selection was vast. When I ordered the other items, the shop was about full with a dozen (very full and not only with the desserts.) What a way to start the week. The cupcakes were absolutely stellar. These are some of the best cupcakes I've tried, coming in at almost half the price point found at most other shops. The cups were made to order, so the texture was excellent, and the frosting was rich icing. The tops were soft, and had a perfect moist texture to them. My favorite of the afternoon tasted somewhat reminiscent of the old fashion Chicago cookies which I used to eat back in my youth. The icing was soft and delicious flavored though. As I was trying to complete my experience, the owner offered me a free cup of tea to sample, and showed me sample from his assortment of the various I opted for the Caramel, while my wife made an appearance with a white, cream flavor version. It was definitely worth a visit if available.

Zook's is a farmer's market in the middle of the business district of Lake Forest. It is not very popular, but it is a wonderful alternative for lunch or a quick lunch break that just goes better with a beer and food. The produce is very fresh and varied. The chicken is tender when you bite into it, the pork is perfectly seasoned and seasoned, and the pulled porks are delicious. The original BBQ is done on a pigsmeal base, which allows the sauces to steep, and then heat for at least a couple The ingredients in the BBQ are all based on the local farmers' market rub. It is no longer cured for a couple of days, but is very tender, and can hold the taste and smell of the marinade together to create The sauces really take the edge of the meat, and create an almost flavorful, rich flavor profile. The meat is delicious, along with the sides. The pork has a very smooth flavor, and has very good flavor on all sides of it. We actually had two chicken sandwiches while we were there, one the hot dogs, and the other the salad. The baked potato sub is delicious, too. My favorite thing to get a good meal at is the pulled Chicken Sandwich. And for the price of one of the items, is a large portion of meat and fries served on a wooden plate. There is a variety of snacks - from sandwiches with extra cheese, to pastries, and even a few salads. The customer service is excellent, even in the dark days of the market. The quality is what comes from a barn. One star for the quality of the meat, and one star for the friendly people.

As I have stated, many who have eaten at this establishment have indicated that it is a good time. To me this quaint little corner of Pennsylvania was like traveling back in time. Built in 1864 to accommodate the mail, this building still tells a story that is the most enchanting one we’ve found in our lives. The Kitchen is a wonderful stop in on a Saturday morning when you’re passing through this charming village. The main entrance leads out to the long paved side drive in the village whose trees & fields show off the historic architecture by the way. I took a short stroll to the kitchen to meet Kim from the coffee bar where I once found a delicious java bar — my local institution. I ordered a frothy Jamaican mocha made with milk and honey. He was a great guy and you’d never forget him! A lady came by and chatted for a few minutes with a friend who ordered a breakfast sandwich. She took some orders and waited minutes until one of them was here. The butter and cream were fresh and the bread was warm and moist. As I was sitting there, I recalled how I had gotten here at the start of the 1960’s. Kim and I talked for about 10 minutes while enjoying the great lunch. The cafe is a great place to chat, read, take a call or hear a talk of the day. The feeling of the place is cozy with the warm feel of welcoming all alike. It was a peaceful afternoon. What a wonderful setting for a short weekend break. Come back soon, folks!

Salty..yes. Food..mene. Meat..at Sandy's. Whether you know it or not, you may feel that their signature dish is very much what you want it to be. It's not a place to visit out of choice, just for the sake of sampling. Sandy's has been in business for over 55 years, supplying the area with both good and bad meats. There is a bar, which I referred to as "The Hot House", and also a private room to hang out during those down times. Sandy's is all about the meat. In fact, the meats are cooked specifically for the bar before being served. This place is always busy with people, so keep an eye out for a wait times sign. Their meat sandwiches were fine, but the sandwich bread was slightly under-seasoned. The pork pot roast was a good medium-well meatball sandwich, with some nice texture (at least on the buns). It's a perfectly good sandwiches for a night out. It was tender but wasn't rubbery. It was very easy to make out the meat, and a solid skewer, with good flavor at the core of the roast. The sausage wasn't as much of a challenge as it should be, still had a very flavorful meaty flavor, but still wasn't This was one of the odd little experiences with the meatballs. The rolls were a little small, and hard so you could hardly scoop the meat out with your finger. It wasn't a bad roll though, it was just not particularly good. Our three meat salad plates were delicious; primarily with the home made sauteed vegetables, and the salad dressing with salt and pepper, all tasted absolutely The sauce had an interesting heat and texture that gave a nice contrast to the meat. You'll see them more on the weekends. Not at all a burger restaurant though.

One day on Yelp I looked up Bantle Stop and learned that there was a one-stop shop offering bagel's north of Hamilton I've seen this place on Yelp for a while, I wasn't sure about it. I knew there were good Bagel & Coffee around Jersey City. Is that even possible? Yes. I did take a tour of the city of Brookline, but I couldn't really imagine my next visit being anything amazing. Got on my way to try it out for myself, wondering if I actually got a Bagel? The atmosphere was very inviting. No one there, just the bartender who came to get me a bagel. I was welcomed with a warm welcome by the staff. I sat down and ordered. I had been looking for something quick and easy, and ordered a fresh bagel. You can do this with either a regular bag and cup or an extra large cup. That's about 25 cents a bagel. I couldn't believe it. This is what all good bagel joints should look like, with a huge selection of halal food, excellent service, and excellent onion/ It was warm and ready to eat. The inside structure was not asggy and not burnt, but it wasn't asggy or overly soft. The inside was soft and tasty without being too dense. The Onion Flakes were firm, but giving. That being said, it would have been a great start to the day had I not been starving. The consistency of the crust was not the kind I'd expect, but it was a good match to the consistency and chew. I enjoyed it as much as I have enjoyed anything from East Hampton to Jersey City. I'll continue to try it out.

Huong Tram is a large, new Vietnamese house located at 1021 Washington Avenue with a nice view of Hanoi from its large covered patio. They provide a service with a resounding "Yay!" There's not much room for a small car in the restaurant, but if you are at the right time for Vietnamese, you will get a It's an average dining experience for pho lovers - lots of Vietnamese  dishes - and it's quite pricey. The decor of the restaurant is simple modern with a couple of vintage Vietnamese style signposts. I tried the chicken and rice dishes from the new menu. We ordered two soups: one with beef pho and S/S Chicken with fresh veggies. Wished we'd ordered a side of Chinese for everyone. The Wonton Noodle Soup was excellent. The noodles were thick, smooth, and topped with a sprinkling of Vietnamese-style wontons. It made the dish really nice. I also got the bonus of a nice bottle of lime juice. There was a tad of heat from the hot soy sauce that had a very robust flavor, with just a small amount of extra It was a strong broth, with thick layers of noodles, thick boiled carrots, and a light sauce that tasted great. A couple of the vegetables were under cooked, and needed to cook a bit longer. They were just soft and they had a delicious chewy texture. Sweet & Sour Chicken was not all that spicy at first, but more on the sweet and sour side. This is very much like their Chinese chicken cousins, but with creamier sauces and better seasonings. It was served at a high temperature, which kept the dish cooked as if it had been cooked all day. The sauce was rich and thick with just enough sauce to keep everything moist. They have a large selection of asian sides including Thai, Indonesian, and Vietnamese dishes. There are a variety of Thai menu items with variety of meats and veggies, but only the chicken and sweet & sour chicken can be served hot I should say the Thai sandwiches look good too. We are already enthused!

The pho tai nam soup was very tasty and quite reminiscent of a Vietnam soup. It did not have the characteristic "fishy" taste, but there were plenty of dry noodles. It is something that is especially good in the Southern United States, so I do not like it very much where I live. I ordered my usual teriyaki bowl and felt it was not at full of vegetables and meat, like the rest of the servings. There were some bites of the beef that were not too salty, which is typically what happens to me, but definitely not the kind needed to bring it After the meal, our drinks were empty. Vermicelli with BBQ pork was a little spicy, but not enough for my tastes. Vermicelli with BBQ pork, with its nice dark golden color was a little off-putting, but nothing to write home about. If you do, you would save a bit of money.

The first is knowing that it is fresh. I will be back for more, and to enjoy their lunches.

At the Blue Angel location I have been eating here for the past few years, and find it to be excellent. It was the smallest of the Mario & Franks locations, and the price remained more expensive than a meal at the restaurant of the same name On our first day on the campus it was time to try the Parmesan BLT. However, upon eating, I realized this was a colossal piece of food. There were two sandwiches with cheese and chicken. The whole ham was not cooked very well, and the chicken had no flavor. Was probably cooked just enough as it was. It was served with just an empty can of cole slaw and an obscene amount of mayo on top. There was no sauce on the parm, so I added some salad and my glass of water, so I could keep going without over eating. Food is nice, so I will probably get better at this restaurant someday.

Jessop's Tavern is one of the oldest surviving pubs in Old New Castle. With a strong French influence that continues through the current owners, Jessop's was formed in 1926 as the oldest pub in Delaware. Jessop's Tavern is located on Delaware street between Old New Castle (Wilmington) and the new, and enlarged, shopping 167, between town and Maine. There is also a restaurant on the ground floor that serves both Dutch and English cuisines. Among them are "Dutch Pastrami Reuben" (a large breaded meatloaf sandwich), "Dutch Bar They also serve a variety of food and have a menu of sandwiches. And they have a great selection of pastrami, beer galore, and all manner of other regional classics. Visiting Jessop's for the first time, it was stunning. It was a beautiful, and quite romantic feel to the tavern. Jessop's served us a very pleasant lunch at a reasonable price. A couple came for lunch, and we both ordered the hummus-potato sandwich and pastrami. Service was friendly, and food was excellent. They were both excellent sides, with sides of charcuterie, bread, and olives. The food was excellent. The  Tavern is open daily in the summer, and offers patio dining. They also made plenty of recommendations for places to go out for drinks in Old New Castle and in the region. So, come check it out!

This is a rather odd review. The last time I went, it was not good. I was not looking to give a big criticism of Yardley, since I felt it doesn't deserve a two star. DeLo's is a very difficult act to beat. The atmosphere at Yardley Pizza is nothing short of the best. They provide a lot of table seating, and they have even a kitchen. It's not supercrowded, which is welcome, even if, like most restaurants (you get served at lunchtime) the price on top of the They also carry a variety of beer and wines. There are two slices of pizza available at Yardley. Very thinly sliced, with plenty of sauce and cheese, and plenty of cheese. A side of sundried tomato sauce (I ordered this with onion) was added, which was a nice bit. Not too hot, but not too cold either. I guess the sauce and cheese deserved a little help on the outside, but they weren't really that good. The thin crust and its well-done crust gave way to a substantial bite of the tomato. Also, the cheese was very good. The cheesy sauce was not quite enough to make it good, but it made the pizza taste good enough. This doesn't affect the quality of the slices, but it was a poor example of having them as my "go to" for pizza after a Good food, but really, who is it for?

My food friend, who was out of town before I stopped for some lunch, had been waiting to check her boyfriends online. There was a new place close by called M Kee, and I was excited to taste their "steamed chicken" and "raw noodle soup M Kee is a Chinese restaurant in Chinatown that had previously re-opened on the second floor of Chinatown at a much higher price point It was still in early lunchtime when we ate, and we had plenty of time to explore the menu before returning to Changchun. My friends started with the Chicken Fried Rice, and a small bowl of the Korean Beef. We ordered off the Menu, and decided to split three items. They loved the dishes, and the chicken Curry was a perfect balance of vegetables, spices and chicken, covered in a sweet sauce. It's always nice to have hot cooked chicken! The Rice was in a light wheat flour noodles soup, seasoned with soy sauce and some ground sugar. The soup was good, tangy but not nearly as rich. This soup also had plenty of green vegetables and mixed in with the chicken. I tried the a la carte - hummus, guacamole and steamed garlic rice with fresh cucumber and lemongrass. In all, 4 portions, with a portion of rice per person (see Photos), with a bit of drink for each. Despite the low pricing, this is an excellent fast food joint, and a great place to enjoy a little dinner in some style. It's an area of the Chinatown where I've been inundated in the past, and a good place to pass off my lunche It was a nice change from the atypical Chinese Chinese restaurants, where we all had to sit. Please see their site for more details.

Located in the charming old house near the river, MMT is a restaurant/bar whose history is as old as they are. A true Carlucci fan, I had been avoiding this one due to the fact that its founders are brothers and fathers. I ate here during an early lunch and if you are familiar with any of the restaurants or Carlucci's, you may have seen him as He had always been kind to the employees - they seemed to really enjoy his food. At some point and day, he will have an annual dinner there and I would not be surprised to learn that he is focusing on family. I had a feeling I'd be back soon. Once again, we were told that this place has been awarded a Michelin star since it first opened back in 1999. What a treat we had the food and service! The space is inviting, clean, and the servers are polite. There are booths with comfortable chairs to seat ten to eight people as you get through the restaurant. My husband and I ordered something to share at the table next to us. I tried a sweet potato pie and a melanzon pizza. So we had an Italian meal, all seasoned with our own favorite elements, including a nice crust, a generous amount of fresh Italian breading, A tasty and refreshing vegan pizza based on a classic tomato roll with a sauce of basil, garlic and sun-dried tomatoes, in a Vegetarian penne, white onion, carrot, capers, black beans and garlic puree. A thick thinly sliced melanzon served on a plate with a rich sauce. I really enjoyed his vegan approach to Italian cuisine and have already seen his other kitchens in Italy, which are reflected in the cheese. Equality mixed with flavor. The meat was thick, tender and was just ok, but not as flavorful as the ham! In an already delicious lunch, the ambiance of this place was quite relaxing. The eggplant parmesan was also good. A place for an intimate evening dinner with friends. Look out for the grand reopening, just on the same night, in November.

I was very charmed by the food and bar. The new bar is nice. Even as the old pub and bar has changed its decor, this old timery still is there. Just in case you'd like a review as negative as mine, you can always read your local paper with a smile and a sense of humor They now serve a more diverse selection of beers, but still have about a three-barrel well over an eight-barrel line It may take a few visits but they are worth the effort. It's always been good, but they have made the addition of an old house & a couple of newer rooms. We'll certainly be back again.

...the place where the name 'The Star' comes from is almost always full of stars. The pizza joint is a real classic, and I cannot imagine anyone else doing it. No cheese..no meat. No special occasions.. No kid stuff. No bolognese. No sides.Sorry, no salads. The Star is in the shopping strip off of Park Avenue in the center of Easton, NJ. It's in the middle of all this. The neighborhood is shady from every point of view. In a nutshell, they have a small but attractive shop that is not all wenseekers will notice. They do come with a hot dog and soda, but don't expect much else except a 'no frills' and an old There's no wait or line up. No waitresses. They also have a hot coffee machine open for all to use. A quick phone call and I ordered a special fried chicken slice with two slices of bread. It was a good deal - only $4.77. While it is possible to order it - the waiter could have used the time for something far more satisfying. Also on the table, a pizza with a little more than a little extra sauce was recommended. It was deep-fried, topped with an inch of deep-fried chicken, and was well-topped with mozzarella cheese, fresh basil, garlic, olive The sandwich contained fresh slices of eggplant and a generous dollop of marinara sauce. Very very good all around. Food, service and prices were outstanding. Great little shop - with good prices and excellent food, you can't beat it. If you're in the area and ever in need of a satirical, family-friendly dining experience, be sure to stop by.

Crossing Vineyards is a beautiful and unique winery located along the North Shore of the City of Philadelphia in the quiet rolling hills of a small town Crossing Winery started out as a family run family operation, so in the summer time they have a large patio with a nice view of the This is one of the early vine growers in Bucks County after the land was given to the family of a nearby family farm in 1750. The staff has excellent knowledge of the grapes and wine techniques. In fact the winery offers a wide variety of wines from the entire grapeline, from the French varieties to the California regions. They are among the best of the best in the region but this one is the standout being the Red Blend, a perfectly well balanced, fine tannin- The reds, red and white grapes that Crossing Vineyards produces are aged from a combination of dry and hot, and each vintage is judged Even if they are your first choice be sure to read the vineyard rules. The wines are at market in the area, and Crossing Vineyards has been awarded an prestigious “Best Of” at the Newburyport Winemakers’ For more information or to purchase wine, visit thecrossingvineyards.com.

Xiao Long Bao is a small dumpling restaurant which satisfies the needs of those who prefer dumplings with some It is pretty small. What strikes my attention is the yellow Chinese lettering of the name, or more precise, the black lettering of the menu. I was struck by the zebra print on the jackets. The layout gives an impression of a modern Chinese kitchen. The restaurant is not very well located, either. I was sitting with a couple of mates at a table in the guise of sitting in 'the club'. The whole bar is set up in a room above the kitchen, which gives a nice air of the atmosphere, rather than a hard walls, which I was seated right away by a server who was taking orders and walking by the counter. It was a long wait, and I was not at all surprised to have been seated at a good table. The first two dishes on the menu are dumplings, or "XLB," or Shanghai dumplings. Stopped at a nice location on the roof, the staff and servers made it a little more attractive for me. The dish has several different fillings (garlic, egg, and peanut), and if you have the time, have fun learning how to eat Of course, the wait staff doesn't really care. Took two minutes to get to my table, three minutes to get my plate out at the end of the line, and about twenty minutes to take my order During the pre-dinner chat, the server told us "Another Dumpling". I had a vision of them being filled with pork breast, but there was little meaty or fried egg on top of it. They lack the garlic flavor typical of the popular Shanghai restaurants. This is a must for anyone who is not up for the task of cooking a dumpling. When the owner came by, I told her the Dumpling Garden was in the back of some house and that I thought we would enjoy ourselves in his house The decor was nice though, although the only complaint was the lack of decor and the taste of the pork. I will definitely come back. The service staff was friendly (for those that don't know what being a waitress is), but not as experienced. Yummy!.

Called "The Sports Bar," this sports bar has a quaint feel, no doubt due to the "sports themed" decor. The menu is relatively small, with a large selection of draft beers (a bit of a mixed bag of craft, but not too bad at all The food is quite decent, though. The chicken Parm sandwich on the menu costs $10. I ordered the chicken parm sandwich @ $8.50, the Tomato Sauce @ $2.50 and the Chicken Parm sandwich at $3.50.
