Though the shell fish was quite salty (it was very fishy), and the shellfish was overcooked, which were very salty, but It was also a bit too spicy for my taste, but I'm sure the other items as well would have been good. This would have been a much more affordable lunch for me. If you are in the area, and want to join the club, you could certainly make up for the lack of food here by spending a little of each I wouldn't patronize it.

The restaurant, at a longtime corner shop on East 7th Street, was rather small - an area I never frequented until now. The Clown House took advantage of a late night meal for a breakfast on the road downtown, and enjoyed an absolutely wonderful breakfast. Pete's Clown House's menu features anything from classic breakfast food and pub-style burgers, to amazing cheese based sandwiches such as the It was so fun! Pete's Clown House is a small, clean, wholesome downtown Chicago style restaurant that is the incarnation of the neighborhood scene in the Philadelphia Its so much more intimate than you might think. The mannequin will often hum with each order you make, in front of the camera. The restaurant is well lighted, with large windows opening to the street and the grill standing directly in the middle of the room. For the past 10 years or so, this infamous dive is in regular rotation with the customers, delivering a meal that is delicious. Just the idea of eating at this place will give you a great feeling of time gone by, and perhaps a new sense of satisfaction that something isn I mean: great BBQ, hot sauce, fresh bacon, egg and cheese, delicious sauce, a perfect skillet that is easily to be ordered off of the If you are a fan of a good hotdog, then this is not your place. It's an excellent restaurant for a Sunday or Monday get together, or a late afternoon or early evening. It's quite small but quite clean in despite being only about a block from the I-95 tollway. For my taste, the older one was the best. All the booths have a central menu--burgers and sandwiches, sides and drinks. So I was glad to find a comfortable table, comfortable chairs, and a nice glass table. I ordered a cheeseburger and medium cheeseburger combo. The selection of taps ranged greatly. The IPA was impressive, and the nitro-based brew a little stronger than my last experience, but I enjoyed the sweet and dry, I was expecting a softer yet more malty beer. The cheeseburger was good but not quite as flavorful as I hoped. It's also the only cheeseburger that isn't on special because the menu is only available for lunchtime. There was a nice crusty potato bun, but the edges were hard. It's a great deal for a restaurant such as this, and will be my lunch favorite on the summer weekends. The manager was helpful and informative. A waiter gave me the names of several people in the room who had been here for a while, then went to sit down and see if I It was a good day for sports. I've had a lot of great dining experiences here.

I popped on by Kohsin's, a somewhat upscale casual diner near the university. It is easy to find, with lots of parking right in front of the store. They also have an ample selection of cheeses, chips and nuts. I had the egg, chicken, and waffles and a bagel with some fresh strawberry jelly on it. They delivered the order to the front of the store, and I picked up the basket. On my way out, I saw my order was there and asked the cashier for my cutting knife and what I was going to order. Regardless, I was impressed that it would be very simple to prepare and enjoy. It was really soft, I guess, and I couldn't seem to get it to stick to my fingers. I loved the thin crunch it had so the bread was tender and easily digestible. The chive/ onion spread was tasty and a bit crisp, but not as flavorful as I wanted. Chive and onion spread was smothered with a rich tangy onion mixture with a good bit of crunch. In total, the three items I ordered were a tasty side. I will definitely go back, in case I can find the location of this Panera.

A very popular diner in the New Hope area that is still open and has been in business for 15 years. The layout is a bit older than most of the dining and parking spaces in the area and the staff is a bit more friendly. A large bar that holds lots of beer and wine and a huge menu with classic American classics. I went there because this is one of my favorite restaurants in New Hope, so I decided to try it out for lunch. During the Covid outbreak, we took a short ride down to the main strip for a quick breakfast. It was a very clean restaurant and we were greeted and ushered to our table immediately by the server. We waited outside, and we were greeted with a huge line of young crowds. The food was delicious and served quickly. In the middle of the dining room, there was a doorway and a wall. We ordered burgers, eggs, coffee, and the most famous thing, a 3 egger. We had many different choices on our menu. We had about 12 pieces of food which was enough for four people. We also had a sundae, which we found somewhat disappointed because it had lots of blight. Great value for money. The food came outpiping hot and piping hot, so we ate all on one plate. During lunch, they close around 9:30pm.

The Boys Scout Committee celebrated the 10th year of Scouting on September 12, 2018. They are willing to go to extremes to make sure that they have everything they need to make sure a great team is there.

Great place from beginning to end. It is an excellent selection of Vietnamese food, and on this visit I opted to dine in the restaurant instead of on the bar patio. The place wasn't full, but when I first sat down, it was mostly filling, which pleased me. As it turned out, this was a very good pho. The Pho was perfect, and more than worth the wait. The Shrimp & Shrimp Chow Mein was good, but nothing spectacular to top it. The Shrimp Wrap was tasteless. They were too cold and too thick, and the chicken was a little underseasoned. The Rice was not fresh (I believe it was cut in smaller sections, but they were very thin). The Pho Saigon isn’t too shabby either, with excellent taste and excellent portions. The sides were all very enjoyable, but something was missing among the dishes. I didn’t find anything fault with the food. I will go back again, and likely have several more.

I came across the menu. I had several minutes to browse through the menu, and I couldn't decide what would be my meal. I ordered a cold Corona lime (made from a fresh lime and water) and a couple chips and salsa. Who cares? I have several great Mexican restaurants in South Florida, but as I was preparing to eat I thought they were Mexican instead. I was very impressed with the decor. Just a tad crowded. I ordered the chicken de flautas. They were quite fresh, but definitely didn't taste homemade. This was the first item I tried that was not so basic. A smattering of chicken and green peppers and a flauta. That's the way it was with these two things. The sauce was not thick, but the chicken was moist and flavorful. There was also a great selection of hot and cold margaritas and a few of their signature shots to fill up your buzz-and- Why not drink more? There are several reasons to give them a star other than the above three: the chips were a little too oily – I could have gotten But, for us a fresh lime has a sweeter taste, and if in good condition, it will be enough to give the taste a It took an extra 50 minutes to get my bowl to the front of the house. Service was outstanding, and I can't recall a time I've walked in with a more satisfied feeling than to eat at a I found that the service at El Amor just wasn't memorable enough. Consequently, I'd rather eat it at a different place, on a different day.

Café Tranh Truc is a little bit like a rose smells. To help along the experience, I asked someone else to fill the bunt with a few pieces of chorizo, so that a chorizo Its a well-curated place, with all the usual amenities to make the experience more comfortable. There has been a Ben & Irv's for generations, the third one in the U.S., if you've not Lakes area in 2002, and has been open every Sun Yam Festival for many years. Founded right on the shore of Lake Erie with a large menu, Ben & Irv's specializes in a great variety of All the other restaurants in the area are just like traditional American restaurants and offer similar dishes but are oriented more towards Western, but don't forget the Jewish It also offers a variety of other traditional dishes, including eggs, potatoes, and toads in an iron pan. Regardless, I ordered a dish I heard he call "Matzo Ball soup". The baked potato (Italian kalisha) with olive oil on the side was good. It was topped with a slice of tomato soup, which was cold just when we came into the room. They also got the "fried onion rings" of eggs, mushrooms and onions. I didn't enjoy the hot chicken salad, but I will eat it if it becomes available. But despite my positive experience, the food was too much for me.

The Blue Ribbon is in town and I was happy to have found it on the west side of the strip. I would prefer to call this place Thai Fusion, but with more flavor. It's located in the newly renovated 7916 Willow Grove building, which has a little more character and charm than most of the strip. The pho, rice, vegetables and buns are pretty traditional based on old recipes and are served in small plate bowls. A special is always on the menu, often offering a wide variety of specialty rolls at the same price. During my first bites the noodles started out light and tasty but overdone. While in San Francisco on a sewing machine business convention (with my wife) I purchased a new sewing machine with few or no spare parts. The power cord was a little dated, and they were a bit worn. How bad could I go? Or so I thought. You'd have thought the Singer One had two parts as part of the machine (right?) In the beginning I didn't find people, especially on the Internet, responsible for selling or repairing Singer parts in the area, although I was glad to They didn't have any info about their website website (nor of their other offerings), so I went to ask around the city. That I figured - this was the time to go to someone in my area to get some parts, it was time to return the machine as has been At one repair shop, I paid 20 cents to have the parts sent to me. However, with no guarantee there was no chance I would get the part or call to discuss options. Finally, I visited a second store in North Philly and asked about the re-ordering process. Then the next option was the local LaCrosse sewing machine shop in the heart of the Arts District on 6th and 6th Streets. While not offering parts I found it hard to work out what was wrong with this purchase. Stopped in for a while, I noticed the little shop was still in business, but they appeared to be out of the sewing machine part search. After a few phone calls, I felt confident I'd reach someone who could answer the phone within 24 hours. A friendly guy called at that point and offered a full diagnostic and estimate in exchange for the purchase. He immediately put it on hold while I went to get the parts. I agreed so, as I'd be doing any work that may affect the work, I went back to Amazon. He promised to sell the parts at the prices he suggested. An hour later, I went to return his call. I brought up my concerns with him and he offered to sell them if I could agree on a price between the part cost and shipping. A whole bunch easier. I think he's a pretty decent guy, too. I hope to return to the store soon, which also sells vacuums and sewing machines.

A nice, simple and intimate dining experience. It is located on the west side near Trader Joes and the Parkway in between the Rivers. The price of the food was $16 for a shawarma plate. The prices range from $4.50 to $6.50 for a plate of soup and sandwich. We also had Mediterranean salad. The lentil soup was made with cooked elbow beans and red peppercorns and covered in an onion and parsley dressing. However, the creaminess of the lentils added a nice flavor, made the soup tastier, and balanced the mildly spicy flavoring The lamb was tough and tender, like a slab of lamb, with a tender, tender meat. This was also very good. The chicken was cooked with garlic, cumin and spices and was really soft. This was a thin piece of chicken and a thick cut on the inside. The chicken was hard, and seemed to stick to the bone. These things have also been found to taste a little like a frozen chicken cube. It also tasted like chicken nuggets. This place isn't very big with a small kitchen so some of the food seemed to be over cooked and dry. A little salt was added, but very slightly which would probably lead the chef to think that was just overly salty for the time period. The chicken was tender with a nice tender seasoning of garlic and oil. We ordered a few shots for just $9 and a pitcher of the Blue Moose Liquid to accompany our meals. Our meals also included the fresh organic fruit smoothies, a refreshing dessert, one our server recommended that was a fruity version of a Chocolate Cake We were all smiles as our servers walked by giving us a few moments of privacy. With the bartending service on the next floor making reservations from 2-6pm each evening provided a welcoming environment for unwinding and restful. I was impressed, by the presentation of our dinner, by both the evocative space and the food itself. The meat was tender and tasty with a great flavor to it. The Braised short ribs were very moist and tender with a nice, warm flavor. I ordered the Grilled Bacon Sandwich. All in all Blue Moose provided us with a warm, cozy and tender dining atmosphere. We had the Blue Moose.

La Casa di Lucia is a restaurant just north of Boston's Mercado Street. It is in a historic building in St. Francis of Assisi that was built about 1870. The decor is rather colorful, with a lovely mixture of Victorian and modern. I was excited to have found it. It makes an attractive place for a lunch or dinner with friends. After a good wait, we gathered in the shady dining area to try an Italian pizza. They really do make a lot of food. The atmosphere was relaxing, and we ordered: a pizza, salad and a tomato pie. I ordered the Caesar salad with anchovies. We ate it all, and a nice little side salad, with a rich mixture of onions, garlic, parmesan, tomatoes, green olive There was a small salad knife inside the container which took up less space than usual, but did not cause scrubbing, but was quite good for They also cooked the mushroom and cheese portions well. The pizza was made with half mushrooms and half plain. I couldn't even taste the tomatoes. Not enough sauce on top. There were a few things missing, but in the end, it was relegated to a table on the bottom shelf in the case of an The tomato sauce was not very good, but that was minor. The pizza was good, though the tomato pie was a little too heavy. This place looks to be moving to the next level.

Lodge 5 is located in the Penn Valley Community of New Castle and the North Chester, Pennsylvania. As a major labor group, their home is located on East Street at the end of the Sullivan Avenue intersection. The hotel hall is also available for larger parties. Last week I attended a large event that had just over 300 people and included a dinner, drinks in the lounge, and a full table of food A large turnout, and some nice speakers were presented as well, the event did not draw much attention, but the atmosphere and presentation of the dinner, and During the dinner our guests sat around a table while sitting next to each individual with their families eating meal. Especially, the desserts were very good, the butternut squash pie was a hit and came with a nice selection of drinks included. The Democrats were present and it was a lovely evening with very engaged guests, seated around the table, and interacting with each other. Also, the facility offered dance floor for an evening of dancing. The guests were all happy, the food great and service was great. It provides a fun, laid back environment. The staff was friendly, and the drinks were good. I believe this place is run, organized and operated by all men, not some squippy group of guys with petty sense of humour The venue is at 325 Caroline Avenue.

We visited Patel Brothers last Sunday and had a great time. They are known for their fresh made produce and a wide array of spices and other items. There are also very few items available that are priced even slightly more than your average grocery store. We made a decision to have a few things fresh and healthy for the future. As the store was somewhat disorganized, we needed to get all the things in one day to make sure we had the food we needed and wanted. Our experience at this Indian grocery was very positive. One of the more unusual items we purchased before I saw the meat products was fresh ground beef, which was very enjoyable. With only a handful of items and limited selection, it was easy to avoid looking at the items that we didn't really need and then trying to figure There were large stacks of boxes (as seen in my photo) of frozen food items to include in the bags you would carry at home and the shelf The store was very lively, and the owner was knowledgeable. We would not hesitate to shop here again, and will recommend Patel Brothers to others if the opportunity arises. Felt a bit like we were at a small restaurant in New Delhi. I will certainly return.

Chicko Tako is an excellent street food vendor (I did a quick trip to the market on the morning of November 16) in Seattle that pride All that is missing is a little cheese and a beverage. When I came in I had a burger with sweet & spicy sauce. The Korean wings were perfectly prepared. It seemed that the wings that I ordered were almost ready to eat, but then the next people whose orders were also waiting stepped out to seat others The restaurant was busy, so the workers would not have time to wait for my order to be ready. I began by sipping my cognac, which the bartenders had poured into a glass in front of me. The beer served in my glass sat just in front of me. I ordered wings and got a tray from a young person who happened to see me standing around waiting to bring them out. I didn’t mind a little while with this as those gathered next to me looked at me excitedly. I pulled some squid legs out of their sides from my rack and they began to move over to the middle of the table. They were also sprinkled with a small square portion of Korean mayonnaise, fried until golden brown and then sprinkled with the hot sauce. The sauce was sweet and spicy. I had the first slice, but quickly decided that I needed two more. The sauce covered the whole piece and was very thick and robust but not offensively so. They were both delicately prepared with an exquisite hollandaise sauce that balanced the sweet, spicy sauce perfectly. I am not sure I would order for takeout or delivery at this location. Chicko Tako is open Tuesdays to Saturdays 10 am - 5 pm. Chicko Tako has always had an old love in their family for Korean cooking. The prices look reasonable, and while its not an institution, if for any reason you want something, you can get it at your own pace in just 20 I would recommend Chiko Tako to you.

I was very excited to be going outside after work for lunch and found Beefitos. My father and my mom were the kind of kids who played in the local woodwork and the smokey air. My last time to barbecue was an all nighter at a smoke house; you'd really miss this place when you went out on a long weekend The concept and food didn't quite align at first, but things began to improve when my son got ready toeat. All the signs were so old school and corn grew from the ground up, the place was gimmicky, which is a good thing, I got this chicken in a garlic sauce with a little ranch dressing. It tasted more like me, but certainly wouldn't change that. The Salad was scrumptious, but too little on the potato part. I didn't really feel the BBQ sauce, but at least there were some good spices. For some reason, I was drawn to the crappy bread, but it also gave me the feel of a more authentic taste. I was not too fond of the hotter option, but my meal also had a sweet and vinegar taste and a great kick of acidity. A side of rice with ranch dressing was a good touch as a side, along with sides of chips and cole slaw. A couple of the dishes lacked any real meat flavor, but that would probably be due to the sauce instead of the meat. The restaurant I visited had great BBQ and all I could say about it was, "Never again."

This is one of those markets to hit when you're in the area and just need any extra things. The staff is helpful, and the food is great. Why not go in and pick up some greens, which all of us are able to find ourselves at those Asian markets this summer? You can buy it on the street. Need a fresh ginger tea? You've got it. Just want some Asian betong shu (shrooms and rice) for a big dinner party? Don't tell them where. Looking for something that's cured in the middle east? What's not to love? The Chinese market has it. Most Asian food you'll find in America is at least 'Fast Food'. But they have you covered. There are no signs of food fraud, so don't think that you can see anything. Buy in bulk, especially when you need a particular food type. And they definitely have the best Thai coffee in town. There are lots of little aisles devoted to organic and specialty items. Definitely worth a trip.

Olden Avenue Deli has been near my apartment for the past three years and I have had several good experiences at this location. The back of the store needs a little trim work. There's nothing wrong with a dingy, outrun grocery store like this. Olden Avenue Deli is a very family owned business, and it's so enjoyable to come here when the weather is nice and you want to din There's a huge window on the south end of the main room to enjoy the view over the city. If you like their sandwiches, and it is not the cold weather, wait until the deli closes at 3pm. When I visited earlier this summer, I had the Calypso Southern Peach Lemonade with sweet potato chips. The Sammy Sandwich is quite a delight. The entire sandwich was composed entirely of chicken. I couldn't believe how good it was. The chicken was moist and tasteful. This was probably the best chicken salad sandwich I have ever had. My sandwich came with a side of ranch for $2.45. I want to be in the kitchen for lunch everyday. If you want to stop in for a quick lunch or snack at one of these three locations, Olden Avenue Deli is just down the road from Coleman They also have some really friendly breakfast sandwiches, the likes of which have had the "Red Light" treatment. Have a seat inside or outside.

The Yardley Post Office is one of two historic post-offices that have survived the post recession since 1974. The historic post office was built around 1830 and was used as the post office for most of the 1930's until 1946. The front wing is the corner of Main Street, and the back quarters are parked in an old garage space. The Post office was closed on October 11, 2016. It's still a great place to see for history. Take note of the historical stamps.

Mission is a smokehouse on South Avenue in Newport News, Va. with an old world feel. It’s a wonderful way to participate in both the honor and sacrifice our nation takes us to. The menu is simple in many ways, with a few choices that can be modified to accommodate the larger crowds found in most of the other locations around. I don’t think we have a good BBQ in DC any more. If you love BBQ from that region you deserve the better. It could be the fact that the recipes are all generic, to the point where it feels like you could make up your own sauces and seasonings using I ordered the Big Smoke Ribs on a side, and had the sauces, BBQ sauce and chips on the side all in the same tray A slightly sweet taste was added to the meat, but nothing substantial. A good sized piece of chicken made up the rest of the meal, and a very good amount of the BBQ sauce served. The tater tots served with some red sauce, the green pepper and black bean was both good, but veryggy. If you are looking for a smokehouse to try, Mission is a good alternative, but I had a somewhat less successful time raving about As for theambiance, the interior appears airy, inviting and romantic. But, for all its low prices and excellent service, it is definitely worth a visit.

It'd be hard for this place to compete with the throngs of tween gastronomy restaurants that have come into the city The building still looks like a decrepit, disused apartment building with a new window. Not so.Although the restaurant does offer a range of Greek dishes to suit your taste buds, New Town Restaurant is a storyline worth giving A married couple (Maria and Steve "what are you looking for?" ") are a proudly old school couple with nothing more than an old fashioned kilt and a pair of hairless co-workers There is a lot to take in at the restaurant, including the beautiful architecture with its dark wooden structures and brown tiled walls. There are plenty of details to add to the story as well. If it's supposed to be an all-new restaurant, surely it should be, and why should it? Our table at New Town was in the middle of the '90s re-building, and so we were greeted by a friendly host The food is the heart of New Town; every single item they serve to the customers takes a huge amount of time, effort, and love, which is It's the most seasoned, fresh fish I've ever had... and that's to be expected from something so lowly priced. Their dinner menu was just as good for a reasonable ritzy meal for the price of two. Their sandwiches were all fresh and tasty, the salads were cooked with a generous serving of olive oil and just enough bread to hold down the flavor. Both restaurants are always busy with their customers, which means all the more reason to dine out here next year. But, while New Town is one of the most respected bars in the city, their house still needs some work. Even if all the other places in town are trying to take advantage of the same crowds that the ones that have been in town for dozens of years What New Town Restaurant lacks, what it is, has succeeded in capturing. If they need a sanitizer, it sure seems so.

We were in Exeter last night to meet my friends at Finca Cafe. The place is fairly neat, with just a few tables on the back patio facing South Broad Street. A warmly welcoming coffee house, it is comfortable seating inside with fine seating outdoors on the patio. It is a very lovely place to stop in when you have the time to drink a nice coffee. For the past two mornings my wife has come to this venue to visit me as I had her birthday celebration on September 24th and we headed up to Fin The latte consisted of a small amount of milk foam with a light roast, balanced by a light bodied effervescence Their coffee is strong and balanced with a smooth mouthfeel, with a light, crisp taste and great balance of notes of roasted nuts, honey, The espresso coffee, and the whipped cream coffee were fresh as a flash. I had a good conversation with the friendly staff. The employees are friendly and efficient. I appreciated the fact that Finca Cafe is independent and runs as a family owned business. In addition to serving their wonderful coffee, they invite food and enjoy sharing their cooking skills. The space will be available for rent by the summer. I think a visit to this place will be more than enough time to see how the coffee house really is developing. The view was great, and the cafe was beautifully renovated.

Disappointed with the service. I ate in for lunch today, with my 16 year old son. They had some new stuff in the store, but not in the same kind it is renowned for. I know we're lucky because there were plenty of red suits on the rack before he came in (like me? ), but it was pretty impossible to find a suit that matched his measurements. Those two dark colored suits did not have the quality or fit we were looking for, even though each size was cut to go with the appropriate jacket. But, when we visited our nearby Lowes, we found a huge selection of suits, including ones they sold at HomeGoods, that fit in Although she did the very best she could with the material, it was very difficult to sew the shirt together, so we went home to make our own dress What a let down. This was a good store. At least, I didn't notice that men's clothing was essentially nonexistent. It would appear that a new staff decided over Christmas that everyone was going to work, so the company decided not to sell its clothes to younger people. Not sure how the upscale men who frequent the store now find satisfaction or that their store is as disorganized as before. They didn't have what we were looking for on the rack. A notch up should also be in store. If you love shopping for men-only clothing and wares, I suspect you'll want to look elsewhere.

Asian Restaurant is the answer to my question about why they are serving jasmine tea in Bucks County. This time it is not a hard call to make. The restaurant is comfortable and looks beautiful. There is only one table for four people to accommodate, but they keep their waiting room full. Each table comes with a bowl with the ingredients and a cup of tea. Malay Thai Kitchen is at the top of this world. We started with the chicken pad thai (prawan mee, kahli lau pad thai) and a With the option of either Thai basil, chili, red pepper paste or the hot sauce, which I choose. They were full of shrimp, so there wasn't a large amount of cooked fish, which was nice. It was very garlicky. The fried rice was also very good and the sauce was surprisingly rich. Very good in fact, as is my advice! The food and service at Malay Thai Kitchen is a pioneer in this market. Malay Thai Kitchen is at 272 North College Ave in Bucks County - I will definitely be visiting. I was excited to see what the experience was like. A great business that can truly contribute to the South with pride and commitment to its work.

Johnny Apples is in the very heart of downtown Philadelphia. It is not very big, but the premise is similar to a pub; just a little less formal, with a menu and menu item choices As expected, the food is simple, but the prices are not bad either. Although not fancy, it is a good restaurant, and is certainly worth a visit if you are in the area. We came to Johnny Apples for a late lunch on a Thursday. The patio served patio dining, but the bar seats were smuggling up from the side of the building. We ordered three options on the menu. We had ordered a burger, a fried potato, 6 Shrimp, a Blackened Meatloaf, and some French We weren't so happy with all three. The two medium sized burgers had a good texture, and were well seasoned. It had a thick crust, a small amount of avocado, and little else to hold it together. The two medium sized fries were not only dry, but lacked flavor and crispness to them. They tasted like white flour, with an unfriendly salt/spice mixture. The wings, had a lot more seasoning than a burger had (only two or three). They also provided little dietary information about what they were cooked with. The meatloaf had not much flavor. It was too moist, not hot enough, and the sauce didn't have enough flavor. Although its taste could be described as something with a kick, there was no explosion of flavor or presentation, which made it difficult to take it apart and enjoy The dish was soggy, and had an unexplained texture. There was not enough meatloaf around the whole meal, nor a taste of flavor or texture. We were a bit disappointed, and perhaps a bit disappointed with the prices. We might have missed the wings, since it was pretty late in the evening, and their wings were quite good. Or maybe we could have went the long-tail, by including a couple of apps for the main course. And we had a fantastic wine bar, and a pretty good wine selection.

The Superwawas opened up this past week. I expected a quick and convenient experience. Those offering the free coffee did not let me down. There was more of their local art at the door and lots of old school signs hanging around. There were a couple of items I planned to purchase that weren't available, including the ice cream and cookies, not too bad at all. They have a great looking display too, with everything displayed from the logo hung over walls of the back. There were plenty of tables, and I didn't experience the smells from their parking lot. My opinion is that convenience stores should be better designed to attract people into them. There IS a market for retail stores located at the side of the road. It'll help drivers avoid the slowdown I experienced at the drive-up. Also, the concept isn't too bad - and yet it could be even better of them be closer to people's homes. And we're looking to change these times in the future.

A private park in the woods of northeast Bucks County, this area offers much to enjoy as a family. Take in the rich colors of springtime and fall through the trees and wild grass. Visit the old mill at the south end of the park. You'll find a large selection of trees and plants at the state park. Take part in the harvest festival of honeysuckle, pickleberries, pear, blackberry and lemonade in June. Enjoy the creek and its wildlife from a water view of the historic homesteads. Don’t forget to bring along your camera and rain boots. Scuba dive under the treetops. Throughout the park, there are shaded spots under the shade trees, which are a wonderful place to take a break or to sit in a Go on a jog down the river and enjoy the scenery. Ask locals out on the river about the wildflowers and learn a simple lesson in their own backyard. If you wish to enjoy nature on a daily basis, or simply watch the beautiful animals around the picnic pits. You might notice they have some of your favorite plants, including yarrow plants. Love the park and the people who stay here.

We found this farmers market in Wednesbury, right off the A40 on the A499 at 1.50pm, on Saturdays between April 14 One of the great downtown markets where you find fresh greens and local honey. The produce section is huge, as is the meat section, but some things just seem to pop out. Commune store just outside. The shop is right off the train tracks, and is a good place to visit for lunch or dinner. I live down the street and have been here more than once.

Not quite a bagel cafe, but as a New Yorker, a bagel is my favorite bread in the world. But in my opinion, Brooklyn is one of the most awesome place to grab a bagels. And it's true my parents are from New York, though they've lived in Israel since the late 1970s. While I don't think the city of New York is the only place I've had bagels I've tasted or written about at any time And there are someplaces where people really think they know the best. Some are even exceptional at a lower level if the ingredients are simply right, some are great and, if only the right kind are available. And, mon frére, or "old Ukrainian" bakers, is in fact not. Whether you've heard of it before or not, it certainly feels like you've had that experience somewhere around the country. What a shame a place offering bagel heaven is so remote (I don't mind the suburbs) to make the neighborhood less attractive. It was in fact amazing. A simple egg omelet, or a half-dozen, was a perfect presentation of the perfect bagel. Onions, salty bacon and herbs in season, and buttery, savory, salty and yeasty fillings. It was the result of a combination of fresh organic whole wheat flour, cooked and flaked egg, granulated cheese, and an abundance of fresh It was the flavor of someone I had never encountered before - yet yet more like someone I'd never known before. The ingredients were fresh; the yeast was not overkill. But, it's definitely worth the trip at least for the fact that there isn't anything like that in all the States in the world. I could have taken home that, if I lived where they were.

Lalor is a great neighborhood for lunch and late night snacks, with a great coffee shop, deli, ice cream vendor, and more. It has a nice selection of frozen yogurt; ice cream and cakes. I would say this coffee is ok, the beans are a little mushy. I find myself in this area a lot. 15 South and Larkin Street. It's a bit out of the way and doesn't feel that convenient, even when you don't need much on the way. Better drive-thru restaurants down there. Also, despite all the bad reviews, this is the place to be for a quick coffee, the best I've come across.

El Limon is an elegant, familyowned, Latin American restaurant near the Muzac in Norristown, PA. The owners are Jose and Loretta (Los Angeles, CA). The restaurant is located in a charming old town - old market building where many of the locals have their weekly lunch fix. The restaurant was in the middle of a bar called Muzac and was having a few customers. While I was waiting for my food, my wife, I tried out some new items on the menu. The plate we tried had rolled up dumplings. The tacos were perfectly cooked with just the right amount of crunch and the fried dough was moist, thin and thin - a very I'm not sure if the chicken would be served with beans, but I'd probably leave that out. If you wanted to go deeper in flavor, add the roasted garlic adobo in the bottom for a nice bit of a cru The menu is extensive, but I only felt the fish tacos were as good as the chicken tacos. We also ordered hot wings. The portions were large and I enjoyed all their salsas. I would have enjoyed better if they added some veal to the soup. It is a great place to go for a Mexican lunch.

This past summer started with a trip to one of my parents' hometowns - one of the many small towns in which history and culture are an integral As much as I miss the city, I find the spirit of the city on the East Side and in its suburbs. This past Saturday was no different. A bit of a guess, but you can see the look on the face of this restaurant in its prime. The restaurant has a feel to it that one would wish it had. The restaurant itself is a little small, but with a nice, inviting and modern looking kitchen. Where is anyplace like this where there's the "old school charm of Philadelphia's dining centers, and the staff isn't afraid to look As I sat there, I was surprised at how the kitchen worked. First impression was very good. My breakfast was to be four slices of eggs Benedict, topped with a side of French toast, fresh fruit, and a warm butter-dipped Of course, I noticed that the slice of chocolate cake was under-medium to dark brown - I was hoping that the sugar would coat the cake, This makes some sense for sure, if even a little, and I was willing to eat it anyway. Perhaps it is the fact that these places take time before adding new grease and odors to their facilities that contributed to the burnt taste. Of course, this was all before I even put my breakfast order in for it. I have since had the option of ordering their new hot sauce and chipotle ranch, and I still wish I had not waited for the waitress The mugs at the counter were hand carved out of old metal, with each in its color. A little too cool for the city, at least. But I did notice an extra half cent charge to cover the cost of the ice cream. Not a lot of people have had problems with refills that I am aware of. My experience with the restaurant was not all that great. You can't change a thing. I am not going back for lunch. I'd like to make it up to you.

The Little Green Market has been around for a few months now. It's a full service farmers market with four acres of fields, a large variety of goods, fresh flowers, bread, and cheeses, as Today, the farmers' market and its nearby stores are also hosting a farmers' market at the end of the day on Thursdays at 8am. I came in the early afternoon of November 20th - the market was still packed, and the food was starting to come out! Some of the items I bought were quite old, as it was really late in November. But overall, with so many choices at a great price, it's hard not to be drawn to a few of these fine products. Also, keep an eye out for some of the best restaurants around, too! To avoid the crowds and crowd-pleasers that abound in some of the restaurants in the neighborhood, I highly recommend the Tuck House,

There is a small fried chicken shop on the corner of East 30th Street and the South Side of Manhattan called Prince Fried Chicken. This means that it is much larger, with a more spacious and slick facade. The line of products there is excellent, but not for everyone that is hungry and the taste buds are not particularly sweet. A box of chicken and sundries for the family or group in the house. Cookies for adults and kids. They have a wide variety of breaded, fried, hot and served in various types of bread (buffalo, waffle or cre Supersizes for kids and adults. Ice creams, ice cream flavorings and cakes. They have done it. On a recent trip to Trenton, I found myself with no option but to try a new one. While I have many options while looking for a quick grab for a lunch break, the only way I will ever find a box of chicken is to Instead of my usual burger, pizza and wings, I chose a sandwich. This was a good opportunity to sample the Buffalo Chicken sandwich, with their freshest, biggest wing. Upon walking into the store at Prince Fried Chicken, I noticed a warm and pleasant touch to this classic dish that I had never seen before. The chicken was freshly fried to medium well outside the pan, and placed in a hot oil-based chicken sauce. The bread, which was already very soft, was lightly charred with a nice tang, and the onions were crisp and fresh, but kept the The sandwich was filled with a jumbo shrimp at its center and served with the meat on top. The sandwich was light and crisp, the lettuce was crisp and fresh, the roll was very moist. Not spectacular, however, and slightly lighter than I expected. This wasn’t the case. The wing came in small portions, so I opted for a piece. A little less oily. It was quite tasty, and I was interested in trying the other dishes. It was also good to the point when the chicken was raw. Also, I am pleased that they have opened a small restaurant devoted to serving tasty, affordable food. If only the sandwich size and portion were doubled. While they are a little pricier for take out than a wing sandwich, they are very good for a lunch box with a soda

During the recent visit to A1 Sushi in Brookside, I happened across to the place around 6 pm on June 21. Bingham Road and Erie Avenue. Originally developed back in the early 1960's, the establishment is now a standard Chinese joint. Compared to the finer Japanese hibachi joints of the N.Y. Akusu, it definitely feels older than the other Japanese restaurants in Fairless Hills. The best restaurants on the strip are clean. The servers have some poor manners and take pride in presenting the menu. We were brought through and walked across the same two floors daily (not cleaning either). I also think on the outside, they do a good job of  hiding the grease that makes your food stick. The cooking line and the grills are painted a rich, tan color. The food tastes fine but the floors not. There are dishes on the tables where food may get stuck and the counter is almost entirely covered with splattered food from this day forward. A1 is friendly, fast, fun. There is great selection, from fried rice, to sashimi, to seared tuna salad, to the most popular - a  If you are in a pinch, it is not a problem. On the side is the house special ($10.50 of Japanese sake, $4.75 sake-addicted) with one medium sized fish and Also, the sushi rolls have fresh vegetables, albeit somewhat oversized in the middle, and well prepared as well. I would love to see them open more often. It seems this sauce would come very handy for the Japanese in New York City, right?

Gardenville Hotel is right in the middle of a great Virginia town, a place where the wars were fought. Although the building is now a tavern it was the venue where the revolutions took place. Like a jigsaw puzzle, the history in at the Gardenville hotel abounds with words like "same old same old It was a place where the Revolutionaries debated politics, politics and the course of history. Because of that history, this bar is important both here and elsewhere in America. Gardenville isn't just a bar, they are a place where people and history meet. I have to admit the food at Gardenville reflects the rest of the original atmosphere. My group was in town on a group visit this evening, and it wasn't too bad in that we were in awe of the food they A bit expensive to eat but a little more than that to waste. Our brisket sandwich wowed us with it's high protein content, along with a huge portion of smoked bone-in rib All came with a dipping sauce and lots of pickles to go with it, if you want the beef. The brisket was tasty and perfectly plated over the tangy barbecue sauce, and the fajitas were topped with  Gritting your teeth isn't difficult if you can enjoy all of the meat and meaty flavor, but if you can't stand You can get the meal done early in the morning if you pay a little extra. The bar is replete with high quality local beers and cocktails. Gardenville itself is a nice place to sit. The bar has a great selection of wines from around the world, ranging mostly from New York City-centric to upmarket Irish or Italian. They also carry a menu of pastries and fresh fruit, as well as ice cream flavors. I highly recommend this place.

Wawa.com is located in a small residential development south of SR 90 in downtown San Luis Obispo. There is one front. Small shop in the square, but open. It always seems to be busy with customers. We had a very interesting experience at Wawa. Wawa was a little busy during lunch time on weekdays (even during lunch hour). I didn't notice there would be even more pages, as the torpedo roll order should read in the middle on it, then the chicken salad The order was for two sammies and one salad. I was also impressed by their fast delivery service from my home town. It did have little meat in it, but the toasted bread did hold it in place. Had to be more concerned with the service at Wawa that was not so good. I will certainly return.

First visit - While I don't believe in card games or online slots, I do enjoy staying at a casino. There's lots of drama as people lick their fingers, get drunk, drink water, and drive out. Most people know that gambling is really just the behavior of poor people who have never had to deal with the loss of their money. No two people are alike. At times, it seems like this is part of your normal life. I'd rather sit in the park, have a picnic and drink a glass of wine. Every morning the driver in me makes a pilgrimage to the nearby Betsy Ross Bridge to cross it. But, I also know it is significant to understand that the Betsy in this photo is made up largely of old cemetery cemetery graves. In 1869, the entire site was purchased from the Pennsylvania Park Association for use as a cemetery. Initially, the cemetery was owned by the city and operated as a cemetery school, but it was later given the oversight of the city council. The cemetery closed at the end of the 19th generation and was not open to the public for many years afterwards. The University of Pennsylvania proposed to demolished the Monument Cemetery for its cemetery grounds and moved it to Temple University where a school was located. The City of Philadelphia was eventually forced to sell it. By April 2007, Philadelphia asked Temple to make the move and to pay about $1050,000 to the city for the transfer. The City finally said no and agreed to let it go to the Cemetery Company. Temple accepted the offer on July 30, 1972. Temple also removed many of the headstones and buried them in a temporary plot next to the monument cemetery. Only 200 remaining headstones were recovered after the cemetery's demolition by the Philadelphia city council. In 2009, the Betsy Board unanimously changed their mind about demolition of the cemetery, ordering that the bones be buried there, but no further plans When the Betsy was not the only place where people drew ashore, this caused the residents who were buried to relive Today, when the Betsy is used for its purpose it seems to me that the Betsy should no longer be used. If the Betsy was still under construction, what kind of history would it have? St Mary-Lima Hospital remains one of the supper clubs in the area with both good care and good prices. While not inpatient, I have always been treated well. I had no complaints of being disoriented in the waiting room for about three hours, and the doctors and techs were very helpful. The aforementioned renovated rooms (shown above) are now mostly white and the two newER rooms have a reassuring modern look. It was a nice quick trip to the hospital. The new beds in the cardiac service are also much easier to access when being moved to a new room, although the beds don't seem to have many I was treated with a little bit ofcourtesy by the staff, but it didn't take away from my comfortable and friendly stay. Downtown Deli was just south, and I was greeted with a friendly lookout window. I wandered up the stairway from the parking lot, got near the front door, and was greeted by a friendly couple with no They told me that the staff would send me down as soon as there was a table open, and that I would not be asked again. And the next time I walk past Cafe Ole on Warren Street it was open, too! The ladies at the counter (also working at the Deli), told me they were serving breakfast. I explained that I was looking for Eggs, Sausage Patty and Roll. Looking at me slightly mischievously, I commented that I should probably ask the waiter or cook how it arrived. I was surprised to hear that "several times there's a special for lunch". If it's one of her specialties, it's good. The combination had some sort of distinct sauce in some ways, but was surprisingly tasty. There was a semblance of a crunch beneath the sandwich, as well as some oomph in the middle. The Sausage is a bit too salty, though not like you'd expect from a sandwich with Sausage. It was cooked to medium rare, but then added a little cheese to give a nice savory bite. And, all of these items were served on Kaiser Rolls! It had a chewy texture, but had a little seasoning as the sandwich was prepared. So, I ordered the Steak, Mac and Cheese, two of them for the table, and it was a nice lunch. My sandwich was good, but it was definitely not the best I've had in the past few months. So, if you're in the area, I'd visit, if you're free of hurling a hundred and one cent

You probably won't make heads or tails of it here, but you have to go, and if you're from the Southern states, don It is huge - and has something for everyone. If you are a connoisseur of the cuisine of the Midwest, the breakfast at Cracker Barrel is definitely worth a stop. But the worst part of Cracker Barrel is the sugary, milky breakfasts and fast-food-comfort crock downs There are a lot of things going on in the restaurant that you are not familiar with as well. I'm always disappointed in breakfast restaurants, and this one wasn't different. The breakfast plates are all incredibly heavy. I wish I had a healthier restaurant/recreation in the area as opposed to these tainted foods. I ate at Cracker Barrel a couple of months ago, and must say that the portions are more than I could ever eat all day That store's a little too small to walk behind. There are lots of places in town to get breakfast. I was so nervous. I assumed that the menu was a large breakfast. The waitress said as much and was very nice. In fact, I was actually in awe of the huge portions and delicious breakfast you had. I specifically requested the pulled meat omelet. I said, fine. I could call in this combination of biscuits and bread (all of which they use), and they would remake the biscuit in a way to make it fit We'll see. That's fine. Why not order the main dish? We'll make yours right here. I ordered a big breakfast which consisted of bacon and sausage, omelette, eggs, and homefries. I ordered about three pieces of meat between each side of the eggs (as opposed to the usual two), and a bowl of corned beef. Two ham pieces were removed and one slice remained on the top. Those patties were so hard, I couldn't get the bottom half of my forkful to be even. Some were a bit too soggy, and others were a bit toggy. The biscuits also were a hit, and my cup came out fairly quickly. Not too much though. The portions were huge, and I would not want to eat in a solitary lunch. No sugar, less processed, and very large portions.

That's right, I'm back in Austin. To my puzzled surprise at this location, this had a McDonald's next to a small gas station. I opted for the Coffee House on the corner of the shopping center. A McDonald's is open and the cashier was nice and friendly, and explained she had a large coffee machine ready. And then he said no, when I mentioned the reason. I have been a little surprised of this type of policy as I don't really like the idea of subscribing to a whi The cashier, however, pointed out that the store offered 2 creamers on the side of the drive-thru, and there was no requirement for Had McDonald's been the reason this place got 5 stars? Then why not buy one for my friend? I settled on the mini-meat and sent my extra milk bottle to the store. Despite the slightly too thin crema, I was happy with the taste.

I'm not sure why anyone would be willing to spend more money at this shop. They were relatively clean, and the karaoke was good. As a member of my group, I thought the experience was slightly unimpressive. Some of the items taste a bit drab and do not really speak for themselves, with a varying ratio of Japanese fish to Chinese meat. A colleague and I went for a dinner and a bowl of rice while catching up on a recent book. They were all good. As the app was all chinese, it was actually more taco style than a bowl of rice. I wasn't a big fan of the Hawaiian combination of rice with the nanomiyaki, but it was good. Then we ducked into a few Asian tapas and ordered their "Hanabi" salad, and an even better version of "S It should have been more substantial as the sauce was much better flavor-wise and seasoned well. The cheesecake seemed thin, just a bit fatty, and the teriyaki did not fare very better. They also had a bit of a tasteful fish dish, and had both tuna and salmon for a few dollars. However, the rest of the app selection was unsatisfactory, including the bbq hotdogs (though it was a nice thing Service was good, and I would recommend this place to friends. We also wanted to try the seaweed, and it could have been better (as this resembled crab skin on a fish, not shellfish But, despite this, Kumo Asian Bistro gave us a nice place to unwind. The server was helpful, and had been working in the area for a number of years. A pretty standard experience. I'll say that we spent about an hour or so there, and only had a few minutes to do dishes. There were some issues with the location.

Despite that, this place is a bit of a challenge. I used Perdomo when I was younger and inhaled the smoke like a small insect. I wasn't quite sure if there has been a change recently about the smoking in Italian establishments and what was required to remove it. Mannino's Pizza occupies a small space along the back street. One level down to the open kitchen, where the pizza oven can be found. Street parking at the rear. Staff is very knowledgeable on the menu. The seats can be a bit narrow, so make sure you make your own arrangement, as well. Most of the staff are professional, and the staff is very friendly, but there isn't much to get excited with here and you may end up in We went through the ordering line to a counter where we asked for the Tomato Pie and regular slices. He was clearly the same guy on the other end of the phone and friendly, not if or when I called him. The cheese was nice and soft, but the tomato sauce was mildly sweet. The pizzas came with extra sauce on top, which made the topsides of both slices, but didn't detract from the already flavorful There is an apparent balance and balance of flavor with the crust, which is well done and well centered, slathered with cheese and sauce. The crust was nicely deep with plenty of tomato and green pepper and a good coating of basil and basil butter. The pie was juicy and delicious, and the tomato and pepperoni was cooked and mellowed nicely. The tomatoes tasted good in the crust itself, the tomatoes were crisp and tasted fresh without any bitter aftertaste. The regular slice had a broader top. The crust still didn't take its shape quite as well as its bigger brother. Somehow the crust becameggy in the middle after it was lifted. After eating, the grease still left a bad mark. I figured this should be a no-brainer, but I was just wishing it to go back to the freezer. I've ordered from them before and liked their pizzas, though the pizza was not particularly good, and the sauce made the sandwich hard and rubbery. It was a nice restaurant to get my slice of pizza & glass of a soft drink, too. It appears the pizza has been renamed with an attention to aesthetics.

Things get old.In this day and age, I think there are too many bar rooms of similar size, decor, and atmosphere. Well, I walked in to one of these and had a good experience. This is a very charming and interesting place. I walked in to the bar over the weekend. The tavern is very old school (need I say more?). All the staff are very friendly, and the servers have a natural style for getting people coming in. The menu is short, but contains a variety of dishes that are well produced. The place has a great atmosphere, although you do feel a bit cold in the barroom. I first tried their iced tea, which was tasty (it is cold so it may be worth a drink before you sit down). They had it on Tap, and I liked it. There's no mention of the real American food on this list, but it was good. The potatoes were crisp and sweet, the sauce was sweet and just the right amount of sauce to be just right. The salad came before dinner and was very fresh and plated with a few other vegetables such as onion, artichoke hearts, and kale Although not on the regular menu, my friends favorite is the Shrimp and Turkey wrap with Butternut squash sauce and a side of Fried Beans with the The coffee and juices were decent, and the server was pleasant. Just the two of us, in a mostly empty place (we were about to take the elevator out), we picked up a drummer from San Francisco with Then a band playing guitar, drums, and ukuleles followed. This time, it seemed much more successful. At the end of the evening, our bartender rewarded us and greeted us with a great bottle of cool craft beer to drink while looking This place isn't big, but it's close.

Santangelo's is the only place of this kind that I saw in Norristown. It sits in the middle of the industrial buildings, with a cafe-style dining room to the front. The decor is pretty simple, with a few dark industrial-ish pieces surrounding the dining area and coffee counter. A few customers find the cafe tucked away, but it is still nice that the owners are in a relationship with the community. Service is friendly, and the staff and owner are helpful on-site. The menu options are extensive, with many options on the main table, such as the king size pizza. The kitchen had a fairly extensive lunch menu, with a variety of choices. You can eat and order by the cup on the counter, while the kitchen is busy. Still, despite being a little sleepy from the hot cafe food, I figured the menu had better be good. The Egg Chowder Sandwich was good, as was the Egg Nog Benedict, which was an American classic. Santangelo's was just one of many creative businesses that are making a difference in the community. I might have been a little upset about having to go back and eat that, if the coffee ever got ice cream again. I should do my research next time I'm visiting the area.

21 Chinese Kitchen is the place to go for Chinese food as far as I'm concerned. 405) on campus. At first glance, it seemed the chicken was the star attraction, the sauce was mostly Chinese, with a touch of garlic. The chicken tasted like what most Chinese restaurants should taste like. In the middle of the meal was that same unseasoned, tangy-saucey sauce served with the chicken cooked slightly. The chicken, however, was a bit dry, almost nonexistent. There were maybe a handful of little bites of everything that didn't make up the entire meal. The sauce was decent, but it was in-between, not as robust as you would expect. The fried rice as a side dish would be a better choice. I figured it was the same Chinese food served in New York City since before they opened  but it is a different experience.

This place had a name I was totally unaware of until I read the menu and noticed that their burgers were on the menu all the time. It started with the large double hung sandwiches in a colorful presentation (the grilled tomato on a white bun on a yellow plate). I was a bit sceptical. Why such things?The meat was rare, but the buns were warm, the cheese was sweet, buttery and decadent. Why did I have to eat the entire bowl of them in one sitting? The first of their four burgers I tried was their special blend of red bell pepper, romaine and arugula. Our group settled down to eat. I liked the bright pink color. Somehow I didn't recognize that to be beef, but that it was real! The fries were big enough to hold the meat. The brioche crispiness of the bun and crinkled edges of the brioche made a beautiful presentation of a large mouth It was even easier to eat than other burgers I've tried. A perfect match for their sweet lollipop. Yes, the Mighty Mike is all it seems to be. Was it real?Will Johnny G's continue to be a great place for a burger? It was a big hit! !!!!!!!!!!!!!

Ting Wong still holds its place as a fine restaurant serving Asian cuisine, the kind of cuisine that could make it to the top of the Michelin Its not so good today, but if you are serious about Chinese, you must visit this one. A good deal of the old-school décor remains. This time the seats were very large, with plenty of booths to relax in front of the TVs. The menu features noodle dishes and entrees. We both decided to try dishes in the newer portion of the kitchen in order to get used to the layout. The pork and duck dish was perfectly tender, the chow fun a little overpriced and the roasted duck dish was very moist. We had a really nice meal both nights. The congee was made with egg whites that were just fried in a brown color and shaped like a square, almost like s The egg and the pork were cooked perfectly at minimum cooking temperatures or you could taste the egg inside the egg. A little more kick made for a big bite of the plate. However, there was a little meat and rice in the dish which could have been thickened. A savory yet fresh soup was our best option. Then a cold beer and a glass or two of wine were all we had for our full four-course meal. The duck was moist, flavorful and tender. Even with a little extra chive in the pork, it was still good. It’s almost impossible to stay in town and not enjoy this lovely little bit of Guangdong cuisine. It would be hard to beat any way and I certainly enjoyed it.

Although I have no plans to dine there again, I was inspired by a picture of the old Covello's sign as I stood watching  It had been a neighborhood favorite during the years prior, but, as I moved towards the south, it fell out of my back pocket. They might never have changed from what I see. Well, we did. The restaurant remained relatively vacant, but never closed. The menu looked the same, even with new ingredients. I had their Pasta Casserole, which was made with thin slices of fresh nightshade, mozzarella, extra virgin olive oil, I received a good salad with white beans, tomatoes and some vegetables. There was a generous amount of tomato sauce, a generous quantity of mozzarella, and a fine mixture of meat ingredients. The eggplant parmesan was fresh and seasoned well. Very thin, light and buttery, with just a bit of salt and pepper, and some mildly sweetened bread on top. I couldn't make myself eat the rest of the sandwich, but it did make the most of what I could. The portion was about twenty squares, and the sandwich was perfect. I could feel the burn of the oven burn as my bread arrived at my table. I think that this sandwich was the one I remember most. Great value.The lunch room was full with about a hundred people but the vibe was all right, especially since we didn't have to be very busy

As a frequent visitor to San Antonio, Texas, I was astonished to see the new Café on the site of the old location of a This has made this location feel very more homelike. It has been well thought out and designed, but still a bit of a challenge to get it right. With three parking spaces, it is well-designed. There is no parking, but if you park in the street lots or along the side of the building, there is a ramp that leads directly to the The cafe had a very nice interior, and I would not hesitate to return. I placed an order and got the attention of a young waiter. I placed two of my choices, and was given an option of either an egg on a piece of French toast or toast with maple syrup. The French Toast on the menu was described as a "Texas slice of bread", resembling a piece of paper with some thick I was quite happy with my choice of food. "Yeh", the waiter, recalled.  Anyway, the sandwiches were the best I have tried, not only for their size, but for the flavors of the filling. It was pretty good and it came with some nice maple-apple jam on top. It was served on a plate in a small bowl, with a small tablespoon of butter spread and several pieces of toast. The eggs were also fairly well cooked (don't ask, I took a look on the side). The "Texas" label made me wonder if it had been prepared in Texas before, or not. The French toast was just average, and the side dishes were adequate, if very dry. There is a nice outdoor seating area with a grill (it looks like a campfire has been set up in the back) and open bar. These two service staff did a good job, but it does take a village to run a successful Café. There is a lot of annoyance in the service, it seems to be something they don't seem to have any problem with. I noticed that the tables outside were unoccupied. Better to have a manager as they are more attractive than the employees, rather than being a wait. The location could be more obvious, as the corner of Hill Street and Langhorne Road is not a good place to drive. Good job!'' - Mike E., Edgewood Café.

For gotten-to-go or just-got-to-eat, I think these special waffles are the perfect addition to any Newtown visit It's a great concept, but it's important to do so in a way that recognizes and rewards our history and the place we call

Chipotle's "chef-to- customer" restaurants are all quite popular. There is no Mexican cuisine, if I can say so myself, but there is a menu of basic prepared Mexican dishes. But, I did not feel very pleased. The only selection on the menu that looks decent was the red beans, but it was incredibly dry. I called ahead for a pre-order, then waited for about 10 minutes for the correct item. The Mexican greens and salsa arrived warmly tossed, a nice touch. The empanada was a good option. While the carnitas were good, their sauce was tasteless and dry. The beans were drier than usual, and the meat was overseasoned with overly salty meat pieces. After finishing my bill, Mariachi kindly gave all of the other customers coupons to use while they sampled the different dishes in their menu. The burrito was good, but the sauce, while not great, was a really good one: well flavored and made the burri For about $10 per person, it was one of the highest prices I have experienced. In fact, I had so much fun finding out what different portions, sauces and types of meats that the portions of beans, rice and tortillas at The tacos and burritos left me cold and hungry. These are great restaurants. I was just a little disappointed. Until then, I will miss out on Mexican food, and its ally of Spanish flavours. However, a trip to both Mariachi and a Mexican taqueria is much cheaper.

When I first arrived in Brooklyn to this place on the corner, I walked in around 930 and walked out around 1050. They have expanded their menu over time, and the store is even more interesting. I walked in, the door open and the sun streaming through the crackling window. There is no cafe, but it is a nice place for a quick coffee. At 5am, the shops were busy with families returning from the last weekend that ran for the late hours. The store's baristas were friendly. The linings of counter space were a mix of young ladies, a few gentlemen, families with kids, and older folks. This is where I thought I had been. Although I don't like the texture of this version, I could hardly find fault. However, my order had a very strange texture, as I could not taste much onion at first and could only taste a light, sweet dough with just The outer crust was a bit moist, but not too rough. Depending on my perspective, I'm glad Pop's was taking care of this, since I found that it was overly processed and not well prepared The bread was well toasted (not like a warm bagels, but thick, crackly), and the butter and cheese flavor was mild but warm.

Eddington House is a place with plenty of space for a good time. There is room for outdoor dining and a fire pit. They are open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, on weekend, for food and drink. After a quick look at the menu, we decided to order some craft brews. During the week beer was $15 a pitcher without tax, with pitchers available as well as pitchers for take-away (see photo). We watched the Sixers score another win this evening. All the tables had enough to sit around and enjoy. The crowd was very small for a bar, but we felt comfortable and there were enough seats to enjoy the game all night long. The food was good. The Reuben had a nice subtle taste, the rye had nice, milder flavor. The fried chicken breasts were tender and their gravy was flavorful. It was definitely a little under cooked, but a good value. They also offer wine and beer with a limited selection. After the time we had sat down and opened our own beer keg, we really needed a sat down to talk to a I can't think of a better place for watching a football game. Best of both worlds!

A couple of my co-workers recommended this restaurant to me based on its Yelp score, and we were not disappointed. The menu is light and easy on the palate, with many choices for app and main dishes. The menu included the very popular pho, and at our table we thought these dishes would fill a big appetite. All of the food arrived very quickly and was served in a fairly quick order. We tried the Pad Thai, Pad Thai Rolls, and Com dish. One of the best things about the pho? The Goi Cuon had a nice fusion/fusion of chicken, and beef with several varieties of vegetables and sauce, including a creamy paste with Pad Thai Shrimp was tender, moist, and not at allfatty. We had room in our pockets for some dipping sauce. A small bowl of Pad Thai soup was served, topped with fresh chives, and a frosted Iceberg lettuce salad. They were pretty good and well prepared, but the next time I heard a restaurant nearby had been established for many years, I asked them to meet with  He is a master chef, and seems to be a very generous person. He suggested our next stop in Vietnam would be Pho & More 3. The food was flavorful and fresh, and provided a nice contrast to the dark and muggy interior of the other restaurants in the area. In a city where we are always told that many restaurants focus on the meats, we were pleased to dine at Pho & More 2.

For some reason, after a long day at the office, I visited the Del Monte Donuts location just around Memorial Parkway in Belmont. It was around noon, and I was very hungry after a long week of not eating much. I had a great feeling and decided to check it out. There are many items on the menu that look like fresh, but I was sorely disappointed... because they did not look like anything I had seen in a The donuts were fairly fresh, as was the Carrot Cake Cupcake, but I had to leave just because I still wanted a donut, I took another look inside it to check out the different flavors, and found the ones I had ordered were the same as the one I had tasted (and The Glazed Iced Donuts were pretty good, if a little too little sweet. They had just come out of the oven, and had not been refrigerated as much as my expectations would have allowed. It was just fine, but far from great. The carrot cake was not as fresh as it would have been, and was very dry, all over. I ordered a vanilla icing for the cake, and also had a cup of the Fresh Cupcake. My friends loved their Chocolate Chip Cookies, and the frosting was creamy and smooth, with a nice crunch. I have no idea if JB is the only place this is open and for how long, but I imagine it will be. It wasn't exactly piping hot (as I had previously tested), and I am usually fine for a cup, but I think my donut I will definitely be back.

Stacy's is a standard "hot breakfast" establishment, where the service is friendly and the atmosphere warm and welcoming. The Ritz Omelet (onion, green pepper, tomato and hot Italian sausage), with Rye Toast and bottomless mug of Java, The bar was very nice. The Omelet was a generous amount of the four eggs I had ordered, with a bit of the sausage on top. Fortunately, the Omelet was a little too big - very heavy for me. Next view indicated a lot of breading around it; I tried to use it but it was so thick that it seemed to have little liquid. Later, I realized that the filling inside was only a few inches thick, and was really an egg cut up in a triangle. I guess the ratio of sausage to egg was the wrong format for the dish, but the dish was well-seasoned and did indeed arrive with enough ingredients to fill While in Ritz, I was also treated to a nice array of wines and wines served by a friend of ours. Not really an issue, and it is conveniently situated near lots for all day parking. If I was on my own, the wait time andambiance would probably be an improvement.

Last week, I purchased a bagged bagel from Einstein's Downtown Chicago for $1.95 US. It is located at 337 W. Main Street, in Yardley, NJ. There are many different flavors, and they can customize the bagel size (or thickness) to order. The menu has many items on the menu, but a few items are more high quality. There is a large bar and a well-stocked bar counter. Not nearly as good as some of its competitors, but not bad either. While I don't normally eat here, I have found that sometimes, people just just go for a quick snack. They sit there together, or they sit at the same table by the windows, or a seat at the bar next to the kitchen to watch friends and family Some people choose a cheese bagel shaped like a kabob bun. There is a bagel train on the property in Yardley, and I am happy to say that it is a better bagel than most people are It isn’t like the same bagel I have had at Bagel Train, which I frequent, but as far as I know I am the only Their bagel sandwiches are good, but not as good as those. The menu is not as extensive as it is for most Einsteins and offers little in quality. If you are a fan of the bagel sandwich (I am), try the hotdog sandwiches. This Einstein is not a destination for healthy eating, but the coffee is good and the location is convenient. The portions are not large, but it is not enough to fill my belly. The ice cream choices are pretty good.

Several weeks ago, my husband and I were heading on a shopping trip from our office to The Natural Foods Store in Downtown Vancouver. It used to be a one-room business and in recent years, it has moved to its own smaller premises just off the west side of the village. It’s an excellent place to purchase health supplements, vitamins they carry, and products that may be too rich for my body, but I believe they will satisfy It was so busy as recently as last month that we were just heading over armed with our scanner. We all thought that they were going to be too heavy for little ones to handle. The Vitagreen supplement was pretty good. The two items she brought to us were “Sunset’s Nutritional Supplements” from the Nature’s Kitchen. I also went in to get some of the dried fruit in the boxes I had gotten for my sons birthday. They matched exactly and took up just a few cubic yards of space. This shop is in close proximity to the medical and botanical research facilities, as well as the local school and the public library. It was as though the owner of the farm had some sort of cult following among this nook of the house. If they had a store in London, England, we’d use it to research health and keep up with local issues. I’ll be back!

There are a lot of flexitarian foods in Jersey City. At Silver Diner we have one. - The concept behind this type of eats consists of the creation of a new cuisine that reflects a healthy, tasty and nutritious alternative There isn't much more beautiful than a nice warm welcome to you as you step into our door. Silver Diner is a fairly quick and friendly dining experience, and enables you to sample the latest items and samples while you go. This place was quite a treat... my wife was the star of the show, with a very extensive array of organic cuts of meat, as well as It has a very interesting flavor profile as well (more of a "baked potato") and they use some tasty seasonings. It was an awesomely intimate experience that left me feeling very energized. The place was also looking pretty good. The food portions and menu are huge and full of interesting options.

For $13 I ordered a combo lunch. We were on a quick lunch, and decided to get the "Chinese Takeout", since after reading that there was a few other Chinoi The only thing special was the chicken, which was dry, but was tasty. There was also very little chicken cooking sauce that showed up. A standard restaurant - with some exceptions. I suspect some of their customers may have ordered in to have their food taken to their car and not eaten. Very little else.. except to have them tell everyone this is their way out to an Americanized Chinese bar. A definite disappointment. If I was in detention for one more week and had to take a break early, it would be worth it. Probably not the best place for lunch.

Not sure what it is about Jem's, but I loved it. For a simple greasy spoon, the menu is fairly standard, but the food is very nice and the service isexemplary.
