With a growing collection of gluten free pizzas in my town, I've been trying to find a good pizza joint outside of Trenton. I have been coming across Divine pizza a number of times, but have never been much impressed. Then one day I came upon Diviniti's Kitchen. Dante's restaurant just opened a while ago. I mean, a pizza made fresh and seasoned, with a topping that was tangy, sweet and flavorful. I noticed a big glazed tiled counter with a white finish. I was hoping to find out if I were in the right place. The walls, flooring and ceilings were the same as the kitchen, with large booths, lots of seating and good wall space. The booths and tables have wooden ledges to provide a comfortable, comfortable set-up; a distinction from most restaurants I've visited. There were two tables at each side with a separate oven for making sauce, that we could move to and get ready for. A nice touch was the large TV set. The menu provided choices for the pizza and sides, but they were not rushed. I ordered the Vesper pie, an upmarket-style pizza with the garlic butter that had been on the menu for the past week. The crust was very thick, with very neat black streaks on the top. It was very thick for such a small slice. I could see the top crust with a thin thin layer of moisture under the crust. The garlic was very very fresh, and flavorful. Second bite of the slice showed that even on its smallest slices, it had a small layer of browning. The pizza was tough enough to stand up on its own, without the worry of being burned. Another bite revealed that there was a slight crust overlieing the tomato sauce, all over. I was quite surprised to find that this pizza, which had been previously prepared by the restaurant, was much more than I expected. This was the first time that the cheese and sauce had chemistry together. The cheese flavor wasn't bitter or watery, but there were a few pieces of reminiscences from the first bite that I The garlic was not overpowering, but the Basil was not overpowering. My favorite part was that the salt crust was still hot, and the chew was salty without being mushy. It will probably be referred to with a slightly more modest level of praise. I'll go back to see if they are still around, and might make a trip out to a spot that has more flavor.

The salad was fresh, despite being more than a half day ahead of my schedule, and the sandwich itself had a nice presentation (it's I ordered my order of soup, mixed with cheese. We were quite full with my first serving, so I asked for a second to share. I found a few flakes (it had never been served before) but the salad was enough and nothing wrong with it; I even gave it 4 stars Not all that hard of a task. "I knew what was coming. For all the things you asked of me - good and evil - and all that I had in me - you said I was the worse of the In this quote, the Master gives us the lesson that he knows better than people. The last night we were out in Chengdu we decided to try it out. The Emperor's Wife and I headed off for another night in my neighborhood to dinner. This is definitely where luck meets the unexpected. Empire Szechuan appeared on the map as the second restaurant close by the shopping mall. The sign is beautiful a few miles east on North Main Street. People were standing indoors smoking for the duration. I got used to that. This was the first food truck in a while, and most probably the first in the area. We figured a quick take out would be better for us. I was glad it wasn't. The owner said a "weird thing happened." This was unusual.Their receipts were filled with dollar bills or quarters for only a little less than half the tab value. On both sides of the menu was the menu which offered a variety of dish options. We ordered the cha and a glass of cha. The meal was nothing short of amazing. We soon discovered there was no hot water boiler. So no place setting. No glasses.) And we didn't have a full pot to bring it to the table. No proper glassware. The tea came out in one plastic plastic cup and one plastic cup with the entire contents, except one. When we attempted (often in restaurants) to use the hot cup, a young kid jumped in and threw a rubber lip at us We ordered the hot soup, and they brought out the cha. We were promptly made to sit down, and were shown how to put our drinks down. Slack service, especially with a limited menu available. We were staring at the windows, while all around us were others enjoying the food. At first glance, it looked like the Chinese had dropped out of the kitchen. We waited and waited. On our way out, the employees got to work cooking dishes to be served to us. We sat and took our order. All roasted, deep fried and served with a garlic sauce. We were so glad about this small disappointment. Ordering of food. Our waitress seated us in a booth across the hall to the left of the counter and we waited. The Steamed Dumplings arrived next. This could mean a long wait. The chicken and eggs were cooked perfectly. Looking over the menu in the kitchen; something was missing. I could handle a full bowl of that stuff. We took a bite and discovered our food was a lot fattier. After a bit of an hour this cha turned very tastier. It served just as we ordered. We took a second time to get some of our rice, and finally got it. We quickly finished, and left. Soggy, and not even tasteful. So many problems with not being able to carry all the water, and we weren't able to drink it all. Just like the orange beef, the sauce was not very good. Once the dishes were brought to the table, we took great attention to their small portions. A tasty little skewer of Eggplant in Garlic sauce and a generous sprinkling of garlic butter. My dish matched the taste of the meat, so I am not sure if I will ever purchase it. We ordered the Orange Beef with Eggplant in Garlic Sauce. While they still used to have all the equipment in the kitchen, it was more of a waste of time than an actual restaurant experience. Steamed dumplings. I can see why we were smitten by it. This dish was a bit of a waste. The vegetable was charred, accompanied by a garlic infused sauce around the edges. Then we ordered both Orange Beef, which was slightly overdone and cold, with what appeared to be an overly tangy sauce (with It seemed like this restaurant could have made a small town in Chengdu, but the owners here seem to have some great ideas. Ordering took around 5 minutes, but the food was really good.

Shree Fusion Grill is a casual Indian place located in the same building at 1335 E. Highland Blvd., in the middle of East Aurora after This restaurant is owned by Santita, who also owns the upscale restaurant in the neighborhood which is St. Lawrence, New York. Service was prompt, but not a lot of food available. I was greeted by an attractive lady, and was told the menu consisted of several dishes, each with a variety of proteins and vegetables. We did so, and it was great. I was told that they all come in a bowl, and they offer the food at the table and carry it out. I ordered the new thali by the hour, and the clerk assured me that it was ready when I checked out. The server also remarked that they have chicken and beef thalis and beef balls, and fish dishes as well. This was not the first time I've been introduced to the tahini sauce, but it would have already made the dish slightly more complicated. The meal took a little longer to arrive than a standard lunch at American restaurants, but it was worth it because it came with a pitcher of lemon I found the service good, and the location just right for me. The menu has a variety of traditional Indian dishes and sauces, plus several dishes on special, ranging from a garlic butter, mint, and cor The menu is full of dishes from the region, and the atmosphere is extremely friendly and relaxed. All the dishes are fresh, and are prepared with great flavors, and are served with an English speaking Server who also gives great Indian tips. It takes a bit more energy to be a full restaurant, with very small seating, and it does have a limited patio, so it is worth It was nice to see the new building on this part of town.

I am always sad I am unable to make it to Styer Orchard to try out the cafe, but, I did at least learn some things First, it has a deli preparing a variety of meats and deli sandwiches across the street (this is a popular and well executed Second, it is a good bakery, which specializes in oat or almond bread and cakes. Third, it is a coffeehouse, so you will see tables full of joggers and grub, chinos and coffees. You'll have to be pretty patient in your first stop to understand what to expect. You can read my review of the Market at Styer Orchard here. I walked in, walked in and walked out. I took my car to this little spot, which I did not know was there for me. They had a cafe with only three tables set up behind the deli counter. I felt a little like I was passing by a ghost story. For several more minutes I tried phone banking. I knew what I wanted. Apparently there is not one. The coffee, on the other hand, was average. Having a coffee with a dark roast was not that good, and the waiter did not give me fresh coffee, which he normally would have They offered a fairly basic blend, which was just right. The espresso level came out a little too strong, and the crema felt like it had been drank from a coffee bag. It was weak, and I felt no desire to put any more honey on my toast. When I discovered the cafe a few days later, I went in as well. The berries were bright and juicy, with just the right amount of crisp bread to accompany my filling. I had the maple, maple raisin, and smucker's syrup with my toast, which paired in well with the coffee. But, I think coffee is what they really should be making. There were some nice things going on in the Market right now, and I'd definitely go back, for more coffee. Look at this photo: If this is a cafe. So, if you are a Chicago coffee lover, this is a great place to stop for a quick, relatively inexpensive cup, and to say I'm not too impressed with their food service though. You won't regret it. My only gripe is that coffee here is a little too strong for me, which was why we were able to walk around and not even see the So, for lunch, I'd say you pay twice the price at the Market!

This is my second stay at The Luv-Inn on Sunday breakfasts. They serve great breakfasts and it seems like they are having a good night! I had both "Currys" and their Eggs Benedict with potatoes and bacon. The breakfast was good, but very filling, which I had trouble eating. The place is large and clean, although you feel a little bitrushed as you first walk past. I may go back for dessert, but I don't recommend the fried chicken with egg. The rest of the staff is friendly and helpful.

Wild Ginger was originally opened by Tony and Tammy Lee in 1972. This is a very popular place that offers a variety of types of Thai and other Asian cuisines, especially in its Jamison store. Wild Ginger II on the other hand was just as appealing. A simple open floor plan features a warm brick pillar and large glass windows. The menu does a decent job of describing the food, and the server was very friendly. There's also a Thai-style bar that looks like one from the 1950s. You order over the phone, so in the end, the waitress will try to get you the thing you are looking for. The lunch I ordered consisted of a soup, one main dish, and a small salad. I got to try that flavor and let me tell you, it worked. This was a nice mix of Thai seasoning, saffron, nutmeg, salt and pepper. On the other hand, it wasn't as "Thai" as I had expected...I enjoyed the soup, but it still wasn't perfect Very different from the usual Thai "soup." I also shared the thai fried rice with Thai Basil and a couple of peanuts. It was really nice. I added some Thai Chicken to my plate, and a small piece of Shrimp. It was cold, tasteless and tasteless. I thought I'd tried a little kick of spice, but that wasn't enough. The dish was good, but the flavor was not what I expected. The restaurant owner assured me they added the sesame oil and Chili. For some reason, the server got my name wrong. Wild Ginger is an interesting restaurant, I'd give it an extra star for the Thai-con-fusion that came into play. So I guess what we were left with was a slightly more conventional Chinese dish, with some sort of sauce, which was not enough to be worth going back We never had a "wild ginger" experience in Northern Thailand that I wouldn't want to experience in the UK. If you like Asian kitchens, you may like Wild Ginger (II) a little less.

Quick Chek in Lancaster is a quick service fast food place. I've been back over the years, and I know exactly what I'm looking for but not sure what all I've found. I'll definitely be back!

I'm very glad we decided to stop in today. The restaurant interior is dark with only a few open tables. We had a few customers to enjoy our lunch as they were getting back to work, while we enjoyed the food. It is always busy. They range from mild to very well done. There are also nifty charts of the pizzas on the walls. The menu is a rather limited amount of pizza, and the tasting was not all that good. These were quite good as the cheese was well seasoned, not overly salty and had good flavor to it. The Cheesesteak (with Buffalo, Cheddar and Buffalo styled pepperonis!) were nice slices with just a bit of meat on them. They were all fairly large and the Plain, a smaller tomato pie. We ordered the pepperoni with a side order of sauce and extra cheese. We came back today and ordered three sodas, which came pretty fast, but not very tasty. We visited the suprise Chinese cooking house over the weekend (which will always have me enticed to frequent Chinatown), with our lunch time The wait was short and the food was good. This was our first time visiting, but not without some expectations. I ordered their steamed bun fried beef for $9.5 (plus tax). I don't know how this dish is supposed to look, but it was delicious and I am always attracted to that kind of thing. You add the beef and it is in. The beef was tender, the onion was a little bit bitey, and the ground chicken was fine. The noodles worked great, and with a sprinkle of sesame oil and a few pieces of rice, it had a satisfying texture at an affordable I think the noodles may have been fresh when that server came by and brought them out in advance. One of us thinks he ate it up quickly, because you should be able to add more heat to the food. I didn't really like it because I don't usually care for soup and I don't really care for meats too. There are tons of choices on the menu including the spicy bahn mi lok (chicken and eggroll) and a steamed bun with There was just enough room to share, and enough seating to provide a conversational exchange. Not the least bit of a bonus was a discount! I also visited Xi'an Sizzling Woks at a different location yesterday, a house based menu and experience. At home I can never remember the last time I actually had Chinese food in the US. It also has a nice outdoor patio area on the back for a few hours during the summer.

Someday I'd like to take care of the feet and nails. Upon returning to Montreal, I felt as though I had been on a "date" all afternoon. It's stocked with good stuff from top-quality brands like Bifido, Buffa, and Nails by Day. Each one is a full pedicure with lots of fun, but it's worth it. Very enjoyable.I didn't feel too tired later or have as much energy, as I have at times. They had the perfect spa atmosphere. You know - so relax everyone!

I was a little dismayed to find out that Yummy is still open and the menu is still the same. I would love to go back, but we can't do that for another three days. We walked in and ordered the roasted cabbage rolls, but the skewers were dry and tasteless. The sushi rolls are made from hard wontons, and paired with rice. In our visit, we got the whole lot of the usual stuff with just the teriyaki sauce, the shirashi and some r There is a light dusting of teriyaki BBQ sauce on top; not too much flavor, but still enough to make the food look good The bento was average. The salmon also tasted a little rubbery. No reason to go back. No complaints about the servers; they were prompt and efficient. There are other Japanese outlets along campus that are more suitable if you want more than the average food that most Chinese restaurants serve. Don't waste any time.

MaiTai is in a better state on this visit. The menu sounded promising as a little sampler; good old fashioned steaks and some tasty seafood. The bar has a large fire-pit with comfortable chairs, and the restaurant is relatively quiet and casual. One evening after a very enjoyable dinner with fellow Yelpers I sat in for a short cup of Joe and an eggs benedict. At one point we had three people working. The tables behind the counter are not busy, one table is open all the time; two servers are just down the street and another sits down on the front One of the servers asked if I would have a cup of Joe, I said no. The girls were wearing blazers. It included no salt as usual; but the eggs were cooked right, and the cream cheese frosting was thick and rich. The mash potato and white chocolate were also good. They were fresh, and had good butter and seasoning, but were under water. It was delicious and definitely worth the price. The patio was really nice; shaded, lots of sun, and it cleared up very quickly when the wind picked up.

My friends and I spent an eventful evening on June 10-13, 2008 at the D'Antilles Kitchen at Durham, North Carolina. The chef, besides teaching cooking classes for the Department inmates, is also hired by the State and the state to provide economic opportunity to the prisoners and on The idea is clear, and the Inn was opened in April of 1996. The restaurant we were visiting did not have a long wait time. The restaurant was spacious, with lots of white, white painted walls - we had 4 in front of us and 2 in the back. One of my entrees was the hot dog with collard greens and pico de gallo, while another plate of soup and salad was the potato We had a nice dining experience. I was traveling in the Philadelphia area, and  stopped over at a new frozen yogurt store. Uncle Mike's Ice Cream is family owned and operated by uncle Mike & his wife, Pat. I drove to uncle Mike's at this time, where there was a parking lot with the name of the shop on the ground. There is only a handful of people there making very small profits. The shop is small, relatively small. I walked in and unwrapped a cup of flavorful vanilla ice cream while enjoying two scoops of his homemade vanilla flavors. The ice cream is fresh and is a thick consistency. There is also a little seating outside. While they are not all homemade, I heard that he does make the ice cream. My order received 2 large scoops from Mike. I also ordered the vanilla ice cream. Using the simple ice cream recipe for both flavors, Mike had the ice cream in a bowl, and asked what flavor was inside the bowl. He added more peanut butter swirl and used a little cookie and cream. The two flavors came together wonderfully. The next day, I noticed the vanilla was added to the flour mix. But, besides the peanut butter and cookie crust, I ordered chocolate chip cookie & cream, chocolate cake ice cream, and two chocolate flavored  The butter pecan was excellent too. The pecans were soft inside. All three served me in a timely manner, and the ice cream was a solid. So visit often, and you will also get to meet his kids and even enjoy some snacks as well. You'd be better off at the market.
Located at the corner of New Hanover Street and Houghton Avenue, just off the East River just south of I-95. Our website has been updated for better web presence.

I was lucky ni an old friend of mine invited me to come to Saigon Café for dinner last Sunday. That seemed like an error - I was trying to go in a few minutes earlier while she cleaned the fridge. I refused to leave to meet them, and had to wait almost 45 minutes. But a waitress came over and seated me quickly, and was happy to see that I had heard earlier that Saigon Café offers hot lunch special I was glad I came and picked up a hot box of bahn mi, only to be told that by the time the food came back out at 7 I brought a pot of water and a bowl of daikon and carrot, along with a bowl of the beef noodle soup, which I paid $29 for this meal. I then made off with the lunch for the rest of the afternoon. I'm never happy to have to pay for a meal just to snack, so I called my friend up and told him to bring my food and fill  Unfortunately my sandwich was almost too hot, so I had to take another bowl of my soup home. The pho was so tender and smooth with a rich flavor, all topped with crisp carrots, carrot juice and just a little bit of fat They kept their cool about it, and all of the servers here were friendly as I walked up the elevator after I finished my bahn mi in full. I won't say the Bahn mi sandwich from Saigon Café was anything special, but it was delicious, and had all the ingredients I wanted. But the bread was quite crisp though. It would have had a stronger flavor if properly toasted, but it wasn't. The baguette was still quite tasty, but the service was too good to take home.

Italian deli has been around and gone and so fast. It has become highly praised for its excellent pizzas. These bread baskets of theirs are always a hit. The atmosphere is informal and fun, giving you a fresh and clean air for lunch before it gets too crowded and noisy. For a full description of their lunch menu, visit their website.

I did my shopping on the East Side at the Taste Café on 521 South 13th Street. With a menu of the usual American fare, this place is not all that exciting to eat, but I'm not going to complain, because No other menus with pictures, and no drink specials. However, I'm not exactly sure what they are offering. After finishing my soup I reached in and picked up the container of sauce, which contains a whole plastic dumpling and the soup. This is one more example of the wasteful way the food is packaged. The soup itself was over-flowing. There's a clear plastic lid with a red handle on top to catch the hot liquid from the container. The fried chicken had a thick yellow sauce that was probably from cooking beans. The server seemed to believe she was serving an audience. The wings were just overdone, and the orange sauce tasted like it had been marinated for a while in an oily pot. The chicken wasn't particularly delicious though. I never noticed any goop and it tasted like they didn't have much sauce. It was way chewy and too dry, not sure why we're still consuming it after so many tries. It took a while to get any good sauce on it. The service was poor, however, their bathrooms were kept clean and not obstructed. This should not be considered to be a budget restaurant.

The last time I stepped into a Dacey's I thought it would be a nice place to take a while and take a There's something magical in the dark, a place of contrast. It's just a mile of woods next to the prison escarpment that we see in Sodom and Gomorrah. The dark, bleak look of the river is like a scream of death and an attack from a horror film. The whole area is completely black, with an impassable black-and-white tunnel at the rear of the building that takes you directly into the woode And the atmosphere here is like a perfect ghost town, with the only person you hear is a humming hummingbird from the bar, There was a feel of evil about the place, a sense that something was so dark behind it all that I really could not stop thinking about it. A glass of Irish beer or 2 pints of malt with a shot of a red wine IPA was all I could think of. I needed some space to ponder my thoughts, and I decided to sit down and take a bite of my burger. They serve their house martinis and ciders in large bottles. I found myself enjoying some beers in the bar area. I was quickly told Redd's next door was the closest selection. A dozen other customers were walking by the bar, also looking for something. I settled on a fish basket. It was in a very interesting package, but I expected a bit more than that. The premise was there was a special offering containing fish and chips. The sauce was a small portion of the fish and the chips a medium, if you can say that, about half that of the chips. The fish appeared to have come in the package before being fried. The fish fillets came out first, which were also done just a little bit easier on the fish. The fish was pretty good, although it was kind of tough and flaky. I felt guilty that no one else was eating any more of my fish than I was. My friend and I were wondering what was going on there. The first thing I thought of when I finished was an Irish style Guinness-sanctioned song you could play on the tv. These are clearly the bartender's best customers. I finished the meal with my drink at the bar, so I could go home later, but the noise wasn't so compelling. The bartender came over and put a slew of "barbed wire" around the doorway. After lunch, I toured the property and saw that some of the original brick buildings have been demolished.

Purple Pizza is a pizza joint in the corner of 12th and Jackson Streets in Old Town. The menu also features the Pyramid of Bliss as well as some of the most notable Ancient Egyptian statues. Purple pizza seems to have a large selection, and we haven't seen pizza from there (even though we are near one of the largest). Purple Pizza is a well known local pizza joint in the neighborhood, with a good selection of crust types and toppings. Purple Pizza specializes in Pizza, but they have been around for a while and aren't going anywhere anytime soon. I ordered a cheese and tomato pie for lunch, which is an enormous slice of puffed crust pizza. That was the reason I felt so inclined to go. The pizza is very heavy, heavy on toppings, but not so heavy that they make you want to kick back and eat just one slice. What could be good? I ordered the spicy Buffalo pizza and got it with a generous helping of pizza sauce on top. The base is a thin crust with the mushroom layers on top. They used an all natural tomato sauce. The cheese was so thick that the pie did not have much depth in it. The pepperoni and garlic was a bit thick for my taste and taste buds, while the pepperoni was underpowered and overpowering by the Even with the sauce, the topping was missing, making the tomatoes unpalatable. I also decided to see how I would like the Buffalo Ranch Pie. I have a soft drink and my food-recognition is on a large plate outside the restaurant. The food was excellent. I felt a bit overcharged, but overall I was not disappointed. The crust is thick and the toppings are strong. They do have a penne pasta restaurant, and a pizza and dip shop, too, which is great if you want to take advantage of The owner, however, was friendly enough to tell me that the crust was going to be better the next time I came.

I was in town visiting family of the owner and co-owner of Belly Busters, and had not know that they were located in a small me 1 between San Felipe and El Monte. We'd heard they were very busy in the days prior to going there, but, once we found out, we were excited. My husband was impressed with the Mexican-American style cuisine. I guess I won't know for sure until they are open tomorrow to serve lunch. We made our way to the restaurant with a group of four, and the staff was friendly and welcoming. Definitely not a place to get food at 9:30am. Across the kitchen was another server, a husky, a young woman in her 30s, and a woman in her 20s. We'd not heard from his parents until after lunch. I noticed that the coffee shop wasn't just a coffee and sourdough joint but a full blown Expresso. We were told that the coffee was being moved from a tiny space in the back to this bigger, brighter space. We had a variety of lattes and lattes with espresso sauce, espresso shots and a cold brew. You will have to wait a while to get served! We returned, but there were a few others out there as well, just trying to figure out a better location for our delivery. And based on our visit, I will definitely go back, and order lunch instead of being forced to park.

Huang's Pork Garden isn't a garden. Not only is it just a Chinese joint, but a very old Chinese house. You go to this restaurant located on the last-generation family-owned lot on Bordentown's main drag in Bordentown. Where that street ends, is the entrance/exit of this food house that looks out over a greenbelt of a parking lot. At this point in time, the driver of the Van were trying to make sure the place was safe for my son, and a security check had to be He was yelling at me to stay away from him until he went away. He assured me he was coming here for lunch. That's cool! The food was not bad, nothing special, and although pricey, I was grateful they would give me some discount. Family came in for lunch. I was told that the restaurant was open from 11-4, and my guests could arrive at 9pm. I was invited to try some of their dishes - I had been invited to try most of this area, but I didn't want to wait any longer I'm not sure who all was watching but it was not a very entertaining meal. There were only 2 tables left, so at least there were 3 tables to seat us. I saw this a while back with my favorite Asian food restaurant and figured I might as well try it out. But, the atmosphere was cozy. Of course, the Sesame was just a very ordinary and old-fashioned chicken sandwich. The Wonton Soup was the norm, thick and salty, with a bit of tang. It was thin, and very rich, the sauce being rich enough, not too thick, and not too heavy. The noodles were firm, and some of the vegetables wilted a little. The fried rice just didn't do it for me. The Sesame Chicken with a combination of fried rice and steamed egg was good too. The Fried Rice was okay, with the chicken being slightly underbroken. The portion sizes were generous. I was pretty excited about Huang's Garden, and looking forward to going back in our neighborhood. It doesn't feel like it if you live in the south and are planning on dining alone. They do a nice job of making the place appealing to adults and kids, while it certainly does not please cynical Chinese American.

They were partnered with all other groups and members of society, and were supported for the purpose of establishing the hospital; not just the administration for the services Besides medical care, the hospital also was a venue for the arts, and a gathering place for physicians and their families. Approximately 150 people made this donation at the time. The new hospital, now complete except for room and board, had a tuition of one night at 1 a.m., and was costing 2 the founding of the Philadelphia Hospital School for Girls, which matriculated its first students in 2017. Throughout the years, the hospital was recognized as one of the most outstanding medical schools in the country. From an initial hospital with 20 beds, there have been expansions as well as opening of a hospital on the 5th Floor. The staff and doctors are efficient. In recent times, all the patients we saw are highly educated and knowledgeable, and everyone treated me well. I was treated like a member of the family, and knew that they would be keeping me in order, and would be devoted to me, with my It was a pleasure to be under their care. The hospital offered a full, comprehensive examination, just as I would have done at a regular hospital. It was a pleasant experience, and I greatly look forward to visiting there again.

It was quite comfortable to sit down. The parking area is small, but not an issue. Currently, it has a parking lot. An improvement over the old and uninspired "Spike". The portions of the menu are just as good as the previous incarnation of the restaurant. The burger is very fresh. The bun and the overall presentation of this burger is as well. However, this new burger is a bit too thick for me to eat. Typically it was tender and juicy, but when it was served to me in the way it was, the ingredients just didn't mesh well. The burger has a small amount of cheese, but not enough to make an impression in comparison to the rivals that tend to have stronger-bodied cheese The cornbread muffin is also good, but has a very thin crust and is glazed with brown sugar (despite having the same thick crust). Salvadore's Pizza, as the name implies, is located at 105 E. Madison. Located in a new building on the 4th floor of this shopping center, and run by Salvatore's owners, the shop is quite The menu is large, and even has menu items on it for lunch, dinner and snacks. The first has a full lunch menu and the other has a very extensive menu for more substantial and rich dinner items, such as pasta, pizza, and The more casual one is a full menu of sandwiches and paninis. Salvatore's is not as elegant as the other restaurants out there, but it's well organized and there is plenty of seating. When we walked in our first order was a chicken, spinach panini with a rolled wrap. We came along to eat. We arrived about 2:45 pm. We chose to sit in the corner of the kitchen. They brought us our order right away, and were very nice. It did the trick, and the sandwiches were delicious. The bread with the herb dip was very good, with an interesting tangy garlicky taste. The panini was quite nice with a large piece of grilled chicken, Brussels sprouts, onion, and green peppers topped off with  The cheesy cheese was thick, nice and salty, but there was a bit of a lack of tenderness, and the pizza It seemed a bit dry as it was so incredibly little cheese. The sauce was a thicker consistency than usual, although they did put on a little extra mayo. They were not impressive, for the price they charged. The pasta was good, but the sauce was mainly sweet, but that really was the only great thing. The pizza came in a large box with a lid, but the crust was soggy as to make it difficult to eat it. We left and returned around 7:30pm. The pizza was fairly greasy and the pizza itself was slightly tough, but its meaty texture made it more portable; that's not to say it couldn Probably not quite to the standard of the place. We had a favorite pizza place in Pittsburgh, Delfina, and the pizzas there are generally good as well. We will be making it a point to return for the pizza. The food was very good, and not too expensive, but I didn't like the dishes when I arrived at lunchtime. We knew quite a bit about the restaurant by the name of the menu, but didn't get very involved with the food. A couple items I liked, but not enough to warrant a return visit. We do have to stop there occasionally on our way home though for quick Italian breakfasts and lunches. They certainly have a solid menu with a variety of items.

Bristol's Amish Market has a very interesting story of people and their pursuits. It is the newest and closest market to the nearby market in Newtown. The market is open for business Thursday-Sunday, on the same day as the rest of the market, and you can still purchase a lunch and There are only a few vendors, and the crowd is diverse; many are men and women. The market is decorated in local local colors, with a number of tables decorated with small hand-painted signs. It is an old and dark space, and I imagine a lot of people here would like a quick look, or you might like to relax and spend There is an amish section where you can sample the best Amish-made goods in Pennsylvania. More often than not, it offers a variety of products, and you can always enjoy yourself with a cup of coffee and a good book! The bathrooms are spotless. After browsing around, and looking at a variety of goods, I found the majority of the items, a good deal for an Amish store. And there's a real sign on the door stating "Also known as the Newtown Market", so you know there's also If you plan on leaving the market for a few hours, Mary's Bakery is the best place to stop at. Donuts are what you need before a workout or a game of football. When I tried her donuts, I didn't get the glazed topping because I ate the plain chocolate donut. But, they are sweet and just good. It's also an excellent place to stop after a long-day of shop touring the market. They sell it "as is", in order to conserve room for the next ad hoc orders. The store also has a large array of pastries you don't see everyday, all available in a plastic bag, which comes wrapped in plastic ( In the morning, I received a sweet box of peanut butter & jelly cookies. I was really afraid they were going to be stuck in a box with a little of a sticky mess. I think one of the great things about this market is that it doesn't have a wall-of-sale; which is reas After a very exciting experience in the donuts, they were gone. Not!? I mean, why leave them out?

At first glance it didn't look like a very exciting concept to me: it was nothing more than food court, and I believe the whole place was It's like the same old Italian sandwich shop/pub that opened up a few blocks from our house years ago, but that offers more than just the At 4pm on Sunday, our group ordered three dinners. It seemed like a perfect place to get together when you live within a few miles of the restaurant and get a gander at the dishes and The meats were overdone and overdone, and the cheese on the pizzas, with their thin thin slices made the plates look unappe The Chicken Parm was a sourdough that was overrich with cream which made it difficult for this dish to be good. We felt the chicken was tastier than expected, because the sauce had made the chicken rubbery and overly heavy. The Marsala's sauce appeared too thick to cut through the pizza, which made it more like a thick penne with a creamy At a small Italian joint in a shopping center, why not go to this one? For the evening that we were there, the pasta selection was simply incredible. A trio of potato wedges, peppers and red onions, all of which came with a sprinkling of Spaghetti Bolognes Veggies, when they arrived were a little frozen, but we were able to get them cooked (tender) but not too brown or These meals were just good, and not particularly expensive. The pizza isn't bad, but doesn't stand up against the menu. We would have loved to continue our visit with the pizza, and perhaps I will find a new one there when we are in town.

My favorite sandwich place in the area is a location at 2050 Park Ave.. That is the reason I gave Chicco's a two star rating for dinner. I have been there several times and tried a few new things, but always enjoy their breaded chicken sandwiches and their tomato pies. Their dinner menu includes salads and pastas as well. I ordered a Buffalo Chicken Sandwich dipped in a delicious Alfredo sauce that had the flavor of the sandwich wrapped around a thin layer of ground The chicken was smothered in cheese and the rabe was served on a plate on its own. The chicken was a bit on the tough side, but I was thankful that the chicken was a generous portion this time because I was not able to I don't know whether or not to put a side of sauce on the pizza, but I love what the sauce contains! Although it lacked anything special, Chicco's Pizza was well worth it. I'm impressed with the pizza and they were clean and the staff were friendly. I would definitely recommend this place if I was in the area.

Thai Kuu is a Thai restaurant with a modern twist to its kitchen. Like many Asian restaurants, it has an interesting menu of curries and Thai-fusion dishes. I ordered midday dinner with a few things on my plate, including the soup combo and coconut tofu. I noticed several different options on the menu and deciding what to purchase attracted my attention. If this wasn't enough, I also appreciate that the atmosphere and food seemed surprisingly simple. Upon arrival, our waitress was friendly and welcoming. He remainedseated while I was eating and then told me to sit down. I was aware this was not a new Thai place, but an old friend just came over the past few weeks and felt the need to comment. I could never forget that Thai Kuu was an old school Asian cooking establishment, which I imagine must have been very gratifying for the patrons at its I was wishing for hot water, and this was not the case. The Tom Ka soup was thick and dense, with a sweet, sweet-tasting tomato sauce. The soup was well prepared and was fairly priced; and all in all it was pretty decent on its own. This should be enough to have sent me to the back room of my hotel, where I would have thought the Pad Kee Mao had been dubbed It was very hot, but the sauce was mildly spiced. The Pad Kee Mao was just okay. I wasn't sure if they had added a chili oil, but when I tasted it, I didn't find the combination of heat and A noodle soup, but not the "wine" and Thai.

Check out Casa Luisa. Rather it is a well maintained, professional cafe with a refurbished restaurant on an island next door. This is a small operation that has a new owner and is very successful. They have taken care of their employees and refurbished the interior with fresh clean materials. It is also a great place to meet friends, and be savored over a cup of coffee. The shop is situated on a small back lot, and offers a unique walk-in style experience. I had to visit the other side of town to find a new place to eat, but the café was immediately inviting. The restaurant has a nice selection of items, and service is generally good. At the end of the menu is an assortment of home made dishes with home cooking options. I also ordered the classic eggs Benedict with ham and scallions. If you take the bread with one bite, the spiciness would fall off, but the Omelet had a strong, warm flavor all its Next I sampled the chorizo. Not very spicy in comparison to other markets. My favorite was the rice which was perfectly sauteed and very flavorful. A delicious combination.It was topped with an egg and two shards of bacon (which I ate twice). The menu was fairly simple, with a few interesting items I could not pick out. This was not my last meal at La Cabana. In the meantime, the ambiance of the restaurant offered me a small welcome. The waitress was helpful and friendly. His daughter was there and gave him his business card. He immediately jokingly, "well, there is a lot of work to be done, like remodeling and new kitchens, and there, like He said that they haven't been able to get the word out about their business, but he noted that they are still working on it. I would certainly recommend El Caja to anyone who is looking for a home to enjoy a great meal, the most pleasant place to drink coffee and snacks I look forward to returning soon. I am awaiting my next visit, as I haven't seen many other Latin American bakers like Nicholas. The best aspect of La Cabana was the free music. It is a lot of noise.

Tower Hill Brewery is an Irish style brewery in the West Wing in the middle of the city on High Street. They are a member of the Philadelphia Brewers Association, and that has always been impressive for me seeing as that I'm a big Philly If you've been to the brewery they'll help you find it. The shop is dark with an overhang of industrial looking concrete that allows you to walk through to the entrance of the brewery. The rim gave the beer a pleasant flavor on the nose and had a lingering light sweet and tangy flavor. The bacon/scallion was baked together with a savory batter of mashed potatoes with added sour cream. They were prepared as well as you can imagine as they were made with homemade dough pocket patty batter. By the time I left, I had tasted what I thought my friend and I were going to eat. Somewhere along the way the fries turned a dark brown. The perogies were pretty good. All the sauces were good. The dough was fine and moist but the perogies were not as satisfying. I would certainly recommend the Loaded Pierogies. They have a high level of commitment to quality that will make your waistline very happy. I hope that Tower Hill will try to focus on other products in the future.

Dried out for a few minutes before driving over to their small shop in a nearby building, I began to wonder what it was like. There was only a handful of tables in the back entrance with two full-sized high-top tables and counter at the front. So I bought myself a dozen, a dozen, and a dozen. The place was lined with customers eager to sampling the dozen or so donuts that were so close to their table. The staff provided samples on their mobile devices and offered me samples as well. The doughboys were a tad thin, but were enjoyable to eat. I was impressed by the sweet perfection and texture of this fine donut. After a few bites, I felt like a 'death to me', and eventhough a very large quantity appeared out of After enjoying my doughboys a bit more, I offered to share with my family, so the family could try one. Almost everything I tasted was delicious, except for the donuts with the chocolate glaze. They were delicious and satisfying and the coffee was very welcome after their long drive. And...if they weren't glazed, how about chocolate glazed? The place looks old school and authentic.

I discovered a new liquor store in my neighborhood. Most of their beers are great and they offer a number of styles. The Inn at the Jersey Line Hotel is one of those places where you don't want to go if you don't want to be in the It's great for a quick burger or a burger aficionados to settle in and unwind. The building is quite large, so it could get a little stale as time goes on. It's just a dingy little dive bar that has everything...no high rises, no parking, no patio, no TVs Despite the age difference, Hulmeville Inn still caters to a younger crowd. The people are super nice and the music is great. The staff is friendly and the margaritas are outstanding. A lotta people go to Hulmeville Inn, a lotta people stay there, a lotta people hang out. Come in.. Come on down. Buy a drink. Come in. Get started playing. Cheer up!. Eat. Watch sports. Buy a plate of food. The place is pretty fun, but the bar is so much more. And you're in for the rest of the night. One of the things I love most about our visit to M&T was the bar in the back of the pub where the beer always seems to be better then I thought it was great! When we made our selections, it felt like we were ordering dinner from a restaurant restaurant. Food at the bar is the standard and well-crafted food of Pittsburgh. They have been a part of our day and had many great food, especially the grilled chicken tenders, arugula fennel The double had a strong hop notes and the monks were full, robust and tasty. For my friend, he ordered the IPA, mainly because it tasted really good. The kitchen was busy with customers at the counter. Their menu is all organic and everything is fresh. The place is packed! Very relaxed atmosphere.Once we made our seats, our waitress promptly said "Need any sides" and suggested which sides we wanted to add. They were all very busy. And the food came fast. That cheesesteak was so good that the only other dish we had that night was the burger topped with onion rings. My daughter ordered a cheeseburger as well. But the flavor and value was reflected in even more in the desserts. What better way to end a meal than with fresh flowers and fresh coffees? Great place to bring the kids! My husband was impressed with the presentation of the food that included a few hot sauces, and even ordered a drink. The Burger was excellent. The rest of me was a bit full. Served with a slice of pickled onion and arugula.

After attending a local craft festival, and walking by the kitchen there that afternoon, I finally had time for one of Joe's Salsa restaurants that I came here this week because I had been in town for 5 days or so. The smell of cook-your-own taqueria was fresh and all the ingredients used in the meal were fresh and vibrant. In fact, it was a small but comfortable stall with open seating, and a small counter. We were seated right away, but they never took our order for even a moment. The waitress was nice and helpful. The first one, the Mexican Carnitas Carnitas from Universidad Complutense de Madrid Ibérico. There was a large bottle of guacamole on the table, which I tried as I ate my meal. The meat tasted soy sauce on top, but what really stands out is the thick, delicious soft carnitas, instead of all that oil The sauce was not as hot as the guacamole, but the tortillas were still a bit moist. I felt that I had to rush out to get my food to my office, walk up to the restaurant, and wait five minutes for the lunch time orders to There were also plenty of other items I liked. I am looking forward to dining there again soon (hopefully soon).

The White Dotte is a family owned enterprise that has been in business for 70 years, building on the intersection of Routes 154 & 205 20 and 22 in the White Dotte area of Princeton. It has been in operation since 1945. This attraction was a surprise; and, I must say I wasn't much prepared for the experience. Not that they would have much to offer. The decor is simple, mostly white decor and wallpaper. The ice cream (I could do without the cream too), was also better than I expected. In the window was a sign advertising "White Dotte is serving its best breakfast burger until dinner!" They also have ice cream. The menu is large and detailed with lots of old family stories and information. There were still enough slices left over into the middle to complete the order, so I ate them before it came out. I paused to check on the name. After hearing that, I said, "Dette" also meant "the milk of eggs," and they said that the name came from the French name d Pretty chicken. It was about a week before I heard it sounded like the name of a popular TV show that was about the chickens. "White Dotte" was the name of the farm and of the two people who raised the chicken. There were also many little stories about the story behind the farm. The toast was great, the cinnamon spiced flavor tasted like freshly baked cinnamon sugar. The cheese was a real bargain. I was a bit twangy by the end of my breakfast, but not enough to ruin it for me. It was, not too bad either. Very welcoming staff.The place carries a unique feel. Simple look - nice touch. Good view.You get what you pay for. Friendly staff. Beautiful pastries. The menu is well organized, and is easily remembered the next time you visit.

Utsav is a modern Indian restaurant near the San Francisco airport. This restaurant has a re-design and new kitchen made from the bright mango and coconut milk pasted into a colorful Curry paste. I was impressed by the wide range of dishes ranging from dal, karaman and paneer Indian dishes, all seasoned perfectly, The decor is sophisticated but also laid back and fun. The menu offered calamari, paneer, squid, shrimp, chicken, veggies, and meat. We had them all to go. The menu is a list of the dishes that can be ordered if the menu permits it — Indian, Chinese, Nepali or Middle Eastern. All the dishes were great to me, and the waiters appeared to be well educated as we were dining. The squid seemed to go for overkill. The squid was not as tender as originally intended, and the white sauce wasn't very impressive either. It was adequate enough as a starter. It was not even good, so it was a bit of a let down. A great and unexpected dish was the Chicken Amwalla (made with chicken and quinoa). The chicken had a good flavor, and the chicken filling definitely retained taste. At the same time, the Vegetable Salad went well with the warm vegetables and sauces. We loved the sliced avocado on the Kalai was just perfect. We also ate the chili garlic naan and enjoyed the chili garlic on the side. Pappadam was a nice filling snack that we tried. We would recommend the Pappadam and calamari. All was a winning combination. Probably should be in the neighborhood when the local economy improves.

Located in the back of the Plaza Amalfi, El Limon is a locally owned Casa Mexicana, close to the I-10. El Limon is a Mexican place called El Limon. I was the only patron, with the narrated, but loud, sound of a few people being thrown. Two employees came around the corner and greeted us, offering a glass of soft drinks. The kitchen looked somewhat like a typical Mexican shop, with the ovens and kitchen worktops in white. The inside was very clean and there was a small kitchen counter, open to the side. The menus are arranged on a wide yellow table surrounded by plastic chairs and bar stools. The menu was completely encapsulated by the walls of the store. For breakfast, I decided to try their margaritas. As an aside, this was the first new restaurant I had ever gone to, so I feel like it is about time that food was not only fresh but at The store was empty and not crowded. We assumed they wanted to earn a little money on this bill so they could hawk their products to patrons. For some reason, it looks like the menu is compiled by a guy who has a passion for Mexican cuisine, not Mexicans. After taking a few bites of the torta and tacos, we knew we were getting a good deal. The burritos are a thick and perfectly seasoned pork mixture, covered in a generous amount of guacamole, and But their aji sauce was perfect, not a huge amount, but one of the best I have had around town. The tortas on the other hand had a little heat to them, but other than that, was light, tender, and tasty. My only reservation was with a friend, but the restaurant did not sell any other items. The owners and employees were very friendly and seemed to understand the experience of being in a Mexican restaurant, but were mainly friendly to our American friends. The tortillas were dry but very tender, the salsa was not too salty, the chips and salsa were hot and made better. I would not hesitate to recommend El Limon to anyone.

The Trenton Pizza from Brooklyn is definitely the better pizza for the dough and sauce. I've always preferred thin crusted pie pies from Pennsauken Township pizza place when the one that would be on my own wall was Brooklyn. I'm not saying I don't love the American Pie, I just don't like the thicker crust in the center of the pizza. I'm still partial to the Philly-style pizza, but the Trenton-style pizza is much better. Also the meat on each slice is just right, and paired with the delicious salad dressing. Since it is not sold online, I may return in the future to eat it at home to try the Trenton Pie, or something like the pizza that

We were visiting the Trenton Farmers Market this morning. Here the owner Paul Pulaski had been in the business for some time. The restaurant was seated, with the kitchenette looking out over the park. It was even bigger in several directions. We went for the red and white which was quite good for being seasoned well with salt and seasoning... and then seasoned with pepper for a The store was even offering barbecue sets in bulk. It took a little while to figure out all the different types of meat and what they were made of, but I couldn't forget. So we needed to pick up some specialities. That's where you take a look at all the choices in the piles. They had a price. One of my friend's got the onion stuffed potato and a king sized pierogi. In the box was a bowl and a little amount of mascarpone, and two baggies of potato/onion mashed They were from the Bronx, and had the distinctive brown sauce. They were very dry. A double was $5.26 (the package cost $7.10). I've had better pies on a stick. Did not find the thicker filling as rich, and the cheese to be soft. The pork was tender and slightly chewy. They were luscious. The market is in good hands. On the plus side they were excellent, so we will definitely come back for the sausage.

Fitzwater Cafe is a classic French cafe in the heart of the River North neighborhood. As you would expect in this area, this cafe has been in business for years and now is a wonderful old historic building. The owner John has been there for several years, and a few of his staff have been in this place for 20 years. The small rooms at the foot of the bar are spacious. Fitzwater Cafe is a little expensive, but at around $30, this is a good breakfast place to try out if you are interested. It is always busy, with people waiting to eat and drink, and it is a popular breakfast spot. As it turned out, our breakfast consisted of a burrito and a sammy. The stromboli was generously filled with fresh greens and green onion. It was a little spicy, but that is what you do when you bring in a gourmet dish. In my experience the burrito is very good but very dry. Also, very good, very clean. We ended up ordering the French toast. The menu items are also slightly varied by region. A nice little spot but in the middle of town.

Located at 1675 E. St. Louis Avenue in the slum, Deli-Licious Café is a coffee and breakfast joint where The place is a casual and open environment. There is an open layout with three tables and a small bar area for drinks. The employees know their menus and are friendly. Lunch prices range from $4-15 including coffee. The food was excellent; both starter and main courses were very good. It got me right in to the morning, so I decided to try this on at dinner. It was tasty, but I could have used more bread since it was only an hour before and I had only one hour to finish. The bacon was tasty, and I did like the way it was prepared by the chef. Both sandwiches are excellent and would probably be recommended to friends. We ended up ordering additional items on the lunch menu and enjoyed our selection. I would have given better than 2.5 out of five for this place.

I tried the Chinese house at 1150 W. St. as one of my first stop when heading back to California this week. It seems to be a neat little place with well decorated decor, and a neatly constructed kitchen with a hooded grill above and below A few tables are available, with many of the offerings set on one large table. The only thing was the service. There is also a menu for food preparation and take out. I was at this location to pick up just about three dishes, one of which I had selected was the orange chicken salad and another was the egg white and crab There was a good amount of red and orange meat, paired with strong grilled beef, as the chicken was very tender but soft and a little I figured I would be able to enjoy these in the most ideal way possible. Once the food was served, however, the temperature issue was a real pain. They were not hot, either, and were completely cold to the touch. While both items were decent, I would question their food safety. I was glad they were willing to serve their hot dish, but I was less envious that they would then have to be served cold, a little It is also possible that the food was not prepared enough before seating.

Newportville Beer House is a charming pub set in a historic building with some semblance of history. Just one day before it was remodeled. With the building now home to the Newportville Inn, the historic building is relegated to the blighty of its past. Its eerie architecture reflects the past. It is easy to imagine that Johnny Bartender, the owner, was working his magic as the pub was transformed into a German restaurant. I had an impromptu dinner at the bar last week with another tourist, and it was just what I needed. The chicken was marinated, but over cooked, and served with little salt, which I didnt mind. It has always been my main weakness. Next we ordered the cheese curry. I'll be coming back someday to enjoy more of the Curry (I've definitely heard it taste better when made with real Paneer). The garlic naan was nice. They would not suggest putting this on any other roll, and I doubt that an individual roll would have a similar flavor profile. No dryness, and very good sauce and seasoning. I got one of those for dessert, which was a hit, although they didn’t make me feel like we were being served Indian at a fast Spice Rack offers a variety of Indian dishes and is well rounded, but I would not come back. I hope to return there in the near future. Good? Yes.. Not really. Nope..it is actually in a strip mall in a quiet area, by a pond, and is a few blocks from the Good? No. Nice? Yes.This is just the reality of an Indian restaurant in the area.

During today's post on this blog, I got a tip from my good friend, who'd recommended the delicious food at Veggie Haus Having made a long run from my home in Philadelphia, I walked to East Liberty Street. No photo ID was required in addition to my vaccination card. It was a nifty bit of security, and this is an all-nighter (at least in the afternoon). In a country where everyone is crowded and the public travels a lot for religious services, this is an easy reason to leave or return home. I didn't get the message and I would not have gone to this restaurant if there never had been a mandate to do so. The breakfast menu featured several dishes of my own creation, and a selection of other guests' lunches. There was a big area for restaurants that were fully stocked with fresh and delicious cuisine, all within a few blocks of the mall. They also carry an extensive selection of organic Jewish snacks. I did order a Fried Egg for a single person, but as a friend called the bacon to go, I decided to have my lunch at  The "By-By" was a full patties, beaten together, made with seasoned seasonings (as requested by me It was a medium flavorful and had very little pepper or salt and was light on the spices. I also tried the roasted potatoes, which came on a bed of a tasty mix of wheat, peppercorn, and onions. I took a full plate home, with the additional Sautéed Onions. The morning wrap was also excellent. The Fried Chicken Tikis are just way too salty to be anything, so if you like the sauce, you should have them. A great experience and, a bit sad to have to deal with. Lastly, I will never forget the Omicron vaccines my doctor prescribed as an answer for me and my little grandson. But I certainly know I'll try. But I'll never be too concerned about getting sick there. Still, I liked the fact that we could be on our way to enjoying our family's meal together, without having to pay for dinner. The service was excellent, as are my meals.

On a chilly winter's day, I wanted to stop by while the world was not humming, so I decided to head up to Pi On the first visit, I ordered some to go, so that I could fill my mouth, because that looked so good. We ordered three and the dough was extremely soft and flaky. The cinnamon sugar coating could be brushed on and you could easily see through the layers. Nice combination. Probably would not have been possible without the addition of the doughnuts. Their variety was really impressive as well. They also have homemade cookies andcakes. They're also open on Sundays in the shop, but are closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. A trip back - I don't know if they'll still be open for lunch-time hours.

Dairy Delite No. Rt. 70 in Asheville, SC used to be a very large ice cream shop. Last weekend there was an open house in the early 20th century. One day while we were there I thought we were invited to an event at New Year's Day for a treat, so we decided to stop for an I ordered an entire pitcher of a creamy vanilla cream ice cream! That simple ice cream is the best I have had and I love the unique packaging that makes the cup that much sweeter: no ice cream is better What a treat! And the best part, it was still like 1970! Nice ice cream joint.

Golden Dawn is a chain diner with a lot of variety in town in the Fairfield, PA area. The dining room/diner is comfortable, with a large selection of dishes with good flavor and great service. It appears it has been primarily a coffee and breakfast coffee shop for a very long time. I had the egger, but with the side of potatoes and coffee I could have enjoyed it better. The Omelette was smothered in a mild-medium hollandaise dressing, and topped with a reuben The hash browns were good, but had the edge of a wet shoebox, which gave them a better crunch and depth. I thought it would be too large for my husband, but that's only a matter of time. Also on the menu was a classic French toast topped with sugar cubes. The service from the server to the table is top notch! I wish I could have found a time to visit this diner on a regular basis. For a bit of dinner, I ordered a sandwich and their signature Hamburgers. They're all well worth a visit, and the food is as impressive on the menu, too. You would not want to miss this gem.

Despite a week's lack of pizza outings, the following day was a nice meal out. We parked, threw on our shirts, and went into the Italian Food truck. The location was the home to the very original Stamster Pizza factory and is operated by a family of cooks. They look like an old-school restaurant with fresh woodwork, colorful paintings, a couple of big ovens, and a giant mural of the This was the 1st order I had taken before a friend had returned home from Europe. From the beginning I felt like a police officer. A lady asked us what time we were ordering and asked to see my ID. A hot order with an already waiting waiter, beckoned, and we were seated very quickly before the stench of Carryout or My masks were still attached to my head from the time I got home, but that just means that I still must be sitting on my phone waiting for the So we ordered as an example of what we thought we wanted. Our tomato pie was huge and had a heavy coating of globby cheese clumps. And, as you can see from our initial review, it was only OK. However we wanted to see the sauce and taste. The chicken parm was huge, but was basically what you would expect a parm sandwich, but with little of the meat components. Almost like they had gone into a factory making their own tomato sauce instead. We ate them all and were able to find very little of them. What we did do was eat the sandwich with the remaining bread. It is not their fault the sandwich wasn't overwhelming. We then gave the sandwiches a second helping of fresh bread and the stromboli, but then sat on top of the rotisses Our next meal was a side of sweet potato chips, and one of the two dishes on this meal, a Mexican inspired tamale. The only thing left was half of those sammies. Well, as to the tomato pie, it was almost not even in the zone.

For the past two years, I was frequenting Deli Freak & Deli. It's usually more of a casual deli space without any really grander ambitions either. We made our way from downtown to it. In comparison to other sub shops, FD has more options for sandwiches than many. FD's hoagie is a big size and that means they know how to wrap it up and deliver before you leave the store! The deli itself was quiet and relaxed, with a lot of the flavors in the meat being showcased. I had trouble trying to imagine myself being so filling because of all the fresh food and meat - plus the fact that it was so hot outside that I It would be a good place to stop for dinner if a couple of hours are needed to complete the sandwich. It's an easy lunch to enjoy at a good price, with the deli and fresh turkey in a very nice place.

Ho Sai Gai is located at the junction of Sai Gai and Ho Yuan, just down the street from the old Chinatown (Me They had the remodeled lobby, but that did not affect the food. It could have been more relaxing, but it is one of the smaller diners and restaurants that provide an excellent dining experience. The atmosphere is good for a casual coffee experience, though I would not normally go there for a full meal. The book behind each table has a variety of traditional Chinese dishes. Many of the dishes are made with real beef and cantonese vegetables – some of which come in fresh out of their own pots. Most dishes are fried, but sometimes the menu is a little more extensive for the taste buds. So we walked in for dinner, but we felt like our hosts might have changed since I was visiting (he isn’t the same person as we This isn't the best of their offerings. After some wrangling, we settled on a chicken drumstick, chicken dumplings, pork chop and dumplings, and some duck egg My friend was served the first plate, and was surprised to find she was served in the same order as her friend at the other tables, but it was obvious My Beef was too tough and unseasoned, but a touch above the standard. She also felt that both her pig and beef dishes took an excessive amount of time to cook/cook, and as a result there were a The sauce was pretty standard, and tasted like duck. All three dishes were reasonable, and in total we had four servings. The portions could have been larger, but it was definitely not our favorite meals. Ho Sai Gai is ok for a casual meal, but it is certainly on the list for lunch at night. Their dinner menu has less variety, but they do offer a lot more options and is a little harder to find near more popular shops.

I was in Pottsville last week for some historical reasons, and Coventry Parlor was on I-395. I was just passing through on a Sunday afternoon, and found myself here, mid-day. We went to Pottstown around lunchtime to see what the old downtown had to offer. We had taken in the pubs around Pottstown, but didn't stop at any of them. I had a really strong desire to get some taps for my snuff, but the tour didn't look interesting. A couple of beers later, we found an interesting little parlor, right in the middle of town. It turned out to be Laurel Locks. We opted to explore the store. With a few exceptions, there was a lot of history. Those peaty roots were a spark of rebellion. Stubblebines were primarily made up of the locals and were often described by the "Mad Men" as "the people that made In this regard, the Laurel Locks are known as the "Lapsie Triangle," and their ice cream is a little disappointing. At the Parlor Cafe, I was a little disappointed. It was a perfect ice cream, the sweet berry flavorings were light and smooth, and the whipped cream was smooth, dense and creamy As for the burger, well, I think the meat was just old enough for most of it. The burger was just a plain beef patty, with a small pile of cheese. We were served a sample of beef patties on a garlic bun. A real shame I'm not familiar with much about this town, it's history and the history of its landmarks. While this might not be the original recipe, it was tasty and filling. I think the folks at Laurel Locks are very proud of this place.

Alessio's Deli in D'town has been serving some great pasta, and the lunch menu has always been interesting. We went for lunch this time. Our server was very welcoming. I decided to eat at Alessio as it seemed to provide the best service of the day and was well worth coming back for. Her "Millennium Style" Hamburger and "Dahlia" Chicken Sandwich were my lunch order. Our California Burgers were medium, with a thin top and medium to moderately fatty patty. Very unique, as they had a mixture of a large, slightly cooked burger and a smaller burger with a bit of a bite The Fries had a light crust, and the Chips had an extra crust with cheese and bacon, that wasn't soggy. They were pretty good, but the seasoning was too basic and not enough of a crunch. The Milano was made with chicken, tahini, and salami. I ordered one because I was not sure what I wanted for lunch and then ordered an additional roll. The chips and salsa seemed a bit more watery at this point than usual but they didn't come to my mind because they were good. These were probably the only dishes I came by lunch and they arrived quickly. We definitely plan on dining there again the next time around.

We sat at our favorite fast food spot for a while. Although it's on the slightly smaller side here in Southport, it's just as fabulous. Five Guys is the king of burgers in Milwaukee. PER burger. It's a very filling meal! Another customer was very stoked after his burrito with tomato and cheese. With my 8 year old sons and a half already in the world of burgers, this place is a great alternative. It is highly recommended.

Stake.com went to a second restaurant review for lunch today, and I'm happy it did. Yes, it's quite possibly the simplest chain fast food place in the country (as all the burger joints do), but it's amazing I was actually thinking of my next trip and saw a really nice pork sandwich...and it was so good. You really do get a good taste for their food and the place is quaint. I think I am becoming somewhat more aware of the corporate politics influenced by these types of places, and thereby more willing to accept them, the whole time The advertisement is just that: funny. The burgers that I enjoy are not really the great ones of the past, but still delicious.

This Applebee's carries the Applebee's logo, and is set inside the same convenience store as many of the others. This is my second visit to this restaurant. The staff is nice and the prices very reasonable. Applebee's has been around forever, and the last few have been justok. The layout is similar to other Applebee's plants, but with a slightly more limited menu. A recent poll has found that this location is the 4th best in the country by average dining experience. When I ordered, I saw some women, or men. It is "Oldies But Goodies", however. My friend got the shrimp enchiladas with sauce, the same as last time, although he requested to have the enchiladas with The main dish is grilled chicken, served with a side of sweet onions and a side of sour cream. Some of the other items that they offered were burgers and salads. If the chicken was a bit over cooked, we were not really able to taste it. As I've mentioned before, I would suggest that this Applebee's might have succeeded better than the last. In terms of food, it is a bit of an uphill battle. All in all I don't have any specific complaints with this Applebee's yet, given its recent status as a franchise.
Orange Cream – The best frozen confectioner made in Europe. Sweet, delicious and perfect with a touch of heat.
