I have been going to My Kitchen for years but this place is absolutely terrible. My Kitchen Chinois provides Chinese Take Out of the South side. My Kitchen is a chain. I ordered the bento burger and the fish. My Kitchen was open from 6:50 up until 7:00, with 5 tables and 2 kitchens. The place is busy, it smells of cooking oil, but it is really hard to eat. The food had some flavor, but most of it were fatty and salty or flavorless. The tuna was just hard to bite. I didn't like the bowl. A nice bit of steam was visible through the gaps between the fish shells. You just cannot afford the food there. Please consider giving this place a try instead.

Angelo's is the only restaurant I have ever been to, and it is one of my favorite Italian restaurants in Madison, WI. It is one of those very few restaurants in East Hampton that is welcoming and friendly. They feel familiar with their customers, and they always provide good food, and service. Angelo's makes a good dough pie (as compared to the other Pizza places in this area). Many staff are very professional and helpful, as was my server, Irene. My two little boys, and my husband went to Angelo's and enjoyed every possible dish that we chose. They have a deli-chic feel. We came with our son for dinner. We started with their pizza, a Minestone pizza. The tomato sauce and garlic sauce were excellent. The soup was made fresh by hand, using the traditional method, and then topped with pasta (mostly spaghetti) and hot sauce. There is a large bar area with large selections of drinks and apps. What was really interesting, was the taste of the chicken. He said, "It was rich, with a little pasta, and it was so good!" I was especially pleased with the sauce, which was very flavorful, and loaded with chicken and pasta, which are both good as well. The Minestone soup, was delicious as well. We topped it with a tangy, slightly creamy Alfredo sauce. It was quite flavorful. I went for a pizza, with an olive oil Alfredo sauce. Served with your choice of sides. All of the staff also had a strong opinion of their pizza. I usually prefer small pizzas with smaller toppings than the large, thick pizzas. And ranging from low to the top? So I am not saying my pizza isn't good, just that at the end of the day I prefer Italian style pizza. It was thick, but I was pleasantly surprised, by the abundance of cheese on the pizza. There was a bit of burnt crust on the bottom of the pizza, where the dough was creased toward the center and I cannot really see  I've now done a little experimenting to improve my pizzas and they are quite good. Also, I would have preferred the sauces to be a little sweeter. I have just received my first order from Angelo's pizza oven. Good thing too though, it was very tasty. Also, I will definitely make a reservation next time you go.

I did not plan on going to dinner, but due to a new restaurant I was curious what the menu offered. I assumed I would try the Rigatones Rigatones from Le Vie-Gatine. Although it is not "non solo pasta", it is a good choice to be served with a side of pasta and two small rolls to go with I arrived just before the restaurant opened so a waiter could check on me. At the moment, it was a quiet ghetto with only a couple of patrons. There was a low level of noise. There was also an additional serving tray next to the table. It contained a few greens mixed together, with some radishes, oregano, and some tomato. It was very good. Good. Unfortunately, the portion was small given the small size of the rolls as they were two small dishes. The seasoning on it was good, but not the dressing that made it. I ordered my first course. A small bowl of the Rigatoni Aglio Olio was also ready. Spinach was very soft, however. The pasta and spinach were relatively large as compared to the large rice bowls. The sauce consisted of a sauce of olive oil, butter, garlic, and a dash of lemon juice. I felt the dish was overdone, and could be improved on. The pasta was pretty ordinary. I am not sure what the reason was for the lacklusterness of the meal. There was an unreal presence to the table at the bottom of the bowl, like I did at The Kitchen in Chicago. I guess I felt I was waiting for a taste Test. Having been there before, I did not expect much. I also expected it would all be relatively well made, and I felt I had enough eatable options to finish it off, but they were not.

Cone Heads Ice Cream is open every day except Thursday. There is a sign on the wall of the shop, with the name in English. Most of the staff consists of older folks, who don't bring their kids with them. The bar is at the back of the bar area. So you have to wait until their window opens and enter the parking garage at the front door. A bigger area could be added, to reduce the noise and if needed, provide a place to dine at in the center. The front counter looks like an old school cone stand. I have to admit, I didn't want to spend more than $2.85 in ice cream. I felt they were tasty, but not worth the wait. There were 4 people that worked there, 2 of whom were managers. It took me 2 minutes to complete. What a difference. It does take a lot of time to place scoops, since their shop is in Paprika, PA, where this is the closest local  I don't really know the whole story, but they use imported ice cream, and they do have an excellent reputation. By not making its own product, Cone Heads doesn't have to worry about price. The pumpkin ice cream is more or less like my favorite sweet treat, though I'd compare it to a cherry ice cream, rather than an One very good cup of Peanut Butter Ripple. The taste was as basic as any ice cream cone, with a distinct orange flavor to it. It was a solid option. The price is cheap, but not too cheap.

One star here for not rushing to RR for an IPA, as it is in almost every place that has this item. Although they're not the best burger place in the city, they are pretty close to the food and theambiance. If you want a good, classic burger then 5 Guys is the place for you. The decor of the restaurant is a simple wooden sign, with an old-fashioned burger style. It will probably be your first choice for a burger, although I think the burgers are fairly strong. You also start with a menu of burgers, a selection of buns and sides, plenty of sauces and toppings. Especially for a restaurant that is so very often understaffed, they have a decent burger. A lot of them are a little greasy, but very good. The shakes are really awesome. This was the last time I eat there without the shakes. The wait time is also average (well below average - this is a neighborhood chain) so be prepared to be slightly disembarked.

Chee Chee is an excellent burger/fries combination in the heart of Mandalay Bay. It's located in Easton, and it's one of the smaller sister restaurants to Five Guys. The ingredients used are fresh, and not frozen. It is easy to find one, but isn't too convenient to buy. The pulled pork burger for me was good, although a little dry, with an excellent sauce and lots of meat. The burger turned out great. The fries did not stand out, but they were still  edible. They also come with side options such as hot dog buns, fried pickles, or a side of ketchup. These things at Chee Chee are certainly worth it for theburger cravings. Some people won't like the idea that they are feigning illness and eat a burger for free, but they do love the A couple of options here - cheeseburgers, pickles, sauce, French Fries, and sauce with ketchup - seemed to be It is certainly a different world, but I think it would be good to return if I could find a better place next time. And it is on the smaller side, and less upscale than 5 Guys. The best I have had at the restaurant is the "Baby Stool" because the burger is not only good, it's really good too A solid restaurant option for those in the area.

I was too hungry and just had to get something going. Came across CFA on the parking lot. Originally, there was only one lady in this place with three children in there to serve. The barista was super excited to see how things were going so loooooooong ago when the order took place, but when her friend was coming However, I had ordered a cup of the coffee, as well as a "spread" that consisted of iced coffee, plain Chik-Fil-A is owned and operated by McDonalds and does not even have their own drive thru in their parking lot. The sandwich was small, but delicious, and I could eat a lot without getting ill-affected by the fried food. I was disappointed that they would have to microwave all my previous orders, and that my portion would be smaller. The food didn't taste even close to as good as the Starbucks Coffee. I'll be looking for a better meal to eat at I suspect, because of the high prices and no Chik-Fil-A being The parking at Starbucks is better, and there are plenty of places to walk.

You think Vietnamese isn't a new thing, but it is in this neighborhood--Bawiyan House and Restaurant--and Just around the corner was a long time ago when the food was good at Pho Xe Lua. A lot of the dishes have meat, sauces, and ingredients that make the Thai food unique and original. Both the Pho Special (the main dish) and the Fish Bowl (which is a soup bowl). What is better is the fact that the staff is very friendly and happy to assist you. They are open till 10pm and are only open on weekends (unless you are on a Sunday or Monday) and Monday through Thurs. When the place is busy, you are very likely to notice the "french dishes" lying on the floors, and the servers at some point tos It isn't clean as a whistle in this situation. If you have the funds in the bank to come in and spend hours scouring the table area, it may be worth it, but a huge effort If you have never had good Vietnamese food, be careful; it is a ghetto. It's close, and my wife is not an ardent Buddhist. In hindsight, it wasn't all that stellar but it was tasty. The serving bowl used for the two bowls was different. As usual, the Pho Special got wayyyy too thick, and while we could still eat the bowls, we only ate half, The only major difference was in the broth. The Pho Special consisted of beef, chicken, vegetables and a handful of fish. I couldn't quite detect any Sauerkraut, or even any other type of fish, or any other ingredients. The meats were quite tender, but very flavorful. Later, the broth came to me, with the Bun Bo Hue ("Hun Bi"). The meat was finely chopped; not too oily or chewy, and the flavor had the traditional Vietnamese saltiness. Also added was chicken bouillon (I had to taste..my mouth felt watery). After the broth had been brought, we knew this would be too thick and could make it too soupy. It was very good in the end, though I believe more people should think about their order in order to choose the right soup for their taste. And, it came with an egg roll. It can be found in the little cornerhouse of the Bung Ta Mo (Viet Nam) on Race Street, at Lai Chung Ph It satisfies most Vietnamese tastes. The broth is lukewarm, but when you think about it, it's still very good.

Son had been camping in Newtown all morning and got up at 3 a.m., but didn't see anything open on the side of the He wants a short but sharp cut, so I made me look for a place close by when they were open. I was in a bad mood and had to put the child back in bed for a little bit and go to the bathroom. Son called to get a quote before I left to see if he'd been here, but since it was just me, I wasn't Son came in just after 6 pm, and was treated quite comfortably! The stylists are uniformed, and we were treated to some great service by their stylist as well. We walked around for a few minutes before we stopped by again to talk to my son. Son was very friendly, getting his hair ready to blow dry, and was a little nervous at first, but later, while he was getting ready to I didn't get a chance to ask questions of the workers, but it wasn't long before they were out in the parking lot, ready to His stylist cut the length and style and he had a great time. He asked us for his "tip". We left about an hour early, though, and came back on Thursday to pay. haircut (more expensive than the one he's received to date from the chain), I think he only paid $23 total for the haircut. I visited the Belmont Museum in Philadelphia over the summer of 2005 in October. Not many places in this city offer that degree of serenity, the level of feeling you gain when being close to a historic site. This is the best view in Philly, or anywhere. There's no better view in the city. Belmont..and a must see!

Went with some friends to a drive-by diner called Coal Fired Diner on 4th Street in downtown New York City. I thought that made it more upscale than I wanted mainly because I like to shop at cafes and restaurants, rather than at a diner. The interior was just spongy, and no real sense of order. So, I opted to dine in with my lunch and ordered something different, just to test it out without really trying it out. It was fast food, though it lacked the upscale appeal that I hoped for from a diner. It was Monday, and it was a Tuesday, so I paid just $7:30 for two slices of toast, a burger and a cup of The waitress said they knew the breakfast item wasn't open. For lunch, I had a plate of French toast with a side of coffee. We ordered my favorite breakfast, the simple French toast. This means, that the omelette isn't the regular panini that's traditionally served, so this was my first taste of it. I ordered the vanilla hen omelet, which was pretty good, too. But the eggs were no good. But I had no intention of squeezing it. As the waiter had told me, their burger is made with no eggs, but this is a burger made with egg. What's worse. I probably would have liked to have ordered one of the more interesting things on the menu, an egg Benedict, but was unable to bear to do so. I'm not sure I'd want to go back. I'll let you know what I get when I go back. Good to hear, I guess.

This is a nice little restaurant located in the middle of the community at 665 North Main Street, just off of I-515. While a good idea (and the service, especially from the friendly staff), I was actually disappointed with my food, which was served in a cold, For those of you who don't mind cold and winter (I would recommend that you bring a jacket). The chicken was moist with a nice thickness to it, but still had a nice sauce on top. The orange chicken was well marinated and slightly more crisp than I've ever found in the past (if there were more chicken than a little soft). The bok choy had the texture not just of a tai chi, but also of soup; although with the soup, it The Hot & Sour soup was not particularly flavorful and tasted like a frozen broth with little flavor. The Fried Rice had a nice bit of chew, and the sauce came out rather sweet. The Hot & Sour Soup was a bit on the thick side, but not a bad one.

I have to say that this is the best cheeseburger I have EVER had. I'm still trying to eat them all, but this was my new favorite. With Mother's Day being around the corner I decided to find a place to get some cheese. In the midst of a busy day, I came across Steve's. I walked in to the small little shop. The atmosphere was casual, clean and relaxing. One of the employees asked for the rolls, and when I turned the plate around, it wasn't the old thick paper. The order began rolling out in front of me and it was packed with tender sliced beef, onions, bell peppers, cheese, provolone and  It was huge.. I tried to chew each morsel with a plastic spoon, swishing every morsel that matched that would slip into my mouth I was not expecting any real meat, a thin meat coat, or crispiness. It certainly is not as good as I would imagine. Nonetheless we enjoyed our food and will return to Lai Lai Garden.

The restaurant is located in Canton, New Jersey (just north of Main) a block North of a corner of East Main, and St. Mount.It has a number of tables outside and inside and it is not far from nearby Subway Lines. All that stands in its way is that it is located on the eastern edge of the shopping mall, with parking available behind a door. The decor is very traditional Chinese but nice touches make up the small town decor. I ordered a chicken wing with rice and wonton soup. These are what you would expect from such a joint, which is also very similar to those on Broadway. The food was well-dried and had the consistency of old wonton soup. The chicken in this soup was very tender, but not very flavorful. It was very delicious, but nothing special enough to warrant the price. The Rice was served on a side plate, with a few extra pieces, topped with fried pork, egg, and the usual vegetables. The serving size of both dish was a cup, but it had more than enough for the 4 of us. You can order online in advance, and in the restaurant, you can order in or takeout. The only issue was that there are no takeout orders allowed, so the server had to wait a few minutes before I could have my food arrived. The food overall was good when they were doing the take-out.

I visited The New York Times's Food Network for lunch today. I had expected the restaurant to suffer. Besides the fact that the place is a little sad that they are losing the fun factor that started it all, the fact that the menu is still decent The restaurant remains in a somewhat crowded niche (see the review below about that time), but today, it's not an outstanding place for Chinoi For this reason, it didn't need to be changed entirely, something I found interesting. In fact, it's easier to find similar Chinese offerings that aren't much better elsewhere. At ducksauces, this does not make sense until you try it at home. The menu seems to have left a bit to be desired, though: it left me with very little to fend for myself. While it still got an amazing serving, it wasn't so good that I left hungry. The Chicken wings were really, really good, but too heavy and salty. It did fall short of the fresh ingredients and the sweet sauce. The Fried Rice was the highlight of the meal. The restaurant was also the last with all the traditional foods, although no new menu offerings emerged, so it was not my choice. But as always, I would return if I could. I will say it remains a very well run institution, but it makes very little sense to take a trip to it just to eat good Chinese food

Valley Square had a great idea for a shopping center. By allowing a retail center with a commercial area that focuses on service (like a grocery store, bar, restaurant, and pharmacy) they They believed that shopping malls, on the other hand, would create an overly busy downtown and it would make establishing commercial space more taxing than necessary Do not take these steps backward, they are an approach that will be successful. Asian House is located in a strip mall in Morristown, NJ. It takes the drive through to Iroquois Mall and then the turn towards Walgreens. The food was a bit pricey for what you get, and I found it to be somewhat of an experience. The counter has a large menu of Asian dishes, and quite a few unique items as well. There is even a "Vegetable Platter." I was expecting quite a bit of a mix-up, but got one of the Chicken Wontons, Fried Rice with Wonton soup, and The soup was disappointing. The beans were just fine. A bit undersauced, so I wasn't sure if the soup was meant to taste like beef soup. I asked for extra spicy and was offered no option. It had just enough salt for me to eat the rest, but too much salt, and you could not even feel the taste because there were still ble When I asked for special sauce to be added to the Chicken dish, the chef denied. In short, I'd say the Szechuan Chicken dish was subpar at best. The Wonton Soup was very good, and my mouth was just watering throughout the course. There are also some other Asian items on the menu that should serve well, namely fried chicken, a few dumplings, and some fresh vegetable I stayed for the service of a lovely Asian server, Mrs. Wang. She's very friendly, knowledgeable and helpful. She is a very nice person and seems to have much in common with a Chinese or American native.

Viet Thai is located between the city center and Penn Station on the corner of Green and St. James Avenues. It has a large, comfortable dining area with a wide table on one end, and a few tables on the other. The inside is very upscale, and it is not something that catches the attention of the casual traveler. The menu is quite extensive, spanning from Vietnamese to Thai to Chinese, with a few special ingredients. We had reservations at 5, and arrived at around 6, due to the large group. From the time we first moved here, we had no idea of the many options available along that broad river from San Diego. The dishes were both solid, and made us feel at home. We opted for two dishes: coconut tofu soup and summer rolls, both of which were spectacular, with nice presentation and fresh ingredients. Our bowl of soup consisted of a thick layer of coconut, tofu, and a few sliced, chopped dates. The sauce itself was mildly sweet, and the texture was very good. Summer Rolls had the texture of frozen vegetables, and had Thai seasoning tossed in, and served alongside the tofu. Both dishes were delicious, so much so that we came back the following day to add more to our menu. The salmon dish was a surprisingly solid serving, but it suffered a bit from a lack of flavor. It looked rather old, maybe because we took it home to cook, so it was not fresh enough to cook in the house. Lastly, I ordered the ice cream for dessert. The batter was very buttery, the whipped cream was rich, and the bananas were soft. I was quite hungry for the rest of the day, and was satiated by our experience. This place is still under construction, and we are trying to make plans to come back soon after.

Took a drive up from NJ to Washington, D.C., to a McDonald's. The location isn't exactly a star star. At least there were no other customers in sight. There was a small selection of hot dogs and cold sandwiches on display, ranging from $3.85 to $7.75. I said no.What would the other cost be? I felt that the one at the drive through was too long, and a third one was not going to give me full use of my Dollar Tree credit, I love a good burger, but I was on a budget, so I was willing to accept a dollar discount. The chicken was cooked fine, but needed some seasoning and fat reduction. With a little extra effort, I could have ate a few more burgers. Now it's me, if only I could remember just how many miles I'd lost at home when I ate a burger.

The Rosario family's pizza place opens on the west side of Mt. 385 in the back of a small town in southeast Pennsylvania. The couple still has a small operation, including the pizza oven still working in the family wood oven and the shop's long-gone antique signs. Many pies at Rosario's are original, a little thinly sliced by hand, wrapped in paper and hand-rolled in cardboard, made I went by to check out the store last summer, but could have been a little more snobbed. It was around noon when I visited, but as we were leaving that took some time to get from our car through the car park, to the restaurant...n They paused and then sighed as the waiters offered them a slice of pizza which seemed to evoke an old timesy feel. One of the kids called in for a hotdog with mustard and mustard-spiked ketchup, but then got a very bad cold and The dough was not hot, so I was surprised at the lack of crispness. This particular pizza was a medium and it was pretty flavorful. It wasn't like something I had expected, but certainly not too bad. In my old-fashioned ways, it was a nice time to eat out, especially while the burgers were hot and juicy (I usually do At Rosario, ingredients are fresh. Why do I like to eat the pizzas as I wait for dinner instead? As if that wasn't plenty, the place could easily easily grow on me, if only for your good sense and not the other way around. No one can be under a week without a full pizza. I loved the atmosphere. It's one of those rare places these days that you just can't leave it there. It was worth it.

The good news is that Indian Hut has a fine selection of Indian-type cooked dishes that all have a unique combination of spices. But fortunately it is far too commercially focused, and the food here is essentially quick eats and fast casual. There's not a lot of creativity here, but based on the reviews I read, Indian Hut is clearly an under-powered food establishment. I've been here several times and have tasted a lot of dishes dripping (or overflowing dripping) and it's My friend who had had the Hyderabadi Masala, whose flavor was not quite as overwhelming as he hoped, thought the curry was overly The chicken Korma had a subtle nutty tones, but wasn't as crisp as some of their other preparations. Although not bad, not great - moreover, the portions were quite small, and the portions are definitely enough to share. Although I've heard the Indian restaurants at Bensalem are decent enough, this is not one of them.

Dunkin' Donuts used to be my go-to for all that I ever needed! But since then, Dunkin has gone on an upswing. The old days are over. I've had a sedentary pasty and have really hated it. A new Dunkin opened in our neighborhood today and I think they were selling pretty gross hot dogs out of a bag. I was never able to get on any other side of the store as it was just a regular Dunkin-Bencher and a lack of But then I got a burrito from there. However, just as there were a few nice cafes around this city that offered better coffee and sweets, this one didn't. So it probably wasn't a bad idea for those who are starving for something to eat, but not for the ones who are not. I would be willing to bet that they felt that no others were too dissatisfied, so they kept me going, but really I did not

The Carvery was great. Great selection (and great value for your money). It was the only place in our area that still has their original cars, but it's still a good spot for lunch on an extended road trip. Very good service from our waiter in a suitably 1940's leather t-shirt. I had the ham and cheese sandwich, and the eggs and sausages with cheese and maple syrup were very good on an early morning. The breakfast was great. But one problem was that the syrup they used was all-purpose, so I had to use the non-organic sweetener on my omelet The cream was soft, but could have been even richer than the filling. The maple syrup was excellent though. My only complaint is some of the decor was dated, but the breakfast is still very popular.

The restaurant is tucked away in the small corner of the old town of Trenton and is easily accessible. It is located close to East Orange and within walking distance to the center of Trenton. We were seated quickly after booking a table on the patio. On our visit, we ordered, we were seated and our waiter asked where we would like to sit. And a 5-10 minutes of waiting between us. They have a large menu for seven courses in total, with a small selection of specials available. All the items were made in house for dinner. There are several delicious food options at Metro Grill each Saturday morning for lunch. The Thai Chili sauce was something a little unique with a bit of a peppers to it. The brussel sprouts were tender and moist with a fresh green olive seed. The chicken franchais was delicious, the sauces were solid as all were. The shrimp and pan-fried fish was good enough to pass up. We shared their filet with rice, beans and black beans and rice was very tasty. There was a special sauce special for their pork chop plate. It was tender and absorbed all the flavor, meat and seasonings just sitting there, waiting for you to get your fix. The meat was rather dry as the chef wanted to keep it as moist as it would be, although that was not one of the reasons we went for it The desserts were quite good. It went down in the fast food menu history as one of my favorite restaurants to eat in Trenton. The bar and atmosphere both fit the style of the restaurant and the atmosphere. I am very happy we tried it.

JBC&P Bread and Pastry Store No. 83 is at the corner of Main Ave. and 76th Street in Westfield. The old street signs were very clear, and they worked well until I didn't arrive at the location. This time I went into the small office building, but came out of the main entrance to find a sign warning there would be no open doors until 8PM They were offering free coffee and soft drinks, but the front window had a small section of glass that was blocked off by the other doors. I couldn't tell if I'd missed the door, or if I would actually get inside. The restaurant was located in a building a few blocks from the I-90 exit near I-90 N, but they had just been repainted The place smelled like a good bar, and everything was ordered in advance to be delivered out to the table shortly afterwards. I had no problem with any of the food, but I think that if they were that good at the other side of the parking lot, I might have The bagels were fresh and well-baked. The bagel was a pretty good size, about 1/4 inch thick, with about a inch of each side of the bagel. My girlfriend had a fresh cut deli with fresh tomatoes, onions, green onions, and a delicious chicken Caesar salad. The bread was very soft and I could taste the light nuttiness that would be typical for this restaurant. Very enjoyable experience I've had in a while. So, it was all very good - a wonderful casual dining experience in northern New Jersey - that all you need to do is order on the drive

I decided to take a trip to the newest Thai restaurant in Phuket. It isn't a "fusion" joint with Chinese on the menu, Korean, or other. It is not trying to be just like the "Idai" in the tourist department. Yes, it is all Thai, with a bit of Chinese and Chinese, but a touch of Americanized. The menu is traditional - traditional Thai house style - but with a modern twist with a couple touches of fusion. The restaurant serves good and fresh food, with a definite Bangkok approach. A good variety of Thai dishes. There is a small bar/lounge/sat area which serves an eclectic mix of fresh produce and some good bbqs. This one was a little less formal for lunch, but still more interesting than the more expensive dinner meals at similar restaurants around the area. For about $30 I got a fried shrimp bowl, a bowl of coconut soup, a bowl of panang curry, a bowl of chicken At the time this was a week in advance, so I chose the soup/salad item to try and see what I was missing. All were incredibly moist, fresh and flavorful. The dumplings did show signs of being made fresh, but not too much. They were tender, not too salty and the flavor is more of a Thai version of some Chinese dumplings. First bites of the coconut soup, which contained only carrot, Thai basil, and green onion. coconut soup. But, it was delicious. The chicken and hot bowl was the best. Its the entree: a chicken and hot chicken, served over rice. So, while I liked the dinner portion, this lunch I tried it, it was unmistakably Thai and great. The ambiance is very pleasant, and the service was very friendly. All I can say is that Lemon grass is deserving of four stars. This restaurant is worth a stop!

The decor at Pho Ben City is simple, modern on the outside, but on the inside. Inexpensive with reasonable food, but not nearly as good as Pho Palace. Its location is convenient and doesn’t take up much space. I went at lunchtime and the food was somewhat average. Food quality has been consistent, but the price is up a little from last visit. My pho arrived quickly, hot and fresh. There was a nice flavorful blend of meat and vegetables, with no seasoning. The broth was thick, but wasn’t thick enough to hold it together, so some of the liquid could have come off while adjusting to the temperature. There was a slightly bitter taste left from the basil. The rice noodles were slightly chewy and watery, and the noodle bowl was very salty. A good beer selection as well. I was fairly impressed with all of the dishes. Some people like the use of less MSG and added salt on their main dishes. There are few places to find Vietnamese cuisine to this quality, not to mention a relatively small portion, which is only a minor drawback. I would suggest that you try this place for some good pho.

The first round of doughnuts I had at Dunkin' Donuts at the San Juan Center got me thinking about the days when they were served like The donut bin was completely open, the plastic lids were hanging off, and little more than the one bag of peanuts kept laying there. Unfortunately, it took a couple of minutes for the clerk to clear up everything on his desk before we were to be seated and sat down. We stood outside looking at the dugup shop, waiting for it to clear with the help of the restaurant's helper. We moved onto the corner and asked the waiter for directions to get to the bathroom. The manager was absent-minded around with most of the rest of our group who wanted the food and the drink to be good as new. He needed to clean a little while because his apron was soaked and stains came from his floppy hat and other items. The other patron was in a hurry and came through a short line: "You got this place just yesterday from the pizza school." To be fair, the staff was friendly enough, but clearly had to do a bit more work than normal. If you can avoid it, though, please keep it clean. Regardless of the fact that the shop was dirty, it was pretty odd to be standing a couple of hundred feet away from the place. Yes, well..

The restaurant is located on Park Drive, about 15 minutes away from the theater that plays the theater. In June, the owner bought the operation in 2005, and he has continued to expand the pizza menu. The menu has a wide variety ranging from plain. The interior was well stocked with the basics, including pizza sauces, crusts and sauces. I saw them there over at Pizza Express, but not very impressed. As for pizza, they do a lot of the same stuff at different prices, but nothing special. Food was fine, and the prices are fair. It has a small open space, the same size as the rest of the restaurant. I usually don't go for deep fried pizza, but here a slice on a plate was seasoned nicely, covered with heavy melted mozzarella The crust needed a touch of chew, so we asked as the toppings were covered in copious melted mozzarella. The sauce was a thick consistency with about a few drops of olive oil poured ontop of melted mozzarella, which was not necessary. The cheese was melted with excessive amount of margarine. The crust was thick and thick, absorbed the sauce and cheese thoroughly enough, but not enough sauce on top of it to give it a real depth. So I asked them to give it a sprinkle of squeezable Parmesan, adding a little extra olive oil and a thin layer However, the pizza had a nice crust and the sauce was good, but not enough to make it stand out. This morning we had a burger, and another one of dinner: a nightshade. The ingredients were ok, but I don't remember how it appeared. A tad undercooked, I could taste the ricotta. We also ordered a burger. It was cooked wrong in the grill and left some of the meat dripping off. The mushroom was salty, but nothing else stood out. The beef flavor was very heavy, hard, and flavorless, which I really don't think a burger would be better served under a grill The burger on top was well done and still had a nice sauce side, although I thought this was rather overdone. We will not be going back. I'm a fan of Italian restaurants in this area, and certainly wish any of the restaurant owners more success there.

"Mentioned a customer called, said he needed his vehicle sanded." As a customer I found out i was going to be the first to report this particular auto wash. If you drive in, you will be met by a person who claims to have a full service workshop at the office. There are many problems in the restaurant, and in their attitudes. The Newtown cleaners occupy a large space with space for their work and a wide grin on the face for all the other people in the Their new shop is very fresh, clean and organized with a big selection of specialty items made by well-known local growers, and also offers a The move was a good move for the shop, although it is not the new shopping center it is the commercial building that will benefit from the growth of the While I don't know about their actual products, they are very much a small family business. With the new space, the entire staff there is better trained in the field, and this was not one of the better dryers at Newtown. They are great and are great people. Their coffee is not only quaint, but delicious. My husband and I often go here for breakfast, or anytime after, and I think the coffee and food is the best in town. The fact that I've stayed here for more than a year, makes me very happy.

Some people know that I've been to the South Asian barber's shop in Beijing and have never gotten to experience the style there. YAAAAAAAYAAAAAAAAAH! In the end I went with Lao po to get a cut at the salon I frequent at home, as I would often do. From the beginning, it was a casual-looking salon. The dining room is large, with ample open space to accommodate an extended dining table of 14+ with a small menu. It is always busy and their servers are always doing the cooking but I can't picture my self as a non-Chinese in-the- I came from the surrounding area, having worked in the area for nearly a decade. On my way to the table, a worker approached and said, "Come take a seat." Their menu is usually a mix of the classic American fare and a variety of American dishes. I was excited to be in the restaurant, having been on a culinary trip around the region for several years. The food is tasty, sized just right, with enough food to satisfy a large family. One afternoon, I was looking for something more light and smoky, I asked for a tray of potatoes, tomato, onion and spinach with I ordered the Greek Salad & Greek Rye, paired with fresh tomatoes, onion and spinach pieces. It was a smooth and moist dish, well balanced between the thinly sliced turkey and potatoes, laying down a little crust. The hot cheese rub made you want to dip it in oil, but just wasn't enough to do it. My favorite part was the toasted cinnamon bread and the melon (the fruit was on a small tray, along with four sundried tomatoes After finishing the meal, I noticed a splotchy white swab of pasta covered with goop which had not been cooked The menu was out of date, the portion sizes were tiny and not in proportion to the portion size it represented. I had a couple of problems with the facility as a whole. I ordered a glass of wine, which came with a sweet tangy sauce.

This was my first trip to Calebs Cafe, in downtown Sarasota. The dining area was packed with people inside, and the decor consisted of a simple wooden railing between the doors and outside. The patio looks out across the street to the untamed Atlantic Ocean, and there was always a beautiful breeze blowing in. Their menu has a mix of modern and classic items in a small and cozy atmosphere. The outdoor terrace with the covered patio deck was a perfect place for a quiet a quiet late lunch or early dinner. Immediately, the aroma of fresh eggs was laden up the kitchen, with a menu that looks at the kitchen with pride. The menu choices included some of the freshest egg dishes I have ever tried. The menu's bread selection was fresh and the items were made from local ingredients. This was one of the many signature dishes I ordered. With a side of my favourite fried home fries (choppers), extra crisply seasoned and sweetened with a few tangy spices So I had no idea what was under the wrap. So did the sausage. Because the brioche roll was so soft and easy to bind together, and it didn't take a lot to get each piece as far We ordered the side of fried chicken that was served on the side, and after reading reviews, I decided it would only fit on the roll, and would One of the links was rotten and was steamed scumm in the middle of my mouth. As mentioned earlier, the sandwich was absolutely excellent. The egg was tender and perfectly cooked, the bread perfectly soft and soft, and the sausage was delicious. The crisp, hot white eggs were tender, bursting with seasoning, and the fresh bacon added a great crunch. The potatoes were a treat of the best. Caleb's used to make a wonderful salad, and when I heard of their new dressing a decade ago it was perfect indeed! One never knows what would be in it if this served as a breakfast. Caleb also baked these potatoes, and they were a perfect addition to the breakfast. Yes, I'll be back. It was a great lunch on the outskirts of downtown Charlotte and I am looking forward to many more great bites from this new coffee house in the

I was lucky enough to hit up Avria while visiting our daughter and she loved Kuchkovskaya. The decor is a bit traditional, featuring wooden tables and a glass pan-salad with a side of fresh baked bread and fruit. Each of these ingredients has been handmade and incorporated with various herbs and spices, and this was a treat I had never experienced before. It was a thin, flaky omelet and had the texture of ham and tomatoes served with an egg; the omelet had a This was another excellent preparation so fresh and tender you would think it had been a steamed fish - but I still had a taste for it The tomato was perfectly cooked and the feta cheese justmelted right on the top. It was excellent before I moved onto the ricotta quiche on the side with the cheese and wine. When I went in for more it was hot. I ordered the Fried Chicken with Mushroom. I opted for extra chocolate ice cream while I shared the cheesecake. We decided that we would make another round using the next dish, the risotto. I would also say you must try the food. I would recommend this place to the best of my friends and family.

I am a rerunt aficionado of Mexican food, so I was very nervous that I would be disappointed there. I visited Don Chile after visiting The Oyster (and nearby Delft's Don Jose) for a few days, on a Sunday afternoon The restaurant is very well decorated with an attractive Mexican flag on the front wall. So, I ordered at our house, got to the counter while the guys were serving, and then found the girl behind the counter, whose name was also She had plenty of room for me and even gave me a place to eat. The chicken was tender, just enough heat to keep me full and the whole thing was very flavorful. I ate all of the chicken cheese flautas, with chicken in a tortilla surrounded by grilled chicken on a bun. They had great acrid smoke flavor. I wasn't much for the guacamole, but it was a nice and creamy choice. Tacos al Pastor were equally delicious, topped with guacamole, lettuce, tomato and rancho, not overly oily and A big smile on my face. But they were perfectly done and tasted wonderful. The tortillas were cooked to perfect doneness, the meat tender and moist. The beans were tender and silky while the rice tasted like your favorite Mexican stew. I left the restaurant feeling satisfied as the meat was tender and delicious, and the vegetables and beans were moist and vibrant. All despite the somewhat salty taste of the food, which I thought was a touch too salty, that we would eat here again. Don Chile won a 5 star rating from CRI, and I will return. You won't be disappointed.

Einstein says, "A man whose brain has been expanded to the extent of creating an idea cannot understand his mind. The coffee shops and tea shops in Ctown are everywhere. Not since the 1990s have bubble tea shops really been popular, and as a beer drinker, I'm not surprised. Many of these outlets are run by the same owners, with Vivi being one of the better examples. There aren't many that still seem to have anything for me, but I must admit that I've largely resisted the urge to drink Vivi offers a fusion of bobba, sangria, and sweet teas. Vivi is open Tuesday to Saturday at 7am. The staff is friendly and helpful and the prices are somewhat reasonable. One of the owners is bringing all the tea out. I had to pay by cash instead of credit. This was quite good. The tea was inexpensive for a tea'snack'. My favourite part of the drink is the tangy and slightly nutty bite. Other good options include kabobs, tea-eggs, hot cocoa, and hot and sour vanilla mochi. Good. $8.30 for a plate of wings.

Keystone is a small bar-type fast food location just off Market Street between the corner and New Hampshire Ave. I visited for my first meal of the Some of the items are on the freezer, but that's all that matters. In my view, it's a fun little place to come for a quick coffee while you wait for your meal. You can have a bagel on any of the three options, and the toppings you choose were extremely good. Some of the bagels are a little soft inside. Or, as I have suggested to my sister, it didn't have any kind of coating, which is very fine if you want a bagel But I was pleased with the quality of the ingredients (in particular the onions). They're also a bit expensive too. The creamies, which are made with 2% cream, are reportedly made with 2% milk. The milk looks like plain boiled water. It would also have been nice if the location had more milk options, as it offered more options than the regular coffee options. The sandwich is small, but it's an excellent way to start the day. It was a pleasant experience, but no one was actually making a cup of coffee at the counter.

Shagun Palace is a small dining experience that is a little off the beaten path and quite a ways from downtown. Shagun is one of the oldest and most prominent Indian takeout centers in the area. The menu is pretty standard, without a definite twist. But the problem with the restaurant is that the restaurant lacks the proper bread that makes the food come out perfectly. We chose chicken since I had been a fan of chicken at restaurants, so I thought it was worth sampling. The vegetable samosa and baingan bartha also came out good and tasty, although the spice level and texture were slightly off. The garlic bread was excellent. No garlic was made tasteful, which wasn't at all an issue. We finished up with the korma and chicken bbq of the day, which was very enjoyable. One could only be certain that Shagun has a tandoor and a back oven with a large rack. The menu is extensive with specialties that are not available elsewhere. The food is very well prepared with attention to detail, and is very flavorful. I think they could do more to improve this aspect of food preparation. If they don't do so, it's time to get serious about making their food better.

The landscape of Lorimer Park contains numerous landmarks and sites influenced by the life and work of a renowned poet, Richard L. Lori It is operated by the Pennsylvania Park Commission and is a family owned park. Lorimer Park and the rest of Lorimer, as well as the adjacent Parkview Community Center, are located on the same block. The trail continues across the park via Laurel Hill Avenue through oak and oak meadow on its way to Laurel Hill Marsh (the most beautiful The trees are well-maintained, almost all have a color distinct from those along the creek, and the river valley is fairly undulating due to A short bike path ties us in with this park for both walks and biking. Upon entering this historic park you are greeted by beautiful hardwood trees with a historic marker reading about the pioneers of the Pennsylvania National Guard. There is a new wave of independent coffee houses emerging in New Jersey, and the area appears to be overrun with them. One of the only independent cafe houses I frequent, and the local treasure, is Rojo. This is a small, full service coffee shop, with three employees, and about 20 tables. In my experience, customers like everything there. There are also a full bar and very large counter, so its no surprise that there are regulars. It is a robust taste, and the coffee itself is very strong. Their menu seems a little limited at times, but they are the best I've ever had, and most of the java I try, I have The people who work at Rojo are from a large group of farmers in Eastern Pennsylvania. Neither the other houses nor their food are nearly as good. The same blend of beans with different blends, or the same roasted brew and roasting process. It is also strong when you go from iced tea to a light chocolate-treme. The best thing is, when you check out any of the other coffee houses in the area, they all offer Rojo as their coffee source. But Rojo is still a pretty good company. Unlike Rojo, their selection is dominated by the local or regional brands. The best coffee houses are good only a few miles from Rojo. It is an even nuttier selection, and an excellent value, even if it is slightly less robust than some places. It is a place for lovers of fine coffee and good food. Their coffee cake is one of the best I’ve ever tasted. No comparison with the quality and freshness. There are even pastries on the menu, and good breads and rolls by other local bakeries. Buying a good cup of coffee may not be hard. The Rojo Coffee Company is a nice place to sample your coffees.

A generation living in a big city in Korea, that is absorbed by the local Korean culture, from one generation of Korean parents (I think) living More change.More time. More Integration..more mobility. The Uzbek language is English, and in Ukraine it is Urdu. More Expansion. The menu consisted of mostly traditional Korean fare and a lot of Chinese dishes. We ordered the hot, oily borscht, potato salad, pierogi (made for my grandmother from the city if you remember me) So much food, so little time. The Pierogi was more like a bowl of mashed potatoes and a handful of meat with a few slivered, crink Not incredibly sweet though; the meat in the pierogi had an excellent flavor combination, with tender beef chunks and lots of onions and mushrooms added to They turned out as good as my grandmother's, but I was sad to see the potatoes go cold. While the borscht was quite flavorful and fresh, it didn't have the rich, creamy sauce you imagine in a Ukrainian borsch Like a thick and hearty soup. This is a definite hit. The kimchee was light, tangy and flavorful, mainly made from ground chicken, tomato and beef, and served with a fresh It was a spicy pressed kimchee with a cream sauce and a little spicy sauce. A unique experience with some very special food from a family who has adapted into New York City and whose kitchen is a must on the list of I've never before ventured into a kabob meal in a restaurant. Very interesting food..but a little strange. Here and here.. There is no way one can go wrong with a full plate of culinary surprises. Not sure if its their version of the Chicago pierogi, but I was certainly not disappointed. Somewhere, between this menu and the menus across the street is a chinese restaurant with an interesting menu of Korean/Uzbek

You can order the restaurant's food in bulk, and you can pay by credit card. Taste King provides authentic Chinese/American foods from Hong Kong and Vietnam, and it is in a wonderful old house across the street from the University. It's a few blocks away from my hotel, and is near the top of the Buena Vista high school and the Bustleton City library But its mainstay is the chef and his family, whose sons are a successful businessmen. The restaurant is a quaint piece of home decor, with a small, cozy dining room. In fact, there is just about everything I've ever wanted to eat. You pay cash at the staffed counter, and they will prepare your food immediately next to a spit burner that has been turned on to high. Done.As you would expect, your platter takes about several minutes to get down from the shuffleboard. A meal or two. Our food had three main plates (we had two meals). We ordered a bowl of hot & sour soup, two bowls of chicken corn and a bowl of white rice along with some very good The chicken was Grandpa Chicken, and my wife tried the wonton wonton! It was very quick; the chicken was cooked through and moist - not that I feel very confident of the chicken – and although the texture was good In fact, we had only a couple bites and were able to easily share. The rice was not soggy, but it was hot in the center. The noodles and wonton was too hot, and was even more so with one of the noodles soaked in sauce. The chicken corn soup was excellent. We found the wonton soup a bit too flavorless, so we opted for the duck sauce sauce and a dipping sauce. In the end though, it was a pretty good chicken bowl. The rice was good, if wilted more. It ended up having a lot of bones and gristly meat, which would have been quite enjoyable had the chicken been cooked with a thicker sauce We shared the bowl of white rice with another couple while we both shared a bowl of soup and chicken. The server was pleasant (if a bit unnerving). It's not an ideal experience to go to this place, but if you have a chance, give it a shot. The servers were cheerful, courteous and helpful. It's likely that the chef will be more hospitable if he had something more innovative on the menu. We ended up giving the restaurant one star instead.

We had a wonderful time chatting with the guest menu manager, who was very friendly and very knowledgeable in the area. All in all, all the beers were great and the waitress was very nice. My husband and I shared a small portion of bread of brussel sprouts, a delicious baked baguette and a large beer cup of You can find the Washington House at 2945 Union Avenue in Sellersville, Pennsylvania.
