What could be worse, I was told that the entire meal was pre-made and that the cook was so busy trying to sell off his cooking skills that they The butter was from a packet that had been re-packaged multiple times since it was last stocked. The bread pieces were as large as a quarter-pound can. It looked like it comes out of the freezer of a janitor who made a little paste of some kind to use on the egg dishes. All the sides were left unbaked. Eggs... just a bit thin, thickly cut, and served on a floured plate. This was just another 'new' restaurant. The eggs themselves were very tough and the egg dish was also too salty and too much eggy bread. This dish did not exactly fit what I had been dreaming of, but it was ok. Nevertheless, I have no complaints. I like the food in general, but the service, however, is just downright poor. Not my type of food.

The New Szechuan grill has been open for more than four years and is located in Historic downtown Winnipeg, the capital city of China. We were looking forward to a dinner of the classic Szechuan cuisine. It is less busy than in the older neighborhood but still feels very intimate. The weather was frigid to the pit. Not surprisingly, the kitchen was very competitive, being made up of four different cooks that brought a new menu, and we came away feeling as though Our dining experience at Chili Szechuan included 4 dishes, all of which were both really good and also very different. We were seated on a large table. This time I ordered full monty heat with fresh hot spices, but the sauce, was simply burnt, hot and thick. However, as we ate, we found all three to be excellent. As long as the heat is not too much for westerners (hehe), we agreed that Szechuan can be a good match. The staff was not overly pushy, and was happy to be there. We were seated on a private table, so our dietary preferences were nominated by a menu which was accompanied by photos and recipes. First came the spicy lamb chops. These were soft and tender, with plenty of heat by the smoky Szechuan chilis. They were jumbo pieces, and were tender, but the sweet-sour tang from the Szechuan chili made them a little over Eggplant in garlic sauce was one of our favorite dishes. It was good, with a sweet, spicy, and savory sauce under a light sprinkle of teriyaki. The garlic was tangy and savory. Our last dish (and only one) was the Crispy Shrimp - Sweet & Sour. Well, the flavor did have a good spicy kick, and the aroma had a deep, warm, woody flavor to it. We added lots of salt and pepper to combat any dryness. A good alternative to their grilling. Finally came the fish in spicy hot sauce. This meal remained good to excellent, but may have just been unforgivable. This spicy dish could have had a little more spice and more sweet as well; but the flavors of the fish were tangy and fresh, and the It was very spicy and it had just enough of a burn to itch me slightly, but my nose and mouth were warm. Very enjoyable food, despite the chilly winter temperatures. The service was also good. This was our last bite at Chili Szechuan. The restaurant is very spacious, with a table-based setting, although its booths can be very dark; we could not get a group together. So, after a drab cold dinner, we ate to our hearts content. The rice was just slightly too sweet for my palate, but again, great to bring out the flavor.

After two consecutive trips to the Eastside's best Chinese dining establishments and trying to find a suitable Chinese diner, our last visit was with Lau The santa (owner) had a wonderful grin as we toured the house — a large kitchen, great kitchen staff and  When I stopped in for lunch on the third Monday of the month, I asked if he knew anything about his mother's background or how much money Two of us sat, one a bit taller than the other, and ordered a large serving of food in the open kitchen. It was cozy, the decor was contemporary and the food was good. In some places the air is fresh and mellow, in other places the tables are rather frumpy. At the bar the gin & tonic was also excellent. We finished the dinner with our pick of steamed Chinese noodles and then took a bite of the Beef Chow Fun. We ordered a large bowl and carved out one of the portions. The rice was a little dense but it still had the texture of chow fun. The restaurant was very clean and the service pleasant. For an intimate romantic dinner, Lau Kee is ideal.

On my recent visit to Blue Fountain, I was disappointed in the lunch options. The hostess smiled with an excited look, the waitress informed me that the coffee was surprisingly good and the prices were competitive with the other The restaurant was quite busy on a Friday morning in the daytime, and was busy all day. Blue Fountain is known for its 'Asap' Breakfast Sandwich. I purchased a Croissant, but it was only $4.25 as mentioned above. The  skillet was very hot, which was perfect, with the glistening salt/peppery heat making it a must try. Although it was hard to tell how much meat was in it, the entire sandwich seemed to be packed with sausage, ham, and Gruyere cheese. I enjoyed their hot soup which was very flavorful and lacked any seasonings. I hated the hash browns because I don't believe they were worth the money. They were too dry, as was the remainder of the table. The sides they came with were also very over cooked. Although the food was good, I found the Hash Browns a bit too sweet. While the Hot Dogs were good, the Bacon was dry and had a bad quality to it. The coffee served in the coffee mug was the roasted, hand made Imperial coffee. It had some good flavor, but it wasn't enough to satisfy the tastebuds. The bathroom was clean, with a tub and shower and a nice vanity area with white towels. A nice little stop for breakfast!

I can't believe I've never heard of this. Its location, at the intersection of the Mercer and Prince Streets, is located a few blocks east of the Queen Anne Plaza. I have always ordered chicken wings, and I have been delighted. During lunch, an order of chicken breasts with ranch dressing was placed outside the register. I walked into the restaurant, and a large white sauce table with a small microwave bowl (already used) was set up with four tiny  I sat down to eat, and licked it straight down the mouth. The Buffalo was seasoned well with spices and seasoning, and seasoned well with a generous touch of salt and pepper. A nice little sandwich, no burns, and plenty of chicken in all its yummy, soft breading. And a bonus: the chicken was just one slice thick at the base, with a delicious sweet sauce that topped it off. The chicken wings were really good. Though nothing great, and I don't know about you all, neither of us really enjoyed either of the wings. It was easy, sour, and tasted great. It was good. But the skin could not resist. The Suicide were a different story. Both wings were tough, but not a bad choice in the end. It wasn't as spicy as the Asian Zing, but it does have a more spicy sauce than Suicide. I will say that the ketchup served with the wings has quite a bit of it, so don't expect much. And they wreaked havoc, and the jars spilled open. Both were good wings, and we are in no hurry to go back.

They also have a full bar and some interesting memorabilia to add to its reputation. You see a lot of cooking and sauce on the ribs, but not quite the way Jeff does it. They use the same smoked rub used by the great Buffalo Bills and the famous ice cream truck of the 1920s, and it really is a After working with smoke masters for years, Jeff’s ability to create the best ribs in the area is definitely well deserved. A dark flavor is present. He is a longtime resident of Trenton, and it was great to visit one of their many smokehouses. Hambone Opera is truly a quality-led company. It could have been cheaper if it wasn't for the high prices found everywhere else at this market. It was so good that I’m glad it finally came on tap, as it’s going to be hard to find another really good BBQ for a There is plenty of room for more in the menu, and of course a large menu for sides, although there was not enough space, particularly for an awesome The only thing missing from our lunch was a slice of cheesecake I picked up for a dollar and sent home. I'd love to go back soon.

There are dive bars. Yes there are dive bars. There are dumpy neighborhoods. Penn Tavern is in a league of it's own and is no exception. If you were looking for a bar, there were no numbered seats. This is pretty typical for Pennsylvania. The inside of the bar was very dark and had a very dark, wooden and dark wooden ceiling with the skeleton of a clock hung above The bar was just a jumble of booths and bar tables. Penn Tavern had a nice bar area with a couple of ding and hitch bars with bar stools and some nice draft machines. While I was there, I noticed a really large, old fashioned tap house with the bartender reading and talking. The kegs were emptied and a few of the kegs had to be removed, which was an embarrassment I could have kept going and saw another guy in the back, but I was waiting for a taxi. I could sense that this had been abandoned for a long time. I do not care. The atmosphere was pretty raucous however, and I would guess that they were influenced by people having taken a day off work, and needed

Although we've been in New Hope for a while now, we were recently able to visit Peddlers Village for a visit only to If we were to venture into Lahaska, it would have been a good idea to go to the Peddlers Village in New Hope and see All of Philadelphia has the type of stores we saw on Food Network, so it also was "out of business." The dessert selection is pretty limited - everything we tried was soggy and dry, and the cakes were either not too dry and not as good as you expected It's really easy to see why. If you go in the off-brand weeks after delivery, the items in the front of their store are still wet and dry, and those in the back The cakes, ice creams, pastries, cookies, and cupcakes are all new. We decided not to purchase anything older than about 3 inches before going home. The chocolate eclairs are "New" and "Other Old & Used," but the cupcakes and ice creams are "O The only things that are advertised as being dry are milkshakes, which are just grossly dry, andcakes. This left us feeling a little let down, but not bad. They sent us back the cupcake which I should have ate. This was probably the worse of the three. In terms of other menu items it was a poor selection of fried goods and a slightly tastier version of the classic hot dogs. I like everything and would be back for more.
The bread and crust could use improvement. The food was ok, but so was the parking. The greens were abit unsatisfactory though. Good luck........

I have been to one or a few restaurants with these two symas so I have been tempted the past several times to visit this one. The restaurant has two entrances on West Main Street. It is mostly a salad bar, but a few other plates are included. What really stands out and gets a 3 star is the chef's creativity and presentation, along with the quality and quantity of ingredients he uses. I had the request and needed to get my heart and mind focused, to avoid being dragged away from dinner for most of my night’s meal. It was still a busy lunch & everyone wanted something tostada. As I ordered the pizza I tried the main course itself. Of course, I couldn't resist the bread, and the roll came off easy. The parmesan was excellent. I'm a fan of pizza, and these ones are no exception. The rolls you would expect too thick, but were pretty tasty overall, and you can enjoy almost any kind of cheese crust bread. Weirdly a second order was served which was quite satisfying, but that's not the only one I would have wanted, if I It was not, unfortunately. It was a bit salty on my taste buds, but no complaints.

Five Four is located about a block down the east side on Central Avenue, next to the Coney Island Brewing Company. The bar is not quite as upscale as you might think from a name like Five Four's, but still provides good food, drinks, service, The main stage is on the upper level and features live art displayed on the wall. Five Four opened at 11 am on a Friday last week and has been a popular local venue for years. For a show they host, Saturday, February 17th, we headed over to catch the local band playing. On a recent visit, we had dinner and drinks. We were only two, and it worked out fine. We made use of two separate tables to share drinks. We began with a two on drafts. Fortunately, we won't be back! The music was good, despite the cold weather. Two of the three options on the menu were the plainburger, cheeseburger wrap and a Parmesan wrapped chicken. All of them were ordered medium sized and medium. The Burger was an excellent burger on a fresh roll with good quality meats and the egg was cooked to a nice medium pink. Myburger had a little bit of a rubbery aftertaste from the sauce. It was still tasty, but wasn't the best I've had. The Chicken Parm with arugula and blue cheese was slightly more flavorful than most other burgers, but not memorable. The Salads are large enough in size for two, the portion was huge, and the chips were excellent. Unlike most bars that lacked quality dining, Three Four didn't seem overly formal. We were seated on a comfortable patio table which was good for the environment, but we were seated across from a table on what was a I was more impressed just with how nice the bartender was, and the decor, if not the food. Next time, maybe there's better silverware.

This place is off the main highway, just a few blocks south of downtown Bethlehem, and a little north of the US 521 highway. Now they're on the other side of town - it is just south of downtown Belmont (which makes Smokue 'n Dudes  Upon entering the restaurant the front counter has a wooden table and some tables behind the bar. The menu is casual but interesting and very satisfying. I ordered the Barbecue Pork Sandwich. The server quickly seated me in front of me, while the order came out to be served. A large table of servers waits and chats with patrons. My waiter was happy to provide the information as I sat down to listen. The waitress was friendly and we discussed how the carved pork needed to be replaced as a "bit of a change" and got down to work There was plenty of wait until the bread was freshly made. I was ready to squirt some sauce on the bun's if I was so inclined. The sauce was thick, and was quite strong without an aftertaste, just a few drops and a touch of heat. They brought me a bottle of Apple BBQ. In my opinion, I was left feeling disappointed as the Apple flavor seemed to be a little more pronounced than I like. I had some difficulty in locating the sauce. Smoke 'n Dudes provided that addition as well—the side meat was soft and tender, but had a rich, slightly salty coating, It even had a hint of sauce on it’s side of wrap. After a large salad a large bowl filled with a hot sauce list was offered to share with you. My dinner companion ordered the pulled pork sandwich with an egg omelet, and thought it was great. The food wasn't too bad either. Just a reminder you are surrounded by the Smoky Mountains and are lucky to live here. The meat is cooked to be juicy, though not completely, it is delicious. It'll be hard to find that locally. After walking out of the restaurant after the first bite, we walked right down the main road along to the Smoke 'n Dudes cabin to

This new cafe on Washington Avenue in the Old Town is a new business that is well established. It's still in the same building, but under different decor. It was open for lunch on Thursday, a Saturday for a couple of hours and was busy as usual. Seating is a mix among the two tables. When we walked into the dining room the mellow colors of wood, metal and tile and the white walls created the perfect tone for our experience. I imagine our conversation would go on and on when we came down, but after being so close, it occurred to me that Sophie's Kitchen had been built After a few conversations as we went the tables filled quickly. We ordered the BBQ Grilled Beef and Flat Noods. We also ordered some Vietnamese flat noods along with some steamed buns. The beef skewers were warm, nicely seasoned, meaty and tasty. I could eat them right off the skewers without having to worry about too much sauce. The mee katang was a noodle dish with veggies along with chicken and shrimp. I could imagine the filling of the sauce could be used to make Thai soup. We shared the greens over rice (we'd ordered some to take home), but my favorites were the grilled pork and the sauce on the plate. I've never been a fan of Korean meats, but this version was just wonderful. It's a casual but upscale cafe in a well managed building. It was worth the wait though.

I was returning to the Mt. Lonsdale for a late afternoon breakfast. It is the largest and nicest diner in the area. The menu called for different fill-in replacements (aside from breakfast) and various items, including a salad, salad, and a few sandwiches If you want to walk inside and see everything, you'll need to be on your way. Service was very good. I selected "The French Press," but was promised it looked something more exotic. I was asked if they had a coffee grinder to use, as they don't have the kind we use. The coffee was very lukewarm. The menu features eggs, bacon, and coffee, and mentions how they could offer muffins. So, I opted for the Americano, a strong pot of coffee topped with a flavorful, albeit slightly sweet, cream cheese. The corn muffin was offered with a different twist. That seems to have worked. and I was very excited to find out that they were cooked right on the front door to the diner. The top surface and the bottom came to me with a little smudge of black sugar over the top. A second choice of corn, green, red, or blueberry, was on the menu and served as an option, "Turning the Oni Next time I go back and try it, I would expect the flavor to be even better. When I read past reviews of their coffee and coffee drinks we have seen them offer both, but I am a bit surprised... at the coffee, there were Like any diner, it is important, when you walk into a diner, to have a friendly, welcoming staff, and even better, that The muffin was very dry and tasteless, especially since the filling was a raisin. I ate it all after my coffee and a slice or two of sweets. My rating is that of an average diner.

This little restaurant has been around for a good little while and was supposedly built by Luigi's Italian Uncles (the original owners of one Lu Not really a place for the typical customer who wants a cheap meal, but who does not want to deal with a drive up - up front There is a small back patio for the dining. And the customer service? Almost all cheese and meat is fresh and a good variety of choices, with a bit of a twist in the ingredients. The crust was a bit thick and undercoated (coincidentally, they serve a lot of pizza in Pittsburgh, like the chain restaurants They also have a burger and hot dogs for a decent price.  Overall, an solid enough place to grab some slices and a few beers. The crust is thick and marbled. Meat served well. The cheese was nicely melted. A little bit of cheese but not as much as I've found at other places, I'm not sure what exactly it tasted like. They were warm, thick-sliced and crusted a little thick. Good value.Tell me I'm mistaken.

I'm trying to remember when I was a kid the oldest diner, located on Carmel Avenue at about 50 years old. Mount Pike is unusually small. For those who like their meals very thin and light, the place definitely is a bit smaller. I didn't notice how busy it was and it wasn't as busy as I'm used to. There is a bar on the back patio. I walked around the dining room before lunch on a Tuesday. It was a very well-attended restaurant. And all that noise was a welcomed sign, because I knew that there would be a wait. After looking around, I found a table filled with local residents and local business owners eating breakfast with a large group of friends and coworkers watching in The server told me about a graham cracker plate and a dozen breadsticks, made with locally grown fruit, blueberries, pecan I opened the dish and tasted the meat and the feta cheese. I took three bites, each with a tiny bit of my own choice (and a little bit more) before asking for the salads in the They served with a side of eggs. All meals were cooked to perfection, and the toast added even more flavor and texture. I can't stress enough how clean and good these dishes were. At the end of the meal it was all I could ask for and I had a great dinner experience. They did not take the time to talk with me twice, nor did they apologize. It's rare to find an American diner that has this level of service. I'll definitely be back.

Very enjoyable and fast service in a big restaurant. There was a lot of seating space available. I took my companion there to catch a late-night show in the bar. Despite the fact that the seating space was limited, it was a pleasant experience. I ordered a burger and slider with an onion soup. However, the wait was worth the wait–not the long wait that might be expected when you're eating at a restaurant. served with small plates. Two chicken fingers were excellent. While I did eat, the bartender mumbled "it wasn't hot tonight, wait until tomorrow." Steam does a good job of being different than similar areas. There's an old school neighborhood feel to the bar and service. The overall experience was pleasant, efficient, and competitively priced. Great burgers and food for reasonable prices!

Giovanni's was a nice family restaurant in downtown. It was the first of a series of two restaurant in the area. The floors are clean and the walls are tiled. The restaurant was pretty empty, even when we arrived at lunch time. No televisions, only a menu with Italian options. The menu is limited, and the pizza is not particularly strong. We had the Italian crust pizza style, served with an Alfredo sauce. Also, we tried our hands at making the pies. Unfortunately, this isn't always good, as the pasta on top tends to be a thick slice of thin pasta. It was very heavy and wet. This also made the sauce more thick (within that a little grain) and not as thick like normal tomato sauces. It's a disappointing pie with some of its ingredients not being redeemed. All other pie items were just average or above average. Not only was it hard and tasteless, the bottled ranch dressing was just more like ranch to the taste of a can of juice. The soup was ok, so would have preferred more stock. We had enough left on each plate to fill our bill. And we saw a few patrons eat there before we even knew about it. The service is good, good pizza and the food is just ok. It was our first time visiting this restaurant, and it is worth the drive.

It was just a Tuesday morning, and I started out on the path to downtown Cleveland with my GPS in hand. A few street corners led me to the aforementioned tubby olive, and then, as I felt a little more settled with the scenery, to  I saw Pizzeria Pizzeria with a sign in the window saying "Pizza & Hot Dogs". I've tried and been impressed with this place, and this one was good as well. I got to talk with the owner. I asked him what was his favorite. I gave him some time to browse the menu and picked out the patty I wanted. That was good.I was a bit of a bit nervous about the'veggie' pizza that was in an oven and being baked on I headed to the counter. Food vendors were also stationed nearby. She was very busy, and I noted that the pizza was cooking just now, and came with it a new dough crust and a cheese pizza bag. I asked what my pizza would be; he replied that it would be a large pizza with a thin crust and a nice thin thickness, all It started with an Arugula Pie fried with a few pieces of cheese topped with more Balsamic Dressing. The sauce was fresh and tangy, with a side of arugula, olives, blue cheese, and pesto. The tomatoes were cooked perfectly, crisp and flavorful, although I would have liked them more to be somewhat caramelized in those two spots. It was also nicely seasoned, with a healthy amount of garlic. I did not like the crust. I thought it would be much better if it remained in the oven for about five minutes, but the top never made it clear. I should have been able to tell by looking at it that it wasn't completely baked, but it was a small inconsistency — I was just disappointed. I felt like I'd never visit this place again. I love pizza.. A lot of my problems stem from the sense that everything is up to me sometimes. Sometimes you just need to re-look at it again. See you there. btw, nope to the bread!

Upon arriving home from the office, my husband and I were hungry for a lunch and needed a hot sub for lunch. After all, I'd heard a great review of Jersey Mike's. The menu at Jersey Mike's seems very similar to what I already had at an all-day breakfast in New Orleans, so I ordered the white tuna I received my order at 5pm with my sub waiting with a receipt. That's a lot for the money, so I've only eaten there once, and as such got a big whiff of the tuna The sandwich turned out to be great and tasted incredibly good despite the odd texture. The fresh tomatoes were delicious and the mayo worked well with the contrasting black pepper, leafy salad and tomato. Second bite revealed a surprisingly poor tuna salad; the tuna was overcooked and had the flavorless tomato and mayo on the center of the I did like the other ingredients, but it would have been nice to have some variety in the ingredients. The tomatoes needed some work, but the red pepper added some flavor and the black pepper went to a point that was not particularly impressive. The tuna should usually be prepared as per the instructions on the package, but if you're after a strong flavor this would be a better I'll be back. Be conservative when making subs, just beware of this "monkey" sandwich.

So, this could just as well be called the "Indian Restaurant" as it is named for the red-red decor and bright yellow decor. While there are a few bars on the corner of the mall and Route 120, the restaurant is not particularly apparent from Route 130, and looks more than  We entered as the food stalls appeared to open at midnight, and we were greeted with a crowded, albeit slightly unorganized, Food was excellent - they do have food stalls to eat at as a good restaurant would but the buffet only served lunch. The total served costs $13.99. It would take the restaurant a little longer to be more generous with the choices, to make room for the additional rice and naan in the menu This made the chicken plate a little too expensive for my taste. I ordered Chicken Fajitas, and they were served with an extra side of rice. The curried rice had a nice savoury flavor and was crisp and textured with no charred overcooking, but not oil I added a small cup of the spicy spicy sauce, and it also showed as an excellent choice. It was my second choice for lunch and it was cooked as per order. I would say this is about as good as you can get in Burlington City. The restaurant's atmosphere is warm and welcoming, a welcome contrast to the more upscale options, plus the fact that it's a hot, I'll still go back at some point. The restaurant features a modern bar and an open courtyard as it is situated next to the rest of the restaurant.

Last weekend I was in the area and decided to get sped up. But I still had the courage to go to V&V again on Tuesday. It was lovely to have an old friend behind the counter. After about twenty minutes I was very comfortable with my first encounter with Judy and her beautiful style of massage. I was quickly greeted by Judy, the owner/woman behind the counter. I woke up early and took advantage of the warm and inviting temperature in the dining area. She gave me a good, relaxing massage with the hot water filling the cup. Later she opened up the area of the sole of my foot to work on the back pain. In two minutes Judy massaged my whole body, from my feet to my shoulder and back (very gentle). Judy started to move my right foot and massaged my right foot firmly to smooth out tension and pressure. She left the table with my back legs straight and I felt no pain and increased circulation while I was at the table. I felt comfortable when she finished and her hands held my feet so completely that I could not feel my feet being touched. My only complaints are that my hands were sore to the touch, but Judy was very polite and patient with my complaints. Judy offered a 10% discount for my next visit if I repeat the same services with her again. Good job! :) Thanks so much for a great massage. A couple of our customers, meanwhile, would love to hear how your massage went after taking the tour!

When I walked in at 11am on Tuesday, one of my fellow writers noted that this restaurant was located on the corner of Waterfront and Alderd The food preparation, quality and service are unmatched in Bensalem. My wife and I walked in there from an airport. There are only 15 tables per row and we spent 10 minutes eating. On a Tuesday morning, I walked in after leaving work, and made my way around to the counter. I was on my way, so I could enjoy the smell of coffee. With the recommendation of the waiter, they chose the coffee-based blend with sugar in it. However, there was still room for breakfast. A delicious breakfast was on the table as I eat. The Omelet with arugula, red pepper and feta risotto was full of flavor and not at all greasy I ate the whole thing in about twenty minutes. The staff also offered several suggestions as to what would work, and I did manage to taste three of them in total. The staff had a friendly personality, so they were not as rushed as you expect.

There's no secret about Bowman's Tavern, in North Adams, MA. It is the source of a great story about the local history, where an outbreak of illness brought the war from home and forced a soldier to go back After many years of running a busy restaurant and bar, the  Tavern is looking to take a fresh approach, and restore some much needed confidence to its At the back is a booth with a large wood plank stove and table in the bar with curved mirrors over the fireplace. During lunch, there was nothing exciting, or innovative, but the portions of their menu were quite large and well organized and were priced fairly well. From time to time, they have a special deal. On one of the last visits, I had been a fan of a brussel sprouts side dish, and the potatoes were just plain delicious. I picked the potato bisque. My friends all had potato bisque, and theirs had potato bisque, which seems to be a much larger portions. I loved its taste and texture. Their potatoes bisque was Creamy, very rich with garlic, and had a little crunch of sweet potato bits. It had a buttery texture that was good, but a bit too sour, a bit too cream based, and not too sweet The Brussels sprouts side dish seemed like it needed a little sugar in it, but was good. A little off, but still very good. The dessert menu included chocolate covered strawberries, and two of the two whipped cream cheesecakes. My lunchmate ordered the burger, and I must say, it was the best I have ever ordered there. The interior of the tavern looks almost real, and has a large picture window to show the backsides of the bar and dining room Will be back..

The owners of The Baker, the owner of the Coffee Shop, greeted me and served as if I was looking for my first home-baking It is located at 8276 Pennsylvania Avenue in Oreland, PA and was opened on June 27 of 2016. So, when I heard of Fill A Bagel and Bread, the idea of trying the business out was a little surprising. I was very pleased with the coffee, and the shop has a very nice little patio area for a casual beverage. The bagel is fresh, the veggies are cooked and the onion cream cheese is smothered on the bread. The bagel itself was the perfect size and texture. My friend liked the combination of vegetables and the overall bite of the bagel. A little bit of liquid went into the bagels, but not too much, and the finished product was a little better. The onion was firm and almost soft, without any crackle or fluff that I would have expected. However, the onion bagel was plenty good. Although, that should be the most definite issue in the review, I still think the experience is a good place to hang. I can't fault the food, but with the prices on the menu. It just seemed that their customers don't know what to expect, and their prices are not fair for the quality and experience. My wife loves the bread and the service, but I am a bit let down by the coffee. So overall, I was pleased with the quality of the product, and would recommend them to anyone. The prices are low when you consider that it is the same staff for nearly 40 years - and they may even have the last employee, but they have been I would not return.

Located on Main Street near MCB, the LOOK out at Red Lion has a somewhat interesting concept. A lack of creativity is apparent, and there's a lot of the sort of eats that are so poor that they were invented in the late However, on a casual level, the menu appears to be a bit less awful than they used to be. In addition, the dining area is relatively big, but is rather uninhabited. The first item listed was their Grilled Pancake, with some egg in it that tasted slightly better than anything that was on the menu. One side of bread did not provide the required heat, especially at the end of the meal. The cheese looked not great either, but the other side of the dish, a thinly sliced onion, did not match the taste of anything at all For dessert there was something called a Cheese Free Cookie, which I decided to share. No Macarena was amazing last year for my Dad's wedding (we had our anniversary party in June), - if it wasn't I was so glad I'd got the chance to work with them again for the Wedding Music Association wedding I was doing in November of 2011. The DJ knew every word of every song we asked him about as well as all the other song requests that were made. Since Karen and I were getting married this year, I wanted to give you our story. Jonas was perfect! When we hired him, we took a bit of time to set things up. He did this by asking me to send him a song listing of songs that I was interested in, and I said my grandfather and his wife so they can Then he played us the songs and played each. He gave me several songs that were pretty much talking about our wedding (and where I thought was such great music to end a day with). Jonas knew it had been a while since I performed songs before and knew it was ok to switch it up. Jonas was amazing on the night, making sure we were at all of our song requests and making sure we got the best sound he could. This turned out to be a wonderful experience and so glad we chose not Macarena for our wedding! I learned a lot by giving Jonas my requests because he was so patient! It's easy to forget to include a comment or call them, but do it at least 3 weeks in advance. We were doing quite a bit of singing during the reception (we were having a lot of fun! and no, you didn't want to go to KNEW!).

Brought to our attention yesterday by an author, this quaint cafe inside the East Village Market space was always a go-to spot for a I'm always on the lookout for new places to find a breakfast donut. When I asked why I had to return for the chicken and donuts and they refused to make any, I was told that they can get you one from I wasn't able to spot exactly what I was eating, but I got my eggs and a bagel to go. At least the coffee is made in a small cafeteria and they know how to make their donuts good.

I went to Bar Fisk in Little Rock for a night out today. Of all the bars I've been to, this one has taken the cake. It isn't very busy, with few patrons inside the restaurant and not a lot on the social media platforms. They were out of the area from what I was told but the atmosphere was nice and was a lot quieter than what I had expected. One evening they gave me a mix of drinks to try - I guess I wanted the traditional cocktail. I decided to try a drink made from juniper, rye, and a cocktail mixer. My drink was tasty, but my mouth was very watering by the time was over. The drink was a little too sweet to me - too creamy. My third drinks were two drafts; a Manhattan and a Manhattan. In the end I was too busy to finish it but it was still a satisfying experience.

YES, THIS IS THE LAST TIME I'VE VISITED THE PASTILLE IN CHICAGO - AND I think It was my first visit to this bakery - first time using their mobile app! First I came here for lunch to meet with Alisha. When I called, her representative arrived and I was able to schedule an appointment to visit the bakery during a lunch hour. She suggested a fresh pastry and I ordered the savory quiche lorraine, with a side salad. In the afternoon, I met Alisha again and offered to drop in for lunch. Unfortunately they aren't stocked with quiches. But they are very willing to make up for it with a quiche on the second visit. We had a bite of the "Grand Misé" (sorry for the technical errors, but I didn't pay attention to how the I love the fresh croutons and cheese! Overall, it was a nice little restaurant with a friendly staff. Well, I'd like to meet with Alisha again once more, but I'd really rather not wait too long for this bakery. What else would you like to see? Love the setting, the feel of the place, the staff, and the quiche...I'll definitely be back. Love, love, love this bakery...and I really loved the Quiche as well!

I'm from the north side. ECO has my clothes ready to be picked up within a week. There's a store on the corner of West 128th in the University Village, and I was pretty excited to drop off my clothes for the regular When they arrived, the clothes were clean and pressed. The clothes came back exactly the reason I sent them - clean. I didn’t have to worry as they were in the bag and ready to go. The cleaners also took the time to explain which of the fabrics in my outfit is to be cut, and also notified me for an extra charge if I'm not sure how these laundry services stack up against my usual providers but I'm super pleased with the overall experience. I'm extremely happy to be back in San Francisco. I'm always glad I can go in and choose ECO when I'm in the area for my next clean and i don't feel
I recently visited Ants Pants at the Alameda Blvd location. It's awesome w/ everything on top. I will definitely be back. It's perfect!

I've participated in Platoon Training's Boot Camp program for the past six week. The first class began with a very positive feeling. I found the class format interesting and I like that there are no "same old same old" workout options. I thought that we would end up learning the “sitting down” and seeing how much easier the next class would be. However, there are tons of surprises throughout the class that will make you take a huge leap of faith without believing that it will be the same. Having them change the course each week has been amazing. I love the concept of each class being different and challenging our bodies, learning new stuff, and building personal strength and stamina. My body has become toned and stronger and it has made me want to work out at a gym more. The best part of the Platoon classes is the camaraderie of the members.

It took all of five minutes for us to receive our food order through Southgate's restaurant. We went to Southgate before the weather got too warm and the restaurant is a nice quiet place to go for some comfort food and rest. A small delivery takes around 20-45 minutes to reach our house, and I've never heard of other delivery restaurants delivering in the city. I really like the taste of the food, and love that it's delivered to our home! They were great and my husband loved them too. We had a huge group so the dumplings were hot and they did hold their shape very well! We both enjoyed that, and added the Korean hotdog buns. Also the pork ribs. It was an excellent sandwich, and my boyfriend ordered the beef and pork. I had to add some black beans and guacamole to my sandwich to make up for the lack of salsa. This was a great experience, and we'll be returning to Southgate.

Our recent vignette for dinner required a place for our latest family fix (who I feel are the most inflexible about socializing in this I found two options, West Side Gravy and the South Side Diner. I decided upon L'Art de l'Excellence at Southend-on-Sea. I arrived at our dinner reservation early, and was quite surprised (my dinner date had been changed to Tuesday) that the restaurant was dead. While we were not quite seated on the patio, there was little that could be done to improve the situation. If the menu made no mention of the bass, the tables seemed far from quiet, the restaurant in itself somewhat empty, and our waiters were rather o We ordered the ribeye steak and served with a potato salad as an app. I immediately accused the waiters of having an over-eating tendencies, because no one was ordering lunch while we were there. Most of us were pleased with the taste and didn't mind waiting for my main course. Our second order was a side of chicken on a bun. When not burned, the chicken was moist and not tough and not overloaded with garlic and onion. It didn't compare to good enough. And then we started sampling the fare. However, the chocolate cake was not as good as I remembered it being, and I was disappointed too. Both dishes were substantial. With a slightly pricey gastronomy bill of about $35 per person, they have the look of some expensive dive bars, but in my opinion,

My partner and I made our way for lunch today at Suraya. I eat all things French, but I'm also a big fan of all things Indian. We ate at the bar and loved the vibe and service. The menu is full of delicious options and the service was perfect. During our lunch and dessert, I tried everything on the menu and we all very happily agreed it was exactly what we ordered. My husband and I had a great time and got some food items to try. It was the perfect excuse to drop off a side order next time! The food was delish. Not a bad side dish, though. We also shared the salad and everything was very tasty. All in all, it was a very nice experience. Maybe there is another location out there. I am hoping to get the chance to see this one in person. Next, I will definitely plan on the gin de cuida!

Buena Onda is a Mexican restaurant based in Denver, Colorado, and I'm not exactly going to deny that. First, I got a burrito. There, I got my food in less than an hour on a Thursday night at approximately eleven. Because I didn't go in, I wasn't able to really be a part of their live experiences, so my review is just going to Buena Onda is famous for the taco experience, and I can see why that's - as I'm used to my typical Despite these reservations, the delivery service was an all-round winner. The chicken burrito was very flavorful, the chicken was cooked well, and the veggies were fresh. I had the tortilla soup on the side, which I wasn't too sure about at first because it came with little chunks of chicken over the top of I did prefer my soup hotter than the colder option, so it was definitely worth getting a larger portion of soup. The salad was pretty good though. That said, it did need a little sauce to break down the texture. With that said, the food was still pretty solid, so I'll be back to go in the near future. When I went back to the hotel, I got another free margarita so I was able to take some of the meal home and share some with I think they will still make a solid impression on me since I was so excited about their tacos and I'll likely add them to my list

It wasn't long after I walked in and the smell of Greek food was lingering throughout the restaurant. It was a pretty chill dinner with some friends in a cute Greek cafe atmosphere. The inside of the restaurant is very dark, but it worked perfectly to provide some privacy and a good social gathering among all of us. Fortunately, we had an excellent server, who took good care of us. I really enjoyed the selection of food. As dinner was going on, I had the chicken wings with two dips: a garlic dip and a spicy dip. Depending on the crowd, you could also order a cup of aikote or Greek tea, which we got instead. I had the pita bread a side dish, which was good although I did not want it. The shrimp frittata was good, but had a bit too much sauce to cut through the fennel. I must admit I hated the seafood. Even though the fish was pretty salty--my wife was so grossed out by it that she couldn't even be bothered to eat. The main course began with a selection of halal meat (which we are not sure about as we've never had this) and a variety They all came with side dishes. I ordered the fried mussels, which had a strong funky flavor, and the Brussels sprouts--a favorite of mine until I started I think that they had my name on it, a "Kanella" sign at the restaurant.

I recently made a visit to the Cider Republic on East Washington. A sign was next to the signs: "You'll Love Cider!". I was super excited to go and take a taste. The service here is just amazing! I chose to purchase half of the Lil' Sunshine and half of the 'Cider Sun', and it came as a gift. I saw so much variety that was hard to choose just one cider. The cider was fairly priced and they're pretty stocked. They have an omitting sugar (which was my choice) for a few extra calories, but it was still fresh.

Since getting here in early 2010 and adjusting to the new bar environment, I've had a difficult time getting used to the new location due to the This is where everything was great in the old world, until recent changes (including my review of Yelp). It was one of my first favorites with the very first Happy Hour in November. I love that they serve them with a sprig of lemon and a generous squeeze of lime. I can see how Xochitl has become so popular... but is it too pricey? So, I wouldn't recommend it again. The rice and two plates of ceviche were not very good. It wasn't bad, but it left much to be desired. The flavor remained the same. The ceviche was also soggy and the accompanying vegetables were all in a slimy liquid. We decided to share some steak and chicken tacos on their patio menu, which came out to be $115. The jalapeo ranchera taco was thick, the fish had a delicious cheese sauce to it, and the rice wasn't too salt My friend had the steak and they were too fatty for my liking, so she couldn't finish it and it was a bit too "fishy The food was disappointing, and I can see how Xochitl would have been better. Maybe it's the new owner that isn't the best and I won't come back, but I like this place. But I'm still sad to say the service is good and the food is pretty bad... too bad!

I went to Frog Pond in this lovely evening of a late October afternoon with my husband and several of our friends to celebrate the Spring Festival. The restaurant was open on patio day, and had an open tent for us just inside the tent. So you could see how much everyone else was enjoying the shade. At the time, Pizzeria La Vetri was the new hot spot in the area, but the pizzas made me feel just as fancy as any other My dinner consisted of some pasta and a salad - the salad was made from a combination of romaine, iceberg and baby carrot My server recommended the basil pesto and it was just as good as the arugula I grew in the spring. The pizzas were outstanding, my friends said too. At the time I really didn't care for the margherita but had to do a post on how delicious it was... it was really good We were both happy with our pizzas, however we needed to order some additional sauces to go over our plates. There are a whole stack of restaurants and food trucks offering dozens of unique and delicious pizzas.

My recent hair blow out bar at André Richard Salon is a little bit of an experiment. They have been awesome, and as I was writing this post, I was thinking about trying a blowout bar for a change. As soon as I heard of André Richard Salon, I knew that I'd find out where to go! But last week, I got invited to a fancy networking event for a new client in the borough of Ocean Park (I was super excited about this and decided I wanted to make the most of it. It was my birthday and I don't even have to work out of my condo; I took an afternoon to figure out what I could do in the meantime The best place to go for a blow out was the one in Westwood, NJ, where owner LB is so kind and so easy to work with What I wasn't aware of is they had a new stylist every week, and I had never heard of what she was called before. It just occurred to me that they'd have a very limited number of stylists available on Mondays (no surprise). When I arrived, LB's hairstylist, Francesca, told me about some great blow outs she has had in the past I got a hot treatment and blow out, and the results were amazing. I would absolutely recommend André Richard Salon even to someone who's not sure if this is a good place to get your hair done. It was truly a lovely session.

The order arrived with 2 extra hours before delivery. The poke bowl had plenty of heat and was a great way to kick my day off for the day. The aioli was pretty good. My friend said she really likes it and I would probably even consider it next time I ordered delivery. I'm not a huge fan of shiriracha as a sauce, but this was just fine. It's a great bowl if you're able take the day off and cook. Overall, a pretty good bowl. I wouldn't order the next time since the flavors here are lukewarm to me.

This orchid came from the grocery store here in the Philippines and is the same as every other orchid I have in my kitchen. I had an idea to propagate my white orchid from a few years back, but never found a suitable substrate or a good place to put it I decided to take the orchid to our local florist to have them trim it down. The girl at Pure made a completely new flower box by taking care of the entire orchid in her old and shabby apartment! So far so good. After that much growth, I feel it’s time for me to buy another orchid and perhaps a couple of rhododendrons

I haven't been dining at the restaurant to give a full review yet because, you know, Jen Carroll has had some busy days. It's just a little hazy as I was incredibly excited about our dinner experience! Their current food list is a bit confusing to read. The menu does include three courses of food, which my husband was really curious about. I don't remember the name of the dessert, but we had to call.  Anyway, the menu we ordered was simply delicious. I was very impressed with both of my dinners and the food, especially all of the breads, deserts, and salads. I ordered the whole roasted fish. I've never had it cooked this way before, so we really asked for a whole roasted fish from the menu. We spent the night getting some food for breakfast and then we left with our desserts. Then we tried a Negroni, which was delicious. It was a very unique and interesting cocktail. The Negroni I ordered was wonderful and I didn't feel guilty drinking it though. We opted for a large cocktail, which made me feel rushed. What we ordered was the Spice Finch; it was great but I'm glad we weren't going to order it. Good food! The price here is fair I would suggest you give it a try. I also have to note that the food at this restaurant is not all expensive, but I would really recommend you try the sea bass.

I am a bit of an "80s go-getter" by nature so I don't really have too much to go on here. Is that a thing? This is not the kind of place I'm just getting excited about, but really, why would I be? What if it's all not that great? I love it. This venue, just down the street from our old apartment, was renovated, completed, and opened. The concept is pretty much a throwback to the 80s. This little gem just opened in March and I can't say enough about the experience. The bar is full of skeletons and there's a big mirror, which is just what you need to relax over their famous martin I've picked a mix of classic hip-hop, funk, and R&B and it's been a blast. I also enjoy the drinks. I'm not a big fan of the '80s, but, just by watching all the movies, I think my brain was made up for If you are a foodie, I'd recommend going to the menu, because I've never made it past to the buffet that is actually The menu is full of the classics in a very contemporary style. There are a lot of choices, but I have to say the crab cake is my personal favorite. I've also tried bites of the steamed breaded fish sandwich, which is actually made with the same soup found in their own kitchen. I'm not quite sure if it was for good or bad. For dinner (which is my favorite), I went with the polenta pizza and the brussel sprouts. I didn't even realize that the butter on my steak was an apple-yellow glaze; it was perfect. The drinks here are top notch. At the end of the day, it's just so-so. I'd definitely go back.

I have to admit, Oh Yoko had me swooning right into it. I was so impressed, I followed the reviews on Yelp. On Facebook, the restaurant was being used as a "hometown" and had a huge following that included my parents. I made my way downtown for my first taste experience and I was pleasantly surprised to find the place was packed and only two others in the restaurant, which in I arrived at 9:30 am at their location, and it was nearly as packed as my car. The restaurant featured an excellent variety of rolls on their menu, which was full of delicious ingredients. I wasn't exactly sold at the price tag, but that definitely didn't stop me from ordering something to go. I had a few questions before I made off on my way to get the roll. I started with a roll that was called La volcano de mango. At the end, each piece of meat was shaved (my brother had that done to his shrimp), covered with a thin layer of avocado and It was very thick and the fruity avocado tasted delicious with fresh tuna, but a little salty and not quite as smooth. Topping the whole experience off, the staff brought me a beautiful glass of cold white wine from their amazing vineyard. This seemed like a little pricey but also quite fresh and was even more delicious than the volcano roll. I finished the afternoon off with a half-gallon of sake (a small bottle of red wine was included with my lunch). Oh Yoko would not be here without both of you!

This is a bit of a must try if you're in the Boston area (at least this is my opinion). It's the best mac and cheese I've had. And it's not just because the Mac and cheese is made fresh to order; it was exactly that way. I was a bit worried that the sauce would make me sick, but nope, it was just a small hit overall. ...and if you want a real dessert, I don't think I'm going to buy one, this is a must try.

It's been quite a while since we're partying at the bar at The Bar for Afecciot, though I don' I had a glass of their sangria and was not tempted to ask for more. It was close enough to the bar to avoid noises and traffic. This one night only, I did not care for the cocktail menu and the bartender kindly took care of the drinks. It was a nice and cold beer that had a sprinkling of cream, which I liked because it had a bit of that warm Our server gave us an additional beer to sip, but the waitress did not mention it and I ordered 2 other drinks with me to go.

I went to Sephora this past Tuesday and had a good time. It was my birthday this past weekend, so it was perfect to shop the store. I thought I was the only one there - so I waited for my appointment. I had no idea the experience would be anything like I thought it would be. It turns out it was a very busy day. My friend was here at a different time, so I was able to come in at a good time, whereas I had to arrive at around This was my first time back, so I was a bit excited to go back when they were offering 20% off all purchases for the 1st time on My first purchase was a foundation which I didn't really remember the brand, but it was the foundation I had been eyeing in various colors since my I bought a lip color, a lipstick, my nail polish, and some lip gloss. This was the first time I ordered online and I am very happy with the product. A couple weeks later, I discovered a missing receipt at the counter in my cart, and wanted to return it. It's kind of weird, since I don't have a bad lip. So on my second (and probably the first) visit, I will definitely be going back to stock up!  Unfortunately, I didn't have time to play with the samples, but that's ok, because I did remeber that I didn

I found this place while looking for a nail salon. The owner/operator was very nice and made it a good experience. After a few minutes, it took them a long time to come to the salon. The chair at Tara's has a massage function and I thought it was a nice place to relax after work. Two machines were there and they worked in one minute, which would make my pedicure take about eight minutes. I didn't want to come back to get our pedicure done because it was very uncomfortable! I was pleased to see that they asked me to wear my favorite top coat, which I did. Then I was seated at a table with a good sized chair to sit by. Then they dipped the tips of my fingers and toes in several different acrylic base colors, then dried with a clear top coat.  Unfortunately, I had a great time and I would definitely go back. It's a minor oversight but I can't wait to see how my nails look. The girl who did my massage did a great job of cleaning up while I waited. But the weather is great for nail salons and I can't wait to use the spa before my wedding this December. The reviews were positive too.

I am absolutely in love with the Hotel Monaco, a rad hotel space in the center of New York City. I'm not generally a big fan of hotels that have a whiz in their design work, but this one does really hit the nail on The reception area was fantastic; I thought that the decor just came together really well to create a truly unique setting that I think would be perfect for a There is a gorgeous space for large wedding receptions, with big drapes hanging just ceiling-to-ceiling. The ceiling and walls of glass reflect the original 1950's artefact. For me, it looks like it would be perfect for a wedding shower, so a lot of fun. There's also a restaurant that will sit 6 people and there's also a great indoor space for cocktails in the lobby bar. You might even be able to find a private space on the third floor to rent for those smaller gatherings that just require a little extra space. It's very spacious and comfortable with a nice setting. I was really struck by the gorgeous decor, and was excited to check out the pool area. The view is absolutely breathtaking. I would definitely recommend it to anyone who wants a more upscale experience.

If you are looking for a new place to grab a bite to eat and drink beer in downtown Toronto, Chickie's (formerly known as Chickie's is one of the places I always stop to visit just to hang out and a good beer. The place's been called "the neighborhood's best beer bar." A highlight last night was the Flyers hockey game at Chickie's. In attendance were several of our team's captains, who are all fans, and local hockey stars who were cheering on the guys. Who else was there, other than Riley and Arron? I was amazed that they didn't have to spend all the extra time running around and taking a break, but I don't want to tell. For starters, you can always walk by Chickie's at the intersection of Sixth, Sixth, Sixth and Fifth avenues. I would have liked to see a full bar, but I was able to sneak in with a little noise-stopping when the game ended.

As I neared graduation, it came to my attention that I needed an updo. I decided Jean Madeline needed to be my first choice. This was a dream come true for me as they were super patient with me and took care of me professionally, in a timely manner, but still really In true fashion, the girls in their class were in their element - so young and not too sure what they'd be doing there. It took her half an hour to put my hair in order and she was always on time! So I came in and asked to have a low back-up for our wedding day. It's actually not as difficult as it looks. They provided a variety of hair textures, including a variety of braided, half-up and half-up styles, which they chose for me She added some lace to keep out all that frizz. Aside from the fact that the updo lasted only two hours and cost me only $25, Gia's price tag didn't come close I won't do any updos on our last few trips, but it was fun and I love the look of this updo. In the meantime I would recommend this salon!

I'm still in the business of working with the Crusty's staff to offer the best gluten-free and carb-free food that I can And it's my least favorite chain in North Phoenix since the food is always too salty and sweet. We've had numerous occasions with some interesting, flavorful food. When I'm around, I have the hummus and pickled bell peppers. Soups that are a little low carb may or may not be a diet option for you either, while the salads are often low in carb And one of their "Best Of" items is their kale salad with tomato and onion. They also have a large selection of their delicious desserts. Besides my favorites there are a few things that I haven't been able to like. You also get their drink specials, which are huge (I think). I won't be making any trips to Kermit's anytime soon since they tend to be very uncrowded.

When I was at the grocery store last week, I was on an adventure. Here's my haul from the online aisle, though I already had other items in mind. But the store was full of products that didn't bring great results. A good purchase from The Container Store, however, took me over 30 minutes of browsing, much to my delight. For the first time in a long time, I went home with the hope that I could come up with a quick, efficient schedule for the things I As an organized mom, I do appreciate those stores. It's not cheap, but the stuff is amazing!

Last night we had dinner with Michael and Alex at Olly's. This is an organic, vegan vegan restaurant with a really fun, fresh flavor palette for casual dining. This place was a bit pricey and had a line on the door (which was a definite plus), but they served so much delicious food I was so glad I made a reservation because I was starving and would of wanted to share. We had three separate dinners to try. We started off with a bowl of kale pesto with a roasted cauliflower on it. I loved it!. I had the seafood cocktail which was a perfect compliment to the cauliflower. It was topped with a nice hollandaise sauce and the mushroom was super sweet, fresh and flavorful. My friend had the sea bass and clam ceviche. and I went for the chicken fennel plate. The cod was really good; it had just the right amount of clam flavor, but still wasn't too salty or heavy. The broth was excellent, and the seafood was served fresh and hot. The dessert was fantastic, too! I wasn't expecting the tart to be as good as it was, and felt like I could feel the delicious ingredients in the crust, but again, the And the apple crisp was delicious! I loved the vibe to it and it was a great place to eat. I knew I had to get that pizza. I'm definitely planning a visit to Olly this holiday season because of how good it looks and how convenient it is. Gigi is kind of like a version of Olly, but I think it's actually a reimagining of Olly.

I had heard so much about 'Gay Hair Salon' from someone I trusted from my friends and family. This salon was recommended by one of my clients. She recommended Dana, and I had no idea - her staff blew my mind! I arrived on time to get my service started and it was packed. Dana was patient and I wasn't too nervous about what it would be like. I was so sooo excited to be able to show off my lovely hair and get my hair done without running in the street with my husband. She took my time and even encouraged me to look down at my hair to see what was left. As I was nervous about how my hair was going to look, she just said it would be and it was perfect! I can't say enough great things about this salon. You can't help but have a smile in your eyes.

One day when I was in the area and wanted a good hot tea, I figured out if I wanted to get hot tea, I would just We found a table on the patio, and the place was pretty comfortable. During our first visit, Kevin suggested bubble tea. The tea was freshly ground after I'd ordered it, and was made in a ramekin or mug. A chai and hot tea (it was my boyfriend's birthday right now, but I think this time he's still around) was ordered I got to drink a quarter and my taste buds became entangled in the cup, which made for a weird experience. When Colleen got in the cup for me, she wasn't interested, though I told her what the taste was for. I'm not a huge bubble tea fan, but it was still very cool; more so than I was expecting. The only drawback of Bubble Tea was not having room for ice cream for a while after I left, especially because it would have been too sweet. I probably wouldn't go back, though, because the tea is just a little too sweet to be enjoyable with just 1 or 2 bubbles in it You can find an amazing selection of hotdogs and sandwiches on their menu too.

Distrito serves authentic Italian pizzas & wings at reasonable prices. Every Wednesday they have a special happy hour special. I had the "Naomi" from the wine list and the mimosa was incredible, and the prosecco was good as well. Some beers are also half off. They have a great happy hour menu which you can go check out. The pizzas are good and the wings are good too, because you can get them a couple of times. The wings were excellent. I would have been happy to eat any of their dessert items on Saturday, but were too busy to get one off the menu. You can also buy drinks that are bottled at a reasonable price. It's definitely a place I'll be going to more often.

When I moved to Chicago in the summer of 2011, I knew Xochitl's was opening a Sunday morning Brunch. I loved it so much I brought a friend with me so we could split it. This spot is packed with fresh-caught seafood in bright yellow, coconut milk-wrapped ice cream cones and fresh-made breads, I was going with my friend who loves brunch, not because it's on my bucket list or that it's a regular Sunday food spot. But what a great experience all around. Xochitl's signature mimosa margaritas is an extra delicious margarita to die for. The edamame is my go-to, because it's always so fresh and delicious. A must have on both visits is the lime soda on the menu, and a great choice for a hot summer day, after spending the day in San But the signature dish at brunch is always ceviche. I loved the egg white and avocado Benedict. A mild mixture of ceviche, lime juice, lime juice and a small amount of tangy coconut milk is sure to hit the spot. Several of the offices had a window and two larger ones (the one on my right) with a lot of tables and conference room space. The office is bright, clean and bright. I had a great time hanging out there on two separate occasions. I know this is not for everyone. I feel that they might be making a mistake by expecting a full-time membership for someone who's already in the industry and/or works in I may return in the future, but I would strongly recommend a trial membership if available. I definitely plan to take advantage of their coffees and eat at the cafe before my next home office project starts.

The vetri pizza at my friend Kate's was just what we ordered. Pizzeria Vetri welcomes all of its guests with a long list of cheese and wine lists. We were seated right away and immediately received our order of pizza and salad. It's very easy to get a quick seat, but with all the food options in one spot, your options are pretty limited. They had a small selection of salads and apps, plus a wood oven salad as well. Then we ordered a large pasta dish, but this was in fact a white pizza I had never seen in the restaurant. The meat is fresh and the cheese is perfect, alongside a hearty side of savoy cabbage and onion. There are a lot of different varieties to choose from, too, so the options were endless. The prosciutto slices were delicious, and I enjoyed every bite. Maybe I went too fast because I don't tend to go for pizza that much. It was so great! They're all great pizzas and the Italian salad dressing is incredible.

This isn't the place I work. I can't think of a more ideal work scenario than having the choice to work inside or outside of an office building. I'm told there is a lot of stuff to do and eat there. It's also pretty pricey to shop there if you're paying top dollar.

I had my last meal at Franklin's back in the summer of 2011 (it's located in Downtown Phoenix and I haven't seen it since It was a pretty crowded spot for dinner. There are multiple places to sit and they all look pretty similar. Franklin's is definitely on the strip, so if you are near any of these places, you know exactly where it is. Franklin's is a family friendly place. The interior space is very nice and has a really nice feel. So we went along with the flow of the night. We ordered the fried chicken and it was very good, but the breading was a little dry for my taste. The hot dogs with beans and cheese were just as good. The chips I had with my beer were better than the rest of the chips, but the buns were also a little crusty and could have used some The wings are also really good. Sis ordered the house special. Also, the food and service were spot on. On the bright side, all the beer is a lot cheaper than some of their competitors around the strip (including the bar).

I've had enough pizza and not much better... and this is coming from a woman who loves pizza. I had read good reviews about it and thought it was the best, so I headed to try it. The staff were friendly and the restaurant was clean and the pizza was on the menu. As a result, I ordered a large cheese pizza and a large southwestern arancini pizza with sauce. We waited around 5-10 minutes to get a pizza before they got it home and we ate at the restaurant. The pizza was well cooked and the sauce was just right. The sauce was tasty, but not as good as that at other spots; it had a weird taste. The rest of the pizza tasted normal, not bad, and the sauce provided just enough heat to hold my interest. The menu on Giorgio's website looks pretty extensive, but the menu just makes sense and the atmosphere is great.

Our second year at The Kitchen is drawing to a close (I'm now looking at our first year in Philly) for our favorite restaurant: The This place is so great. The staff-- especially AJ and Jess--is all so friendly. The bartenders are particularly talented. They are full of love and care, not just to help, and rather than being a simple stodgy, they are passionate people who The bar has a great vibe to it, and the space itself is very soothing. The staff is also amazing about taking care of you and sharing their love and knowledge of a wide-mouthed good old fashioned beer such as the I don't really go out of my way to try each course in the dining room, but there are two main menu options. I saw the menu for the first time on NYE and was so excited. After eating two beets, my taste buds were immediately energized by a sweet marinade. It was very simple to prepare that evening, so I know I'll be back here again on NYE. The oysters are absolutely incredible. This is one of the best ceviches I've ever tasted. I liked the ceviche because of the marinade that Jonny used to marinate the oysters to perfection. I ate the whole thing. Then up came the steak. I love steaks. I can't help but look at the dish over and over, looking for certain subtleties to be incorporated into the recipe. The meat is massive, tender and just so, so good. Honestly, I haven't driven down there in a while; it's just so amazing and I think it's a must- Love it. Thank you, Jonny Mac, for making me really excited to go there again this time of year!

I'm so proud to have taken the drive to find Thai House (on the corner of Market and East 42nd Streets) to try out this week We ate here on Saturday afternoon around 6pm, a bit late in the evening so we had to order delivery. The food was hot and flavorful. Everything was delicious and fresh from the store. The service was great and my partner ordered something he'd never heard of before, his pineapple rice basket. He said it was delectable. A lot of us just can't get enough of this delicious-sounding garlic sauce and we finished it off with their Chicken Salad. The food was just too good to pass up. Hopefully I'll be back to sample the flavors here. But regardless, if you need to eat lunch or dinner for a while, try this place.

The restaurant is a little smaller than you think you'd find in the suburbs, but it's very clean and well run with a nice It is located in the middle of Clemson's historic quarter on State Hill and makes every visit a great one, for all of your Polish I always enjoy eating there, I've lived and worked in the area for years and have used their staff many times. My fiancé and I are a big fan of Kanella's. We visit often, but my friends have never visited and I would love to try as often as they do. So I have to write a little about the dishes on the menu. I've been there three or four times to try the food and it's so amazing. If you're up on the weekend either, and you're looking for a special place to catch some football, try this place. Take a peek at their menu.

The decor of this restaurant is still very Sicilian, and has a very Sicilian feel at the same time. Zeppoli at 1621 Sorrento Ave is truly a stunning dining location. From the moment we walked in, I was struck by the gorgeous Italian decor. No bare walls and just enough natural light to make the experience comfortable and enjoyable. A few years ago, I was a linguist and ate the food. We started with a small bottle of caviar and was immediately surprised by the array of delicious, fresh seafood and amazing apps. We finished the meal with a selection of menu items including tagliatelle, ribgatoni, caponi and gelato The tagliatelle with prosciutto,  mushrooms and white wine caper was a perfect amatricula with just the But I had already started my dinner with their signature soup of tomato-based pesto with a side of pesto sauce - and it was absolutely fantastic It had a beautiful color and had a charred, nut-like consistency. That was a good amount of protein. This place is a little pricey, and I don't usually order seafood. I could never go wrong with one of those dish. The sauce was deliciously rich, with a generous amount of green and dried vegetables and fresh basil that was so fresh that I was not even hungry. I'm still not sure where to put the credit for the pistachio flavor, though I can't seem to think of a place Did I miss the waitor behind the counter? The atmosphere wasn't as awesome as I'd hoped. There wasn't a table available for 6 people - hmm, that's one of the big things I didn't like about there I'm not aware of the full list of stars, since it wasn't advertised or mentioned, so I've never been able to add it Maybe not the best kind, but it's a rare occasion where you can get good food and drinks at a reasonable price, and you don' At $15 for dinner, it's something I'll definitely do again when I'm in town. If you've never heard of a restaurant that you think only Italians can enjoy in town, come here! So did we!? There are literally hundreds of options for delicious Italian food, such as a pizza, pizza, and salad bar. As mentioned above, it's the BYO version of what you'd see at an Italian restaurant, minus the take home section. The food is super good! This place is also open late at night, which gives it an extra extra special treat. My favorite is the kale salad with salmon, grape tomatoes, and swiss cheese but if you prefer them without seafood they have an It's been a long time since I had this dish, but so good. I am a huge chili fan. It was so quick to heat up and be spitting hotdog all over I couldn't help but think how beautiful. A few weeks previously, at the airport to celebrate the launch of The Skyline, Chris and I sat at a table and heard a story When I think of "smooth" hot dogs, I really think of Hot Diggity. The chili was hot and tasted like fudge that had a sweet/spicy flavor to it. The ambiance of this place reminded me of a Mexican restaurant, with a casual atmosphere and a nice laid back atmosphere. The bread was tender and just crunched enough to make the meat delicious to bite into. As she ordered they were smothered in a sweet and sour sauce and dished out a rich, sweet dipping sauce I'm not going to say that my girlfriend's cheeseburger from the night before was worth the price of a regular Hot Diggity sandwich. Now you can eat 'em all! The answer comes from former Philly soft pretzel factory employee, James P. O'Flaherty. There's only one bit of the soft pretzel in the entire thing. The batter was soggy and the pretzel dog was too doughy. I've definitely had better pretzel dogs. Check out the rest here. If you don't like sweet pretzels, you should probably avoid those!

Craft Hall opened its doors in 2013 in East New York City near the West Village for a three-day weekend. The restaurant is basically an old school dive bar with small barfronts. Craft Hall has a pretty extensive menu, which has a bunch of unique items and it is super fun to browse. The craft beer offers a variety of apps. At our first visit, I had their cheesy, vegan pizza and I was happy to hear that they're actually cooking their pizza here ( I wouldn't recommend that they offer a lot of food options for people who're vegan or dieting for healthier snacks, though. The drinks section sells pretty eclectic and creative NA-themed drinks. I don't include water and soda (although I always enjoy a glass of water since I don't go for dessert, when I did get this but most bars at their budgets offer their house branded cocktails. They're also featuring cranberry juice and lemonade. This is a really huge space and the decor is beautiful. The menu also features a few brews that are really interesting. The baristas are friendly and the owners are great hosts/managers. But for a restaurant with a kid-friendly brewpub, it's still a pretty cool spot. It's a great place for birthday parties and children's events. I don't expect to ever visit Craft Hall, ever again now that it's open to children. The food is amazing and the prices are reasonable. It's really an awesome place to visit after work to hang out.
