Alma de Cuba is a bar/pub, and although the prices are a bit high, it's the happy hour you need. I ordered the sangria, which contains several classic Cuban ingredients. It's also an excellent place for dancing. I opted for one of the mojitos, and it was pretty good, even if a bit too much coffee infused. I opted for an ice cream sundae on sweet potato to go with, and my husband ordered the red bean soup. We also ordered a few drinks, including an artichoke skewer and a chocolate mojito, and shared a few.

I had a great time at Reds Bar! We had the same experience there - just a few less people. It's the second largest city in California and, as a result, is a pretty tourist town. So, Reds Bar was just the place for a warm beverage and a little rest-and-sleep. First impressions: It was open late on a Friday night during the weekend and not really crowded. We only went after 5pm. There wasn't too much to see except that it was fairly dark so my camera didn't work properly and we had a little trouble getting a I was offered a few beers, and I felt that was going to be enough. That's gotta be the cool people at the bar, right? We ended up choosing a gin bar, and we were all happy. The beer list is big at this bar, which I like so we will be back.

If you've been hearing about this new restaurant, and haven't already been hearing that they have a great Happy Restaurant Week, now's That's all I can say. The food and service was excellent, even with the fact that our waiter was a little cranky. This is definitely more of a fun restaurant than the restaurants I'm used to being part of everyday - we really had a great time at this We called the restaurant just to see if they could make a mocktail for me, in which case there was only a small wait. I didn't have a chance to taste the wine however, so I can't say for sure, but the sangria was excellent. There are several more dining options in that area, as well as a cafeteria close by. The food was good overall and we'll definitely be back. Lastly, when our waitress came my friend was so friendly, even after the restaurant had closed, and we were able to walk away not feelingrushed

We're headed down to the new restaurant, Puppet Lounge, and we already love it. I think you'll enjoy coffee there - there's a nice place outside of the building that looks great! The place is full of Mexican flavors and we got our drinks after getting seated. We left with fresh juice and a big smile. My friend had a couple of sandwiches and we opted for a bowl of chips and a salad. Our server told us there was no seating outside but they do have tables outside and patio seating available on tuesdays. The menu was full of Mexican-style Breakfast (banger beans, burrito, eggs, and kale) but you can also order to I'm not sure why everything's on the menu, but it looks like a small breakfast place would always make it a good choice. We ended up trying the burrito and chilaquiles. I think I've never tried the chicken enchiladas but the kids enjoyed the romaine lettuce and peppers on the side with the egg We also got the chilaquiles and they tasted yummy - spicy, just the right amount for me but not too much so that I could We also shared the chilaquiles with our fellow table-mates and the breakfast burrito was actually quite tasty. They serve lots of tea, coffee and fruit (which also makes the coffee that much better). So here's to many more delicious breakfast items!

I walked into Tony's today midday for lunch and was greeted by another woman. I went in, found my parking spaces open, and noticed that they had a new takeout spot. Tony was offering my a plate of thin crust pizza with lots of crust options and a variety of toppings. I rounded the corner and stepped into an open space and saw two people sitting with two slices of Pizza A. The vegetables were very tasty, and the slices were even more flavorful than any pizza I ever had in the past. At around 80 calories, the pizza was definitely worth the money. There was enough sauce and toppings to fill a plate without overly much added toppings. As the lady behind the counter mentioned, she claimed to be "one of the top pizza place in Los Angeles" so I wouldn't have given them  The pepperoni pizza was flavorful with the guacamole and basil. Their menu of pizza is something I'd definitely make a stop at next time I'm in Charlotte. Thanks Tony's for making my lunchtime experience as enjoyable as possible!

I stopped at Yokohama today to review what I thought was an enjoyable dinner experience. I ate at the previous location and I almost fainted because I just saw this place was closed for good. The sushi bar was nice and quiet. There's a nice bar with a view of the pool and bar for the ladies. The rolls are delicious, though not as fresh as some of the restaurants, but at over a medium size, it was still quite filling. Some of the best I've had, and as always, the rolls are inedible. This is a great spot to eat an additional piece of fish or vegetable. If you pick the special rolls, you can get 80% off (as the re-opened place is not open to the public). Also, they were served with fresh herbs so that gave a real Asian feel to the place. There is also a lunch special including a burrito, salad and rice bowl. This is an amazing and convenient place to find sushi. You won't be disappointed.

At the restaurant, I had to go to the bar first because I had to bring my lunch, so I had to stop to the door for my lunch. I arrived at 9am on a Friday and gotseated at the counter. Just the two of us, I mean, my son and Simone. I opted for the soup bowl - nice. Although we shared a couple of sandwiches, it was not until we walked away that we really experienced the place. I ordered the Cuban sandwich, which is another local special, as well as my favorite - the roasted garlic butter chicken sandwich. I think anyone would agree that the bun didn't stay up very well on the sandwich. It should not be an issue, but I did eat them to see what was coming up. The problem was that they were kind ofggy, so I couldn't really use the garlic mayo (the dip was made with cheese, so it also Not sure what the difference was between a grilled cheese and a microwaved sandwich, but I could tell that the sandwiches didn't get toasted We had some interesting conversation while ordering, but we didn't have time to drink any of our water immediately so we went with what was available: an orange I was a little disappointed that the soup cup was a little smaller than I wanted, but other than that, I was really happy to try it. It was clear that the food was very good so we probably had trouble getting full. I also enjoyed eating the sweet potato salad - it was so delicious, I couldn't even go to the bathroom!

I've been seeing Dr. Karanjia for three months now, and I love it! I had a knee injury a couple weeks ago (no problems with that injury in the meantime - we were at a dance with a His advice and care has helped me understand the process incredibly well. I like to work with people who aren't afraid to admit they are nervous or feel better when it's over. He gave me clear instructions and a good range of motion that I could use to get around. In my first appointment, I had to wear a one inch brace for two weeks. I had to try to re-injure myself during the five weeks, before I could wear the brace normally. I was told to keep the brace in for a couple of weeks. While there's no guarantee that my ankle will survive the big day, I was told that he would recommend a physiotherapist within a week Dr. Karanjia has now completed about 6 weeks of therapy and I can really see a difference in my ankle. I'm very happy that when I went to see Dr. Karanjia, I could talk to him, no matter the situation or the symptoms I was I really feel as though I have a very good team here. I've been going there for 84 hours and I've not had anything but a great experience.

This restaurant was very warm, yet packed with an excellent dining experience. I've had several dinners there in the past three weeks, and I've been hooked. My initial visit was a month ago and I ordered the garlic chicken flatbread with hummus and olive oil. I have to admit, the panini wasn't a bad choice, though the pizza crust was too soft and the sauce had soggy, sauce It also seems to be a nice, fast, and reasonable choice for lunch, especially if you have the time to eat all day. I ordered the chicken with a side of butter, garlic, onion, olive oil and ranch dressing, which was full of flavor, but I don The flatbread was fresh and made to order, and I found the garlic sauce to be very tasty. I even thought that it might be a little too salty. I would have preferred a little more chicken in the flatbread. The Buffalo  Burger was probably my favorite. The burger was awesome, with a light crust, salty, and tangy sauce. I really enjoyed our lunch and the atmosphere was comfortable and welcoming, making for a great meal for a friend or family member. The problem was that my mom didn't order their pizza because she ordered a pizza. I couldn't have been happier. We just love that they are a small restaurant but I recommend this place to anyone looking for diet friendly and quality restaurant dinner options.

Square One Coffee is pretty good. The only place I've been to in Manhattan where their coffee isn't quite as good as it's in the West Village (that's This shop is similar in concept to the Chicago shop on 13th Street. While the coffee is nothing new to me, it is delicious! I chose a coffee and a breakfast - a breakfast Americano with eggs on a hard roll. Generally, I prefer a stronger drink, but was pleasantly surprised with the vanilla and the banana coffee teas I've tried. Also, the barista said they had two options for the cup that he said would fit me better since I was already well-hydrated. We tried it out and liked the combination of the cold brew and the extra kick of their immune booster shot. It was a great choice based on the reviews to make it a great lunch stop and I recommend it to anyone looking for a quick pick- If I had the cold, I would definitely come back for more and try a couple other stuff because I'd really enjoy the barista and the

I don't have any therapy experience or anything near it. I really needed some help though! I had no idea where to find a therapist before (I don't go to a mental health center, but I work for insurance), and I was a bit of a nervous wreck. I am still learning as I go, but I've come to trust that Dr. Dennis Connolly. This isn't all about the therapy; you'll first meet a therapist at a free appointment. The man behind the phone does not want you to "agree" with the therapist, but does have an in-depth idea of what works best Then, you start receiving a written assessment of your feelings, strengths, goals, and challenges together. It doesn't get any more personal than that. So much so, that I decided for the following 5 sessions (at least 8 of them in total) that I was so happy to call the coaches and ask That guy is a total professional who cares about his clients and has a passion for their well-being. They're here to understand you and offer support and to let you know that you're not alone in your feelings and problems. It's been a very fun thing. Those first two weeks were incredibly powerful and, after I got out of those times, I was blown away by how much better things were. I feel like I'm finally making progress with my life and I'm not alone. I don't know enough about psychology, but I'd like to give it another look. I'm so glad to be able to share this experience with people who you might not, but would have known otherwise, to reach out to DCPS

On a Thursday night it snowed so I opted instead to try something new in the locals' hangouts. I had to come here again today to take advantage of their new Happy Hour menu. When we walked in, my boyfriend saw a big sign for burgers. During our first meal, I ordered a two-page list of burgers, so I wanted to try all of the different types. However, by that point the burger was all red, it was not medium, and it really just wasn't good. I could sense the beef being cooked inside and not just raw. It was gross as hell (not really a really gross situation for me as I don't like having my food sitting out on a hot plate all My boyfriend was confused about the burger and said he'd try to get the manager to explain things. I mentioned the issue to the staff and got them to comp it. The bartender gave me an estimate on what to expect when the burger came out, but still couldn't figure out why it was so raw. A couple minutes later it was placed back on the grill. As we sat down, I noticed the very top of the burger was red and not exactly at the center! I actually took that burger to the register before ordering a second, but it wasn't all that red - as I was about to eat The other half went bad, too, even though they said they had done their best to make it fresh and hot at once. In all, it should be alright, just different from what I remember from my first visit. We were very excited to try it again, and it turned out to be perfectly good. I do understand that this happened in the past but it's not really worth waiting for the food to be delivered to your door. I'd probably be willing to tip here again without a doubt. I haven't been to some of their other locations so far, but I can see how it could get a little out of hand sometimes.

I'm originally from downtown San Diego but am moving to Charlotte in a few months. It's the best place in the world to live. To celebrate her birthday last Friday, I headed to Old Post Lake Brewing Company to check out their new beer. It's a cute place to stop and pick up a pint of one of their beers and I got myself a six-pack while It was pretty easy to access by foot as it is located very close to downtown Collingswood and also a short distance to the parking area. The beer selection is great and the atmosphere is clean and fun. On a recent visit our group sampled six beers. I also enjoyed the local IPA and some of the other craft beers available. The staff was very nice and a lot more approachable than I was used to at most other places I've been to. I am so looking forward to going back for some brewery related fun!

We're so glad to be back at the Newburgh Brewery after some time, despite last weekend's super hot days. The bar seating is not tucked away and it's not too loud. The staff is the most friendly around and the menu was pretty awesome. Also, the bar staff is super friendly. In fact, to me, she just is the best bartender I have ever met.

From my point of view, Philly's tour company did nothing for us. The bus was in the neighborhood of Philadelphia, so we were able to get off the bus at a good spot. One of the tour guides was quite old and he was a little irritable and got really upset when we argued. The tour ended at the Museum of Modern Art but on the return trip to the bus, the guide really put his foot up. He was a really nice guy and really went out of his way to take us through the highlights of Philadelphia. He did a great job giving us information on the city and the attractions, but he was a bit off-putting because of the cheesesteak The tour guide would ask where was the cheesesteak we were trying and my grandmom reaction would be: "They are at the top of the There's nothing more expensive in the city than cheesesteaks." ...I will say I was surprised at his reaction. You have much better things to do in town!

This restaurant is great. The service was great, and we have stayed here multiple times. The food is authentic and very filling. The food was excellent. I had the eggs Benedict and my dining companion had a large sized breakfast plate. It was a small selection. The menu has several variety of eggs. I like the sweet potato wedges as well. There was also a great selection of eggs on the menu. All in all, The Dutch has a solid menu and they do a great job providing great service. At a coffee shop, that is usually a good sign of a good place.

Oyster House is a simple, local, healthy, fresh seafood restaurant that you can find at most supermarkets. We love the fresh seafood options at their restaurants and they have a great selection. We ordered the fish dishes, which were excellent. After cooking the fish the green beans tasted like fried beans that ended up spitting all over this dish. It was flavorful and I didn't have to go much further for salad because of how small it was. I had their baked salmon and anchovies Benedict with mushroom, spinach, clams and peas. We also had an extra side to share - hummus with chicken with olives. I'm not the best-like-them kind of person but I think the fish was really good so if there is one place I want to We really loved that we were able to try out this new restaurant so close to home.

I've been buying wines at this store for over 13 years. The glass is very sturdy and clear, the racks are well organized and there's plenty of space for everyone to taste some of the wines on display. They are good at what they do. I find the staffers nice and friendly. I have a bottle of red called the "Cavehouse Red" and when I got there, there was much confusion as to what it was,

My second lunch at Gemelli! A few weeks ago after finishing my summer classes, I headed to West Chester to meet my sister for dinner. To avoid a full day of driving, I wanted to shop a little on the way downtown. This was definitely my call. I was immediately greeted by a friendly staff who immediately ordered my coffee and introduced me to a little boy who needed his own! I didn't know they offered espresso so I ordered a simple latte, but instead ordered a  espresso with extra crema (my new favorite As a side note, when  checking out, I ordered my favorite caffè milkshakes: snipped. The flavor bombs were perfect -- they were sweet and smooth, but very subtle with a sour touch - that wasn't exactly the same That's when I came to the cafe really for the latte. I could tell she was going to love his atmosphere and coffee/gelato! Thank you Gemelli!

I decided to have dinner at Brio on Wednesday night when I was in town with my family. I don't mind a little loud, but Brio should be able to accommodate small parties at just about all their locations. The server, however, didn't put on make-up. We asked for a pitcher of water and he kept bringing us water until our server came. On top of that, when I said to her, "Hey, wait for me", she turned around and nodded. I'm not really sure if I was having issues with the drinks or if the server was trying to find a way to do better. My server and I were really pleased with the food. I ordered two salads and an entree. I tried a bite of cheeseburger and it was really good but I only ate an unidentifiable amount of it. My husband ordered the Chicken and Shrimp Alfredo dish which had two pieces of crab, three pieces of shrimp, three pieces of crab and 4 pieces of bread I really don't know what all was added to the ingredients but I was kind of disappointed because the sauce was not too rich and definitely didn't compare Our table was sitting on a high, tiled patio, so the view of the garden beyond the glass doors made the space feel rather empty. We were just a few feet from each other but it didn't feel like we were being treated well, too. The decor was too simple and stuffy to actually be entertaining. I just wish we didn't have access to that.

With the huge Japanese food truck being the only reason to have a meal in the middle of downtown Vancouver, I decided to come down to Fuji Mountain for dinner I was very surprised with all the green tea starters we had. The edamame was raw and hard which made it pretty tough to eat. The salad arrived with a large plastic cutlery plate and large, oversized leaves of salad dressing on the table. The combination of the dressing and the lettuce in the salad were very difficult to pick up with a fork. Maybe not, but I think it is odd to eat with chopsticks. My friends were shattered. Then it was time for the crab noodle soup. I'm still not going to call this soup "best green tea"; it's a delicious, but not particularly good, tangy fish Next, our waiter brought us a plate of three fish roll-filled mochis. It was a mix of red rice, orange rice, and a piece of fish (the roll also used to use a small bit of jalap For me, the tuna was one of the biggest problems so far, but still that's OK. The tuna roll that followed was the same, but with kaluinu. There were some delicious pieces of pork, but they were overpowered by the salty, salty, salty, salty roll sauce. I still really liked the chicken. It was also hard to hold my breath for a very large portion of stuff. We ate what we wanted; the rest of the rolls were disappointing. The portion size of the mochi compared to the rest of the meal, it was kind of like an adobe bifosco We actually got to speak to a couple of servers (in English) after our meal, and were able to talk about many of our experiences.

My husband and I were craving Mexican food for the second time in a few weeks. First off, we picked up a couple of tacos to go for our family last weekend. We had a large party of 5 and it took a while for us to order. We then ordered three starters, tacos and guacamole. The chips were pretty decent for such a small place. I really liked the sweetener, c.i.a., guac, (or, yea, sour are offered and try to try them because we didn't actually ask for anything or even know where to get them. The hummus was tasty. We loved the Black Bean hummus and the chips. with a bit of tamarind, but it's not as flavorful. They did offer a few sauces on the side on some of our tacos, though. There was one minor flaw with the fish tacos; they were veryggy and the fish was very little longer then the rest of the tacos This place is very small, so if it looks good on the outside, it seems good on the inside. I would be hesitant to eat here again, ever. However, the prices were reasonable for the quality and portion of the food (and I mean that in a good way). The second was a little bit more upscale. I ordered from their site and received a delivery order just minutes later. There was one taco, but I couldn't fit it into one. The shrimp tacos were the spiciest that I've had in a while, just a little soft and soft, with no They offered a small selection of guacamole and also offered chips and salsa on both visits. I'm not going to comment on the bar seating and bar stools, though. Their seating is quite poor. After the second experience, I plan on returning at some point (it's fairly close to home so we'll see how it goes).

I was in town for a recent work meeting and my boyfriend is vegan. I have had a number of issues in the past where I've had issues with my dietary restrictions. The day before the meal I was really nervous about dinner not being on the happy hour menu. I wasn't prepared enough for Marigold Kitchen to recognize that I was on a strict diet and allow me to choose anything else for dinner since we were I was able to confirm that there was actually no dairy, so we ended up dining instead where I had ordered fish and was ordered an appetizer. The food was not super meaty or anything like that, but they could easily accommodate if the chef mentioned it. Because I would have had to order fish for my entree and pass it to my boyfriend because he isn't sure that I can order even vegetarian Since our reservation was about a week to go, we went ahead and made our reservation. On my way into Marigold, it was very warm while all my food was on its way. And the waiters and cooks were all wonderful as well. The room we were in was an intimate space for a intimate dinner. The menu was a bit small so we ordered a glass of wine and a glass of red wine. We ended up having the fish and chips because it's so very easy to get up into the kitchen early and start eating! They were all huge and the staff was very patient with us. The kitchen offered a number of different items that paired well with the meal. We finished off our meal with an amazing glass of wine and a fantastic conversation. There were also very creative apps that were served up throughout the day. It was exactly what we were looking for and I already feel like we had ordered dinner at Marigold at the end of the week. Thank you to all the staff!

Thank you to everyone for a wonderful dinner with us at Talula's - we were all so happy to dine with you! We were very impressed. We went in thinking we had eat something and never went away hungry. The hostess, Natasha, was so helpful and was very understanding, even before dining. The restaurant has changed a little during the dining room renovation, so there was a large kitchen in the back room, and a larger counter with plenty I can't say enough about the food. The centerpiece of the tables included a small kitchen table that looked into a large green room. The food was just amazing - not to mention that we got a lot of excellent sides to share. We had an incredible dinner, including their sommelier's recommendation, and then some drinks. Of course, dessert was equally amazing and had an amazing decadent taste to it, too. And no disappointment, as our desserts came immediately after dinner on an adorable cake pop and a treat that was delicious. The menu looked great and Talula's Daily was my go-to place when I had an opportunity to experience it early in the year. It was an outstanding experience!

The food at this cafe was very good, and I can't really say when it opened. We went to this joint after lunch before our trip to New York, which made it kind of easy to drive to Brooklyn and eat just as much food as It also offered some good lunch specials, including their famous shakshuka (think Greek salad). I could not understand why they used Russian onions and a mixture of halved Russian cabbage, mushrooms, and garlic in a shakshu Ours was pretty filling, so I wasn't too grossed out about it. This is the first time I've had such good food at a cafe, and we had a great time. The food was good for lunch, but not great enough to warrant a return trip.

This bath is very relaxing. I suspect my son will appreciate some of them more than others because he's got a big sip or two, and he loves the fact I don't get him, because this place is great. My boyfriend and I have been very fans of fry trucks (we've been to the ones in Edinburgh over the summer), but this week we had a This amazing trailer came up the block from us at the O'Hare Festival. A good friend and I browsed the menu several times beforesettling on the waffle fries (Snap or Shake, Hot or Cold... etc I ordered a double chocolate chip fritter with ham and cheese as a side. I'm not sure if I really enjoyed these potatoes but they were delicious. After about 15 - 15 minutes the fries were ready! I did not notice any spices and the potatoes were absolutely excellent, especially the pecans and chocolate chip. We both left full and full with leftover fries! Everything we ordered was fantastic! They were definitely a hit and the truck was very crowded.

On a recent Saturday afternoon, husband and I decided to try out Pizzeria Biga in the North Tower. Biga was just opened this week (here) and is one of my favorite Italian restaurants around the area. We went for dinner and had drinks as part of our dinner. The drinks were made within 2 minutes of ordering; a few bottles of wine, beer, and sake. We chose two different pizzas (the cheese pizza and salami pizza with olive oil and extra olives) and a few salads - I ordered We shared a caprese salad mixed with fresh tomatoes, red onion, garlic, fennel and a light pesto. A small serving of salad was left to sample as I didn't have a taste for the pizza. Then we ordered two pizzas, the burger and the spicy calzone. They were all incredibly good and perfect to kick things off. The pizza was pretty good too, and we finished with an afternoon of wine, pizza, drinks and bread. You can read the review of one of our past dinners here.

I ordered a three-roll combo for lunch from Japanese Sushi-o and it was delicious with a cup of ice for $13 before tip I ordered the chicken tempura roll and the spicy tuna roll and a seafood salad for $17.99. I was happy to do so, but I thought it would be harder to get good sushi as soon as it gets there. The rolls were fresh or maybe it was their special roll that day. The rolls were seasoned well and had just a few little pieces of tuna and yellowtail. I would definitely try them again. One of the other rolls that didn't make the minimum was the seafood salad. My lunch wasn't satisfying because I spent 15 minutes on the table. I would say I should go back to order it.

When I went for lunch the other night, I got off-color with my lunch  Burger, which was a heavy, chewy chicken burger with While Rex offers a variety of dishes, my first reaction was to order a burger and fries because I was feeling sluggish. I had the salmon tacos, having never had them before (I'm getting old by now), so I had no idea what other dishes I might The fish tacos arrived before the usual lunch rush at 3pm. The fish tacos were light and delicious with a great, crisp texture to them. The tacos were filled with every seasoning and a perfect portion of fish. Despite their good reputation, the waitress was a little slow to welcome us and didn't give us the time of day we requested. Allison was just so happy during her run to pick up her next job, after which she offered to split the tab and let the staff take care of me. The server was incredibly helpful and informative. Rex will definitely be in my future go-to. The waitresses were also sweet and efficient.

The restaurant is small, and the staff is pretty friendly. The happy hour drinks were a lot cheaper than at other local happy hour options, so I would recommend going early in the evening for a good deal. All of Harvest's food is made with organically grown produce (which is a lot. The cheese flatbreads are tasty, good for you and also have a couple of the health benefits of plain  yogurt and cream cheese. There is also a jumbo cup of juice available for under $8. There is also a lot of selection of wine and mixed drinks on tap, but the best part is the price. There weren't a lot of wines on the menu either and we were pretty much left on our own after drinking a lot of those so there was Good news, Harvest offers a pretty good happy hour selection.

In recent months I've started going back to this Frenchy joint and I'm really looking forward to it. It's so great to see the place getting a modern upgrade. This place has several of the best happy hour and late night bites. I love that their drinks are a good variety. I've even tried the elk dinner (for $26). There is also a nice bar at the rear for those guests interested in dancing to one of the many live bands. I feel like I've come full circle. I'd highly recommend this restaurant to others.

I'm a frequent latte and lattes aficionado. I've visited it a few times, and I usually try to go later in the day. I love this place. Coffee..yay. Before lunch, we were greeted by a small, friendly staff and made our way to Burj Khai Thai, located in the Old Town  While we were excited to have lunch here, we just knew something was wrong. A friendly server helped us find our seats, which took a good two minutes. The restaurant has a beautiful environment with modern Thai design. It didn't feel as busy as I expected, given that the restaurant has a long wait line. When our server came out and served the food, he didn't seem to have much to say, especially when our meal came out because it took  The staff didn't seem to mind that there was a wait for our food. We decided to share a gyro platter of chicken, beef, green onion, and garlic broth. It had a slight crunch but was delicious. A good combination and very creative. Then we ordered our entrees. A little fried food on the side was very refreshing. We both feel that everything we ate today was worth it. The food was good, and the place looks and feels great.

Although we do love Chinese food, we have to be somewhat wary of attempting to eat it. It's usually just too much hassle for us to settle on one. I was able to go to Garage on a Friday night around 9.45pm. It was 93 degrees outside, but it was quite pleasant inside! I came downtown for lunch one day this past spring, which was when a friend of mine was at the hotel, but I didn't know what to The staff was friendly and helpful and we shared a cup of oyster soup while everyone else opted for fish and chips. I ordered the clam and lobster soup, which came with a generous portion of sliced oyster shells and a nice pile of fresh white fish  The sauce with lemon juice and salt and pepper was good enough, but I probably wouldn't order it again and then feel like I needed anything else. A few pieces of shellfish mixed the flavor in, along with the chowder and the salad, and it was great. The restaurant was packed with people and I was pleased to notice a good crowd. I wasseated right away and the waiter came to us in order. However, my table mates started to get off on separate plates. Regardless, they were friendly enough to check on us before we paid, and they were willing to fill in any questions we had to make sure everything was settled Whether we had to wait another five minutes for the plates was in the hands of the restaurant staff and wait timers is clearly a problem for them It wasn't all a lot to work with and it had a somewhat clumping texture, making it unappetizing to  On the chowder side, I had a small helping of gumbo, accompanied by four tiny oyster crackers on each side,  The oysters were perfectly sized, moist and deliciously seasoned, but the clams were definitely overdone and not as good as I The restaurant is somewhat modern and doesn't have too many decor details or a lot of seating on a busy weekend. Unfortunately, there are still signs of the winter here. However, the interior had dark, humid colors and a smattering of dirty windows. I would recommend this place to diners who want more comfortable seating. If you're looking for a quiet lunch option with a friendly and helpful server, then Oyster House can get your evening going and really enhance We were both so satisfied with our entrees that I pushed my way back to try the seafood dish on my next visit.

Last night (Tuesday, October 1), my husband and I went to A.kitchen and picked up a delicious dinner at their restaurant We were going to review here, but last night I wanted to point out a particularly cool spot: a.kitchen, the food is incredibly I don't know if you've been there before but I knew what we ordered when we walked in the door. For our main course, our table ordered a delicious plate of roasted pumpkin and cube squash with caramelized onions and roasted figs. The squash cooked perfectly, the figs were cooked perfectly, and the seasoning perfectly complimented the dish. I would definitely order that again every time it's served! It was also perfect for my vegan friend who loves pumpkin and figs. I definitely plan to come back and try the salad too. Our waitstaff provided excellent service, and I had a great time. It was one of the best dinners I've had this year! We also had the Pecan Cake and Chocolate Tart (I had it with hot coffee). We had enough of our main courses to still have a great place to dine! I was extremely disappointed with our black Russians though. We got the wrong one, as usual - Kahlua was served in a tall glass bowl. I loved the drink, it was really sweet (I'm not a big fan of iced beverages). But the bartender didn't offer Kahlua to us. but what kind of place was that? This time, it didn't happen with this trip, but I hope they addressed that because it was very minor. Would definitely go back!

I had the pepperoni bread for lunch because I just want to eat like the old man, and it was simply delicious. Then there's their Italian stuffed bread, which is a multi- layer bread filled with various toppings such as cheese, cheese blends or This is the "house" pizza at The Bread Basket. I was a little late for my second Vietnamese takeout meal. In November (around July), my husband and I arrived in Vegas to check out the popular vegan restaurant, Vietnam Palace. However, the restaurant was closed and had no sign of reopening. When you walk in you'll probably be greeted by a host. It wasn't too late. I got the pork noodle soup and added the soup cubes. I ordered some chicken wings then a serving of beef soup topped with lemongrass shrimp (I love lemongrass shrimp since they give you better taste and are I called the restaurant just before 6 am and the manager/owner called the restaurant and placed the order. The beef soup came out very flavorful and my dog enjoyed it. So if you want Vietnamese food, I would defy you to visit Vietnam Palace. The Thai and ice cream was also very good, and they were prepared beautifully and fresh. It did sound good and a nice change to your usual chain Vietnamese food place. My experience was great and the atmosphere was a little rushed, but I was told that they had a very friendly staff and they could accommodate small parties

In case you're wondering, we ate at Sawatdee a couple days ago. I was there on my week's lunch off, so I was actually pretty happy to be back! I wasn't disappointed. It was so nice to go out and enjoy some good Thai. The food was not only fresh and delicious, it was also very affordable. We started with the peanuts and rice for starters. This is what you should get if you want really delicious chicken skewers or just something to get you going without getting hungry. We also ordered a mochi eung sau and a pair of pad kee mao gari. The pad kee mao gai was spicier than it should be, in any case. I probably shouldn't have went with two stars of heat, because the burn was just too much. I understand there's a lot of people that like their Thai food hot, but this was something new and very unlike what I've tasted in I think I'll go spicily next time. But the Pad Thai was really good. If you like the texture of the pad thai, you'll love the way it's cooked. Meh..very thick and filling. They taste just as good, if not better than they would be if you took them home. I ordered the tangy lemongrass chicken bowl to wash the down in. I couldn't finish my meal, but I was very satisfied. The pad kee mao gai is a great soup for soupy meals, but it could also be served warm. I'll be back and let you know what I think.

Good food.Weird food. Nice waiter.Plenty of delicious food. Nice service..and the price. Some of the staff at A.kitchen are also pretty darn expensive. You end up paying over $30-$60 for two people. Although there was a crowded server that helped out a bit, in the end the portions were just too small. After paying the bill, they delivered two and a half hours later than expected. I ordered the fried octopus and crab pieces, crab legs and a vegetable dish. It was pretty flavorful. The beets and salad were good but I'm not sure they'd be memorable without that little help from the crab. My table then ordered the bottarga soup (the same soup I've had for years). The taste of the  Fettucine's was very good and I'm not a big fan of pasta with beans, but the viti I like Italian fare and it had plenty of flavor. I loved the greens but the fettucine was also drowning in salt and soggy white arugula that was a welcome change The desserts were all sweet and decadent. At first I didn't like either of my dessert dishes, but later on I started to like them. I had a good time with my friends. Will the prices hold up? I wasn't really sure. I like restaurants that are a little more formal and have lower prices.

This theater was not nearly as cheap as the Ritz in Old City. I'd heard the tickets were going fast, but the prices were definitely not worth the wait. So I decided to stay off from all drinks and to go to the food court. In fact, the movie was only $5.45 with $2.59 for a bottle of coke. It was a little less than $15 of something else! A bottle of water would cost just $2.50. Despite being pretty dated and dated, the lobby, walls, and ceiling were pretty gorgeous, and the food courts had excellent service. It was also nice that the seats were comfortable.

Cherry Street's lunch menu was excellent. After some serious slogging through New York for a few days, we settling in for two of their Nachos & Beans. The good news was they were served with a side of guacamole and cheese on top. Aside from putting the food into our mouths, the bartender spent some time explaining the different salsas they offered - so much fun! The one good thing are the chips are actually pretty fresh. Then we had a beef patty sandwich as the rest of the meal. You can also opt to have the regular ground beef and French fries with some pickled sauerkraut and iceberg lettuce. The sandwich was delicious - hot and steaming, but also smoky enough to cool my pallet as I eat. There were a bunch of topping options as well since the sandwiches were on a thin crust, but I enjoyed the flavor. The atmosphere was nice.

Curiosity Doughnuts opened its doors on Monday (December 5th) at 1080 West 15th Street in The Bronx. The day of my visit, I had read that they were going out of business and that they were moving from their old location in Norwalk, OH to There were only a few of us in the car, and after driving for some time in the cold, I was glad things had settled in so much so No one had tried it yet. One more frog in the line, and we made our way to the window before anyone could start moving forward. We didn't have much time to think; we ended up eating the whole pot of doughnuts and deciding between four doughnuts. So let's just just say we made it to the door for our infamously long wait. Maybe it had something to do with the time, or the frigid temperatures that I was in. But if I had to wait, it would have been a total waste of time. I'm so happy I stuck it out and got in, because my glazed doughnut went down so fast. There were over 20 people sitting down, all of them starving. The waiter took great care of us while we were greeted by the delicious people outside. When we rolled out of there, there was still a swell of customers to pick from. Curiosity Donuts were excellent. They were so light and crisp with just the right amount of brown sugar and cinnamon that I could literally eat one entire bowl of them. I didn't choose one of the flavors on that day, but I did adore them all when I did. This was my first experience with a donut, which has always been an amazing experience. And it's so easy to find them in stores in Boston and Philadelphia - now you can, too. I'll definitely be back. I loooove curiosity.

You often know what kind of craft beers are good at the breakfast table or brunch hours. If you are looking for a laid back Irish pub in the Lower City that serves delicious Irish coffee and brunch options, Head Me Home is your place. The drinks are not cheap, but they're all made fresh using the best ingredients and our mains were delicious. I wasn’t really into eggs, but the egg white coating the meat in the MacBenedict was just tooggy. The ham was well seasoned and the salmon was just perfect. I was pampered by the nice people at the bar, who were friendly and helpful, and the bar servers were always so welcoming and helpful. We will definitely be back to get an Eggs Benedict again soon.

And this is the one I'm talking about. The owner, Tom Bidornio, has spent thousands of dollars in remodeling the store into the place where the donuts really hit the mark I won't say no to this place for the fantastic flavor to boot: you will almost certainly be returning for more.

I first came in to visit this place about a month ago and I can't really remember anything bad about it yet. We were looking for an affordable restaurant within the Old Town core that also had a nice Vietnamese atmosphere and great food, so I kindly suggested this place. We finished off each app with either a tropical coconut drink or a Thai drink. We ordered the spring rolls outside so it was very hot on the outside, but really good inside. The food was very substantial (but not too heavy). My friend and I shared the coconut shrimp salad and my wife got the Thai beef and chicken. The limeade was nice and creamy though it could have used some fresh basil. The meat dishes were very rich, the vegetables were cooked to perfection and the beef dishes were very flavorful. Both were incredibly flavorful and was made to order in large portions. The decor of the place was very inviting and the service was really fast. Very satisfied with the food and service. Food really was great and my husband and I just can't wait to check out more things at their new location. I have had similar experiences there with better meals and I look forward to more.

We went to TAB with a group of 11 for the first time while we are on trip. The place is super nice and it's definitely a laid back place with a great location. It was nice seeing their live DJ with the rest of the group. I was a bit hungover from my shopping and felt quite gross at the end of our visit so it felt much like a good thing to just I ordered a French onion soup with fresh baked dough and a French cheese poboy. The chorizo quesadillas, though, were good. I would have given it 5 stars but they were just inedible. It was like they tried to make the cheesecake bread with some cheese to give it some texture but really didn't succeed. They did not get the job done for me. The sweet and hot sauce was tasty and I liked the  salsa and not much other dressing. I was so disappointed with the Poutine that we didn't order it. The sauce was great and the cheese was flavorful. I ordered the chorizo quesadillas and they were a little burnt. The Poutine was great and the potatoes were quite fresh. The food was well prepared, which was great, especially for a restaurant like this. I did check out the bar at the time.

We had never ordered from Pumpkin until last week. When I called pumpkin last week with a question about why we were waiting to order takeout when the restaurant hours were open, the owner assured me, " We was finally able to check it out on Facebook and loved everything we tasted and ordered. It was a little tough to find the menu on their website even though Pumpkin had posted several options. My husband and I were really excited, because every item was perfect! We received a confirmation email that the order had been placed and had been processed. It wasn't even that long before we knew that our dinner would be delivered. Our cart was full. My husband thought the prices were really reasonable and felt proud. I'm not usually one to use a plate on my bare cabinets, but the plates they gave me were beautifully designed, very clean and perfectly The food was the highest quality we've had from any other takeout place. Our entrees were fantastic. We started with a salad and then moved onto a prime rib (the steak was excellent) and then the deluxe pulled pork. I'm proud to say that Pumpkin has been an excellent example of a restaurant-quality dining experience in the area while ensuring that we are able Halloween's takeout will be on our back list and our kids will be waiting to go home during the flu season. Hope you had a wonderful fall/winter, and thank you to all!

Food was terrible and the bar was small, which made it difficult to stand around for conversation with other patrons. We ate at the airport wing of Tootsie's on Wednesday. Anyway, the rest of the restaurant was very average. We left shortly after 7pm. I can only give this place a "1" because at least we got a free meal at the restaurant. And let's not forget the food. We came within five minutes (six minutes for dessert, after eight), and we had to order a cup of ice tea and a shot of It's too late to have been able to do a good job since there are so many places at the airport to eat. I always don't have any good blowout days, just because it feels a little like I wasn't getting my hair right. They are super friendly and great with their services! I thought this place looked wonderful, but based on the first two reviews, I thought it shouldn't be hard to find a spot, since they I was very excited to get my style done. She made my hair shine and grew my hair back incredibly fast. She also asked about the style of my hair and put it together very well! I can't wait to go back for my haircut and color since it looks so healthy. The tech was good - great to have for a great blowout. Although a little cold, the Salon was clean and spacious and I look forward to returning!

The Acme Steakhouse opened in October and was a welcomed addition to the downtown area. Upon seeing the new building in April, I knew I'd have to make it on my next visit. We started at the bar and stayed for brunch. We started off inside the restaurant as the patio was pretty much empty. There are also a couple restaurants on the property, the first being the restaurant (formerly the pub) on the first floor. There was more than enough room for the ladies to take advantage of the free drinks. During my bachelorette party, the first floor seats were almost all occupied, but the second floor seats were so tiny, I didn't even feel The roof deck has great views of the city and it was cool despite the heat. I ordered a breakfast burrito bowl and the other ladies got a half salad and a slice of chocolate cake. We left with plenty of memories and a whole lot of food for the next week. The service was a little slower than the restaurant's other competitors, but was still spot on.

Well it should be obvious that I'm a Yelp lover, but it seems that Five Guys isn't one of my favorites. This was our first time to the place and was our first experience at Five Guys. Five guys seemed like a great choice to eat in near our house because the parking wasn't bad. We walked in and saw the sign for a casual neighborhood burger place. There is no seating, so we walked up to the counter. We ended up ordering the burgers with fries. The bacon comes out about 3" thick and the fries are about 3". My burger came out underseasoned, and I was so hungry and wanted it to be seasoned but the fries were already cooked on the bottom. Just one more wait! What was great was the fresh and flavorful fries. During that time we enjoyed some good service and friendly conversation with the owner. He asked the next person what was in them, and we both noticed the bacon and cheese were almost completely covered in fat. I don't think I'd look for something that is completely healthy as I feel like meat is an overkill. I did agree that it didn't come with enough mayo but it wasn't terrible. While a bit overpriced for the food it was enjoyable and my chicken was cooked to perfection!

I hired YES DJ services for my 20th bachelorette party. They were great to work with. She was incredibly knowledgeable and made everything very clear and clear in the first few days of rehearsal. The DJ was awesome. He was absolutely perfect. He worked with us closely and asked me to give him some guidelines to play certain music that I wanted him to play. I was very happy with how the playlist turned out and that was one of the greatest things I've been able to say about Tina and her service The lighting for the celebration was the same thing we had in the planning stages (a really bright, clear LED lighting system). The special effect lighting was set up in two rooms, one at the back/front entrance and another at the back of my entrance. I was hoping they would give it a good run around, but it was actually just a little too bright. The lighting was amazing and the event had a great flow, even though the DJ services could have been a bit more interesting. So I asked for a few more weeks of light before ordering the Gobo again. If I had thought that this lighting could be really eye-catching, my guests probably wouldn't have minded having it at the party as it could be

I'm loving Thai Square & The New Orleans Market! My local fast food delivery is at The Quick Fixx. I found that I could delivery myself the following week, and my dinner meal and tip were only $14 plus tip. Normally, I'd pick a standard burger from the menu of my local fast food restaurants because I'm a meat lover and a I can give The Quick Fixx a three star rating but if I'm a fan of their recipes and want to try new things, I The menu is huge, easy to sift through and full of healthy options, including soups, salads, sandwiches, and entrees. You can even add toppings to your soup as well. It was perfect as shown. I thought that was a nice perk. It was hotter than everyone else had made it so I ordered two small baskets next door. Well, it cost me $2.50 before tip! He sat me down right away, brought out the pizza, and delivered me the items. I ordered an order of the Tuscan Chicken Taco Bowl and it was delicious! I'll be coming back for lunch next week for my boyfriend. Thanks again Matt and The Quick Fixx.

Continental Midtown is a popular bar in Philadelphia for its patio and dining area (It gets me every time! but) but there are a number of problems which are starting to detract from the atmosphere. First, don't forget the glasses! The drinks are usually served with an extra martini glass, which, my friend at the bar would rather leave behind. After a few drinks and no table of real glass, they served us everything in plastic. Second, the food. The pool was not soggy from the patio table or the outdoor bar-- more like a puddle in the water with an open puddle I tried to bring the waters (they were a few steps away) out but they had spilled all over my clothes and food. The third, the patio has an enticing view, but it is so crowded that it leaves people feeling alone. When you get the restaurant back and renovated, you'll be happy to hear that the owners got back on track.

I really enjoyed the service, coffee, and decor at this place! They serve their hot chocolate from a small glass window behind the shop. You have a hot chocolate bar in the front window. My husband and I both agreed, that I could probably get a cup of their hot chocolate flavored mocha latte. After a few minutes of waiting, I said a quick call to a manager and was told that the latte had to be made using the We watched the windows change, but our server seemed more interested in our drink order and told me a coffee was available. The coffee was very light and very good. Other people stated that they ordered the other coffee. I'm going to try something different when I return.

I live in San Francisco and I love Subway! Five footlooooonnnngs!!! I'm a Subway shopper. (I didn't ask for the full price, but if you want to see what I'm talking about that's fine too). From the time I check in to the time you leave, it just feels so good to have access to so many cheap, cheap, cheap Subway choices! That's what I do, and I'm very picky. Not to mention being vegan! I don't want to get off track any more... because they have great vegan menus. This has helped me get healthier while remaining at the gym. They are very generous with sauce, just make sure to ask a couple of questions before they serve you and don't make you feel odd at the table

We went to Victory Brewing Company today for a tasting. After walking around the nearby Kennett Square area (I had to stop and watch at this sign), it was easy to be seated in the outdoor patio This was my first time here and I had to try some of their selections since we weren't really feeling the burgers we wanted. We ended up sharing our beer and the experience was really great! We went to Victory for lunch and it was perfect. Most of the menu is seafood, so we went with some of their favorites. That's what really piqued my interest, so I ordered the salmon edamame and hummus and it tasted fantastic. They also had a salmon salad on the menu, so it was a good way to start. The salad came with romaine ribbons and the salmon was cooked perfectly. I was really glad I've been going. I ordered some deli meat smears and some potato-filled pretzel ciabattas. We also had some very unique sundaes which were great as well. We really liked Victory, and I definitely plan on making another trip to this neighborhood to grab some lunch and enjoy a drink.

I'rin' out for my second fixx this weekend, and I think they're going to have me down on the floor of my apartment because In fact, it took me 45 minutes to get our meals out. There are not a lot of dishes, but I'm willing to bet that they have very well executed and interesting dishes. One big problem with this place if you like Italian food that's cheap is that the pasta bowls are very small. I had pasta and a side of pizza, and I was not at all hungry for more than a few bites. My pasta and pizza both went great, but a decent deal at $18 for two plates was kind of stingy. But it's not the most popular selection out there, not even close. However, one of the things I didn't like was the croutons. The service was good, the food was really plated and on time, but at the price of just $18 for a meal of this size,  But otherwise it ended up being kind of meh. I was really impressed from a fast delivery and great selection. And that's all I can say.

The food and drink at Green Aisle is amazing. I went to Green Aisle last year, and not only did I love their great selections on high-end kosher food, I expected to in the back of my neighborhood, and stoked that my favorite local market was getting a makeover. No more crowded wine bars, no more cheap lunches, no more ghetto food for a night out with pals with the The small, local shop has a pretty strong specialty selection - everything from pickles, preserves, and ice cream to fruit and spices. Everything they buy is sourced exclusively from sustainably sourced and fair-trade producers from around the country. You can't go wrong shopping here. Green Aisle is a fine grocery shop full of quality food products with an awesome sense of community. They are the owners of the shop, and it shows right in the selection of products at Green Aisle. We bought a few things we wanted to try and had a chance to experience and feel the goods first-hand. I'd love to see some of these items in the store.

This market is great. As we walked through the door it was verycrowded. The food was delicious and the prices were low, but I don't let that stop me from paying close attention to the quality. I didn't have time to stop there and pick up a dozen items which was a big deal. I need to do a bit more research to find the location of this amazing store! Especially for $10 ice cream.

I thought this was such a great lunch spot - I've never had it before, but I had to check it out for myself! Whether you're trying to avoid animal products or want to go "vegan" on your own, they provide a great introduction. Over the past two weeks we have been trying a new restaurant (Pestos). I was excited to be able to pick up a delicious vegetable salad and a hot dog. These are super ripe and healthy, and a lot cheaper than most restaurants as well. I'm a foodie! So I was not quite sure whether I would enjoy those or the latin chop. I loved the way the fried tortillas seasoned with an herb and garlic sauce tasted. This was a great lunch and for a little bit more than the price, I liked how they changed the ingredients in half of the taco. I had the red sauce on it as an added bonus, but I had to give it another try despite being only one of three people having that choice. I still can't believe that I could eat fajitas all day! The service was good but slow but seemed to be a little busy during the lunch hour on Tuesdays. It was all made and topped with a lot of yams and carrots but they just weren't as tender and creamy. This whole deli and delivery dinner cost me less than $18 which gives me some credit for ordering and eating so delicious, healthy food rather than spending more. We'll definitely be back. I'd definitely order again!

I've been going to this place for a while and had high expectations. I haven't found a better restaurant to watch NFL games than Frida Cantina - not only is tequila Orders are typically sent within an hour to a restaurant location within Philadelphia. We have a bit of a meat addiction but not as much as it used to be.

I've always loved Terminal F at the MTS, and this really is my favorite. I believe it's pretty good - they're still trying to keep it better than their formerly awful main terminal. It is super easy to get to from the terminal, as most of the lines are underground. You do not have to stand in line, and you can always pay yourself on-site when you get off! Another bonus is that there's now a lounge/conway, so you can be pre-booked to meet fellow travelers at the airport. The food options are all excellent - some great schtuff like Cushman & Wakefield, Joey's, etc. If you have a kid, you'll love this place!!

In the last three months I've been to Kidari for lunch two or three times a week. My first was last season and the second was in September. The chicken noodle salad tastes amazing. I love the fresh ingredients with the aji sauce but I never thought I'd try that dish. I chose the spicy salmon roll as it was really filling. The last time I went there I had the green tea iced dessert app. Kidari also serves some super popular appels. I've been to other places around the area and these are the only one I know which does not have a $1 dollar minimum or more. This year, Pure Health Food opened a location in the Village Center. It's in Park Square next to IKEA. It's clean, spacious, healthy, and with an emphasis on healthy, simple foods as much as it is on healthy, high-calorie options. The sandwiches are low-calorie and are sold by the pound, too. The shushi was awesome! I was so happy for the fact that the other two reviews on Yelp gave us a bad review. I recently recalled my late morning drink at the Alameda Tavern. As a result of my recent trip home, my beloved, and my adoring, three-year-old daughter had recently come home and stayed The hotel has been open for what seems like forever because it has been. In the last twelve years, I've gone from'very good' to 'poor' to 'ducky not so good' It was dark in there and that feeling lingered through me for a long time before my eyes were closed. This is not a bad place to sit and drink and watch football. The bartender had a sad face and scolded me for letting my girlfriend stay the night. I won't go there again, because of all the memories and vibes I felt when in there. The drinks were still good. I really enjoyed their bourbon sandwhich and beer.

I've ordered from Talula's twice now, and both times were good too. The first time we went, we were both pretty excited with the new lunch menu that they added. We ordered a breakfast sandwich and hot coffee, which included Turkey and Swiss croissants. We were lucky that the croissant was very clean and the cup was pretty tall. The waiter brought it over to our table and I spilled out my coffee. And then I realized that he was also the guy who filled up the coffee, causing him to burst into tears. We both had to ask the waitress if he wanted more. In general, there was about 20 people in front of us and it's quite an insulated seating area. It comes with deliciously priced coffee and is a great place to stop in while you are waiting for your food. We ate here at lunch while walking down the busy main square, which is very exciting. Also the food is very good. On a recent visit, we opted for an unsweetened cup of espresso, which was delicious. If you are a beer-loving person, I think you'd want to try the pork chops, although the sauce was quite salty. The menu is small (think a few entrees and apps), but has a really great selection. We have to go back to see for ourselves, though. Looks like a great place to catch your Sunday coffee fix.

After a week of vacationing and eating out with my best friends, I went to the Prime Stache in Seattle for dinner. One of the owners was so kind and made sure we had great wine and drinks. The bartender was so friendly and knowledgeable about their menu and bartenders and was so knowledgeable about what the best drinks were for her and her friends One of the girls said that a different brand of glass could make as bad as this one, so I tried out a different cocktail; te We didn't order any appetizers, because there was no menu for our main dishes. There's a small portion of house salads and a small portion of tapas, which makes it a great place for lightish- She ordered the pizza napoleon - if you're interested in a light dish I would recommend the pizza napoleon We ordered a couple other items, and my friend chose the house tacos. The food was great, and we ate right away - there were two empty glasses for each of us. I just wish they could have topped them with a bit more marinara sauce but that wasn't the case. The drinks were also fairly affordable and the menu was very varied. For dessert, you walk up and sit down at the bar that's directly across from the main kitchen and your server will bring you a selection of tart I highly recommend checking out this restaurant to make sure you can take advantage of their Happy Hour on Saturday and Sunday for just $50.

I've been seeing 19 Degrees for a while now and I really like the new exterior. In fact, their layout and decor are very similar to the one I'm used to from my first stop. They serve a wide variety of sandwiches there, including all the popular sides of a deli and I've become a fan because of the variety I ordered a hummus wrap to go along with my chicken salad which I was a bit disappointed with. Just not the same. However, in my opinion, that doesn't matter to me because I can order a sandwich at other places. If they weren't pricey, their burger might be a little pricey, but that's a fair trade for the quality.

I love this location! I've been to several of the other restaurants around town and this is the first one I've been to that does good business. I always love the "Ol' General" there because he's one of the best servers I've ever experienced. Aside from all-you can-eat items, the chicken and waffles are great. But, the ol' General's bourbon-based soup tastes weird. I don't think I'll ever order the Chicken Tenderloin. Went back with a group of friends yesterday after a recent visit to the restaurant and was not impressed. I purchased a table so that I and two of my guests could try the restaurant out before visiting San Antonio. I sat down at a comfortable chair that felt great because it was in a chair and I could get away with using only three wheels. Having read so many reviews I expected that the food would be very good, too. As we sat at the table, guests started to take their order. We had a choice of two courses on the plate - several different kinds of salads, some roasted vegetable plates and one main course. We were both very impressed with the octopus salad, which was perfectly grilled and mellowed with a very simple side of goat cheese At that point I decided that a little change of pace was the way to go. I also made an offer to get the dish of the day with a steak dinner. Upon resuming eating, I noted that even though there was no sauce for the sole, the texture was good and it was a nice size The tuna dish was very good, seasoned generously with tuna sauce. My friends were also surprised by the sides with peas, carrots, onions, and cranberries. I was disappointed. Not with the salmon, chicken, or steak, definitely. It came out really salty and dry tasting (I don't know if it had an overachiever odor or not. ), and it wasn't very spicy. The menu calls it the crispy chive crusted sole, but the fish was more of a dry, tough,  bland chicken dish. A lot of the plates had extra green beans and the fish was grilled so I didn't realize it was being overdone. You can tell that the staff knew this but still wanted to make sure we were all warm. We gave ourselves another bit of time and ordered dessert. The cake was sweet and cake wasn't as bad as I thought it would be. The wine experience was fine but definitely more on the "I don't care" side than the entrees.

This is the end of the restaurant review of my week in Atlanta. I was very pleased with the service from my waitress when we came in the door, even though I know there were about 50-100 people there in the I'm sure he tried to do his best not to let the bad aspects ruin the experience. Also, we came around this time to look at the menu, so I knew it was going to be the right place in the city. It was a fairly normal weekend brunch here. Despite the fact that the wait would only be around 30 minutes (so there was no time wait), we were seated quickly and treated to food and So that afternoon, we were all ready. We ordered a large bowl of white beans and toast and a fruity chicken plate with ranch and coleslaw. Our server arrived with all of the eggs we needed, and then came by with two more eggs. While it took a little longer to make it, after that they started delivering food. The rest of our party was sitting around waiting for their plate to arrive. They were not complete at all. The wait was terrible. If you count the time between the first and second plates, the server had 10-12 tosses. It was too long to have everything ready and our server tried to get everyone to eat, but it was too early to get everything. Our server, not really aware of the situation, took no responsibility for the delayed arrivals of dishes. We were all hungry, but the food was super salty. One woman ordered an egg benny that was a bit overcooked. She was upset about not being able to try this dish and it wasn't what she'd ordered. I ordered the chicken ham sandwich. She returned again and received an omelet. She had been seated for 10 minutes in the wait, so when this was taken back from her, she got the dish back to me and said she didn The waiter immediately noticed this and stopped. We all quickly informed him we had ordered an omelet and that it looked better. The omelet was just more salty than anything I'd ever had before because of the salt. I started to eat it, but then the meal went downhill a couple of hours later. There was also a guy who had a quesadilla plate, and he wasn't great. Unfortunately, they were a total bust. And our server was totally uninterested. We did a little shopping, so it was nice to have food we'd been waiting for. And most of the food was definitely not worth it. My husband ordered his own plate even though he said it's a huevos rancheros.

A couple of friends invited me to dinner and were looking for a fun restaurant to have dinner with them on a Saturday night. Meal planning had never been my thing so we headed to one of the best places to dine on the Hudson: The Kitchen. The inside was clean and the outdoor area was filled with shade, as we were on our way to dinner time. The drink menu (almost as varied as the appetizers) consisted of 3 options and we shared the pecan beer, lime juice sourd For me, at least, and for my co-workers at the table, they really enjoyed the variety of drinks made for them. We had to wait 10 minutes for dinner because this group of six got up too late after that - we didn't make it to the other side of We all ordered a seafood plate. The.. gnudi. I was really excited to taste the flaky duck fat bread, which was a touch dry and lukewarm. I ordered the squid ink noodle and it was very good. I felt bad after finishing this dessert! This dish is good, but not so good that it's overpowering. What to do..? I wasn't too impressed with the dinner options, so I just ordered the white rice with a side of peas and mushrooms. The pork chops were served with green beans, mushrooms and peppers. My partner opted for the scallops, which was flavorful and had a crusty shell. I won't be returning here much, since it lacked a big splash of seafood, but I'm sure what went on there will go The restaurant was clean and had excellent service. Thanks to everyone for the delicious dinner at The Treemont.

When we first came up to Seattle, one of the places we wanted to visit was this super place on the corner of Grand and Broadway. It is not your average local disco. Not too bad though as if getting there was so easy. We had just a short wait to get in but when it opened, it was packed. At 8:00 at night, the place got really crowded on the dance floor. It was really packed, probably because there was not a lot of seats left in most parts of the space. There were a bunch of local artists walking around the space: The Flaming Lips, Oompah Bandits, a young girl What I didn't know is that I tend to get sick of the party DJs. We had a great time on Friday night and the only downfall of last Friday was the puddle of sweat behind us. It's amazing how quickly everyone is getting tired of it, and it seems to be the same for everyone. The sound quality of the music was good and the DJ made sure to keep us spinning the vinyl. According to the reviews here, this place makes you feel like you're in the desert but actually it's very very cool for long periods of time. It really is the perfect place for a Wednesday night dance party with friends.

We did a sweet greens to go event last night and did very well. A few salads - both in a fusion of red, green, and white - were ok. It was but I expected more, too. I had to spend over $5 on food in this location to get the items from IKEA, which would have been a lot better. The salads were all good though, but overall a disappointing experience. I don't recommend this location to anyone.

I decided to go with the soup idea after my friends suggested that I eat a small lunch, mainly because its in the Midtown area. The chicken broth looks like a pretty good choice but I can't say I think it has everything I'd want. They have different items each day too! The starter bowls are a small bowl and the main bowl is a large bowl and your choice of chicken, turkey, or beef. The first I ordered was the chicken and egg blackened soup and the chicken green Thai soup. The chicken broth was muddled with little carrot chunks to really break up the soup and, I think, was great! I ended up getting the regular chicken broth and the hangover. I was expecting either but I wasn't really into the idea of egg noodles because I'm not a good cook (so..). Although it's not everyone's cup of tea, I went to the soup for a bite. The soup were great and although they were heavy on the soup texture, they were still very good. I felt a bit rushed during lunch due to all the extra soup, but the chicken broth alone was still good enough. I opted for a bowl of a chicken and cheese soup. I don't generally eat much soup, but I had some idea that it wouldn't matter if I did, as long as the cost was I'd rate Prescription Chicken 5 stars but I also felt that both lunch items and the food were well worth the $4.50 price tag. Flywheel is based out of downtown Oakland in the heart of the Northside. It has a clean facility (I've been here twice), so I don't mind having to deal with cleaning. The rooms are spacious, well-ventilated, and there's even a shower. No problem with dressing room/comfort areas, although most people go to showers on the way to the gym. I often do this at any gym, so trying to put on the appropriate clothes is always a hit or miss. I can tell you that the locker rooms are super cute and they've got everything you need. There was a bag of condoms (did I mention I had never heard of condoms? ), but I like to bring my own bathing suits. All of this makes Flywheel so much more than a gym and a gym. After the free shower, I received an email asking if I wanted to continue training at Flywheel. Some of them were the first instructors, while others are seasoned. For those who are new to the gym, it doesn't come as a surprise. The vibe is really laid back. Class selection is really a matter of preference. Every class at Flywheel is held by Emily Gupta, who is also the VP of Programs. She is a blast to work out with and her workouts always feel brutal. These bikes are so versatile, that it will be difficult to stay on them for longer than twenty minutes. There are actually plenty of variations of the same muscle groups that you would find in a gym-style bike workout. I've been able to put into practice several basic and advanced moves, and my arms have lost a ton. The class prices can go up to $500 for a half-hour. After we finish the class, you can take advantage of a promotional pass from Flywheel. And the selection of classes is a little limited. I attended a Blowout class last month, and the instructor played "Sweet Water, Sweet Water" - a song I think You can jot down your notes on what you wish to do. I really enjoyed this class - the first in my new local neighborhood! I've purchased a few months of passes for a minimum of 6 classes. I would say that if one attends the two classes and decides to purchase a group membership (I'm pretty sure I'm getting an I'd like for a free trial trial since I only signed up for an hour and a half. I definitely would recommend it if you're in a tight budget. I think this is the type of workout that I'll never let go of. Thanks for the mentioning though, Jenn. I know I'll keep coming back.

I love to do physical exercise, and have tried to incorporate it into my daily life. As a fitness coach, I've always wanted to learn new techniques to help improve my fitness. I recently enrolled in two Sweat classes. I wanted something that focused on strength training in one go, so I set out to try the SweatX class, which included weight lifter and circuit drill I really liked the new group classes, which included: upper body, shoulders, and upper back. The studio, which was recently renovated, is located at Queen Village in Richmond, Virginia. The Queen Village Sweat gym is my favorite gym to date. It's pretty big and is close to where I live. However, it takes a while to workout there due to the traffic. However, the other location is not the most convenient. I started at this location a mere five or six months ago. For any of you out there who live within walking distance, you may be surprised to know that the gym is quite different. This gym isn't a luxury gym. There is a lot of dust and other dusty debris sitting in the parking lot. It's got lots of cracking, broken glass, and isn't cleaned once a month like some of their other locations. The floors are grey and dis-functional. A simple gym can only attract customers by its clean, classy looks and upscale equipment. With the fitness staff, I could barely tolerate the fucking facilities (and the unattractive decor). Why they do however, is amazing. I had high hopes, but the instructors there are seriously great, and I am very comfortable at the Fitler Square location. Jamel is a truly amazing personal trainer who has been working with me for over a year now. He's a wonderful trainer, and works with me to create a workout plan that works for me. Jamel is always really upbeat and motivational. He also makes you feel comfortable, which is extremely important to me. Jamel has been an amazing trainer, and I'm so glad Sweat was introduced to him. Now I'm officially a Sweat member and I'm glad that I did. And to top it all off, he offers a variety of membership plans.

I ate pizza here at their cafe a couple years ago. I guess I'm just not a fan of the place. Yes, this pizza is seriously amazing.
