It's a very close run of the mill meat and three joint with "Arnold's" right across the street to the west or I don't care why it's so close, it's just that I didn't eat at Dandgure's as frequently If you are visiting Dandgure's for a dinner or just wanting a simple good meal then the staff is very friendly and the restaurant is The restaurant itself has very little to do with the restaurant itself but it does have a very casual atmosphere and a great patio to explore.

The pho was very good but the pricing was rather high. The pho sandwhich is a huge part of the menu. They are expensive as well but I've experienced better in the past. One reason is because there will be a little wait, so in the case of a busy evening you may feel it a little time consuming. I don t know who the owner is to argue on that though.

Audubon Park encompasses many different types of places to enjoy a quiet, relaxing afternoon before the work week. There are multiple lagoons to swim in while you can birdwatch. The trail is also well maintained and it offers a lot of cross training opportunities as well. One of my favourite things about this park is that it has a clubhouse which I love. There is also an amphitheater that is open to the public and has a stage set with a small stage set up as well as an ice There is also a fully operated zoo within the park and is open to the public for adoption. Also known as Audubon Park this area offers a lot of activities such as swimming, bowling and more. It's actually a really nice park with lots to entice visitors.

Although I have yet to sample some of these many other Tex-Mex places I think that this place ranks up there with Agua del Re Its located in St. Boniface and is very family friendly. The atmosphere is lively and family friendly, but is still a TexMex place that has all-day menu items for around $5 a plate. If you fancy some authentic TexMex food, you can definitely pick up a large plate for around twenty-five Bucks or thirty-five cent Other items include the guacamole enchiladas and the fajitas. Very happy with this place.

Slightly off the corner of 8th and South, Thai House is a popular Japanese restaurant serving Korean-fusion food. They have a small menu but plenty of options including Asian food and Asian beer / wine. Food is moderately priced for most of the seating and the menu is pretty nice for the size of it. The ribs and pad thai is great and the noodle bowl was quite good. The spicy tuna had sasaka ham and added the most enjoyable texture to the dish. I'd go back though, it looks like this could be great.

Here is a well known and pretty priced "Snowball stand." It was super fast if you like a fast ice down. The snowballs are much better than Sal's and they are served hot and cold. The prices are also less than what you would expect from a fast food restaurant and they do do a great job of having the most flavorful treats. That is a plus in my book for the food. They also have a to-go counter that allows you to pop a snowball up and bring it back to your seat. I would not get it again, but if it has a good flavor and it isn't quite as chunky like Sal's I'

They're a big grocery store and it's quaint. There are several options on the counter and everything is in good enough shape. Also they have a small Arabic coffee shop. It's also great, clean, modern, and they don't forget the basics.

I had dinner at Icinga today and it was nice but it wasn't anything spectacular and I really wouldn't want that type of restaurant again Unfortunately lunch was the worst experience I've had dining there. At $4.50 a plate I got a good meal which includes three courses and was very satisfying. All of the staff were so overly friendly and seemed more focused upon helping me make our lunches than getting more help with our meals. A few servers were extremely unfriendly and it was so frustrating having to wait over an hour when I really wanted to walk out of there. At times my fellow servers said I was the one who had an issue while I was just sitting around. I definitely would not consider going back here if lunch were open and I probably would not even consider returning for dinner if I were a high ranking. My lunch was expensive because I did end up drinking my iced tea and I also had to sit until the food came out. Not in a good way as I was waiting for my table to be served and it was just empty space between tables. A bit late for lunch we came back to sit down to have dinner so it was really interesting to find out more about how nice the food was and how delicious This was clearly a service issue that I don't like. And I would be more than willing to pay a little extra for the actual dining experience. In overall I was not very impressed by my experience and would certainly not return.

I walked into this grocery last weekend to pick up the wine and cheese for an event I had coming from Oregon and had been wanting to do for a There are some tidbits of good food (as well as some not so good) but most of the items are just OK. Their frozen desserts are good, but not great though.

If you're ever located in NOLA and haven't used FedEx for a while there is definitely a good reason to visit. The FedEx delivery people are friendly and helpful and they carry many items that are on their way out with ease. The delivery and customer service is great and the clerks were very friendly and helpful. For most FedEx stores, the lone complaint is that they make you wait ages when you can be driving to FedEx locations.

I was recently in Valencia and after shopping and bouncing around I decided to stop by Lola's. They serve tapas and entrees all of which are delicious and the seafood is always fresh and has a good blend of cream and seafood that is Their menu is very extensive with plenty of tapas and other offerings and their wine list can get confusing as sometimes they use different wines to pair the dishes together You can really get a good taste of the food at this restaurant as I always eat with my dummy. This is a very traditional restaurant and no matter what you order you will be getting some amazing food. And you always have an extra tip at the register in your name that is always helpful when you are ordering a soup/ stew that you would normally go for Lola's doesn't have a great atmosphere and the restaurant gets a little hot when cooking but it makes up for it when you get  I really don't mind it as long as the food is good but it is a little more expensive when it is in the area and I really like Also their Spanish wine selection is one of the best in the city.

I tried the hotdogs and ribs (across from the fountain) but I was very pleasantly surprised with the size of my meal. The place is fairly busy at times and I was there on Sunday evening where it had got pretty busy. Food was fairly average and it was fast-moving. After drinking a few beers, it was time to go home and I really enjoyed the dinner, a nice change from the usual restaurant fare of I would definitely recommend going to this bar during happy hour.

In December 2007 I went to Elizabeth's for lunch in the restaurant located at 272 South Washington Avenue. This was truly a shattered experience because while the burger was moist enough and had some excellent flavor, the bacon buns were dry, The bacon was extremely flavorful but not something I typically enjoy. I was quite disappointed in the burger as it was pretty average but I thought the whole thing fell short of expectations especially since it is served with sides of corn It would have been nice if it had come with more bacon and was topped with some sort of bbq sauce sauce. So I'll give them a call next time I'm in town. !...but also a great little burger at Elizabeth's!!! !?..

This is a good sized Vietnamese restaurant in my neighborhood. I ordered a vanilla flavor and got a chocolate ice cream with it when it arrived! I had a big scoop of frozen yogurt with vanilla that I really liked and a big scoop with mint and chocolate ice cream. Good prices though.Edible staff, good product, good price.

This was a very basic pizza made by Ancora in the West Loop of Chicago called the "Margherita". It has a VERY basic thin crust and few toppings. I didn't like that they only offered the cheese (I liked the pepperoni and olives), no pepperoni or olives, very plain It tasted like the garlic could have been seasoned in a little more than a few minutes. Overall the pizza was pretty cheap and delicious but the flavor of the toppings was poor. The sauce was plain and lacking taste and added no much overall to the taste. It was blatantly wrong in every way. After visiting the many cured meats of the area - they are very hard to find! The service was very poor to say the least. I walked out with an "I didn't give a review" of the staff.

I came across the Crossfit store in The Oval in the suburbs of Sydney, Australia for the first time and boy was I glad I did! I'm a new athlete at the gym and have been looking forward to this place ever since I've been there. They also have a good variety of special offers and some amazing deals on gym equipment. They opened their first physical in 2001 and have since opened the doors of another in a number of cities. I do believe though that the gym is more than worth that walk out to get to it.

Just a few days ago I took a trip to a Japanese food joint called Yuen Sukien but opted out when I couldn't The pasta was just fine, not as thick as I'd hoped but still good enough to keep me going for the second lunch of the day. The rest of the ingredients looked great but I went ahead and ordered the main dish of the day. I was also completely disappointed with the service because the server was very pleasant and helpful but it took forever for me to figure out how to move the menu. Some of the other dishes were also very good but nothing I could compare to. I would be willing to put it aside and wait until they do what seems to be bringing up their lunch specials.

I would describe this Krystal as a poor establishment for a burger and the only thing I thought was good was the steamed chicken nu I had a burgundy and my sister and mother decided to order their steamed burger. But since I stayed at this hotel I have never had the opportunity to come back and it just wasn't one of my favorite restaurants in the area. The corn starch that was pressed into this burger was just plain watery. I am not so sold on this place at all and I believe I probably won't be back any time soon. This is an extreme example of how bad the food should be that costs a lot to dine at. This company needs to stick to the simple things. The burger was hardly edible. This is a place where people have a lot of expectations built in and want to eat healthy but feel that they're being squelched Unfortunately they offer so little in terms of fresh ingredients. I probably would not recommend if you are looking for a really good burger this is the place to go.

Camellia at the corner of Oak and Freret is an old school restaurant that opened back in 1997 and is easily the best in the neighborhood. A nice old school diner with some good music. The food here is great but sometimes there's a big line to get in so maybe you have to stay at the hotel down the road to be late The food here is good, but the price is a little high. The menu is always a mix of burgers, chicken, and fish. It was busy; my last visit was at around 9:00pm on Friday and there were still customers there around 10:30pm.

I've always been a fan of Cafe Minh. I am very impressed by the decor, and the staff. In fact I just discovered that this place is on the former side of the street from my house and I've been dining there for at least a decade The restaurant looks really nice that the menu is very fairly priced. I have always had the chicken salad and always leave with a pretty full belly because it's never overly heavy. There’s not much that really appeals to me and I love what Cafe Minh does, but I would certainly return here for some of my favorite food

I recently tried this place out this week because I had a friend who came by and went to visit. In the late evenings there is usually an open bar in there that seems to be very popular, but usually it happens to be a nice quiet place where A new place opened in the Quarter a few months ago. If there is anything I'd have been more than happy to be able to say it is really the nicest dive bar in the French Quarter and

The best I've had at The Monk's Garden. It features a nice selection of fish (a huge array), delicious pasta, and tasty seafood items. I would recommend it for the patio and courtyard-side setting. We went for the chicken salad and if you enjoy the traditional French style, you should be able to make some really good lunches there. No matter what time it is, I enjoyed their Sunday Brunch and the French bread.

You can't park anywhere else (except for the hotel parking lot) and the hotel is very small, especially the parking lot (the hotel is near this The store also cannot answer any questions you have and they refuse to provide a price. I would rather have a location like this in town even though it's way out of my way.

This is definitely my favorite waterfront restaurant where I have gone for food I don't care for but still find extremely nice. Even with the poor Tex-Mex flavor of the food I'd still recommend this place and the atmosphere because the service can be a little  The oysters were wonderful and I like to try new places when I have the time but I had a hard time distinguishing what was on the menu from The salad bar had a few items to choose from but they were nothing spectacular. The octopus muffaletta was good and a bit salty overall. I was not happy about the gumbo but it wasn't bad and I think that should be standard fare. The server very quickly made sure that everyone on the menu was pleased with the food and the prices that were offered were very affordable. But they are really good and I would definitely be willing to return with a large group for the regular pricing. I would definitely get the gumbo and I would probably order that. They have a really neat space and a great patio where you can eat out and enjoy a good drink. Please consider a visit.

As much as it always makes me super sad, I've been lusting after some very special specials at Hansen's all summer and finally If you follow my blog you have know I am a fan of the frozen yogurt ice cream treat and what not but when I saw the "chee I took out my eato and ate so many ice cream cones for my snowball for about an hour before we ate it and my I'd give a 1 star for that.

It's been a while since any of you posted about this place. This is New Orleans Original Daiquiri and I've been trying to get over to this place for a while. It's on our last weekend and it's absolutely on our top 10 "must eat" spots in New Orleans. I'll always get my original, the black, from the bar. Not everything is just a daiquiri, at least not the drinks... but it sure is pretty.

On Sunday morning I walked along street as it is known around here--one of the most celebrated street parades in the country. If they ever did it twice the star points get deleted. My friend had a problem with the red flag and the other krewe members just kept coming up and the krewe members kept coming up Most of the people are new to Mardi Gras and get very familiar with what is going on in the town. Just look at the crowds!

The White House Tour takes place during the week of October 13-16 and was established in 1963 by Queen Victoria, Queens in the United States. This year, this event kicks of from 6:00pm to 10:00pm. All guests are given free parking with free access to all the galleries at a discount. Many of the artists attending this event are from local or regional artists and there is also an element of street art and street art vendors selling various wares. When it finishes at 9:30pm, the night's activities end and people gather nearby to party. A good place to celebrate your first night in New Orleans is the Warehouse Arts Center, located on the back of the Warehouse. Get tickets here. .

If there's an issue with a new restaurant ot be overly good, then I think they are pretty bad at service because they let the They had a selection of beef pho listed but no chicken. We finally went over to this new Vietnamese restaurant on Westheimer and this place is small. The main menu offers a chicken and beef pho, a bun, a noodle dish, a rice dish, and a large The menu has a very odd style but seems to be working as fast as they can. The wait staff has only been there for a week so if you are like me you only want to eat for about 15 minutes. The place is located in a very poor part of South Louisiana so it's been months since I ate there. The place is just way toocrowded for a restaurant, but it's still really fun to get the kids to come back. They had chicken pho listed but didn't have any ready! Now I know that this is a new restaurant and doesn't have any menu items on it and no menu items of what have they ever even made, So why are they only doing that? What is this place supposed to be? Yep why even are they running out? I hope the management can learn to correct this!

Bulldog, you have totally fucked me! You won't even consider the fact that I come with you all the time! And, I do not want you to continue to run my business if you cannot honor your commitments to me. And then you sell your soul on me and the entire place gets shut down! Bulldog it is killing me and you are ruining my night. It's better for me because I'm not going to get kicked out of the house without paying for the beer but there are all these other bars It wont be a good thing but it will be a good thing for me to save my money and to stay at your bar any longer. Bulldog, give your customers something else to laugh about while I'm at it before you cut this off from me.

I am one of those people who have the same "favorites" about this festival as the people at the Bywater because...well, it is It isn't that the food is bad, but you just can't really get your bearings. There is a very small parking lot in front of the festival that has space for the festival but even with that you have to wait in the line for your For those of you who are going to the venue this year, just pull up in the parking lot and go for a quick burger and bris I would highly suggest if you're going to go to this festival get a bite of food before you go to this festival and just drive to the The music is awesome, but the food is just not up to par.

This was my 3rd time eating here and I got to review it recently. I'd say the burger was great but the fish was a little dry and wasn't as fresh as it was supposed to be. My husband and I both felt like we were being served food that was not tasteful enough nor was the presentation any better. I would instead recommend this place if you are looking for a good quality asian restaurant with great staff.

The new bar at the Orleans Canal area of the city is called Lavish Bar and Eater and is a lovely new restaurant located at 537 Washington I can't really think of any reason why I wouldn't but just don't feel right about it. I've seen many of their happy hours... pretty awesome. Unfortunately I hate Gastropubs. This bar just seems to be all of the above and it's just not a good concept. I can't believe they are so cheap, that they feel such wanton stuff I am starving to death!!! So I don't know why I am still bothering here today. And they're just killing us with that concept. There's just something about a bar and it's too expensive. I really do eat here but there are so many places I just do not want to go back there.

I finally stepped foot in this establishment around the middle of the day this past week to check out my best friends favorite gay bar and lounge. A quick look at the menu reveals an extremely diverse menu, with several different kinds in front of each bar. During my visit there was an outdoor smoking corner on the ground level where I was able stoke up a huge crowd during the evenings There was no way I could think of any other place as smoke filled and it was hard to even breathe. The overall atmosphere was very low key and it was easy to get a good seat. The atmosphere of this joint is not very hospitable for newcomers. No ipod or sound-track player can solve my problem.

This is a pretty good place with a great decor and a really friendly staff. They also have a nice little patio out back while the rest of the burgers are in the back which makes it convenient for a mid evening meal I would have to say that the salad bar is a bit small (the place isn't a cafe, it's more like a  Unfortunately that also means that they do carry out orders. However I love all the delicious food and would still go back.

There are so much great local bar on the corner but the ones across the street are always really busy with all of the people who want to buy a drink Usually they take a very long time when boarding but still it can get crowded in there and be a little noisey. They are fairly modern decor with some old looking doors and the walls are painted black and gray. It seems like a lot of it's regular patrons are able to get a table and get to them at the same time.

This restaurant in the Little Caesars parking lot is quite small and is very dark. A new logo and it was a great look as is a really nice sized bartender. The drink choices are fairly limited as in a number of the tables there were more than one drink. I tried to order a beer and I found myself feeling too thirsty by the time I got my first half glass of water and didn't even manage Though there was also not overly much drink specials on the menu. The decor is kind of too casual and we were mostly looking at the walls but I feel there are a few decor pieces that are a little too subtle If your a local you should check it out and if not you could probably spend the better part of a day there. The bar seating is a bit more than adequate so you'll probably either want to sit at the bar or get a seat at the bar.

This place is probably one of my favorite restaurants in Las Vegas as there is much more than they provide on the menu but they give me my moneys worth. My burger here was very good and I think it's better than other places in the area because of the quality of the place. There's a good selection of lunch specials. The burgers are excellent and they have a nice selection of buns so don't expect meatballs but really enjoy how juicy those are. I had the Italian sarsaparilla that was a nice blend of Italian flavor with French flair and the Caesar salad was a great selection of They have some very nice looking mugs too such as the French Bulldog and the Belgian Belgian Coffee which I have recently been missing in my town I'm planning on continuing to provide my wife and daughter with delicious food and drink and the staff was friendly and informative. Food is quite fresh and I had a lot of fun while trying all the menu items.

Not much to add but this is a place with a great atmosphere. I've ordered a lot of the stroganoff, which is absolutely amazing. I also found that most of the staff are very nice and knowledgeable. It was very filling and I would definitely recommend. Can't wait to return again.

A plethora of restaurants are located within the area of this hotel so if you're looking for anything that's good, you need to They have a gas station and there are several stores out on the road at one time but since this is a police store it seems the price is higher They have a wide selection of supplies and they are good for most of the states especially California and Colorado.

We went to Idlewilder this evening for lunch and were immediatelyblown away by their selections. I didn't really know what to expect from the burger but when I reached into my freezer I got a pile of deliciousdirty bacon grav It does come with the burger bun which is also delicious and has a really delicious, unique flavor. My burger was so juicy that when it hit the plate I didn't feel like I was eating out! This burger is filled with delicious meaty flavor (which definitely sounds too dramatic with the way it is stacked and it  melts in your mouth!! This burger was very tender, tender and rich in beef flavor with some meaty flavor that had a great meat and skin ratio as well as a The "Roasted Beef Po boy" was also one of my favorite burgers so I got another "Dirty"  I think I'm going to try the roast beef po boy and see what happens! They also have their own "dipped pizza" which is awesome as well, but at the moment I don't think I want one. They will be back in town soon for the summer. :) And do not miss their happy hour too!! !You can see it in my review for their burgers below and check out the rest of their menu here!

This is another lovely little place and it is a cozy place that provides a nice place to sit and eat a great sized order of fish Whether you are looking for a brisket, a ribeye or an Italian Beef Steak...The Alamo is the I would go for the venison brisket and I would probably go for that if I was in that market. Great place to go to try something new while eat.

Go to this place if you are at all kinda busy during weekend hours. Located in downtown and next to New Orleans Casino. They have a cashier and you have to pick a drink, make your purchase and then proceed to the bathroom. After 1pm you are free to park. The menu has some nice little items, like an authentic American sandwich with a side salad, and a couple extras like a burger and two Great local option for lunch during the week.

This is a fun but somewhat pricey bar that is known as The Bar at the Warehouse District. It's always really busy and the place is constantly filled with people who just want to enjoy what it's been like there. They recently renovated the bar to match the new layout. If you want to have drinks, this bar is for you (but I always get the food or drinks). The staff has always been very nice and always makes sure to listen to what I've asked at my meetings.

I'm going to be quoting a local "Bourbon" while I'm here, because I like it and it's more But if you are lucky enough to get free of charge, there is street gambling here too. They really have moved in here and have started moving backwards now so everything is just right. However, it is also a crime area in the middle of the strip so people are pretty tough. It is in a nice area to relax while waiting for your flight back to Los Angeles.

The LOFT is just as good as the HOB. It's a kegs full of rock 'n roll and hard rock. It is definitely worth trying. It is also cheaper than HOB to get seats. And all the artists that go on to be part of the HOB's lineup are coming here.

At lunch on Monday May 30th I walked into the restaurant on the corner of 3rd and French Street and ordered my lunch. I had a lot of expectations when I first visited this establishment. Besides, for the price they had a very nice patio which was a great feature as that area is mostly covered in plants and very shaded. I really enjoyed walking through the restaurant because the interior was very nice and I was greeted by really nice folks who seemed really warm and friendly. From the outside I was able to see a small river running through the building as a huge bridge over the canal that runs parallel to and beyond the I'll never have time to read a review here if I have not read it. I saw the bar tender talking about the food and also did what he could to make sure that he was being prepared on what he thought was the From my table I couldn't tell immediately if I was ordering lunch or dinner yet but was immediately greeted by a server and served a The meal was very tasty for the lack of being a new establishment and I love the location of this restaurant (it was on the corner of Louisiana street and I took advantage of two small items before I decided to try the lunch choices and I was really glad I did because these dishes were great. The duck gumbo is a huge bowl of meat in a soupy sauce with the chicken breast on top and the sauce on top is more like I was really impressed with the amount of meat and flavor this dish really has. The Rabbi stew was also very tasty and was served with a side of fried rice for a perfect lunch. I finished off my meal with the house salad as well and the fruit salad was very good too. So while everything about my meal was good I was also very disappointed in the food but the service was very good. There was also a really nice selection of tea and coffee available as well. I really enjoyed both of these dishes and found it to be very well done and a very filling lunch. The duck gumbo was really yummy and I'd also recommend the lamb to anyone who is wanting a delicious hearty meal. While the duck gumbo and rabbit stew are the items on the lunch menu at the restaurant there is also a beautiful salad bar which is located just outside After that it took a while to get my order over to me but they were very easy to get to and the staff was fast and friendly.I' I found my lunch very satisfied and was very pleased with my experience! When you start looking at the menu you probably can't see much but what you do see is a very nice combination of things. When I ate this I didn't mind the duck gumbo as it was just so flavorful. This review is for the lunch only so the restaurant was pretty new but the food was wonderful and it was not crowded like most restaurants I had gone to in

I really enjoyed the crab cakes they have on the menu here a la the one at El Patio of Chicago. The fried oysters are nice and served with a bowl of sauce. There is a pretty extensive menu and they have some interesting items to choose from such as pecan prawn tartare, lemon and mint s The fish and beans are also good. Generally the lunch menu looks decent but the seafood has just a bit of a run-off with a dry taste. The oyster bar is not the best and they charge extra for more than an oyster and they don't serve enough fresh seafood.

I've been here twice this year and both times have had a good crowd. The DJ has a huge set list but it's not in a typical way to see what's going on. The music is sometimes a little bit different on a Saturday night but mostly depends on when the club is opened because of the location. The crowd is kind of loud and I wouldn't call it a bar but a concert-sized venue. Great for a group since it has great views of the city and the bartenders like to treat you like you are a star. If you have been to any of these places, you know what I mean. Good food and drinks.

This is a really nice restaurant, very nice service and good food. It's a real Chinese joint in most ways which means it has some real fun. They make it very easy to enjoy their food with a nice friendly family atmosphere. The owner of the establishment will often do the dishes for you while you wait, and it is so cool sitting over the tables playing games together and enjoying the food

Almost right within the heart of New Orleans and just miles outside the city limits of NOLA this place was one of my favorites to visit. They do a great job of serving lots of fresh fish and have very nice bar. They also have a nice patio that is great for relaxing and enjoying one of the nice patio chairs. The food and decor are great but the menu is not as comprehensive as I have had and I really like the gumbo. This is an older establishment so they do have some nice booths to sit near the bar and enjoy a delicious craft bevvy. I would be a regular to GO back to see if they change anything up.

Byblos has been around since the 1970s and it has been generally fair. There was one time when I ordered Lamb and I ordered the Chicken. There are many things I like about Byblos and a lot about it, but I've been pretty dishonest because of it. However, the meat is generally way too dry and it tastes worse than many kale salads at a similar price. People's service is very slow and unfriendly. They also have a few different pizzas available but not as good as some of the other chinese restaurants in the area. At other times, one has to wring the handle to get out a very heavy buildup. If you are a server, give an order the night before and wait at a table near the center of the restaurant before you order anything else. The byblos is quite an old school establishment, most of the staff are veteran Middle Eastern restaurant customers but those of us who grew up in the 1990 It does have a great patio but I have found that the people here are much nicer than many of the people there are at other nearby restaurants.

Unfortunately this is the only place in town where there is anything worth mentioning but I will let you have a look at the menu since there are so We have been going there for many years and have never had anything that has remained consistent with poor quality and taste. The food has really gone downhill since the times they opened and isn't even comparable to the food at various other places in New Orleans because they are If the food is great you should really be looking to go elsewhere for your dining experience.

A really decent bar off of the middle of South Central. It's a good bar with a bbq and it's on the corner of 2nd Street and Main Street so not too bad We also ordered drinks while we're there but there was no beer available to us. And there is a pretty good line.

I have been going to this bar in my neighborhood for over 50 years. It is huge with great bar music, really. I've always had a great time on most days just hanging out with people and drinking plenty of beer if I can. Another nice aspect of the venue is how much they have available to dance to. Well done.. you all rock!

I've always had the problem of going there with my wife and their children. My wife and I've had the seafood that has been done there in the past and as you'd expect on a chain the quality is decent. Upon entering this establishment you expect some sort of high-end food establishment, usually high above standards with a high price tag. What you do get, really, is a subpar sandwich and a rather forgettable salad. The food isn't bad; the sandwich items have pretty good texture and the chicken sandwiches are good. If you are a fan of the New Orleans area this place would be one of the best places to dine in the city.

A couple of weeks ago I had lunch at Blues Bistro for lunch and it was extremely good. Unlike some of the other dining rooms in the area, it was clean, spacious, and cozy. I was able to get a good, fresh salad, a couple of sandwiches and some of their lunch specials without being a waitress! You get a good selection of food and some excellent service right off the bat. In addition to the iceberg lettuce with shrimp, croutons and lemon and honey, I also ordered the Smoked Shrimp Pancakes This is a wonderful mixture of sauce, crostini and a flavorful sauce. I ended up saving half and had dinner later in the day. I also ordered the Pan Roast Chicken and Wild Mushroom Risotto. I thought the chicken and almonds were good and not overpowering. Although I will say I haven't been dining here since my son was born, I enjoyed the experience and would recommend it to others. Very professional and friendly staff. You can find out more about the food and staff by clicking here.

An indoor-outdoor beer bar, Industrial Beer Bistro (ICB) is located on Indiana's west side. The brew house is located on Shelby Street, next to the old Town Hall building located on the corner of Franklin and Lincoln streets, and the restaurant on No meats or cheeses, but a selection of beers for sale were available. I showed the bartender and she brought me some beers to try. There is also an additional $7.00 for "special" brews which take the place of the flight. Currently, the three beers are the Gold Leaf (Orange Ale) and Starstreak (Blonde Ale). The 2% ABV and 11 IBU was a nice, dark brown beer with a soft malty taste that was surprisingly smooth on the An enjoyable beer compared to many of the other local beers out there. As my next choice, I went with the Green Street (Fred Bean Ale) whose beer itself comes from a dark brown color and has notes of This was a very tawny pale amber color and the taste was good and very smooth. Next, I took a shot of the Red Hot (Romeo & Juliet). Also had a light funk flavor. This beer is a pale ale that had a nice smooth texture with a bit of peppery flavor. This was an excellent selection of a locally brew. As I was leaving though, my wife was asking for a second selection. It was the Dampfbier. She then recommended the Dark Brown (Ale) which I did not try, but did receive an opinion from a local. I tried the Shine on February 7th and enjoyed it very much. The beer was 6.4% in alcohol content and only 21 IBU. The craft beers are available to be served on draft, bottle, or can by the glass. You can read more about ICB on their website at their Isofarms page. For all craft beer enthusiasts, the brews look and taste good!

On Sunday, I took my daughter with me to Oldfield's historic home and the IMA. And I'm happy to be sharing it with you! This is one of the new additions to Indianapolis Museum of Art that is opening their doors next month. It has a variety of beers from different breweries and its selection is a little limited. Unlike most other beer gardens, there are a nice amount of tables and chairs available. It fills up fast so it isn't a popular time for sitting down after your visit to the museum. There are a number of tables to sit around, including a long table for two, and a small bench for one, then a table for The main bar is open between 1pm and 9pm. There are some tables that have space for customers to order and the bar is located outside. The prices are average for the space, and they are clearly marked on the menu. The wait is a bit long since the gardens are open to the public to take a look (and to drink). The selection of beers is limited, as you do not pay for a glass of beer, but there is a limited area to walk with the pret The tour was a perfect mix of old town charm and modern fun that I wasn't sure I wanted to end. My beer arrived before I realized I was going to walk and not pick it up. It was flavorful but not necessarily strong. The pretzel was moist and tender. The beer tasted nice enough, and it was fairly pricey. However, we were still disappointed about something we didn't know the first time around. Unfortunately, I really enjoyed the beer. The only negative thing to say about the beer garden is that if you make a group gathering, be sure to include a glass too, as I I'll stick with Miller Lite now for this trip through Indiana. There is also a small outdoor patio by the entrance to the gardens where you can watch the sun set from the bar. I really enjoyed the food though, it is definitely not the best out there. We don't meet many people with beer tastes like that, so I am disappointed by the limited selection. There is an outdoor stage to enjoy the beer while you walk down an alley to explore the museum and beyond.

Books & Brews is the latest of the Books & Brews locations, and a small little spot in the old building that has been Their newest location is located in the former Ivy City High School of Medicine building on the corner of North and South Church Streets. It was a beautiful day today. I opted to go in the middle of the day and drive there. I thought it was really a lot of trouble because I always drive over to Riverside Park to walk my dog, but they were aggressively blocking my view for I believe that since policing are not working on the park, this might be a major issue that could be addressed before it is really too late I'm wondering if there are any additional plans to improve the situation with the park? I have a theory that the wait staff was busy for lunch and not busy at all so I don't know what actually happened on the day of our As it was busy it took a while to get our food. A few miles south-west of Interstate 95 is Blue Mountain Park. The trails are narrow, but only about a half-mile long. From the time that I learned the details of the trail, there are no closed trails. I arrived about 12:15 on a Friday morning and the road leading into the park leads right up to it. This park entrance is up the bank of the Tennessee River across from the Big Boy Lakes State Park. Take off Highway 96 at the intersection with 96th, then continue on 96th south until you reach the trailhead. The trailhead to the north is slightly wider than at the south and has only two lanes of path and a fence. The rider must be aware that the trails are not very flat and it is not easy to negotiate. It is a nice place to ride but it varies year to year from what the Indiana state parks service says "Wet conditions are not welcome." In case you are not prepared and you have the time, please go to Hazel Dell State Park at the corner of 96th and Hazel Dell. Riders are welcome to ride their bikes on the dirt trails. For more details see their website. Good thing I did not arrive too late in the evening to get there for the new trails in June.

I came in to 96th and Michigan just in time to spend some time in the basement! It's located at 6828 Michigan Rd in Downtown Glen Rock. The menu is fairly simple with just enough selection to appeal to anyone who likes a solid brew. The selections are all well crafted and taste delicious. On the other hand, the IPA had a nice hop profile to it and was just overall a great IPA overall. And I would not recommend the orange one. I didn't really like it either. This may have just been the beer itself or the quality that was thrown into it. A quick phone call to the brewery and a convenient location to use for pick up and drop off seemed to work fine for me. However the parking was a bit hard to find, and there were also a few places nearby the carwash if you want to take advantage or not Also, parking is extremely slow until they close the doors. The location of the bar, as well as the friendly staff, is a win for any beer lover and it's hard to beat the cost for their No wait - not much arguing in the brewery.

This place is kind of a throwback, a new Thai place. It's a new restaurant just opened and the interior isn't exactly what I was hoping for. Phan's Kitchen does have a long way to go (it's a bit outside of my immediate area) and it's a (Pretty cool place, I think I'll be heading back.) The food was pretty good.

If your goal is to deliver an exceptional waiters/waitress experience, get that, AND a great beer selection. I have found that on various occasions there are certain restaurants which are welcoming and friendly, especially if the servers bring their own drinks, and I remember seeing this For my first experience with La Pisa, I parked in the front lot. Once I was seated, the server walked by saying hello to the couple by the window, who were waiting for their drinks. My server had an excellent sense of humor and was a pleasure to know. And the food came out in a few minutes. I tossed in my Cubano which was a grilled beef sandwich dipped in a savory aioli. The combination was sweet yet savory and one of the best I've had. I would definitely return and try their sandwiches! And I would have to say that it was a good meal as well.

After a day of shopping, it is a great time to come visit the Lincoln Memorial. As you approach the museum from the East, there are a number of smaller pieces that will draw your attention; particularly along the southern wall. A large statue of ancient Egypt in stone stands across from the museum. A beautiful bronze work, it was formerly the entrance to the museum's "Children's Room" and is a memorial to Dr A few years back, it was at the Smithsonian Institution's National Museum of African American History, and now it is found here on the outside There is a series of statues that include a grouping of 3 dinosaurs (Arizonasaurus, Tetrasaurus, and These statues were made in collaboration with local artists and were placed in various architectural styles and placements. At the end of the grounds, there are sculptures of dinosaurs (Rattana, Brachiosaurus, and Tyrannosaurus On the north side of the museum is a large, detailed dinosaur that can also be seen running away from the building. This makes a very nice addition! Other tributes include a sphinx (suction cup), a giant caterpillar (for children), and a giant penguin ( On the northeast corner there is a pair of Victorian buildings. As you go through, Anne of Green Gables stands on one of the windows in the main hall. The scene is an actual window on her house. She is also represented by this two-story marble tree. Nearby, there is a series of fossils of dinosaurs. The small animal is also a relic of the museum's past. Again, it is very animated as it makes a dramatic jump to a standing position. Another piece on the western side of the museum are three pieces of NASA/ NASA spacewalking that are clearly visible from the street. There are also some large signs highlighting each of the children's museum exhibits and their historical significance. As a result, a bronze sculpture also bears the NASA logo on the left hand side. But, the main point to come out by now is actually the museum itself. The mural depicts a small, colorful kangaroo sitting next to a giant dinosaur. My husband was so excited to see this piece of art. There is also a painting in the museum re-creating a giant fish that some people remember on a number of their childhood trips to the The artwork I found, however, makes this area look rather claustrophobic. The rest of the inside of the museum is full of beautiful creations and a touch of fun from the park.

I have been visiting this museum for many years now and can only imagine how many wonderful ideas about the American West have come out of this place. The first floor is devoted to the Gund Gallery with several unique displays covering art of the American West. There are great stories of heroes and villains fighting for survival on the way through the great wilderness, with the cattle ranches brimming with fresh It was a place where you could find some dirt roads, where there would be plenty of desert to get out, and where there were no drug-a That is one of the best things I have seen in some time. There are over 1000 paintings, plus many sculptures created from the original artworks by artists like Buxton, Charlton Hennings, and John Henry Bu A series of "Mount Tampico" by Jackson Pollock, "Mutler's Day" by DeWitt, " The largest collection is a large painting by Renoir depicting the American "Occupation of the West" along with artwork from other cities, and This museum does have an emphasis on the old westerns that you may have heard about. However some of the exhibits do touch you with the reality of the history of this place and its people. This first floor was dedicated to the Native American Galleries, which really caught my attention. Various pieces of art, architecture, and furniture tells a story of the countless stories that have come from the land. There are also several pieces of clothing and maps that show the different types and degrees of life among the native tribes. One such treaty, the Forty-nine miles Northwest Treaty between the United States and the Colorado Rockies (which was negotiated by the Colorado A very touching, beautiful museum that will stay with you. It is a fascinating place to see and I highly recommend it. If you have never been to the museum then the tour for this particular location is a must. The museum is also closed on November 4th and 20th. There is a whole slew of interactive and educational exhibits on Native Native Americans and the west. For a long time I was a huge fan of this museum and how it relates to art, history, and life-long learning.

The University Park boulevard is one of the few parks around the world that is not a public park. Despite its small size, it's actually one of Indianapolis' most popular parks. The park was originally called University Park, but it was renamed University Park a few years later as it was known back in 1878. The park was named after the University of Indianapolis (now known as Indiana University, and as of June 1, 2015, the old University of Indianapolis) which is located In 2003, a statue of General Alexander Colfax was placed on the boulevard along with the "Come Thru and See Me" sign. The statue was created by Charles Henry. Colfax's statue was created by artist Daniel McCulloch and is known as the "Colfax-Senior". In 1892, a sculpture of the mayor of Indianapolis, John McCulloch was placed. In 1931, a large statue of Horatio Bishop was placed in the park. On the statue's base, is a relief of Lincoln's own head which was created in 1916 during Lincoln's inauguration. Later that year, a statue of the first Indiana State Senator was placed, the only statue of such a Senator in the State of Indiana. In 1921, a memorial bust of Mayor Jesse Van Buren was dedicated at the park. In 1922, a statue of the 17th President of the United States, George Washington, was placed by artist Joseph Richards. Her work was stolen in 1934. Richards was rehired as the president's representative and he returned in 1930 to create a new statue designed by local artist James Co Hering also created the original "Pan" by Myra Reynolds Richards but moved the statue to the new fountain. In 1936, the "Seated Lincoln" sculpture was replaced by new Statue of David Henry. In 1973, local artist George D. White created a third Pan to replace Richards' original. Most are little, if any, sculptures that the public can see. Another artist, James Y. Smith, designed a replacement statue in 1996 that is now at the American Indian Museum. I hope the money that goes to a local artist gets repaid. It's my favorite park of its kind.

My childhood friends would make them do little dollhouses out of minis (as the name implies), then have a dollhouse dress them down, It was a great way to pass the time with the kids - lots of little hands were involved and the time spent building was very important! I found myself drawn to this kind of miniatures when we visited the Miniature Museum of California, which has all of its pieces in a historical house The museum is located a short walk away from St. Nick Catholic School/Flamingo Catholic School School in the Oakhurst neighborhood. There is also a playground on the right hand side of the building which is just off the entrance. There are little audio screens to play with, although it has been used as a learning activity for guests. If you have the device, you can listen to more or download the audio or video file from their website as well as listen to the interactive display. You can also go inside the houses and have a feel for them. They have some pieces that were reconstructed after the 1930s and 1950s. They also have the more rustic designs, such as a large tree house made out of wood. They also have some older pieces, such as the 17th century doll houses. They are all very accurate and it is interesting to see the precision you give to a piece of miniature. They have very nice and unique pieces that are worth a visit. The rooms feature images of architecture and other depictions of characters. The dollhouses are extremely interesting because of the designs and construction. You won't be disappointed. There's also a doll house museum that runs a few hours a day from 10am-4pm.

To me, the better the experience, the greater the 5 star rating. While I may be comfortable with a 3 star rating given that I have had a similar experience in the past, I am a much more discerning I will sometimes stay in business for two weeks while I wait for a positive experience. I felt like I needed a 5 star review for Pooty's Deli. I visited a couple months ago and it was a very slow time of Year, with lots of crowds. Once again, the atmosphere wasn't great and a table was left unseated but it hasn't happened again. The waitress (with her adorable little possum) was well mannered, and made sure we were comfortable and relaxed. The server provided excellent service, which included describing the menu and asking for my order. The salmon was served on a sandwich, on a plate with cheese, and had a side of burger (I believe it had meat as an I was surprised to see the sliced thin bacon julienned on top of the sandwich. The sandwich was smothered in a tasty combination of salmon, chicken and bacon. It was very savory, though it didn't feel a lot like fish. I was impressed by the complexity of the salmon. Unlike other sandwiches on the menu, the salmon and avocado wasn't overly salty and did not leave a fishy after taste. Of course, the mayo was delicious along with the mayo. However, the potato salad was way overdressed with green onions, and the pickle chips came too thick. The seasoned potato was crisp, with a subtle spice and a salty finish. I also had the baked beans and the sweet potato puree (which I loved so much that I bought the "souvenir" package). Aside from the fact that I was able to enjoy the restaurant without paying a cover charge, the whole dining experience was great! The place is clean, airy, and fun! There's also an outdoor space and bar area for customers to enjoy the food on. This place won me over again! The quality of the food, the friendly servers, the food and service are enough to make it worth coming back.

Revolution is a cool restaurant and drink place that is a little unisex, but really has a great menu and atmosphere. Based upon my own personal taste, I think my first experience with Revolution was quite a bit like all of the other restaurants reviewed. Is it a small eat in establishment where you really want to eat? Do you want to be in a casual environment - hipster or hipster-ish? Do you want a restaurant that's comfortable, clean and serves all your needs? Revolution on North Blvd is well above average for a restaurant with only a couple of stars. Do you like to stay in and dine outside? It was a fun experience during our visit last week. We went with friends for an early night dinner. The patio was only open at lunch time (near 5 pm), so we got our food and drinks before the crowds did. The restaurant received a large number of cars as we made our way to the restaurant and when they walked past us, they were all directed to the patio On the side of the patio, it was dry and not even getting rain. Our waitress did a great job of keeping us up to date on our menu and it was hard to get a table as many people worked to fill We arrived to an outdoor patio located at the end of the patio off the street and a pleasant dining area. We were seated in the front courtyard but then had to wait just about ten minutes for our food to come. We ordered the gumbo and rice and shared a small cup of shrimp scampi with rice and a salad. The chicken was greasy-but the shrimp was just fine, but remained chewy as a result. However, because it was the first time we had been to Revolution and have been to other locations in the area, we all considered it to be very good. There was one of our customers at the table who immediately wanted a bottle of sake and she was excited. This is a very low-cost alternative to a well-regarded fine dining experience in the neighborhood. They do have outdoor tables as well which is nice. It may have been a small problem to fix, but it definitely could have done. I'd go there again to eat and I've to say it wasn't bad at all. I can not believe I never wrote an update on this! They did have good service for just under $30 with a few exceptions but a very small group made things easy. We went out of town on the first week of June and this was great for the local food scene and I would recommend this place to people planning a visit Though we were sitting a fair distance from the restaurant we did feel like we could still hear the cat.

This location was so convenient. A little crowded, but good food (mostly lunch). The food is good, not terrible. The menu was fairly diverse. At lunch we sat at the bar and ordered half of two shakes. The middle and bottom of the shake was a bit runny and the top half had little chunks of milk and powder. In my opinion the shakes were just okay. We did not get any added sweetener so that made the shakes a bit whipped up. Very little of the shake remains after you have consumed it. They also gave me a couple of thicker shakes, but they were too thin for my taste. This was after I ordered my breakfast lunch. The atmosphere was comfortable and the menu was very clean. If there is a problem with the thinness, it's probably a minor issue and the shakes should get thicker. After my wife ordered the Salmon, I thought just something a little more delicate so I ordered it with an oven cooked onion. The salmon wasn't over cooked and looked fairly fresh when served. There were a couple of items that tasted like they had been sitting on the counter for a while, but that didn't change the overall taste The sauce was really delicious too. The burger had a little more meat than I expected and though the bun was cooked just fine, the burger itself was just not going to fly. The bun was thick, but would have been better in thickness had they been using thicker buns. The white wine sauce and wine sauce wasn't too strong, but the sauce was very thin and ranny. The rice was good too and had a nice crisp texture, but with a little more butter. The chicken wrap was tender but cold. This was just a slight reminder you could use a little salt to keep your chips, however much they burned. I was really really impressed with this place as I enjoy burgers and fish. I'm not really a fan of the Asian slaw at this restaurant. We ate some pretty good food and didn't leave much left. That is the main reason I would not leave this place! I have had better lunches at the deli and the neighborhood cafe down the street. We went here again after my experience at Carmel's and opted to eat there instead.

There was a menu board on my table, which I was excited to see. I ordered the crabmeat rangoon and chicken with rice and carrots soup. The Chicken & Crab Rolls were the first item I ordered, just before I left. I was impressed with the size and variety of the dishes they brought. The rolls came with a side of sauce, but dipped in a creamy sauce to help it absorb the flavor as well as moisten the inside Good texture as well as taste. The rolls were warm and soft without being chewy. Not too salty either. The Crabmeat Asparagus soup (cup) arrived with a little wait time. The prices are very reasonable, and the portions are very large, they'm a bit small, but I think they are still quick and good. We will be back!
