It was a small plate and it had little ricotta but a good amount of sauce. Some people called it a Chicken Alfredo. The chicken was cooked medium-low and was over cooked. I think I would have wanted more sauce because I thought it was pretty good, as in sweet with some kick of heat. Besides the pasta, the chicken was also subtlyflavored, with lots of little bits of meat but not at all. Not only did I enjoy the experience, but I also thoroughly enjoyed the service. I would not recommend Convivio for all occasions.

Breweries are great. You can do the same for your lunch or dinner. They are open 7 days a week for lunch and 6 days a week for dinner. Not to mention the food selection. Often times, people take a little longer and pay for the food because the beers don't take too long to come out. They also have several specials on draft beers, so it's easy to find a beer that suits your tastes. The atmosphere was cozy and comfortable and was pretty relaxing. You can browse the beer bar to taste different beers. They have a long list of beers that can be sampled at any time. They use a keg and a large glass. First up was the Rakue German Rauchbier (2.9%, 16) which was dry and fruity with a salty/funky flavor I found it to be slightly overpowering, especially so fast after a heavy meal. Afterwards, I had the Sangria Stout (8%, 40) which was very smooth after being finished with the Rauchbier. Next was the NEX #7 Pilsener (12%, 34) which was a strong malty beer with a sweet-t The last beer was their IPA (3.2%) that had a citrus taste and a slightly bitter bitter aftertaste. The food was excellent as well. There was a bit of wait after we ate and another customer came in shortly after us and asked for a taste of some of their delicious food. I ordered a pair of cheeseburgers and the spicy chicken (one burger, two bites each). Then I ordered the tenderloin steak and sweet potato fries. There was also a tater tot with a few fillets on top. It had a light pink color and added a bit of smoke flavor. I tasted the steak before eating it because it wasn't as dry as they said it would be. It definitely helps bring out the best in your food to the diners. And finally, they have an extensive menu of beer that I would love to try. Food is very good too. They offer the bread that is made into the sandwiches, but the bread is thawed and then served on a grill for the meal. I had really enjoyed it so I was happy they had something so good. They will provide you with a free copy of the San Diego Brewpubs Magazine so you can read their latest articles while there! The sandwiches all came with an order of fries.

My wife and I arrived at the restaurant about 1 hour ago. As we left we were greeted and was told that they were not busy preparing to be seated. We asked for a menu and received a little more of an overview, they didn't give us anything. We ordered the two items for the dinner. The Mexican cuisine here was pretty average; nothing special. The chicken was medium. The burrito came with a cup of rice, beans, and a cup of guacamole. To help in keeping the bill down, we noticed the tamales and chips had been charged for. The server did help out a bit and he offered some suggestions for improvements which we were very pleased with. This place is a bit clunky, which would have been fine had the food not been so basic. Would not visit again as the food and service were great and the place was cool. If I were a paying patron, I would expect better service, and better food. It would be a good place to start but will not continue to stay with this location.

I was told that this place had been open for about a month and that it was going to be open soon, so I went along and bought some things Despite trying to eat out frequently, I still think that one of the things that makes The Bakehouse stand out from other sweet bakeries is the way It does require some trial and error to get used to the new flavors and products, but overall the bakery is really nice looking, and the staff was very nice The first item I really liked was the sweet potato and banana cupcake. You would think the ingredients would come from good baking, but there wasn't a too hot taste. It was pretty light on the cream so it tasted like it had been frozen a couple of days. I had two chocolate grahamcakes that were quite flavorful and had a nice smooth texture. Yes, it tasted great, and I knew what I was getting with the ingredients. It turned my stomach, but it wasn't too bad for the price, particularly considering that it was free for you when you purchase it. You know when you get the first bite in a bakery you're going to be like, "It's just a bit too rich for The coffee was good, but not as good as I would have liked. I would try it again, if I was not so careful with what goes in. I'll give it a few months to see how it does when it does come to a full serving.

We found the restaurant on a crowded Sunday evening just outside of downtown Orlando late at night. It looks like they're getting a little more organized. I was so happy to find out BRU had a big new roof over the patio. The awning felt clean and clean-looking, although the stains on the umbrellas were still there. It is an area where customers can take a break to relax to the soothing sound of the fireplace chiming in in the background. When the lunch was finished, we ordered our burgers. I expected a nice beef burger made with all the usual ingredients that I know and love. I'd have to admit, I didn't like the ingredients; the Brussels sprouts had a nice flavor and I liked the flavor of the cheese I think I would have considered it a "cheesy" type of cheese because the flavors were still good. I might be drawn back to this one in the near future since I was so impressed with the flavor and flavor appeal. I would definitely consider the burger as a "keeper" for me for the next time in the area. The burger was  tender, but the feta and fruit aioli were overly buttery. A solid lunch spot! If it were possible to make a better burger at BRU, I'd bring my friend back to try it again.

The park is very accessible. It's located at 6739 Walnut Hills Road in Greenfield NE, along Green Street. I did the 1 mile hike that I noted. The paved path was nice and easy to follow. It made walking around the park for about 20 minutes slightly more challenging than I expected. Luckily, I was able to cross it with my dog and walk next to it. The path eventually led down to the end, but it was quickly washed away and I was tempted to walk to the foot bridge in more effort to It did feel quite muddy at times, especially since the river was near. I didn't see this problem during my day trip, since I was walking in the park for more than about two hours. If people are trying to park in the grass or gravel, I'd recommend checking with the management to ensure that they don't have a problem walking There appeared to be an abundance of families parking up on the grounds, so it wasn't crowded when I went there. If you don't need to make a long trip to the park (which may be needed), you can still go by with car. However, the park itself has a great view of Green Street from a small viewing platform.

As a frequent visitor, I frequented CJ's Pizza on the way from downtown. The waiter took my order just as we were walking out, but I made it to the door quickly. I ordered a $1 pizza, which was really convenient since it seemed to be a really low price when I compared to the other fast food restaurants in I didn't think they would be as cheap, but I just figured, they already offer delivery. A simple and straightforward choice. It was a fast and reliable experience. I could've done a great job on that, but for such an affordable pizza slice, I felt like it was a lot easier! I haven't had a pizza from here long since my last visit, so I took advantage of a free coupon to go back. The pizza was very thin and thin crust, with a good amount of cheese. I also felt the cheese on top was good enough to eat by myself. I had two slices for $8.69. There is a great burger there as well!

I had been in the area for years but had never tried White Lick Creek Park. Here's what I expected when I set out, and that's what I got. I walked around the dog park without realizing I was headed to the playground side of the park. I discovered hiking trails, a children's play center, a frog pit play area, and an outdoor picnic area. There is a dog park and hiking trails. The trail system was quite impressive. This section of the park was pretty crowded. It was a fairly logical transition so my group of six headed another direction, taking I-95 to Parkway 51 to the north. There were many trails running down a large rocky ridge and there was also a dog park, a sand volleyball court, and  We parked closer to the community center than I thought, but the whole park was well worth the short drive. I also visited the dog park and playground and didn't see much hiking around, so I was happy to visit an activity center. There's plenty of opportunities for picnicking, for the kids, for the dog, or on trails. But, you will not be disappointed. I'll be looking for this park when I want to make an afternoon walk or a dinner out near us this summer. I believe the park is open from Memorial Day through Labor Day!

I always buy a lunch special at Scramble, and this time, I accompanied it with a drink. I ordered the Chicken, Bacon, and Salsa sandwich in the pepper jack and egg. My husband is into BBQ, but with his runner's up being my pick. All the meat was well cooked and tender and the slaw was very fresh. All the sandwiches are very huge. So good.Their sandwiches are huge and it's a good deal for lunch at my favorite local takeout joint! If you were looking for a quick lunch and a great sandwich, you will definitely want to order yours here.

I visited the restaurant El Taco on January 23rd, 2011. The restaurant is a small restaurant with two floors, with a nice looking patio. There is also a small grocery store near the front of the restaurant with shelves. So, I went to this location in hopes of trying out the menu. I chose the chicken and shrimp tacos as my lunch order (the polb Mole was still under delivery at this time.) But if you're serious about trying something new on a first date, go ahead and order one of the two regular types. So, I chose the Chicken Tacos, and got them ready for delivery. It took them about two minutes to come to my table and the wait was about ten minutes before I had another taco delivered. There were a couple of other staff members in my car (one helping myself, which was great), and it took the staff a few minutes to clear Not as busy as I thought, but still quite busy. There was a bag of chips to snack on (the ones that are not really chips, but they aren't really chips either, since I didn I found it odd that the menu only consisted of sauce and was not including anything for resale. Regardless, they brought my order, handed it to me, and I took the Polbmole and Carnitas for me. The fresh beef was fine and the chicken taco felt a bit dry. I guess the ingredients were good. The overall texture and flavor was average. I haven't seen it in a while and am mainly looking for Taco Shop review opportunities, but I am trying to be objective. It turned out to be a minor drawback. There was a bit of a garlic flavor, but that was about it. However, the lime really just didn't taste that great. The polbmole could have used some salt and pepper and been a little bit more spicy. I'd go back, but only if it was the Carnitas. They were pretty much just like any resto - just plain tacos. Weirdly, the mole sauce on the chicken taco made the chicken taco a bit chewy. I think it's a small price to pay, but not much I find at the local shops. It's a bit sad that the tacos weren't anything special. While this is a typical taco shop, each guacamole has its own brand for a different flavor. For now, I'll just go back and order some more of the sauces. As a whole, I was pretty disappointed.

I was in the area during the spring time and spotted this restaurant. We have always been fans of this place and hoped to go again someday. I ordered the chicken breast with sweet potato fries and my wife had a beef brisket sandwich with sweet potato fries. Not only were we directed to the "includes," but there were also several choices. My grandson ordered the pulled pork sandwiches with mashed potatoes with black beans as his side. He got the beef tenderloin ($8), a large hot dog with a fried egg, coleslaw (cranberry brown) Immediately he asked what meat did they roast there, and with his eagerness, we ordered all four (along with his buns). We shared..it was incredible! I think it would have been great if they got a burger too, too. Our first sandwich, the meatloaf sandwich, was our favorite. It was not seasoned so there was a bit of a texture difference but still a good fish sandwich. There was a bit of sauce and meat so it almost was overpowering when you ate it. The fries were seasoned and tasted great, although not all the dipping sauce they include tasted good. This past Friday was my favorite since our dinner was just a couple of days old! I actually ordered the brisket sandwich thinking that was a little on the lean side, and after much thought, it did not appear to be The two sides were simple. I could have gotten through about 18oz of the meat. I wasn't too impressed with the bun on either side of the meat since it was a bit tooggy, but I think that was a common I will definitely be back for more....it's always a good time. They also had a variety of sides, including a cold salad and a variety of sides. I thought they were nice and fresh, and the food came out fast. It's not a bad restaurant to dine at, though they aren't always the best. We had a large group at lunch and it worked out fine...not too many places that charge for half a plate of food. There is also a beer or wine license that is also available. I'll be back! I'll definitely be going back.

Not long ago before I left the Indy on my yearly visit to Zionsville, I made my way to Patrick's for lunch. On Monday (6-07-16), I parked in the first lot at the front of the restaurant near the South Central Mall after my office (the next This was my first visit at Patrick's and I knew I was in the right place. The service was friendly and the menu sounded good. This place specializes in crab cakes, but I found that the place seems a little lacking in the crab cake selection. Very tasty and good texture. The aioli was very flavorful and had a good taste. At lunch time, my wife ordered the Banana Split Salad - Chicken breast, red peppers, greens, bananas, and avocado. The berries on the salad were a little too tart, but the flavor of the vinaigrette was very flavorful with a nice Overall I ate three lunches at Patrick's! On Monday afternoon my wife and a friend of mine were in town catching up with one another. So, we set to go this time. We parked inside the restaurant andwalked to Patrick's and ordered lunch for the 2 people we planned to bring. They had a nice indoor environment and a nice sized patio to sit at. We had plenty of time to enjoy the lunch in the shade, and it came out fast. It was very tender and moist. I added a bite of chicken. The sandwich was very nice and the flavor wasn't bad. The sandwich was another good option for me. However, the salad wasn't as creamy and could have been served with toasted bread. I really liked the salad in the past, but really it was a little disappointing when it came out second when the entree came out first. We are not having a regular schedule so maybe that will be part of the decision. My final meal was at least 30 minutes later and that one was a keeper: my first dessert. She chose the peppermint mocha. The staff was helpful if I had any questions. I love the restaurant, always happy with the service and food there. If they had a larger cake with a smaller filling, we would've split it up (this review has an explanation). So, I'd say I would gladly return to Patrick's. Another great experience though! Overall, very enjoyable.

There is plenty of parking at this breakfast establishment; but beware the lunch crowd - you will have to walk in everytime you go! On a Monday morning in late April, my wife and I decided to take the family to this little place. We had an earlier reservation on Sunday at 6am and took advantage of it as we were able to eat in. The waitress was prompt, chatty, and friendly. We ordered our food and drinks in the order they were presented, while our server was cooking the food. We chose to order the same eggs for both of us as we like to sample different things each day, and it really wasn't enough. When I saw the Ralston burger (which I ordered with cream cheese and bacon) on the menu, me and my wife thought it was awesome. She really enjoyed the sandwich for the amount of food it had. I didn't get to try any of the foods on the menu, but I did enjoy the Eggs Benedict Sandwich - two slices of thick-cut She agreed it was huge! I'd have opted for the double ham, fried egg, spicy brown mustard, and on the bun, instead of four slices, but she It was even better with the addition of the spicy brown mustard. She really enjoyed her sweet potato waffle fries, as did my wife. The waffle fries were soft and slightly sweet. I decided to order an egg breakfast from there as well. After the breakfast meal, we ordered French Toast and the Crepes with Ham. I would have opted for French toast since it had an almost buttery texture. The bananas were covered with a delicious custard filling inside and was served with bacon and ham. The bananas were wilted nicely, with very little flaking. The Ham and Brie Crepe was very filling and also had two slices of the sandwich. I really enjoyed both flavors and overall the food was great. We thoroughly enjoyed our experience and it's a must stop as soon as possible! The place isn't without its problems, however, and the staff at this location are so nice and friendly to walk in and chat with you. You'll love it! It was a great night out and, if nothing else, will remind you that this place is the best in the city!

We set out for Japan to eat on a day where we were in town for school. It is located on the 3rd floor of the Northwood Market Village building at 2121 N. 3rd Street. We parked in the off lot with a lane through to the parking lot on Main Street. We had a reserved booth, but the restaurant itself was a full front door. A1 is located at 335 E. 6th Street (in the back), between a couple of small strip malls. My wife ordered the Gyoza (Panyaki grill fresh fish topped with fish sauce and dashi). Neither of these were our favorites but both were enjoyable and tasty. She ordered the "Sunset roll" (sadako salad with arugula, fried egg, pickled veggies). It was very good and very filling, and it was very pricey, but since it didn't have anything special in it, this is a Two of my selections were the "Sushi Sushi" and "Salt and Pepper Sushi". I selected the "Sushi Roll" with raw salmon (raw fish with a roll of rice) w/ jalapeno, and on It was served in a large glass container on the counter. The other was the Tori Roll (Tempura chicken, black beans, shiitake mushrooms, aioli, béchamel, The next item was for myself. The Salmon was prepared in Nigiri style and had a delicate salmon flavor with a tender texture. The size is smaller than other restaurants and the rice is smaller (about 4 pieces, or approx. It came with rice and a soy mayo dipping sauce). On the side, they had a nice presentation w/ the fish being all chopped up and served with green rice instead of rice. The salmon tasted really good, and the rice was still really good, although they were served more dry and had a bit of a crunch to There is something really exotic about this type of sushi. I liked that there were no added proteins (like rice), only a lot of salmon flakes. It was probably the best salmon dish I have ever had, even if the roll is a bit salty. Some of the gyoza were a little dry, but overall, a really good and fresh sushi. I feel like this isn't a good restaurant for every type of seafood taste, but the salmon for me was a wonderful experience. The fish was very clean - a good choice for anyone who likes fresh sushi. It was definitely worth the price. However, I felt that the Nigiri style was a little bland as did most of the other options, so this might have been a problem for I will be back! This is my go-to for salmon as well. I am a big fan of the Nigiri style at some places, including the Japanese Steakhouse and Sushi Bar in Boston and their Japanese Ste I ordered a second order the following morning. My last experience with raw salmon was at a different restaurant. I highly recommend the Nigiri style. The fish was tasty, and I thought it was great. Overall, A1 was excellent. I thought the fish was tasty and moist. The portion was about 4 servings, so it was pretty tasty to split. The texture was very good, especially with the spicy sauce that they did with it. I liked it enough that I ordered another piece to share a side. Our server was friendly and helpful. It's definitely something I like to try.

In a similar pattern, I did not need a drive-in from a store I had walked past, but my local Kroger wanted  I saw the sign in the windows saying they were open. I also had a good impression of the host. I came in to see if they were open when I came over. If something was open, they were open and with a sign on the window that was indicating they were open. Upon walking in, the host (or hostess) said "No problem!" The host seemed to have some knowledge of this menu. My friend suggests the Pollo Guizado and the moro (in the menu). The pollo was a dark yellow chicken with red and white coloring with a thick layer of red sauce overtop of the chicken. The moro was an Americanized salad filled with black beans, rice, and chicken flavored soup. The cooking/cooking was very easy, and the flavor was surprisingly good. They were a little tougher on the hands and legs but they were tender. The chicken was tender and the flavor was reminiscent of a chicken stew. Despite the fact that I am not a seasoned meat eater, I am able to eat chicken and pork. I liked the moro best, since it was like a chicken stew with rice and beans. The menu was full enough to order and the atmosphere and atmosphere was comfortable to be at. The chicken stew is served with the meat and rice, and it is tender (with a good amount of juice). I tried the chicken stew with the rice/beans. I would definitely order it again. The tortillas were not quite as thick as I anticipated, but I think that's just my personal preference. I did not taste the dressing, but once I put it atop, it became a smooth dressing. Salad didn't have any dressing on it, but it was easy to substitute for seasonings. The corn salsa was thick and fresh, but kept the yuminess, too. The flavors did not appear to be very strong, but they did a nice job balancing the acidity with all the flavors I enjoyed (banan This place was clean and the food was a bit above average. The lunch prices are reasonable at $24/ea. This was a great experience and I would definitely go back. For lunch, there are a couple of tables out front to accommodate for more. The food is decent, and the prices are reasonable. The service was friendly, but slightly slow.

Sun King opened its new food market at 6:00 am on Wednesday, January 22, 2013. We were really excited to have a little local farm-to-table in town. Its name comes from the location in France where the food truck that transported it was built in the middle of a winter storm. I headed inside and sat at a table near a high-top table with a view of the outdoor area. We rolled into Oca to grab a couple of sandwiches and some drafts. We ordered one each because we had been impressed by the quality of the bread we had at previous Sun King locations. On the first visit, I was just a bit nervous as I wanted to sample the sandwiches, but a quick phone call led me to the Oca I had to wait for the staff for a minute or so while I paid. and I said yes. We took a seat and picked up our sandwiches. The sandwich was delicious, crisp on both sides, and full of flavor and texture, with just the right amount of bread and sour cream. We also ordered the smoked meat pizza plate that includes cheese, onion, bell pepper, and olives. The sandwich comes in a variety of different toppings: French, butter cheese, mayonnaise, green onions, tomato, and black olives. Good job Oca and let's hope that they keep getting better! Thank you very much! The menu is pretty good, with a variety of items to try and choose from. There are two outdoor dining areas (on the roof) with an atmosphere of relaxed fun and an intimate atmosphere, though some of the seating is on the patio. There is a $5 cover for your meals. Please note that this is a diner! It is a short walk into the local beer hall. The drinks are not included in the restaurant pricing.

I had an urgent need to have my personal data recovered at 7am Monday after running a virus attack on my desktop computer. I went to the CIC of the Valley, and was recommended to call the Apple Computer Tech Support line around the time I feared that I would lose the The guys worked to get the hard drive back up and running. The guy was very nice and explained the entire procedure to me. The drive was about 80 or 80GB, so it was very big, but it was much smaller than I expected. I have saved all my important information on my desktop PC and other hard drives. After the transfer was complete, I was able to log in to my PC, and my old files and some software went back to the new drive. After the transfer, I can update the install of the drive. There are no added fees, so I can get a new drive for free. IT Indianapolis is located on 62nd and Broad Street in Indianapolis. Thank you IT Indianapolis for handling the issue so quickly. I highly recommend this company. Also, when you bring back your computer, they will set you up with an additional warranty. If you are planning on a drive replacement, there is a $2 discount to use on one drive, if they are able to recover it. I'll be going back to check them out! There is also a coupon coupon for their monthly cleaning/repair event!

I had the pleasure of ordering my last lunch at the Philadelphia Market today. I waited until it was busy in the back kitchen. After waiting for my order, I walked through the door and placed my order. The sandwiches were presented with two bags of baguettes. Usually, we have to remember the order they made for the week before to figure out what we want. The cashier asked me what I would like to get and we figured out what sandwiches we wanted. When I spoke to a second employee, he told me my order would be placed on a table inside of the back kitchen area. The assembler at the front counter was quick to take my order and even asked if I wanted more fried onions and more pickled peppers to He approached me and he looked at me, clearly confused as to if his sandwiches were done, and looked away from me. I was a little amused to see the sandwich arrived while I waited. Nevertheless, I wasn't very satisfied with the sandwiches. The sandwiches were served with a few slices of baguette and a small sandwich bag. They were held in one thick cardboard wrap and the other was put in a smaller paper wrap. It was hard to notice my sandwich was made out of paper, because as soon as the wrapper separated from the sandwich, it was hard to separate it from The sandwiches were very tasty and didn't have their usual burn smell. We actually made a lot of mistakes because the wrapper did not make the sandwiches any much nicer. But the onions, tomato and bell peppers were nice and tasty. The baguette came out well but the bun was a bit damp which kind of turned it against it. We were then split on the BALT sandwich. The beef was a little tough so I took a big bite and did not notice the bun wasggy. We enjoyed everything about it, but were both disappointed with the price. The price was about the same as most fast food restaurants, although it was actually slightly under $10. I would say the sandwiches looked a bit on the sour side, but that was probably a reflection of the quality, not the quality of the I will be visiting this place next time I am in the area.

I love Graeter's cookies and love their chocolate chip flavors! I walked in and tried it. What a delicious treat! It was a great experience, not to mention the awesome ice cream. It's the size and texture combines perfectly with all the flavorings in each ice cream. What will I do without Ice Cream?

Check out the pics below or this post to see more photos of our first day out of the park! What a great park this is! When I first saw this park, the whole area seemed to have been dingy and decrepit for a while. The improvements went to both halves. There's a lot of green space and a lot of open grass to run around on. The park looks a little dingy and the shelter needs some maintenance. Those who were waiting on the fairgrounds behind the rec center can now park here.

I had a chance to visit Oca a couple times in the early spring, particularly to try the "Sweet Bread Lunch" as an I had read about their plans for the new location and decided to stop by during afternoon hours. Our waitress was very kind and the food wasn't bad. I arrived at 2:30 in the evening and took a seat in the restaurant. We started with a "Groundhog Day" sandwich, which is a sandwich that uses three different bread types (I think, French baguette This is a French classic with a ham and cheese bun and I thought it was an easy deal to order from. We took our orders and were seated right away. There was about 15 minutes before the first delivery took place, so we finished eating and waiting. The bread was already pre-heated and was in the oven for 15 minutes. The sandwiches were well worth the wait. They arrived as promised, the sandwiches were nice and warm, and the pickles were very sweet but not too salty. Oca has a great concept with some great sandwiches with a unique selection like the Choucrote Grnie and is located in the public space at Luckily, there is no butter served on the Sandwich and I loved it! So when we walked onto the outdoor patio, we were greeted by an almost overwhelming menu. This is a huge array of meats made into an incredible meat carving in a wooden box (in the center of the restaurant). Obviously the restaurant is looking quite busy with everything from beer and wine to the fresh vegetables and the cheese. This time there wasn't to much meat on the plate. The rump was served under the French Bread in a large pan; it was called the "Knack" and the meats were all wrapped During the presentation, the Knack is seasoned with black pepper, spices, chives, and a few other spices to give the dish The pork chop was cut into thin slices and the thin skin added an extra flavor dimension and added a bit to the meat's flavor profile. Having read the labels of all the cuts, I was confused and went choking on the red ones. To my left were a large Swiss-style pork chop and a French roll. The center of this meal was full of very delicious chicken kielbasas too, not to mention the thin slices of Sausages and a To the right of the Knack was a small cup of Sauerkraut that I wasn't very sure what he was but it tasted So good!. And to the right of a couple sliced French breads: a large and toasted version that I enjoyed very much. To the right of the Bacchanele was a large slice of French Mac and Cheese that tasted as though there was a pan in the oven. That's a lot of meat and charcuterie for a lunch to start. This is the ultimate in "bistro dining." So much taste and it was all so good! For the next 20 minutes I took several minutes to look at it all and then the waitress came to ask me whether it was good or bad and I  A few minutes later, I had started to order the Choucrote Garnie and a salad was just beginning. We were ready to try the salad! It was very good, too. I'm quite glad I finally tried the Choucrote Garnie.The sauce of the mutton, egg and mustard is absolutely amazing. The rest served in a large container that made a really good little snack. So many delicious options and what can you ask for! The rest of the meats were just so delicious and the presentation so elegant (not to mention perfect presentation). I think these are all about 2 inches on the larger variety. The cutlets were a bit larger. To the left was a "pizza" plate with a wide choice of French bread and their new restaurant food brew.

A lunch sized entree is $5.50, which includes the soup. There are the traditional fried rice and Egg Drop to choose from and any of the entrees. I walked by this place looking for an open bar in my neighborhood today, but since the weather was pouring down it was hard to find parking. I love the atmosphere and it was nice to come in late. I chose the Recession Bockhorse Ale (at a very moderate cost); there were plenty of flavors to choose from, but I felt It had been a long time since I had a burger at lunch, so I ordered it. The burger comes with a delicious mix of bacon, pretzel bun, pretzel spears, and sweet onion. The burger was so good. The potato puree came with a nice fresh taste of sweet potato with a bit of heat added from the butternut squash (added in the process I think it would really add to the flavor or even make the burger itself so much better! I definitely made the pretzel bun a regular at home so I enjoyed the flavor of the pretzel. The onions were fresh and crisp and the greens were well-bought. It was great for a summer salad! I stopped by Bake n Pop to pick up the donuts from their pastry shop. The Maple Bacon and the Cookie Butter were the first two I tried. Recently we ate at Dr. Ralston's in Westville. I eat here about twice a week. Ralston's has a casual atmosphere that feels laid back and relaxed without being pretentious. What I liked most about the restaurant was the large patio, and it is perfect for enjoying a meal. We were seated immediately, and were immediately greeted by a friendly server. My favorite lunch time choice was the Duck Roll-up ($12.95): roasted duck (don't see it listed, I think the place was ): Mushrooms, onion, celery, pickled potatoes, and peach chipotle sauce. The duck was moist and paired perfectly with the gouda cheese. The gorgonzola was a little clogged up, but I liked how everything was just warm from the chicken. We also added a little egg and served it with a pickle spear. The sauce was smooth and not overly sweet. The sandwich was served with two sides. It was the Seared Shrimp, an explosion of fresh shrimp in sweet mayo and a touch of sweet buttery mayo (I added the honey Nice addition!.I have used this place several times now and it certainly serves well. The Fries were too salty to eat, but that was the primary reason I picked them. Great food, excellent service, and wonderful prices! Ralston's has a great atmosphere and offers great services.

I've been coming to Butler's on Lakeshore Road for more than 2 years and have had nothing but good memories. The landscape is just as beautiful as I could have imagined and looks so fresh and clean. With lunchtime around the corner from the office, I decided to check out the Nickel Plate location. One of my favorite stores in Indianapolis! The owners seemed to be very young - they had opened up in 1900, just before the Great Depression started. They started out as a chocolate factory in the early 1920's. The store at this time has been maintained very well. The caramels were great, so smooth and light but made with a strong butter flavor. Some of the flavors are made out of locally grown, fresh ingredients. All of the candy items are made from very fresh, well grown chocolate beans. Some are just chocolates. At an early lunch restaurant in the afternoon of 12/22/2017, I was in an area of the city with all the other people at lunch lunch. The Newfield's Museum Pumpkin Festival is going on at the university/new campus today and tomorrow. Originally, the festival had been slated to take place in August, but the plan was cancelled in early September. It was a very pleasant day for a fall festival. From the pumpkins to the fall decorations, the pumpkin garden is a great way to get outside. It is more than a field and field in the parking lot. There were also a number of fun activities and a craft area, like jar painting, arts and crafts from several local artists around the area and  Newfields opened with the local pub Oldfield's, which has a selection of beer and cider you might want to try. There is an outdoor area filled with local food vendors (Boeffer's, the Village Tap House-Gastropub, the Oldfield' Oldfield's is on the east side and another large tent serves soup and snacks. Two other vendor space is along the east end with a few coffee shops and gift shops. Some food vendors also have kegs with hot or cold tapas on hand. The music was great and everyone had fun on the floats. The entrance to the first day is through the east end of the museum, so it was a busy day that we were at the event but it seems to You get $5 off to get in and $15 off to get out. Once you are in the exhibit, you walk through a series of narrow pathways to walk up to the small room with an interactive interactive sculpture by Yayo That's because the entrance to the exhibit is on the 4th floor and you cannot go in until after 11 PM if you have an incompat I think it takes the Museum about 3 minutes to get through both doors (that's almost 90 minutes of wait time per person) for you to get in Most of the exhibit takes around an hour and a half to complete. This is where Kusama uses light to create the light patterns, which in turn creates the light patterns created by the mirrors. This is definitely one of my most favorite art museum exhibits. You feel like you are on a piece of floating glass. However, the art and this exhibit really brings back more memories of childhood. It's a beautiful display and, well designed and executed, there is lots of movement throughout the time at the museum. I think it was about two hours of exposure. You get so much light you never notice you are missing something.

My friend and I decided to stop in today for breakfast so that I could try out their new lunch special. The restaurant was located in a converted ice cream store in the basement. Meals were served promptly and the restaurant seated quite a few people. We were told that there was a limited number of drink choices and drinks available in the bar. The restaurant is very bright, with several tables located down at the bar next to the counter. I then ordered the Steak and Eggs with Bacon and Brussels sprouts and chips. The Brussels were good and I don't think it was all that expensive. I didn't like the addition of the celery topped with an overwhelming tartness. A little bit of sweetener worked well to accompany the rich and delicious flavor. I had a little bit of a kick that was still not too overwhelming, but it was definitely a bit too salty for my tastebuds My friend ordered the Wisconsin Classic Smoked Turkey sandwich with a side of chips. This took two bites to complete. The sandwich was warm and buttery with a light touch of heat. The Gouda was tangy with a little bit of salt just the way I like it. The sides we ordered included a chicken parmesan ranch salad, steamed broccoli, pepperoni chips, and a side of sweet potato fries The fries were deep fried thin with no flour. They were cooked perfectly and the texture was just right. The chips were served with some delicious sauces that were not as spicy as the meats or chips I was served. They were served hot, but they had a soft exterior. We opted for the slow roasted pork sandwich. The sandwich was slightly thicker than it should be, but didn't taste so salty and did a good job of getting the meat into your mouth It was so tender and didn't have any bad bite to it. Our meals went well. We decided to end our lunch with the restaurant manager as he had a busy day working the kitchen. Overall, this was a good time, but certainly not as great as an average restaurant downtown. I would definitely recommend Repeal to someone who does not see the place as a good place for great food and great price for excellent food. Food was also excellent for lunch. The patio was nice too. The price is a great deal, especially with the specialty cocktails that you get during the happy hour and after the bar.

I would like to see the restaurant become more familiar with the Japanese palate in the coming months because they have a lot of new dishes that I'd love Service was good.The decor and menu are also very nice. I was pleased with our dining experience, but didn't want to keep the place open for another large plate of dinner.

I have been astone creek fan for 8 years now. I think it's one of our favorite places in Central Illinois. I stopped going there almost 5 yrs ago and have been coming here ever since. Overall, it has been good food the last few years, although after living here quite a while, we are starting to give up the restaurant due to its We get lots of choices. The most memorable meal for me is the Shrimp and Scallops that everyone says is the best in town. We like to use the extra sauce on the shrimp and roll it up and serve it with a salad...or with a little pickle for a I also choose the Steak special that comes with a side of ranch dressing and a side of Louisiana shrimp. I like the Chicken special. They have a really good variety of fish to choose from and all of them are very good. It is a good choice for a cool lunch or dinner with friends or family. There is a lot to like about this location, but it is a little pricey. So there's really not a negative thing to say about this restaurant. The menu has become a bit more open to options like breakfast, lunch, dinner, breakfast and a bit of brunch. For us, we aren't going to miss the classic "Flatiron" style of dining which is really missing from the South Side in  It would be nice to take a meal outside or eat by the pool. I think this location is still doing fine and I am glad to see them getting some attention. A good deal of people would say that we lack any good restaurants here. If you have a good restaurant to support and a nice patio, you should be able to live here and love it. We like Stone Creek and we would hope they continue to be very successful for decades to come. As an aside, this place has a good reputation, which I applaud.

I was driving the drive from Cleveland to Detroit for lunch one day when I started wandering through Madison (Wilkes-Barre). It's located at the corner of 7th Avenue and North First Street and is located in a pretty interesting building that looks like a warehouse. Beech Grove is open from 7am-4pm Tuesday through Saturday and from 12pm-2pm on Sunday. The restaurant interior is quite different than this, but the tables are lined by huge white marble bar tops with marble floors. At that point the doors open. From here we could see the big window, a little bit off to the side next to the bar. This mural really does help to set theambiance for our lunch. I am not a huge fan of the decor but it's a lot better than most bar or restaurant settings. This makes me feel like we are in Italy. We had a nice seat and were comfortable. When I opened my mouth and I bit into my plate, I was immediately taken to the table, so I took one of the salads and sat The service was good, but the food and ambiance was just not quite up to par. The menu is a little limited or has a new layout which is nice for lunch. Best fresh Italian bread I have had in a long time. It also had a nice flavor. We ordered a couple of different sandwiches and salad. After the butter packets were removed, three plates came out, each containing two of their salads. Both of our lunch combos were great, with the bread being perfect, the presentation being beautiful, and the menu delivering great quality. The menu also came with a couple of recipes for their original house cheese dressing. The vinaigrette was very flavorful and very creamy. I actually ordered a small cup of the dressing because I was just hungry for the salad and had no choice but to sit down and eat the rest of My wife had an Italian sandwich topped with a thinly cut piece of cheese, a small amount of ham, and a piece of  It was also topped with the house garden salad. I had the Ravioli alla Reggiana with prawns and it was very good! Had a pretty good meal! The ravioli was pretty good as well, though I had to try more of their pesto sauce and some fresh basil. Also served with 2 sides as it had no cheese in it. I think I can have about 2/3 of what her sandwich had and the difference was really quite noticeable. We started out with our beverages and then our starters. I did not finish the sandwich until I finished mine and it is still on a plate. It was a good lunch, but not the greatest. I ordered medium so my sandwich was smaller and the lettuce was very tasty by comparison to it. Great lunch!I will definitely be back! Very fresh salad, but I can still taste the garlic from the dressing. As we were eating, the salads started out with boiled eggs then went back to the salads for a while and they took care to keep the I thought the sauce was a little less complex and served me overly garlicy so I would have preferred a lighter sauce. The food came out and I was looking for a pizza.

Great location on Park Avenue, close to South Side (very close to the intersection with Westside & 92nd) and the light rail train station. There are 8 tables and the atmosphere was intimate when I first walked in. The front counter has a large bar area with booth seating for 4-6, seating for about 15+, and a wall of tables and chairs. There are various items on the menu in the counter display, but one of the pastries is actually on the counter. After deciding on a pastry to try, a menu comes to me. Also, when I arrived at 11:45 to check out the coffee shop, the front desk was empty, but the staff was friendly and it seemed like there I was seated very quickly with a quick drink order to go, a small Danish, and a shot of coffee to go. The coffee had been sitting in the oven since 10am on a hot day (despite the early afternoon close) when it was ready to be picked up by While my Danish heated, I watched my order being carefully prepared by the workers and stayed in the middle of the counter area. The staff was very friendly, the drinks were priced well and there was no reason I wouldn't drop in to their little corner shop and enjoy a beverage My favorite part of their coffee was that they have various kinds of milk shots to sample and they have a nice selection of teas and creams. There is a faintish (?) square piece of debris that could puncture your skin (see below) and injure you. This was my only complaint and will probably be the last I ever go to Cafe Argentino and I doubt I would visit again. The cafe is not open on Mondays, but on Tuesdays, open on Wednesdays. Drinking at Tea Time Coffee is also non-perishable. Good food - excellent service. Great coffee!Great for a quick drink and a relaxing coffee experience.

The coffee shop is the same as both the Coffee Republic and Leibniz Kitchen stores. The bar is open by the counter, with a juke box that appears to contain the drinks (I wasn't aware of that option in the They do not have a bar or counter as their menu appears to be composed of smoothies, but they can provide drinks in the counter area. There are other flavors available out front, too. The servers then take away several glasses of your choice between a fruit and iced smoothie. After the smoothie was picked up, I realized it was an orangeberry, so I was a bit put off with the name. I was told that the coffee is infused with a lot of spices and my coffee was hot. I also liked that there was a small serving of fruit available. I would have liked it more if they added a dash of frozen yogurt. Note that these people are a little busy all the time, so I would suggest calling and being patient as you wait.

The Ogden Public Shop is an attractive tea shop located in the Ogden area of Ogden, Utah next to the Denver Mall. There is a large entrance with a small display of antique items. To the left of the entrance is a tea room with tea cups and a gift box located in the middle of the shop and the main entrance area to There are a number of different areas with large displays for books, plants, furniture, and other small items. There are various seating areas ranging from one to two people. This arrangement is very helpful if you know only one of the chairs. The shop was pretty busy at lunchtime. The restaurant only seats around fifteen people. I waited to be greeted, but the shop has a menu with a good variety of sandwiches and soups. I ordered the Poached Eggs Benedict and Mac n Cheese Sandwich. The menu has a variety of sandwiches and soups with large portions made with ingredients including a few eggs. A tea bag filled with loose leaf tea was offered for me a few hours later although for the prices of the tea and the service I probably would not return The tea was pretty good after steeping at about 60 seconds. To be polite and prompt, the waitress proceeded to provide the menu with the correct information and added the hot water and Earl Grey Steeple The tea came out and there was a little bit of a flavor difference between the two teas, but overall, the tea tasted fresh and not A fun little tea house with tons of unique items. Also, there are a good number of items at the tea room. Yes, it's also a restaurant.

It may sound bizarre, but many people have to miss some amazing places they visit around the country. So I decided to go to the great local coffee shop, Tinker Coffee, even though I only had walked into the space once. There was a long line to get in (by appointment only), but I made it before it closes so I could take advantage of the good things. Because I had never been on this particular street before...and I have really enjoyed it since my time back in the late 90s, I have become very  I walked over to Tinker Coffee atop the building (constructed ca. 1778), which was rumored to have been built for wealthy men, in a time when there was really just an abundance of small places. There is also a small gift shop or store next to the coffee house on the ground floor. If you're a downtowner, you probably won't be so surprised as I was when I came in: the place opened up very quickly. I quickly noticed that these people were lining up to receive their coffees, so I didn't know that my meal would be ready in the time it I wanted to meet the lady who would have an appointment with me when in was ready to take my order. She just made my coffee and then walked me up to sit on an open spot, just right in front of the counter. I felt free to order a bite and I was pleasantly surprised. We did this while the coffee was still on draft. I got the Pancakes. There was also a savory sandwich options on the menu, but the one I chose was the French Fries with Apple Preparation, which was  What a fresh, warm, and flavorful breakfast treat! It wasn't very filling (not even fresh). It was a good-sized sandwich and delicious. We shared one of each, and didn't even realize how good it was. It took a couple of minutes to get my food there, so I had to go to a different location in the hotel for the coffee. And, a coffee that is so fresh and enjoyable, it doesn't burn. This place is a quick, comfortable place to visit. If you have a special time, order at least a lunchtime and dinner time, and be open during happy hour. All of the food options were fresh and ready for you to enjoy. Food is made on orders that go out first thing in the morning. I didn't stop by the counter to pick up breakfast because it was getting really early, or because I wanted to visit the café. And the price was also reasonable for the place. They have been doing this for years and I would do it again! No, I wasn't busy. It's a cute little shop with a small coffee shop, but that doesn't keep them away from the people of the neighborhood. So, if you are a fan of coffee, and you'd like to go on a lunch date, this is the place to go. If you do want to, just let them know upon placing your order. The staff has become friendly and helpful as the bartenders have made many friends from this neighborhood cafe.

So we recently went to the Walnut Creek store, and one of the things we thought was great was the amount of art they had. In fact, I had just visited their website and was impressed. There was just about every type of stuff you could imagine. We actually met the store's manager, Scott. There was even a store named SECURITY GOLF in the store, so I thought it was good to check it out since I do not Our first interaction with the store was with the owner, who was nice enough to look over the products for us before taking them to the shop. He came back and did not want to even talk to us for like 10 minutes. HORRIBLE! Good for a limited time only. Our next stop..

First time here and wanted to review our new neighborhood restaurant. So I asked around and found this one that was close to our apartment and I was really excited to check it out. I am really happy I tried this restaurant; very well done! for a limited time. The entrance is located on the corner of North and West 12th Street by the entrance to I-80. Turn west to the right by the median and walk past several McDonald's to access the entrance. It's about 7 minutes from downtown Chicago. The entrance is not clearly visible at all. The next to the order counter are the tables and chairs and the register. There you order.) A lot of tables are surrounded by outdoor sitting space. There is little bit of seating in front of the counter, but if you look at the sign that says "You can sit here... but it takes us We have an automatic water fountain, but I don't think I'll be trying it until I'm done eating. We stopped for lunch around 4pm and everything came out pretty quick! The salad was very good with the sliced onion, tomatoes, and cucumbers. With tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots, and celery. The chips were good and thick but not tooggy, not tooggy like some other chips. I then went back to the sandwich and ordered the Chicken Portobello Sandwich and a side of chips. As far as the chips are concerned, I haven't tried the chips here, but they are still great. The chips were good, but to be fair, they are a bit salty. I was pleased with the quality of the food and would definitely return. On the next trip to the restaurant, I will definitely try the "farewell" menu option! I will absolutely be returning soon for their lunch special menu. You will have to go in for your meal and it was very fast. A LOT of good things to say about Taziki's! And the chips were always fresh and on the side. I would eat there again, and again and again.

The Goodies and Pet Supplies is a pet supply store located in the South Side. There is a great selection of new foods as well as a nice selection of "known" pet foods. There is a whole wall devoted to animal health products, including animal & human-derived supplements. They even have a small display of toys like balls and cuddlers that the dogs do not usually see. The dogs here all drink their treats, which would be good for you to do to them if you don't mind a little rancidity. There is even a bowl and toy that your dog can run around, just like a pet. In the back there is a large selection of treats for you dogs to choose from. There are a ton of bags of dry dog food to chose from. They carry their selection of treats in a variety of sizes for your dogs. After visiting, I decided to come back again and see what was out and about. He then gave me some sample packets and I placed them in the treats. All of these are vehemently safe for dogs to eat. Obviously, the portions are small, but they did include enough for my dogs to eat all day. Overall, I would highly recommend this store. It was very close to where I live, but a 45 minute drive away. I wish there was a Pet Food Store in New England but you definitely find one in our area.

I was going to the Wal Mart store and have to say, this one is an attractive one. The store does have the same large selection and price point as Pier 1 in the Willow Lakes. A great way of saying thank you for all the wonderful items you bought here to help make the shopping experience so easy. The jewelry is great and they are constantly adding new items as well. There is plenty of parking on the main driveway/lot, but you'll have to park near the door. There is only one entrance to Pier 1. If you ever stay in the area try to be a bit careful so you don't miss out on any opportunities. I was there on a Saturday so I thought it was a good location. With a couple short blocks in the center of town, it won't take long to find parking.

This is the second time that we have had a lunch here. The wait was pleasant, as I was able to get into the restaurant as late as 10:30 a.m. or whatever time was convenient for me. They also added seats to the waiting room and they provide extra lighting when needed. I was greeted in a pleasant manner. The menus clearly stated that the place had Japanese bento and was for lunch only. While I was waiting for my lunch, I asked the waitress what the lunch combo menu entailed. Not too long after my question, they informed me that they only offer lunch menus and that they do not have any items available outside of their original lunch menu I ordered the rice a bit too soft for my taste, so I went with a side of nigiri salmon with a bowl of They had two packages of nigiri salmon at the time and I ordered my own. The seaweed salad was very different. The salad was surprisingly fresh and the texture was perfect. This seemed to be a really good salad. I will add that the sauce on the salmon was very sweet (not very satisfying) and I would have loved more of a sweet tangy flavor in This isn't because of the fish itself which I found the pieces tender and flavorful, but because it was missing the fish sauce used during the preparation The rice was a little on the sour side and too much water was left over for me, but the sauce was still flavorful. It took me about ten minutes for my food to be refilled. Count me out of my review! This review is based on myself and my wife's experience, so I wanted to give both restaurant and reviewer something to write about.

After visiting a friend for a few days of beer and wine and not wanting to go in today without a visit or a side meal, we I didn't want to give twenty tips, but they were really great! This restaurant, based in the historic Old Town district and located at 1775 West University Avenue (McNeil). This place is clean and the staff are all very nice and helpful. Looking for an appointment, I parked at the northeast corner (the one near the airport). We made a nice, long walk of about 15 minutes to get to the door and had an easy time getting to the inside. There is a sign that says "20 Tap" on the door, so be prepared if it's a little crowded. I wasn't disappointed! The staff was friendly, chatty and made sure we were comfortable while enjoying their wonderful food (so fresh, juicy and flavorful!). When I was brought my food at one of the counters, they brought me a drink and served us right away with coffee (and they were great). The menu has a good beer selection, but I don't think I would have been able to go back to try a beer off the menu When we arrived at the bar, we were seated right away and the total bill came to about $100 for two people. Headed up with a really tan colored beer head, but a strong, smooth tasting, cold beer. Two of my favorites were my sandwich and the salad. I also ordered my favorite sandwich for lunch. What better way to eat short rib than with grill-side fries? I made my order at 3:00 since I needed to reach a car before that appointment (about 20 minutes later) and had the sandwich by myself. The food was deliciously flavorful with great, but still slightly meaty flavor. Even though it was a  grill, the hot sauce inside really came through! It was really delicious, and my mom ordered both pizzas. The bourbon glaze turned a little dark, but really only tended to brown the meat up. The jalapeno marmalade added a whole other layer to the sandwich and it kept it from falling apart. My dinner companions ordered the French Waffles and they were also delicious. A perfect ratio of heat to potato. Also, the garlic flavored salt sprinkled on top for a delicious garlic taste. This was one of my favorite lunches of the summer and I'm sure next time I will make it back and try something new and awesome. The sides were likewise well prepared and served with a little bit of a kick, albeit a little bitter. It was really quick to get in to get our drinks and order, and we would be back soon for lunch. All their beers are craft beer, but brew-a-tasting is always fun to try and you really can't go wrong!

Having frequented a few other restaurants over the years, I was quite surprised and pleased with the new look of this restaurant. The new location is a bit small, but it has plenty of space, even in the basement bar. It was just like every other place on campus. They also have a nice selection of IPAs and craft beers, and have a bar/pub next to the patio. There is a nice, warm, and inviting light-filled interior. The food and decor have been given a fresh, bright look and feel. There are several seats on the patio. The selection is good, but we were not sure what we wanted. The bartender brought us their special drinks before we even got in! My wife ordered the "Big Mouth" bacon burger. The burger looked great (as per the sampler, it came with a good amount of brioche) and was tasty too. The bun was really nice with a tender little bun on top. The breading on the French fries was nice and had a nice golden color. The burger served with bacon and egg was delicious! My wife ordered the "To Die For" Beef Tenderloin Burrito. I wanted to give it a try, and thought it was a good choice. All the sides of her dish were good, with a thin layer of dressing on the bottom. I really liked the garlic chicken, although I don't mind the garlic. She had asked for the fire cracker shrimp of the previous business, so we ordered the "fire cracker shrimp" and she was blown away! The ketchup was not as good as I have liked, but had a nice consistency. I will definitely return for dinner. This is a great place to go for lunch as well as grab some drinks before going home. The portions are adequate and great for lunch time dining.

Joe's Butcher Shop/Joe's Next Door is one of the best food shops I've been to in South Florida. I feel that it is so important that I make myself a stop at a deli when I want to get a burger before going back to But if they have some great sandwiches to go with all of the great ingredients on the menu and are served fresh daily it's all worth it. Or even a cute little sign on the side of the shop that says "JOE'S". What more could you want? The deli is located in the heart of the retail community (not just for those putting together the house party). Joe's is a two-story shop with a large covered patio and many convenient items in both the back kitchen and the main meats section. The butcher shop has a variety of cuts of meat and meat cuts from local butchers. In the back of the shop, you still see a small dining room that is open on the weekends and closed on Sundays. We were greeted by an owner, who had already taken our order and was able to give us a quick look at the menu with us. The description on their website listed the ingredients for the sandwich and what we ate. The classic bread served with the sandwich is house-cured bacon. The cured bacon cheese is so soft it melts in your mouth. The meat has a unique texture, almost like it was naughty and made with the freshest ingredients. On the bottom of the sandwich you'll find the house pickle on a house rolled egg white (I always like my cheese on a soft It's a great sandwich for me. The sandwich comes to a medium on the outside of the deli, however a small one on the inside. The roast beef was very tender and flavorful. The beef was tender, sliced thin and seasoned well. The sandwich also required salt and pepper since most of the ingredients were house-sourced. One thing that needs a bit more attention is the coffee so it was a nice change of pace for us. We left happy and ready for the workweek. The sandwiches were ordered and delivered without wait, which saved me considerable time when I were ready to go home. The sandwich was brought out before we were finished and we both enjoyed our sandwiches. Order your sandwiches and then head downtown and enjoy the wonderful neighborhood while looking for some great food.

I had heard on the radio about El Palomo being close and wanted to give it a try. We stayed at the Wyndham at this address for two. Initially, the manager called to remind us that we were only on a special and apologized for that. There were a few tables outside and outside of the kitchen where you could see the host. At an all-suite restaurant, service was really good. At the end of the meal, their names were marked by an amuse-bouche and asked us if we wanted to try other dishes. The waitress was the older. Long waits on the kitchen counter and chairs. We were told they were moving to a new location, so we waited while our waitress picked up the plates. Waits for food was pretty long and there was no cheese for my tacos despite having free chips and salsa on the menu. It took my wife a while to explain to me that there wasn't cheese with our tacos (even though she had cheese in her shirt). She mentioned the menu was very limited and that we went to see if anything came in that area. And then the meals arrived and were a good size. The chips were the same as the salsa served with the tacos. Also, the chicken tortillas (in Spanish) were very good, almost like chicken burritos with the chicken flavored tortillas mixed with beef All in all, it was not bad, but we were more excited about a taco than we were about the entire meal in general. The steak was seasoned well, had a little bit of a smokey taste that I didn't particularly like, and was a little tender They had a peppery kick to them that was a bit overpowering. We ordered another salad and the manager offered a little bit of her own ranch dressing, which was ok, as I like my ranch dressings to run We would recommend trying this place, however. In general, there's a lot more options for Tex-Mex restaurants.

The park is located on the border of the village of Eastwick and is used as a park or an educational center. The park is surrounded by beautiful woodlands and a wide series of trails for hiking, running, biking and horseback riding on the hills. The grass is tidy enough that it is easier to walk out and get a cup of coffee. No one is allowed to use the bathrooms here, but it does not take children or pets. The house is a beautiful building on the site of the old West Family residence. The houses sit on a large site west of the main road that runs from west to east of the city. The James C. McKinley house was built in 1916, just south of the park entrance. The area was later used for commercial purposes by the West family for over a hundred years, including serving as the home of the U.S. Secretary of There is a picture of the site from a newspaper article published in 2002. The original house was purchased in 2006, and in 2007 the house was sold to the town and is housed on the park. The West-Harris House sits as part of the 96th Street Park. At around milepost 12 there is a small water park with a paved water way which can be pushed by foot or car. We did go back on Saturday, September 30th, but will again be closed through October 1st due to the construction of the road on 106th If you do not believe any of this is true, look for a map that gives directions (towards the entrance at the end of the road at Then go west to the park entrance on North 106th Street and then East 106th Street to finish the route.

My family and I had lunch at Nada at the Wyndham Marriot this past Thursday. A few weeks ago, we had both visited the San Diego location, but with an empty dining table we thought this would be a good time to try something Looking through the signage made us think Nada is a busy restaurant. The restaurant was small, so we all sat outside, with the patio just behind us. The menu looked very different than what it would have been if I had known that the food had an English word – “taco,” which would The tacos we ordered with our lunch consisted of the "Al Fuego Salad" and the "Que El Cianfuego They are also topped with some of the best guacamole I have ever tasted. The next item to try was the tacos. Third, we started ordering the main courses. Some of the menu items that you find at Mexican franchise restaurants contain chicken or fish, and the beans are served on a toasted flour tortilla. The pickled cucumber salad was good, but the chicken tacos were a bit dry. Each taco had a fresh filling and the rice was served with the rice and corn on the side. My other friends ordered the fish/tequila combo, which was excellent. My group also shared the fried egg as well, with just the egg thrown in. We shared the rice bowl and the beans and rice on brown rice also. As they go out of business this will be their last visit. It is also a fun place to go solo, which is nice from a food perspective, so I would definitely recommend this place! Be sure to mention on your first visit to Nada you saw me with my dog.

I walked into the store to find it kind of like my previous version. On this occasion, it was a bit packed. There was a lot of selection of cards and other items and one of the things that attracted me to this store was the nice gift box that they had There was a little line and it took a bit longer than usual to check in. I will be returning to enjoy the other and will recommend it to customers. If you want a shop that has some kind of customer service, this one is a little less than I had.

I stopped by Mead Sushi and was happy to find there was open. It was nice to see Captain Sushi located downtown, on 2nd Street and N. Ladson. This was a dark, somewhat sterile environment. On the other side is a bar where customers can order kebabs and salads as well as drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic). The entire place was busy during lunch, so there was a wait, but not this long. I decided to order the spring rolls, spicy salmon and sushi roll. The Spring Rolls came at about 4 AM. The spring rolls were an amazing combination of fresh and sweet flavors. The sushi rolls had green mango-yellow and yellow/amber-green fillings and were perfectly cooked and moist. The rolls were light and airy which is a good thing on a hot day because they were moist and delicious. Initially these were slightly hard and a bit cold, but over time took on a "thick" and crusty taste. It took only about 2.5 minutes for them to be made. The salmon nigiri was a medium (I think it was a little bit underripe) serving of salmon. The salmon was 5 pieces that ranged in price from $5.25 to $7.25. The insides were layered on but still had excellent flavor. The nigiri was wrapped in romaine, with a little sauce to bind the seafood. There was also an orange sauce topped with salmon, raw egg, and yellow tail. It really stood out in the dish and the flavors were so strong. The nigiri was also very good, but the rice tended to get a little too dry during the chewing. So good that they did a full take of my favorite sushi rolls from Iwane, Japan! I was in a wee bit of a pickle funk and didn't go very far. I think the eel-avocado rice will be hard to find out from my regular roll and it wouldn't be my first The nigiri, however, was more tender from start to end, and again was very good. I recommend coming from the south or south east for a few minutes of dining here, then back for lunch. Not bad.. If you walk by, you won't miss this place. Would absolutely eat here again. It was an excellent experience!

Yummy Italian Pizza opened and ran as a franchise in 2012 and has continued to expand since, but this restaurant has remained in business. It is easy to spot this place from the parking lot behind the movie theater. I knew nothing about the place other than the resolutely pizza-y smell in my fridge. The pizza was on the menu, but I decided to order something from their menu which was a little less than the size I requested. The pizza had lots of toppings including pepperoni, pepperoni, tomato and ranch on it. The pizza arrived just a few minutes later after about 5 minutes, the pizza was about half made before it even arrived. I loved the sauce and the flavor. I liked the sauce, which had a little salt on it rather than the usual pepper spray/hot sauce that you should find on most Pizza places. My favorite topping was the olives and marinara sauce. I didn't finish it, but there were plenty of smaller pizzas than my usual pizzas. If you plan on going, it should be very easy to go with a car and that's nice because these type of places are becoming more of  Upon my review of the pizza I had to go to this place for the whole week of October because I've only been by this place once, and If you're looking for some quick yet solid fresh pizzas with a slightly higher pricing (and less cheese) go get it down to Marco's

We stopped at this shop for one of the local quilt shows, and were a little concerned because some pieces in the shop were sold out. We were both on the fence about trying this store because of the lack of seamstress and quilter sections. My wife is an upholstery and seamstress. I wondered to her what the "quilt" section was for, when we came in to view the selection. She also was very interested in getting a free pattern to use to create her own clothing. No way she is going to get it all, but what I can confirm is that it is a well appointed shop. All of the supplies are high quality. It was packed.! Sometimes they have "unique cloths" (not sure if they have it in stock), lining fabrics (i.e., the fabrics  at the shop.. I had never had egg rolls before and this was the first time in years I had had egg rolls. It was the most delicate and soft-tender rolls I've ever had! The eggs were tender and the spring roll was just a touch chewy. I was told they were not too dry so I ate more, because I didn't feel like being dipped! The egg roll was topped with mayo, but with a kick. I wasn't completely impressed, but I felt good after every bite. The Tiger Roll was next after the egg rolls. It was so much smaller than I expected, but the actual meat was a fairly tender bite even though the rice was dry. When I bit in, I could see that the middle was about in size and the bottom was about half the length of the top. I ordered it and was surprised to be seated in a corner after that. I had to bite a bit harder to get the sauce onto the roll because the rolls do not like the sauce so much. Not as good as the egg rolls of course, but I would imagine that a better roll would have made it easier to hold. After the Tiger Roll, I took my Magic Salmon Nigiri order. I wrote down the ingredients in my order and the name, so I assumed that they would include salmon and a green onion. When it arrived, there was only 1 piece of raw salmon. I was so disappointed! With all of our experience this is definitely something to recommend. They actually brought the nigiri back to my table, but I didn't know it would be done this way! Oh, and the nigiri was not cooked. The nigiri was so good! As a result, my review was incomplete by the time the food arrived. Didn't really get an idea of what it was. Also, I was pleasantly surprised how quickly I was able to be served without waiting. It was tasty, but a little pricey for lunch!

I had dinner and a drinks at this family restaurant on my way to work today. The restaurant was called Slenders Restaurants in the location known as the "Foxmarket". From the outside, look for the building which is over a block and was used as the former home of the old Sears department store. The space has been converted to an upscale restaurant including The Red Bar. It's veryreminiscent of a large department store when the building opened on Market in 1930. This means the dining room is smaller, and the restaurant serves primarily lunch. In addition, there was a large bar next door that is open to the restaurant. There is very little seating for parties of four or more. There was no additional seating in between the dining room and the bar. The menu does not take to the menu very well, but the entrees were good and had a good variety. The prices was affordable with reasonable lunch prices. The drinks were decent, considering it was a Sunday and the menu had a good selection. While I will admit to not eating at this venue again, it is certainly worth a try. No tables outside of the restaurant, so you have to walk to the patio for the rest of the meal. You never know if a person could be behind the work table to get a seat after 15 minutes. It is far from the City Hall, along Market Street and Meridian Street, and the parking lot is in a bad location. Although there are a few available parking spots on Market, this is clearly a work in progress due to the low traffic and the lack of signage and parking I had a enjoyable time, albeit not as good as I hoped or expected. We were glad it was still a restaurant with no wait, but I would not say that lunch was particularly enjoyable given the price. The staff was too friendly to offer a refund or exchange (at their discretion) for the bad meal and the wait.

I finally made it to Oakmont. Good food but just too busy. Oakmont is a great restaurant and bar. It is currently occupied by 2 bars and a restaurant that sold on weekends. This place has so many choices, it was pretty hard to decide which one was the best. Even though I was expecting a sandwich from any home, I was pleasantly surprised when I walked in. The sandwiches were good, but the sweet potato, peanut butter and mayonea sundae was over rated. They even have a ice cream parlour to mix with the PB.
