I think I am on a winning streak with this place. Maybe it's the restaurant itself? Just another place to wait out the Summer heat in hopes it won't kill the fish. Maybe it's the delicious meats, especially Prime Rib and crab cakes. This is a place I had originally seen on "The Tonight Show" when I was about ten years ago (I can only remember once). We have visited many times over the years and have always enjoyed the food and service. After arriving a friend and I decided on the shaded patio to sit and enjoy the view. After reading the reviews (or should I say reviews?), it was really obvious we wanted to be at the restaurant. We waited for 10 minutes before the server brought us our food and gave us our seat. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and if you were in the mood for Mediterranean food, do what I did - it's delicious! I ended with the Wisconsin Beef Tenderloin Sandwich. The sandwich was warm and piping hot with little bits of cheese, but still had a bit of the richness to it. She asked for horseradish but it was actually mixed in with the cheese. The prime rib had a great flavor profile that combined well with the sauces. It was moist and had a nice tender cut. The sandwich complemented the au jus. The ketttlechips were sliced nicely so they were nice and tender. In the meantime, I was a little dish overjoyed that I had already ordered the Prime Rib Crab Cakes. These were served with a spicy mayo, green onion, and crabcake filling. There was a large cup of sauce on the side which I loved. The crab cakes were baked to crisp at the center and the sauces were similar to those that come from the Maryland Shrimp cakes, but they were covered for I never thought crab cakes were any different than the other crab cakes, which makes them a good eat for lunchtime and dinner tables. A must if you are coming to the Mansion! I really enjoyed my crabcakes. Finally, I opted for the Prosciutto-Gryeran Asparagus Blankete. My husband couldn't get enough of the blankets as well. It was served in a blanket which was filled with toasted ciabatta bread. The asparagus was seasoned with salt and pepper and then the wrapped dough was thinly cut into half-slices. The menu looks very diverse, so this is a good change of pace for a lunch before going out for dinner. The asparagus pieces were wilted and then baked in an oven to perfection. The sandwich came with a dollop of sweet tomato juice which was perfect for a light lunch. The fish is served with the sauce allowing the fish to cook under the cold light. There are always a few more fillets in each blanket, which are paired very well. Yes, it's like the inside of a palazzo. The bread was perfectly done and I enjoyed the flavors. Great food here in the Mansion! A very nice lunch idea and a very happy time. The restaurant is incredibly large and you will be seated on all sides of the patio (on the lower level only). The blanket was delicious, too.

At 6 am, my wife and I were driving via the north/south freeway to Outlier Brewery for a light lunch. We were there for a local brewery event, and wanted to try a few of the beers available. At first, we sat on the outside patio at the front of the building. If the patio is open, the place would be great. It was rather quiet for a patio restaurant. This was not a very good looking patio. At least that was my impression.  Anyway, we were seated and had a pleasant wait for our  drinks. She took a very friendly interest in our order and gave us good suggestions. They have a variety of beers throughout the menu and seem to be of a good quality. I went with 2 of the 3 beers (The Farmer's Union and Hop Girl.) Like with most beers in New York I expected to enjoy all three. I thought Mayfly was a bit too bold - I like my beer dry, but not overly so. However, for the price, I couldn't feel that the beers here were anything special. My wife ordered the crepe canton. She then chose the Garlic Aioli sauce to dip the crepe, which I am not sure was as good as I had hoped. She thought she had noticed some salting on the crepe when it arrived: the milk and orange juice that it was cooking in seemed almost too salty. It was definitely a little lacking in flavor, but just a little lackluster overall. It tasted a bit salty and we probably would have ordered something else to snack on. We were hungry again, so we walked over to the patio to get the Sandwich and dip. The sandwich was accompanied by a small glass of wine. The marmalade was an excellent flavor, but that was definitely not what I was expecting from a duck Confit. In addition, there was a small amount of cranberry jam. It was definitely a side item, but since I wasn't in a rush, the sandwich seemed to be the only option. The fruit and cheese, though I would have liked, had something to add. Like the food, it didn't have much flavor, but that wasn't really a problem either. The other side - the side of calamari was very good. It was surprisingly dry. All in all, I definitely will not return. The food was priced modestly. It was tooggy. I wouldn't say that I was winging it. And then came our bill, which was a bit steep for the amount I paid. There are lots of restaurants around here where the fish can be served with cream and/or a pickled side of raw fish. They should think about that.

Lilly Lake Park is located in Indianapolis on a 100 acre piece of land that is bounded by Otis Ave on the south side, To be fair, not all of that is a waste, since most of the park is riparian forest. The park was donated in 1999 and opened September 29, 2010. The area of this city park contains about 17,000 acres of habitats and provides a variety of activities for the public. Before I made my way to the park, I began on the Red and Blue Trails. Since I wanted to get to the boat ramp, I took the river path. The first section of the blue trail leaves the park just northeast of downtown. The entrance to the park can be seen on the east side of the trail near the south end of the park. The trail starts with a simple ascent through the woods past a tree and then past a few ponds. These are shade trees, picnic tables, and tables with an air pump so you can stay dry during the summer. While that may not be a problem in areas where the trees are so dense, it can be a bit tough to reach them at times if you The path enters a small marshy area at the entrance to the lake at a point where the path runs parallel to 2 roads. The trail then begins to take a turn towards the yellow bridge and ends here where it loops around before continuing. There is a large waterfall and a lot of natural moss on the path and a lake that was formed by a river. The loop around Lilly Lake is about 3 miles and I would recommend this two-mile hike for those visiting on a summer day. There are a few steps back from the wooded path. The road to the lake, however, is very narrow and passes through the middle of a field and into a pond (it's also  The remaining part of the park is pretty typical of the nature park - lots of park benches, shade trees, and playgrounds. If you do the trip, be aware that it is an easy hike for most of the way. Unfortunately, the wooded trail runs almost immediately after the blue trail, so the northern half of the park is rather uninteresting.

The McBean County Forest Preserve had an open enrollment meeting for October 20-21, so I signed up on their open enrollment/mini-season plan Not sure how I feel about this new program and haven't been formally affiliated with the center, but the nature center is open every weekend and is I knew it was not going to be a hike, but figured the locals would enjoy the day. This particular tour is only scheduled during the first week of March. A couple weeks ago I used the weekend to get my family out and enjoy a little something we don't do for a few hours each month. There is an information booth and then a short rope walk. There were a lot of nice displays throughout. Some have small displays of plants and animals. There is a little gift shop with toys, hats, shirts, and other items to look at. There are also lots of educational displays - a library, a field guide, and a little kitchen area. There are also displays for local plants and birds and some interesting pictures of native flora. The manager, Tammy, was very knowledgeable. On the tour, we were also able to hear and see the different species of plants that were growing in the back yard. Just wanted to mention the tour was pretty cool because after about 15 minutes of talk, she got all the details about the wildflowers that we were to encounter The first part of the tour has a walking loop that the park officials took me on to find the "fannie" that the center wanted. At first, we thought it would be a simple walking path, but we quickly realized the path had some cool twists and turns. The trees in the area are so diverse that they are completely different as they are in an area surrounded by manmade vegetation. It was nice to see the animals on the trail while sitting and drinking my hot tea. The trail follows trees and is a loop around the lake. At the end of the loop, you walk around around the area to view some of the wildflowers that have started blooming. I was really impressed and it looks like many of the trails are open seasonally, so you can go during the fall and spring. I think I'll make a stop again to see what's growing at the park! If you are able to participate and find out about some new things about the area, this is a great place to start.

Wabash Brewpub offers a great selection of beers that are both delicious and accessible. This place was on my list to try. I found the place relatively small and dark. The restaurant is rather small, but they don't have much space to do other than fill up the bar. There is a small entrance to the brewery as well and they have a little bar on the right side of the building that you can enter by way of The counter is not very well staffed and the bar is very busy. There are six styles; a couple of beers. There are also additional choices such as a special flight of three beers, a double flight, half flight, and one flight. There are four brews to sample in this flight as the menu is on the right side of the counter. The first and closest drink I sampled was the Light Blonde (4.9%, 10) from the Barefoot Brewing Company in Chicago. This was a stout style wich had a medium body with a nice fruity, sweet flavor. The malts had a nice taste of menthol and fruit. I then moved on to the Blue Beet Red Ale (6.9%, 34 IBU). I feel like the cherry scent mixed in with the sugar brought it back into my taste buds! It was fairly smooth. I then went with the Belgian Style Red Ale (4.6%, 16 IBU), which was a clearer beer. This was a very nice Belgian Blonde with nice pale color and an excellent Belgian taste. Just like on a flatbread, this pale epineph line poured on itself. When I finished, I pulled up my flight and had my pick of the BaconFace Brown Ale (5.8%, 20). This didn't have any taste or flavor but overall didn't feel like an IPA or Belgian pale Ale much like the Wentworth Brown Ale It was a very mild beer that tasted like an IPA or pale ale. Overall, this is a great place to check out. Not bad overall though and a welcome change from the typical IPAs. The flatbread came out good, but the plastic container was difficult to lift with the glass. I guess we'll have to wait until after they have a weekend event to see what their line up has in store. Good local food place with something for everyone!

In late October, we walked over to the brewery for lunch and not even knowing it had reopened yet. For my lunch, I received a "thank you" for sharing my story on how I got here. It was a perfect day so I went down there and took the front steps. I was quickly informed that all of the bottles are new and the freshness is better than that of the traditional brew that is used at many places. And I love the bottled selections also. The pilsner was pretty dry and the peach was really tasty. The two sandwiches I ordered were excellent - the tomato soup with the beans and the beef patties. The bread was a nice tan color with a light nutty aroma. With the burger, I had a delicious, moist burger. I added the smokey potato soup which served as an extra bonus (and is a great side dish for mash potatoes). The service was also great, the waiter was friendly and provided interesting suggestions to me. I added that I also ordered the bacon wrapped chicken breast with a side of chicken salad and the sandwich was a delightful start to the meal. Not one of my favorite bars anywhere. There are plenty of places to go to try their food and find some nice new places to sit!

I visited this location a few weeks ago. This is located at the southwest corner of S. St. George Ave and I-85 (off I-585). The interior is a little modern looking for lunch on a day like this. Inside the restaurant, seating ranges from the back seating area with many tables that look out to the side. The service in both places is good and always appears positive with smiles and a friendly staff. My server brought me one of their specialty burgers: the Barbershop Americana burger topped with a smoked paprika  The burger was cooked perfectly, with a nice med. doneness and a well flavored beef. It was full of cheese and was served lightly wrapped. One of my coworkers ordered the "Farmer's Speciality" chicken salad and ordered an Egg nog. The side is available for delivery. At this level, the food service here is very good. Enjoyed the lunch and would definitely go back! I will definitely be coming back soon.

I think my son was a little upset when he saw at all the kids playing in the Big Elm Park since he was standing too close to The park is very busy and there are a number of things to do and see in the park. The lawn has several weeds or trees which make the way to the southeast. There are also trees and grass. There are a few smaller plants on the south but they look cool and are the reason to stop by this park, rather than any other park that has not The seating is small and the stage is probably used primarily for concerts. Near the amphitheater is a small pond and a water feature. There are plenty of picnic tables near the pond for fishing, including a dog park and dog swim area. This is an excellent location for dog exercise or as a good walk-off area from the pond. A short distance away from the dog park is more woodlands. It's a bit of a downhill walk from the dog park. There is a large playground with slides and toys for kids. The Big Elm is a very cute and unique addition to the neighborhood. It is very open and there are a lot of swing areas for children to play on. It's the perfect play place for kids of all ages too. The greens at this park are very inviting as if they are part of the community. There is a new small fence/fireball field nearby that's open. It's a great place to go to hang out for a little while, but would also welcome visitors to use the play area and trails for more It looks cool too!

On the second Tuesday of each month, the winery opens its tasting room in an old house in the northwest corner of the city. It's a quick visit, easy to get to and not expensive. This is a new winery on College Ave. on the corner of Boston/Norwalk, which is just north of St. Joseph. The tasting room has a large, open space, with a few more tables off of the main one. The room is comfortable but it does not include a bar. There are some cool booths in the main space so don't miss this part. The wine selection is limited to the Sonoma Valley California line, but there is a wide variety of California selections. There were a lot of great wines on display from three of the four winemaker's. One of the more exciting wine varietals is "California" that is a blend of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir When I got more and more, I added some other wines and took home the "Red" an "Flight" from Napa Valley, "Gra The winery and tasting room is located on the Lower Level inside of the Hotel Monterey. What's nice about this place is that despite the lack of a cash register, there is a small cash register. It is a fairly small space and is a quick stop if you go downtown. The tasting rooms are open from 10 am to 4pm or 10 am to 8 pm in the mornings. The tastings are incredibly reasonable. One of the Buckets donates a portion to a charity of their choice and I didn't find it particularly helpful. Donations go to a local non-profit and so you can always enjoy a glass of wine or a drink in town without having to do any

I would give this place 4 stars, since it takes a little longer than I would like to dine, but it is really a pleasant and friendly The food here is really good and there are many different options for the menu. I have had my share of problems with the food, but despite it happening a couple times, I always leave pleased and satisfied with my meal. The staff are very friendly and helpful. The menus were fairly basic, but still very nice and tasty for lunch during the week. It seems that they had an open lunch during Tues. Mondays and Sundays (Tuesdays and Thurs.) The salad bar is always clean and there are several good options for salads. The menu has very few options, but it is always nice to be able to change it. One server and I talked a while and I spotted the Vegetarian Special. The food was good, but a little dry. The Brussels Sprouts were very good. On the one hand, they were cooked perfectly, but the texture of the veggies was so soft that it was just like you would put a burger or The sauce was also very good and the savory flavor was more than I had expected. The fried egg was a little dry, but the egg was good. The meatballs were fine, although some of the vegetables were overdone. Their ingredients were the same as what I can taste at home. I tried them both and found they were similar in flavor - the flavor of the bacon was a bit more salty than the chicken because there were more I think we are dealing with a certain amount of fat in this style of cooking. As my review said, I don't remember if the Brussel Sprouts had enough sauce, but the meatballs had enough liquid The menu also includes a cheeseburger and a side sauce to accompany the meal. I can't say something negative about the ambiance, the price of the food, or the overall food quality. I think it's worth a try. Hope to see it in another day or so. There has definitely been a few complaints about the chicken, but I love the meatballs.

As the year wore on, I would add another great feature to the University of I. A couple weeks before my visit, I had seen the museum to the north and the sculpture and art center to my left. It used to be just a parking lot with lawns and fences. It was then that I became aware of their long-term commitment to the arts, beginning in 2007. While I could not resist a stop along the way, I really loved seeing the extensive collection. Many students are admiring the works that were left inside some of the buildings that once stood on campus. The art collection has been enhanced with a variety of forms that range from sculpture to ponds, fountains, lighting, and water features. It is easy to read this review and I highly recommend it. You may even want to check with the director of the university to see what other students have in mind.

There isn't much other bourbon distillery in the northwest Chicago area. It moved to their current location in the formerly occupied former P&G supermarket at 63rd Street and is just down the hall from them. The distillery itself is very nice and there is a nice restaurant in the back, which is what I was looking for. They also are moving into an empty apartment house on the corner, with a nice kitchen, the convenience of a TV at the bar in the middle of There are also some nice restaurants around the area by the name of the place. The cocktails are quite different than many other craft distilleries I have seen in the St Louis area, so it is good to check out one to really give I haven't had the Colonials, All or Nothing, or 3rd Degree, but I was interested to know more of the mix. They all have interesting names, but the names are not the same. My first flight turned out to be 3rd Degree which is corn whiskey distilled in Louisiana from old bourbon barrels in a French oak The 2nd Degree was a single malt bourbon and had a rich malty flavor. The Red Hots is a bourbon. Overall, this was a good whiskey. The other two were all bourbons. I would recommend this whiskey as a great way to try one of their specialty blends, but I really didn't enjoy the wait time to have one The place was busy around 3-5pm on my visit, and I was a little pressed on the hour. There were so many people there that the tables were nearly empty. There were hardly any staff there and it was still quite an undertaking. On a Saturday, the situation was much worse. The main dining area could accommodate up to 150 people. I will be back. I did, however, feel that it was a lot more comfortable to wait there in lieu of the crowded bar area that was much more comfortable. On Sunday, I stayed at West Fork and really enjoyed myself. I would rather stay at my favorite spot in the neighborhood, especially if it is a locals only place.

The Indy winter market is open for breakfast every Thursday in fall and spring. The highlight came from the Fresh Market bakery and bake sale which had baked goods available in their wares. The vendors were a mix of traditional and modern. The market is a pretty small space, but as I was coming in I was ready to walk out. The market was held indoors, and was closed for the winter. Although it did get busy, there were still an abundance of vendors showing their unique products. Be sure to stop in the Indy City Market on your next trip for some fresh and interesting vendors. There are still plenty of good bargains for all to enjoy.

During the Pacific War, the USS Indianapolis sank below the ocean – burying its seamen who survived in an erratic and I had the privilege of serving on the "Indianapolis Waterfront". When the vessel was about to attack the enemy, German submarines, a group of fighter planes were ordered to take possession of the islands. The mission fell apart when one of the ship's crew fell into a rock while waiting for it to break up. The memorial to the Indianapolis was dedicated by the War Department and opened about ten years after the Navy was inactivated. In September 2008, an official memorial was constructed, located at 4050 North Central St. in downtown Indianapolis. My wife Anne's great-great-nephew gave me four of her framed photos of the ship on the west and lower decks If you are interested in seeing the ship as it really was, visit the Memorial's website and click on the link below. The memorial is made of stones, and is open daily to the public.

Gallery 924, located at 2600 East Adams Street (near the corner with Main and Park streets), is open on Saturdays from 10 a. The gallery is located on the 2nd floor of the Art Center and is managed by the Art Center of Illinois (ACI), a non-profit organization The two rooms are linked with a glass wall, so you can walk back and forth between the buildings. As with most artists, the show is featured on a rotating basis, so there is always something new to see. You must take a taxi out to the Gallery to go to the gallery. The gallery is small because all these artists usually assemble for one show once a year. I find that most of the art looks better in person, so some of the works are not what someone expected. Unlike most artists I am aware of, who are not in the business of making money, I do not like the shows at this one. The artists are relatively unknown, so most of the time I find myself getting really excited when I go here to see something new. But if I were to label my reaction to each work, I would just point out that I do like street art. It is not about finding a piece you "lik" but about looking at an artist first hand and just seeing what they do without thinking about how it is I do look at artwork and critique it, but if I don't like it, that doesn't mean I won't still pay attention to I had a hard time getting into the creative side of painting, but now that I am in college, I find it really enjoyable. Art carries you through it. I also appreciate how things are made or finished. It can be a great adventure. It's like an afterthought.

The shop at the corner of Washington and Washington Street was very busy that Saturday night. I've seen this place before on several trips to New York City, and I'd really like to check it out. I enjoyed browsing through the shop and I could easily have found something that I would not have picked up anywhere else. While shopping there I noticed a huge, bright, brightly colored display of Christmas items. A coupon at the front door was available for $2 off all items. I was also treated with genuine care given the location. I didn't buy anything, but did find a great deal to use toward another purchase. I definitely recommend this shop and would definitely visit again!

Great location in an easy walk from the mall. The place is cozy and cute if that isn't your style. I was expecting a lot from this restaurant, but I was surprised at how delicious everything came to be when I ordered! I ordered mine as soon as I discovered it and got there before 10am. My sister really loved this tea so I used half the pot up, but it was still a nice tea taste as I didn't like the color in The spring roll was just how I'd pictured it....a fresh vegetable egg roll filled with chicken, veggies, and other veggies....YUCK! I didn't like the yellow flavor on the outside because it wasn't as crisp as I'd like and the rice was a little dry. There was only enough vegetables to cover the doughy edges and had a nice texture. The egg drop soup was a light brown color with a dark cream sauce. This was a very flavorful soup that actually had a nice flavor to it. Sweet and Sour Pork was one of the best dishes I have had in recent weeks. The pork was really quite tender and the sauce was quite sweet and thick. It turned out to be quite tasty, because it wasn't too salty or sweet. I also liked the meat and vegetables on top of the rice (but also the green onions on top) which I thought wasn't too much of a The spring rolls were thin but very tender and were filled with meat. The noodles were cold, but definitely still kept their texture. The server was a woman who smiled as she made me feel welcome. I feel she was very quick to answer questions about menu items and to get our food out the door. When I came in to check in, she made me feel welcome and really gave me what I asked for. The restaurant was busy so it was a bit unnerving to actually feel the waiting area. Great place to dine in!

I recently had a breakfast in Montreal at Le Papillon and stopped in to satisfy my craving. It was a pleasant surprise to find a smoothie bar on either side of the shopping center. I had a coupon I used and I immediately noticed the smoothie was about the same size as me. It would have been more comfortable to sit at an open restaurant since there was a lack of seating. The store is small, open to the ground and small enough to accommodate only one person. I waited fifteen minutes when I finally realized the smoothie wasn't finished but instead was still in the fridge. The food is a little rushed and seems to be made to order and eat. It is just not my idea that a bakery with so many topping stations is meant to lure people to the place. So, I think that I should not rate this place positive. I really tried to like it a lot during my stay in Las Vegas. I saw the sign for the place.

I discovered this store while driving from downtown, since I was unable to find it. At that time it's almost all Christmas and holiday decorations and products in the store and the mall location is just down the street. My family has always loved Pier 1 - I have been going to their Christmas Market for many years now and never miss an opportunity to go back to their store I love the way the store looks and feels, with all the lights. I am happy to go back every year to see what new items are on sale. I will definitely go in again soon with my dog and grandchild.

The place was very nice. I was looking for a good casual place and my family had to try the food. I had to wait a couple of minutes for my order because the wait was so long, but it was good and the portions were not huge. This was served during a very busy lunch rush. I had it warm, which was great! However, this was very busy. Fortunately, someone brought my food to me just in time. There are chairs on each side for people to sit on. There are tables around the kitchen that are only busy when the waiting is done so it's a bit of a wait to be seated. I ordered at 12:20 and it was waiting before my seat and even after my order arrived. I hope they figure out how to serve the food better. No wonder they are so eager to open their doors. There are definitely plenty of places out there that serve really good food for a little less than $20!

After several reviews of this place, and because it was next to a school I work at, I decided to give it a try when it moved to This was a frozen ice pop place that had surprisingly good customer service, and did a decent job of serving me. The only good thing about nicey treats was that they carry more choices than other restaurants. I went with the dark chocolate and I was pleasantly surprised by the texture and taste. I was not a huge fan of the dark chocolate, which I thought was too much like cherry, since the flavor was not prominent in the cone. I chose to buy a chocolate cone instead of a stick because I wanted to try the coconut flavor and didn't want to waste the chocolate. It was a little hard to taste (I wasn't a huge fan of coconut) and seemed like it wouldn't work with the flavors. There are three different cone sizes to choose from which I felt would be a better ratio to have the Chocolate & Strawberry cone dipped in the dark Unfortunately, I was slightly disappointed that there was no fruit added, although I do want to try more of their fruit selection. The scoop I had was good, but small. A note, you DO need a cone. Despite this, I would say that it is worth the money, not without some criticism. For more information, check out their Yelp page here.

For my first time in Atlanta, I was pleasantly surprised at this new cafe on Ivanhoe Avenue for lunch, after going to the cafe on I was really impressed. There was a very cozy atmosphere at this Tea Village Tea Shop, which opened in 2012. There was a nice spacious, open area with a few tables and a bit of a space to sit and relax. I figured out from reading the menu that I'd be grabbing some good food. The counter took a brief wait time of only a minute or so while they were waiting on their lunch order. They also host specials each day at their Cafe Bar, where you can get a free bagels with a lunch order. The sandwich was excellent! This sandwich is very thick, not tooggy but still has an amazing amount of bacon. I also tried the Turkey Mac and Cheese Sandwich. I thought it really complemented the sandwiches perfectly. You can have that on any bagel without going mad and stuff all the veggies on your bagel. I also ordered the soup, titled "Spicy Soup" (I thought it was a red sauce though!). This was amazing! It was served with delicious cream, veggies, and fresh soup. There was an abundance of vegetables in the soup, which isn't usual for a soup this thick in texture. I then ordered the Hot Chocolate Tea. The chocolate chip was just perfect and topped with perfectly flavored vanilla ice cream. Also got a small whiteberry tart that was very fresh and had the right amount of vanilla flavor. There were lots of options at the counter to choose from, and their menu varies quite a bit. I'm not sure how many servers there are, but the place is very quiet and comfortable. A waiter is available to take your order with a smile and serve you, although the waiter was very busy at the table. The staff took care of me so I didn't feel like I was a "wannabe" as I didn't want one person's The staff was nice, but I had to resign when it didn't take long for my food to come out. All the drinks/food are handcrafted and the staff/service is knowledgeable with the menu and its options. Although I was there for lunch and a few drinks, I got there just before closing. I'd love to have something to try here again, and I look forward to the opportunity to go back! This place must be very busy though.

I went to the Artisans Antiques for a day of shopping on Saturday. However there are several lines in the entrance so I would not recommend getting there early. At first it was a bit dark in the entryway, but the people were friendly and I stopped in to browse. It's a local antique mall, and I have to agree that the layout was nice, and I can't wait to visit it again. No complaints though.. I like the antiques and its an awesome shopping experience. I'd definitely visit again.

On the way home, I stopped in at a local Best Buy, they opened at the corner of 16th Street and South Main St. Most items are really fair, I don't care for the prices, so it was worth the drive to get there. If you sign up for their online club, you get a discount. This doesn't help you if you have bought many items this season. The price for this stuff is a bit higher than most places and you want to know they are "in the business of delivering quality, efficient,  And I was really bummed because I thought I was going to enjoy all the treats I had purchased there and I hate that these stores charge full price, Be prepared to spend a bit on items because of the price difference. Will probably never return here again; that's the only positive I can say. So, this was the best place for me to get my dog food I needed from.

I can't imagine where I would be without Delaware Lake State Park. The park has two trails, the Harrison Trace trail and the Duck Pond Trail. The paved trail is not very challenging, but is not very large. The trail map and a trail map are available at the entrance on Main Street. If you're up for more challenging walking or taking photos, please check out the paved trail on the west side of park by circling around through You get to it by parking in the lot next to the golf course, and securing a free permit to park inside the parking lot is required. It is about a mile and half long. There is a large rock wall at the beginning of the trail and some short steps. I think it is a good idea to take advantage of the steps if you want to see the Fall Creek stream in all its glory. Throughout the walk, the boardwalk has a pond, but I was still able to view the waterfalls. There are four unpaved trails within the park that climb as steep as 2.5 miles. With a full day in the park in hand, it is easy to get lost. Because of the steepness of the trail, I was pretty discouraged by the thick brush and dirt. There is also one of the parking meters and a dirt track that gives you access to the park. The park features some beautiful scenery which will provide good memories as you walk the paved trail or explore the unpaved trail. There was nothing near trees that I liked, but I didn't come across anything that was difficult to identify. It's not as popular as the Fall Creek Trail, but it is worth the extra effort for the views of the surrounding area. The public library is located in the area. There is a visitor center inside the park, but this facility is not open. With a large collection of exhibits and an extensive park listing, this is a great place to take a day trip.

I first got there around 1pm to try their "Buffet Mexican" and after speaking with the server, I knew that I wanted to try it. It's a somewhat intimate/open-air restaurant. The area is a good size for a small table, and it is filled with a variety of booths. We were seated in the bar so we didn't even recognize our server. On a warm day. So, I sat down, ordered a drink, a large salad (not at all large) and a glass of margarita I ordered the Drunken Vodka which looked like some slush drink in there. My drink consisted of 1 lime, a blackberry juice / passionfruit, and 3 ounces of margarita. I liked it and it did its job. The waitress also took good care of me during my meal. I also chose the Mexican tacos which came with a yellow enchilada shell as my starter. I ordered the drink and I was told "the waitress can get you something else for you", which is a nice option. So, the waitress led me through the menu. There was also a full bar menu, a Mexican menu, and a number of food and drink menus. The food menus are printed on a sheet which is pretty standard for a fast-food place. You will then take a form to fill out and write on it how you would like your entire taco to look (in a very clean (but The option also came with the "Suggested Tray" (as opposed to the BYO version of the Tray). The form for me was a little easier to understand. A total of three different options are available, namely peppers, onions, and cheese, which I added. If you have a pre-made shell, you simply put that in the circle next to that line item (in the case that I chose the spicy Mexican A few options came up that I would not pick, but I decided to try them. A side of guacamole was also included with the order so you could chose how to season your taco. I went with guacamole but they charged me a $1 additional for it. You can also add "neither" to help with the filling process. Don't forget the ingredients to complete the BYO. Note that you still have to make your own sauces, salsas, and other accompaniment for a nice presentation. If you aren't yet figuring out your menu, you can take them to the bar. That leaves a side of unopened eatable plates which they put on your table. You can also take out all the toppings from the paper menu. The BYO is really simple! The "Made on Site" option is very optional which will give you a couple choices when it comes to "building your own" tacos This is definitely my favorite "build your own" experience at the bar. It's not very easy to get a seat. And if you want to build the "Savory Tacos" you just need a couple of these. I probably would have chosen to go with the appetizers and the BYO menu. And the price is affordable on a very reasonable basis. They have a special section labeled "Build Your Own" on the online menu. I ended up with one of the "baja chicos" and some hot chips and salsa. Just be aware that if you want to order a taco in multiples of the same toppings that may be a problem. Also, you'll see a small photo of something that makes up your final bowl. They had a small menu of small selections for the BYO. You make your own personal version of it from the pre-made "tastes" to the flavors (and many of the variations among different menus). Don't forget that you need to bring your own plates to the table to use.

We took a very short tour of the Indiana Health and Sciences Center at 221 W. 8th Street to see some of the many buildings that once stood While many students at our college were visiting the IU Medical Centre, I did not get a chance to look at the entire medical history museum. From the basement, to the ice-cold ice room and the autopsy rooms, the museum is truly a fascinating tour-of-a All tours are conducted by volunteer volunteers. All tours arrive at 6:45 in the morning, so the tour is scheduled around that time. Your tour may cost $5 per person. For entry, you'll need to register for the tour (see below as well as the entrance to the first floor entrance). The tours are free, so bring your iPad or smartphone for this experience. As stated above, the museum is very well-organized and the staff is not pushy. Next we visited the Amphitheater. The amphitheater was used for medical lectures and autopsy training. The autopsies and lecture hall were used to teach students for Medical College, and were also used to teach students for the American School of Medical Association as Some of the students were also students from the Indiana Medical College. This was part of the transition from medical school to emo. The lecture floor was in the large hall, the lecture hall was a part of the larger lecture hall, and also the large lecture room at the entrance. A pond and well were located in the space behind the glass window. After the tour, you are allowed to leave the room. At the far end of the lecture hall, two rooms were occupied by patients and doctors. The autopsy room was originally the only place the researchers conducted their autopsies but now, they utilize reams of wood to complete their auto The autopsies were performed in only the coldest temperatures at that time since the body could be frozen for several days. This was our last stop on the tour. There is one other place where students did not pay attention during this tour - on February 15 - the University of Tennessee Medical Center. A big white board with a black screen would be needed, also. All of the rooms included full sized toilets with toilet paper. There was a small table for the autopsy assistant, an open area for posing questions, and some of the patient records. After the autopsy room, there were a few more stops in the museum. Also, be aware that if one of the patients was not in the autopsy room at the time of the autopsy, the autopsy would have to The entire museum was closed as of February 23, 1998. For those interested in the history and psychiatry, the museum also houses a collection of the files of the various patients who came to the  This tour has been canceled regularly since its creation. The autopsy room also held the remains of two of the most famous patients and medical students in the medical history community. At the end of the tour, the students were allowed to enter the autopsy room with the remains of the past patients. The next stop was the Pathology Building. The last entrance to the Amphitheater was the medical building. These were built of the same materials used for autopsy autopsy procedures. The "pathology" room is not one that you see today, but it's something that still lives and that has been preserved. You have to be physically able to stand and walk on these things by yourself. The autopsy room had been used from at least 1892 and was not in use very long. This room was used to hold the forensics of the former patients. We were unable to find any artifacts, so the museum gave us a tour of the autopsy room. All autopsies were performed by the IU Department of Health for the patient's own convenience. By the time the group entered the Parapsychology Building (which is the older one) you could feel the chill of the old room. It is amazing to think how well preserved the autopsy room was. This room also contained an old door with a key. In addition to the autopsy room, the museum had many other interesting exhibits regarding the autopsy of patients and their "family history". The autopsy room and other rooms were part of the Indiana Medical History Museum.

A few weeks ago I was running out of seasonings to buy for my Mediterranean spices. I left about 10 minutes ago and did not actually find it until the parking lot opened at 1230 that afternoon. The store had 4 islands of olive oil from different regions in the US and Europe and all of them were set up so you could actually taste the different flavors. One of the island's workers would guide them through tasting the vinegar. On the second island was an oil aisle with flavored olive oils. A small cup of olive oil was on the left side of the counter, the other was placed in the middle as well. Also, a few were from the Old World locations or even just from Spain and I ended up picking up half a bottle of the Italian one. The third island had an assortment of scented olive oils. It was a great option for a grocery store visit since you can pick one out yourself. The spice selection was awe inspiring and I was glad to meet the manager who took time to educate me on what all of the spices were and even made There were also bottle openers, so you could quickly find a size that you liked as well as one that you didn't like. The man then removed the spigots from the wine and put a small amount of olive oil in a large silver bottle. was very kind and put the oils in plastic jars to keep them nice and hot, and put two of them into a glass jar for me I knew I had a bit of a problem when I left. After I bought the oils and tasted them, I came home to find I saved $$$$ of my purchase because there was a price difference. So, I would say it is worth it if you have the time to sample the selection. The oils are made to order and you have only three days to use the bottles. The quality of the oils is a great way to add a nice healthy dimension to dishes that use the seasonings. Don't be fooled into thinking it's in the dark). I would give the Balsamic Vinegar a try (it's worth the drive from Carmel!). My goodness, they were super-quality items. I think that you could spend hours trying to find these things. I am definitely going to make an appointment to visit in person and try some of these tasty beverages and oils. I am definitely coming back!

You can look at the history behind Hoops, check out the history of tennis with our favorite player, play a quick game of pool, and play around They have interactive displays about what was and wasn't a regular basketball game, the greats from the past, and the players who played in the league There's also a few sports themed areas. Throughout the museum, the museum features a variety of pieces by local art artists, many of which are also connected to the Museum inside. The Gallery is very nice, though you don't really get a chance to see a lot. You also should go inside the exhibits and look at the original exhibits. There's also a tree, as you enter the Park. And I love this part! You are then divided into three levels in the tree, and through each floor there is an activity center and basketball court. (Note: Beware of the steep climb. You are sure to have a great time exploring and playing the slides). The next thing you know, you're standing on the top steps above the water and the water on the bottom is the Lake of Champions below the tree for There is also a large outdoor ice-rink which is open year-round. This park looks much cheaper than other places in the museum or other sports museums. (Note: They do not give admission for kids over 6 years old. The top level is the World of Sport area and it is open to the public. The exhibits are located across two buildings that look like a giant golf course. On the upper level, the paths lead up to a giant hoop with three levels of activity. At the top of the tree, you can look down at the trees that are in the area we were on. You cannot actually go up to the top of the tower unless you look out the window. There are slides, rock climbing walls, climbing ropes, swinging slides, and more. There are even some playground options which children can play on if they want. The "Hoops" theme is a very large and fun display. My kids loved to climb the spires along this section and they were having fun playing all sorts of games with each other. There's a huge "Grand Finals" area which you can enter if you want to be the first to go along the top of the The swings are huge, and the ropes are great for pushing your way and swinging for the kids. You can try a few different types of swings, some rope, and even a ping-pong ball. A water slide is on top of the tree for some dramatic views. They have a small slide for little fingers and a smaller one for big kids. The park and museum are located at the same location for all three tours. All in all, the entire park was a fun place to see the kids too! Chef Tia's, located in the city of St. Louis, is the first restaurant in the town of St. Louis' west side to open. The menu is simple and has plenty of options, but there's certainly a good selection for those who want to order a takeout. I went with the Chicken and Sausage Gumbo and was not disappointed! Chef Tia's is located on the corner of Washington and Auburn Streets. On this street you also see a second building. There is a "service station" in the parking lot at the front of the restaurant. You'll arrive at the restaurant after driving down Auburn Street. If you come in on a Saturday morning, you'll find the inside to be not too crowded. There's also a little stairway up to the front. There is some seating in front of the bar and a kitchen section for hot dishes. I had the chicken and shrimp Alfredo in bowls complete with rice on the side. I ordered the Beef Andouille Soup. I tried this in my lunch-time hour and it was a little salty and a bit hot. It was good with a side of ranch style pulled chicken (a very good combo). Its not the standard "Hot Cajun Gumbo" style that is a commonly used soup in some of my neighborhood, but it was a I then ordered the Chicken and Beef sandwich. With the two extra fries, I can only add a starch to the sandwich. The Chicken wrapped in a thin layer was nice and tender. It was not overly salty or fatty and tasted good and fresh. It was delicious and was so flavorful. However, the sandwich was quite thick, because it was folded and so it must have been too thick. (It's usually easier to get the meat straight out of the bun to avoid that) However, a couple bites could not get everything right I feel like one could get good portions from it. The bun may have been a little too thick, but the sandwich was well-made the whole time. The sandwich was slightly under cooked, it was a touch dry, and I wasn't really happy with it. There is a nice outdoor patio and it's a great place to get some drinks! Ultimately, though, the sandwiches were perfect. I did cut it open on one side, but it was still just as tough to cut through as the other side, as it was just too thick. But overall, it was ok, and I enjoyed it enough to finish it. The sandwich came out to be fine but I definitely would not be ordering from here again. You don't want to see the bottom of your sandwich!

I stopped by the McLaren Museum of Racing about 10-12 months ago to check out the museum’s collection of cars from the 1970s and 1980s It's definitely my favorite museum. I didn't really look inside the museum, but I did try to find a number of the cars featured. There is a museum featuring the history of the Indianapolis 500 and the state of the car industry as well in the west showroom. They have not had any of the cars moved for decades. There are all kinds of exhibits within the museum including a restored train carriage, a vintage bicycle, a vintage truck with a painted sign on On my visit they had lots of cars including the first 500 winners and the champion, a 1950 car driven by Frank Bechtler. All of the cars are located in the front of the museum and in this case, I spent most of my time in the North Showroom looking at troph The majority of the winners were from the 1950s and 1960s, although they were never competitive. Other winners included the Red Dog and the first NHRA Daytona 500 winner the El Chávez. I also saw two historic 1926 and a later 1926 Wabashville Roadrunner. I loved seeing these wonderful classics! It was great watching them drive round and back! The car displays and cars and the history of racing in Indiana are aesthetically pleasing. The history and heritage of Indianapolis is not always well known but if you visit, you can definitely get behind the car.

My wife and I went to Taco bell for our weekly dinner after visiting Austin and found their Yelp reviews and ratings for that reason. Indy has a new canal and I have had the privilege of working along the canal in the past few years. I had been working on the construction of the "Circle of the Town" at the time and I was at the canal during the 1980's As you can see in the photos below, this was no different from other parts of town. The original idea was to give this lane access to the water via bridges and a circular section of trail through this area (as the name suggests Now, however, the renovation that took 9 years has been finished just about in time to become a popular recreational area in IN. People were rallying to clean up the canal, make it look presentable, and keep it clean. The next morning, the canal was officially completed...a jumbo container for water. This area was so long (at least for now) that they put the canal base up. The canal base was dug out and used to support a concrete-topped canal. It took weeks to lay it flat but in 2005 when the canal opened it was nearly 8 feet in diameter and it was the largest freeway in town! There were new paths and a little walkway. They also added a new culvert to connect the canal line to 10th Street. As it progressed, the canal began turning outwards at certain areas as traffic levels werelowered and pedestrians more easily access to the space below. Nearby to the canal were a new boat lift station, the storied "Brother" station and the new "Nationwide Bank". Pedestrian bridges were set between the canal and the new downtown landmarks of The Eiteljorg Museum, Astor Place, and Franklin Avenue They moved remanufactured concrete and replaced it with natural material. It was a great place to walk and the community looked forward to the return of people and tourists back to their homes. After the canal's opening it was determined it needed more than just that alone. Here is where the plan was to turn this area in a vibrant way. It was a big event and a success. and it has a wide variety of houses and condos (we found a great new condo downtown called "The Staircase" in 2012! they opened last year and still don't operate well ). Now, the canal is the perfect place to spend a relaxing morning or an afternoon. Despite a few mishaps, the community seems to be happy with the design and the overall effort. Today, it's still empty and the canal looks fantastic. At the same time, it is getting even busier, especially during the holiday season. We spent a Saturday afternoon out there in August this year. The Canal has not only changed in appearance and its location but it has improved in amenities! That's the beauty and the beauty alone can make a place a great spot to get started. Yes, it still looks dingy and that's ok just not worth it. There have been several people who have purchased this area with their own money, but they were paying $2000 per year.

At least once in my life I've had a great hot dog, so I was just eager to try this one. She said we should try the Wiener Hot Dog with the Italian Beef and ask if you liked it. My wife and I have been visiting Montreal for several years and haven't been to a place other than Anthony's in La Chaux-de This place is really cool and we decided to sit out on the patio. It's definitely worth the visit. I don't want to tell you about it, because no, I wasn't dishing out, but, I couldn't wait to write about My wife loved this too! This was my first visit to 3UP and it will soon be my favorite in Chicago! What we will probably order next is the grilled Salmon, which I'll probably order one more time. Great restaurant! :) You are currently reading "3UP review" at Restaurant Review Center.

If you're looking for something to take home you'll see many vendors offering their food from local farms and other rural areas. There are many wonderful vendors including the Farmer's Market, some of the meat vendors, and some of the breweries. This year the food was good, but I can't remember how much I enjoyed it this year. I think the Fair is great for people of all ages, whether children or adults. There isn't quite as much variety as last year but it was fun to see an event similar to the old day. So, while I've always loved state fairs, this year was even more memorable because of how much time and effort it took me. Yea I know they can do better. But there were a few areas that I'd say would have been appreciated. Probably the best thing that could be added at the fair is asking if your farm is on local television, if there is an exhibit available in  The animals that were located on the grassy areas had names like cow, sheep, goat, pig and horse. And the animals were incredibly slow, which was frustrating for me for it's price. Another thing that I could've done better was with the fish. I didn't notice until after my visit when I was there that it was even worse. When I did visit the animal exhibit, several of them were a little difficult to see. You can still see many of the animals, although the show had stopped for the night. And, of course, the food and entertainment was top notch too! There were many other great things to see, but I would say I would consider making it a go around. And the crowds and smells was so much better. My only complaint was that the food wasn't fresh and delicious. I think it's a minor thing, but I think it would show people how it is done and if it's really needed it is. Even if you are visiting for the first time, it's worth visiting at least once every couple years. There's so much to see and the food is really nice.

There is a firefighter museum in the former firehouse of the Indianapolis Fire Department. Its purpose is to showcase what it takes to be a firefighter; it's not for all ages or interests; it's for The majority of the material is relating to firefighting in the City of Indianapolis. You can also purchase an Indy badge and show it to the exhibits. There are 2 floors to the museum. They are not trained but it is always a fun experience to talk to a local firefighter about all sorts of topics. To get to the museum, take a elevator to the top floor. You enter the museum through a small door leading up to an open brick stairway. There are a couple of bathrooms on the second floor; one with a shower, one with a tub, and the other one with hot water. I feel as if the museum is pretty wellcurated although the second floor is filled with a more rural feel. The displays can be visited by calling 301-258-7299 or visit www.indpls.org.

The Conservatory is not particularly well-known, but if you are looking for a fun way to escape the winter cold, then it makes for  Usually, you can easily overlook a display or have some fun while looking at the plants yourself. By traveling clockwise, you will see a complete photo tour of the Conservatory, complete with additional photos of each plant that is represented within the brochure. As you travel along the pathway, you will see more flowers and other plants. The path also includes two numbered markers, the first at the bottom of the path and the second at the top of the path. You will see that the plants have many names on the labels, but they are mostly the names of one species of plants. For example, the caladium is in a plant that normally isn't on the center island. There is a small waterfall across the path. The flowering grounds are not as extensive as they appear the pictures above. The Conservatory has a little bit of everything. I would recommend taking plenty of photos at home and avoiding any "folk" plants. The Conservatory is located at 110 N. Shelby Street and has an admission charge of $2 per person. If you can't complete the self-guided tour, then the staff can take some pictures and answer any questions. Some items in the Conservatory are only offered to the public. One of the nice things about this Conservatory is that it is not overlycrowded. The Conservatory is one of the few museums that is open to the public, and that is part of why I chose to visit it. At the front of the Conservatory, there is "a secret garden" where plants and herbs can be sold at special price. I was glad that I was able to experience the conservatory. In addition to the Conservatory, Sunken Gardens are well worth a visit as well. There are a few plants that seem to have different names on display and are not clearly indicated on the label markings. The Conservatory is open for all year. Please note that the Conservatory is very popular with local celebrities who also participate in a number of artistic showcases, displays and photo shoots throughout the year If you need a little help you will find staff at the entrance and the main entrance as well. You can access the Conservatory at www.GarfieldPark.org or call 1-855-241-2000 if you would like to see the full exhibit

The Indiana Wildlife preserve is located in downtown Indianapolis near the southeast corner of the downtown block and is open daily from dawn to dusk. The name of this park comes from the fact that many people come and go in this area during that season, which can have a lot of rain s Several trails were created to accommodate the bats. The Park features a large wetlands area that includes a pond that you will find in the middle of the park. Once you enter the preserve, a small brochure will take you to the visitor center. The park is easily accessible through some unpaved roads and from I-55 there is apaved path to the north and south. There is also a snack and beverage stand, snack bar, and a full services park office, where you can find directions to the preserve and other nearby Oak Trace Trail (1.18 miles) is located on the north side of the grounds and follows a circular path. There is a parking lot across Oak Trace and entrance to the main entrance, from which you can enter the preserve on foot or by bike. The Oak Trace trail also has a few benches abutting the trail that offer some shade. The trail is fairly level throughout and when you turn the corner, a few grassy fields are nearby to enjoy the view of the area. Once there, I took the short trail, Bat Haven which leads from the parking lot up to the trailhead. The trail is a very smooth path, although it was a bit muddy at this point. It has a narrow path that makes it easy to follow, but is a little hard to get around with your knees. The trail offers excellent views of the park from the bridge over the pond. Although the entire trail is roughly level, the leaves can be very strong and can cause a lot of water damage. The trail has two small crossings to the north and south of the path. The trail is about 100 feet long and has a lot of shade. In all, there are a total of 6.5 miles of trail to explore within the park. There are some shaded spots along the trail that also have shrubbery nearby (I was not happy with the shade provided). My next stop was Duck Ridge Loop (0.8 miles total) which gives you a view over the valley below. The path does not offer views, but there are some pond and wetland areas to explore. The best part of this 3.5-mile short hike is it is only 3.75 miles round trip into the preserve. This short walk also offers views of the pond where birds are nesting and ducks around. The woods are covered in shaded areas, so you may need a couple sunglasses and warm clothing. The park is open from 6am - 8pm and is open seasonally.

We also visited the Cassadee's Bar on the first level which has a wide range of alcohol, including wine, bour There were mannequins and an indoor Santa from the early 1900s, and the "Holiday Tree Lighting" was held early in the There are a few rooms in which museum guests can view artifacts from the time they were alive. The IHS is located north of downtown Portland and has a storied downtown history that provides much to absorb. A few of these were taken by the IHS at her original presentation at the 86th annual IHS Convention in 1984. The exhibits are fun and the architecture and design are beautiful. There are also some exhibits in the basement. This was a perfect way to end the fall. You can either make out like an uncle, or you can just wander the collection.

The Indianapolis Art Museum has been having a permanent exhibit for the past two years in the form of "Two Sides of the River" (see This was an initiative of a bicentennial committee to select items representing 200 different people living in Indiana and the state of Indiana. If you come within 1 year of the exhibit start closing, you must check in early for updates on your tour. Those are temporary exhibits with some of the pieces remaining until the gallery closes. I usually come early or late depending on what is currently on. The other positives include the new "Experience Area" on the third floor, and the many staff that are excited about what is currently on display. It does have a small gift shop stocked with framed and sometimes non-framed artifacts. The museum itself is located along Main (north) and High (west) Canals on the south side of Indianapolis. The grounds are primarily filled with an old 1812 canal, the canal-like area and the old State House. There is also a boat house, bar, and information center that helps visitors stay informed via a series of events. On a clear day, you can view the canal from both sides. The museum offers its visitors a beautiful grounds to explore and a museum that includes a nice shop for gifting ideas and a gift shop for the The Museum at the State Museum is located at 7337 Washington Street NE, Indianapolis, Indiana 46237. The best time to visit is if you are in the winter when it is warm and the grounds are lush. If you don't think you have seen the museum before, take a time to walk through the grounds on Mill Street. Besides the museum, take a walk and enjoy the sweeping views of the lake, which is beautiful during the summer. The entire museum is about 100+ years old, so, if you have never been in the museum before, it is well worth a visit. For those of you who don't know Indiana, you will have to drive past the State Museum by way of Wabash to get to it. When visiting on the weekend, expect to see an "open" hours on the website. The museum is always changing and one of the features I enjoy the most about being a part of it is that there is always something new to explore.

The Otterness Museum has been in operation since 1983 and has been exhibiting three pieces of public art since 1983. It is a collection of his recent sculptures that were commissioned by Art Strategies. For example, in the photograph, 3 sculptures have been placed on the steps of the Veterans Memorial/Renovation Building at 123 Commercial Street in downtown The large bronze is titled "Free Money". It measures 34 x 20 x 10 inches and is probably one of the most well-known of the three sculptures. This sculpture features a human head which is surrounded by two bags holding bills, which are the same ones used for all the other sculptures. The first piece that was sculpted is titled "Big Big Penny". There is a small figure, also nimble, standing outside the sculpture and carrying two bags of money on his shoulder. The piece is a boy attempting to make a sale on a street corner while taking a picture overlooking the Indianapolis River. The fourth figure is titled "Educating the Rich on Globe" and was sculpted from 1996 to 1998. The dimensions are 23 x 24 x 10 inches. The final piece is titled "Miser" from 2008 and is 3 x 24 x 30 inches. The third figure was in place again on July 17, 2005, and was removed on October 14, 2005. The statues really did not mean much. Many of the three figures, however, had a deep message that could be found in the context of the figures. "Free Money" is a recent example of this. They were actually all on the steps of the City Hall and the Museum of Contemporary Art. I can't think of a better example of public art than the one that I saw on the War Memorial.

The restaurant is quite nice considering the cost of a meal. The kitchen area is pretty small and it is a quick bite to take care of for a quick eat in. The greenest park in the area! It is full of play equipment that has lots of different options of play, as can be seen from the map it gives. It is a great place to spend a day-the playground is full of colorful rocks and bright red bricks and the "splat" area There is a walking/biking path to the water park, which allows you to explore thewetlands and the surrounding trees while enjoying the view of the The amphitheater is very close in size to the play area with a large stage and plenty of chairs on the lawn so little children can have a Near by is a baseball diamond with an extensive variety of volleyball and basketball courts that are very helpful during the long summer months when the weather can change rapidly. I am a big fan of French pastries from across the country. Because of that, I hardly ever stop at breakfast buffet stores. I had a great time when I went to Campbell's Bridge Park, a public park established in 1975 that I had just finished walking to from the It really was a nice location to spend a day. On the south bank of the Greenway, I walked to a little playground called Beulah Cox's Playing Green. There were several pieces of art available for children to play with. There was a sign of where to sit with a description of each space. The kids were playing on the big slide, and there was also a swing set. This particular playground area had a series of "houses" (one for each of the children) depicting their families. Every child loved being there and I think that the parents benefited from being there as well. There were also wooden chess pieces that looked like fun while they were being played on. The decorative bridge was built at the southern end of the park and separated by four girders. It was made of glass, and was decorated with carved figures holding birds, plants, and animals. There were also some sculptures on the side of the bridge commemorating the city's centennial, including the ominous "King' The children's playground, and the decorative bridge were beautifully spoofed by a variety of wildlife and birds. There were a few bench seats to sat on with a few more people at the amphitheater and there were seats in both. The amphitheater seats 120 people and it's a little pricey. There are several benches and a table for children who were waiting for their turn at the play area. I would definitely recommend this park to others in the area.

Situated on the northeast corner of the Mandalay Bay and Seagate Streets, I had the opportunity to enjoy lunch at this location. The outdoor patio is a good place for eat when the weather permits. Service was great, we had the full menu and the waiter came over right away. The table has seating for 4, but there are a few tables behind the counter where you can eat while standing at your table. It was nice to see an older couple bring some drinks to the table, but I think they could have done a much better job letting your partner know The half sandwich was a cold one. This is a great sandwich which you can find at a variety of places around Atlanta but not at any of the top places. However, the bread was soft and my aversion to the fried cheese tasted more like a soft cheese sandwich, the cheese being nice, but Although my sandwich had some good texture and flavor, I think it was tossed in a flavorless dressing or dressing that was sprayed with a If I hadn't been at the restaurant, I may have gotten the greens over dressed to its liking. I ordered a soup with 1 cup of fresh lobster plus a side salad and the soup was good, but I would have been happiest  The cream and sauce were strong but not overwhelming, and they really brought it together. On June 28th, we were driving to the show to enjoy the night out. All we did was wait outside the entrance of the AMP so it took us about 40 minutes for the two of us to get inside. Azucar has taken the AMP by storm. The decor inside the restaurant and the menu is similar to the ones at AMP and has been well laid out. The entire restaurant appears very clean and the employees were very friendly. The biggest arepas are available and they look like fullsized sandwiches. They offer two sauce options from mild to hot. The meat is tossed in a sauce and then topped with the shredded cheese and lettuce. A corn-based dip of some kind with black beans, rice, olive oil and then a guacamole. The patty had a thin slice of chicken and was topped with a tangy cheese sauce. The sandwich comes with two sides and then a side that I later saw being sold out, so I chose the lemon rind dip instead. There is a little room at the bottom of the sandwich for a few veggies so you do not need to worry about taking a big bite. There is a few tables available but the staff does not seem to be swayed by the cold at all so I decided to have something warm The sandwich is served with a simple guacamole bowl so that you can try a guacamole dip (I used You need not be on the menu to find out that they have live blue chips too. There was enough seating to fit 10 people if you want to have lunch on the floor. The wait is really about standing in line at the counter, so you can feel secure and the restaurant is open. I don't consider myself too familiar with Venezuelan food, so I was pretty excited to have this at the AMP and I would recommend it to anyone I thought the arepas were great, but I don't think anyone would expect anything over-the-top from them.

I first went to Poke Guru a month ago, and haven't visited the other restaurants in our area since. Among them is Poke Guru. You start with a southwestern tamarind/lime/green tea/lemon, and then a green radish / cucumber You also pick any vegetables you want ( cucumbers, Korean radish, yellow beans or radish) and pick what you want to top your bowl You then add the sauces or dressing, seasoned with salt, and then you walk away with a bowl to hold as you can't eat Each meal comes with a wooden spork that you can use and a bag of raw ingredients to use as your serving bowl. The bowls range in size between a couple of ounces to a half cup each, so you don't have to pay much. If you haven't tried poke before, their menu features many of the menu items. Although it is good to not eat the whole bowl, the meal I had was delicious. It was very moist and tasty. Overall, it was a very refreshing meal and a good way to start the day. I'd go back for lunch later on in the day. I would definitely recommend Poke Guru to anyone who loves poke.

I was first introduced to Four Seasons by a friend which included a Brunch on the Upper Level at the Wynn's in the Valley We had reservations and they were happy to see us, but the restaurant was packed on that day. However, I was quite surprised that the staff was friendly and it was a relatively inexpensive brunch. We were asked to stand for a few minutes to wait, and then the restaurant quickly opened and had usseated right away. Initially, the restaurant had a lot of people to handle so this would have been a major inconvenience, especially at the front. Their menu at the lobby was extremely comprehensive. The breakfast consisted of various items-- eggs, biscuits, gravy, bacon, cream cheese, toast and coffee. The menu includes some items (like eggs is a great choice) and they also have some other options for those who want to upgrade. That is the most comfortable bacon breakfast I have ever had. The Original Eggs Benedict has just the right amount of biscuit, poach egg, hash browns, and biscuit sauce on the poached eggs. There was hardly any butter or any seasoning there. The hollandaise sauce was rich with flavor and was a delicious addition to the hash browns and their biscuits. Another option, I liked them even better with the biscuit. It definitely comes to an entire table. This makes the eggs Benedict delicious. The coffee served is a good and varied blend. I'm guessing if you'll enjoy being in my seat that is a good reason to have some coffee. I wonder what added flavor they added to the coffee? Maybe not. The food was good and we had alot of fun. We also ordered a couple of other items which were nice enough along with the coffee. The wait staff was friendly and the wait times were reasonable (at least for our event). I'll definitely return for dinner. This is a family establishment and I highly recommend it without reservations. Having found this restaurant, I will definitely make it my top choice for breakfast!

I don't have a fan of chain fast food restaurants because that is just not what I eat so I tend to stick to those. The store was clean and easy to spend time with. I particularly liked the furniture section in the middle of the store which had a wide view of the area. This delicious fudge shop opened on Saturday, September 23rd. Great fudge! The door to this shop is a small shop on the corner of Washington and Main in the heart of St. Louis, MO. The shop is on the second level in the first building off US 36. I saw the shop on opening day this afternoon when I came in. To the left of the stop light is the service counter and a small bar area. At the counter, you can order a variety of fudge. A few hours later the shop changed hands and was still busy. Other candies in their section for sale that are made in house are branded with the original flavors and colors that make these products that much more appealing. Among the assortment is a display of some of their new flavors. The entire shopping experience was a good experience. You can try samples of a few of their other specials too--I bought an entire package of milk chocolate hazelnut, soggy and sweet Another place I would not recommend is the pharmacy/spa. And there is a bar area with some ice cream and beer. I can even picture the boxed toffee w/sea salt in my mind as the ingredients were in the package. We picked up two pound's of fudge and two jars of lollipop. There were very few of the "scratch-test" samples to take to the grocery store. I opted to try their Milk Chocolate and they were wonderful in both taste and texture. The milk, no sugar, fudge is made in the store. There are a few small things that I love not to mention like the peanut butter, a light batter with less flour, and a chocolate coating. That requires you to check that everything is going to be just right! And I know I'll tell my friends about this shop because I can't wait to go back and buy myself some. I will be back at the shop. You can probably put the ingredients together easily but it is still very hard. I am a very discerning and loyal customer (despite the price!) This shop has been on the list of must-visits in Danville for the last three years. So I had a fun experience in one piece. I also appreciate that they have their own chocolate making facility and I would purchase it myself to save money! There are also instructions for cooking the fudge. I have made it every day for 16 years, and for the price it is almost worth it. For the price difference, I expect to be reselling this shop as well. I have never gotten a butter and cream fudge.
