I started my visit to Northridge Reservoir by car. However, there are several reasons this park is on my list for a five star review. There is a nice play trail. The park has plenty of amenities to offer: a covered picnic shelter, two large grassy areas, a paved walking path and apaved vehicle There was some very strong odor at this park but there are few serious concerns due to the nature park being located in a very dangerous location. As I made my way through the forest trail to a bridge crossing over a creek, a few frogs appeared that made me feel slightly The only trouble I had was when I tried to keep up with my route and eventually found my way back to where I began. It was clear and I could barely see the frogs that were in the creek and the small creek with its little branches. The trail itself would have been better when it was clean. Due to the many visitors in search of a new experience, the trails are littered with grass and mud and are hard to navigate without shoes. There were several old signs on some of the trail indicating this was a common problem and the park manager did a great job clearing the mud off There was also a steep dip for trail access as you approach the parking lot. The steps are well marked and are the most stable of the many climbs in the region. There were plenty of places where the steps made a hard but necessary loping down the hills at the end, so be smart and take care of your It appears the steps had been placed in the middle of a forest, so that is why some of the steps were being overturned. It is still in poor shape and not recommended for ages 6 and up. There is plenty to see in and around the park.

What can I say about this restaurant? The food was fantastic and I had a number of dishes to take home. We walked in from the west parking lot, going towards the south entrance. The entrance is fairly narrow compared to the rest of the shop, and the parking lot is actually part of the interior. Note that it is the very last door, and as a person who is getting food to go, it is just a bit difficult to find. The items on the menu are all fairly simple. There are two available options in the catering section of the menu. The Asada and tacos were meaty and had a little rancho style sauce added. They were just plain plain corn with a few small pieces of cheese (pecorino cheese), peppers and tomato. I ordered the Elote. This was definitely on the "you know what diet" level...I think the taste just seemed like a lil bit of ground beef. If you like your tacos with some chile sauce, you can get it online. The food portions were not small either because the items you order are "to-go". I also ordered a burrito with pico de gallo. She mentioned the sauce was better served with ranch from the dispenser bottles and then added a dash of red to the queso and was very satisfied with We shared it between two people and she didn't feel as full as her husband. The restaurant is nicely decorated for casual dining, with a lot of chairs and tables and is open to the outside. There is, however, an on-site bar which is open from 6:00am to 6:00pm. So my wife was happy until the order counter opened and we did not see anyone in the dining room. The staff was friendly, but one of the other tables at this location would have really had an easier time cleaning it. Overall, we would definitely return and make sure we stay at the Wynn. Good service and parking.

On a recent trip to Downtown Detroit, I visited The Bar at 12th and Madison in the basement of a building that was on the receiving end of The location was convenient and warm, and a great venue – particularly because it was only a $10 cover fee. The place was packed the whole time (I was on the last day of business). Ellison Brewing is in the former Town Hall. Because of the new location, parking was extremely difficult. The parking garage is located on the east side of the building. The outdoor bar area is separated from the main facility by a bar with a built-in wood stove to a dining area and kitchen area behind it For the first seat, I plopped down in the bar along the middle of the lobby with a view of the kitchen. Inside the bar, the employees were friendly and helpful. In the back corner, is a small area with a bottle store, but not a dining area. There is a bartender next to the main bar, as well as behind the bar with chairs to the left. The only way that I could have ordered in a flight is by bringing the items in. Normally, I'll be able to drink an 8 ounce. There is a "Shorty" (50 oz.) I ordered a small flight and was able to sample a couple of beers from the menu. I ended up paying $9 for my flight, so it's much more than I've likely ever paid before for drinks. They also do "in house" drafts and a draft selection. I ordered the Imperial Sour Ale. It was a great way to start with an Ale! It had very little hop character and was not overly floral. I ordered second but chose an IPA. A slightly bitter taste that I knew I was chomping down on because of the dark color and full bodied – I was a picky This beer was full bodied with a nice smooth taste and the beer was very strong. This can be a bit dangerous for those of you with more strong IPA preferences, but it's a fresh IPA! The PilgrimsIPA (6%). It only went downhill from there. In all, if they had less staff available, I would have ordered the IPA. The other beers are a bit more traditional pale IPAs. I love that they put all different craft beers on tap, which means that they keep the beer on draft. It was good and was a nice evening as usual. This was a good start to my evening. You should try these beers if you haven't before. It was that well brewed beer with a soft taste. When I think of this beer, the only other brewery I could think of that might be an IPA, but I don't have any of the specific

Just as I was about to give good bye to this great place after almost thirty-six years, Rebellion Doughnuts decided to move their Just to note, in my opinion, Rebellion Doughnuts is a great place to get a donut fix since they serve multiple donut The selection was very good...very much! They were all really good, everything had good flavor and was on offer at reasonable prices. They are pretty much just plain doughnuts, there are many types. I can always be a bit picky about how the center area is filled. The Boston usually has a strange looking cream filling, which isn't very filling since you put it in the center. I prefer the smoothest, lighter cream. The doughnut with chocolate chips is on point. We had the bismarks and the blueberry cream. I did have a question as to why the Bismark didn't have the cream in it. We've only had their glazed ones, but the cinnamon cream is enough to make it worth a visit this time around. They even have cheesecake on the menu if you like it! If you are in the area, stop by.

I recently found The Village in downtown Los Angeles, CA a place to work for the morning. It was a bit crowded because of the large crowd, but if it's crowded and packed, then you'll probably find a Its pretty crowded and there seems to a good amount of regulars. Good atmosphere, but a bit overpriced for what they serve. If you're new to the area you can walk between these two doors to pass under the restaurant, and then order from the menu at the bar. Orders for the fish arrived immediately upon arrival, before any neeps arrived. I ordered a side order of garlic aioli. This seems to be something for a vegan/vegetarian person to order. The fish was very nice and seasoned as needed. These were delicious and I wouldn't order them otherwise. It was cooked perfectly and had a nice flavor. Upon the first bites, they were very tasty with a thick sauce. The neeps were beaten down into a nice smooth consistency. They did not have any other toppings on the plate, and I can't seem to find anything to substitute for the tartar sauce. They were quite soft and had a similar consistency to traditional potato chips. This was not really the flavor I was trying to recreate. I like the flavor. The drinks have a nice refreshing kick, but was fairly pricey. The side orders were served as a group and were very fast, even with two children in them at lunch. The decor is very nice and has a very hip feel to it. There was a staff member at the front door to collect my check, although both are female, so I did ask for a separate check. Go for the fish and chips. I'll definitely be back.

Our first visit to Brick Arch was Tuesday, March 19, 2016. We decided to dine inside the brewpub. They offered a beer, wine, sangria, and a few specials. We decided to try four beers and split them up. The one on the left was the "Blood Orange", which was in a dark gold color. My favorite ale on the chart was the Coffee Blonde. This came in at 4.2% and tasted like a mouthful of blood orange. It also had some notes of dark chocolate. The "BOB" was available with a nice selection of drafts and beers. After trying a couple the next day, my wife decided to try something new. She ordered a combo of two desserts and it was amazing! The texture of the cookie was very chewy and had a nice chewy texture. She decided that the combination of chocolate cheesecake and peanut butter cookies would be a good match. She loved it as much as I did! The patio of Cafe Red isn't long, and although the patio is not completely covered, it was still a comfortable place to sit. During my visit, it was very evident to me how beautifully designed this place is. The sign below the mural says that the brewery is not affiliated with any organization or party and that all food is provided for the patio. Another cool element was that there is a live drummer to keep everyone busy with drinks. I thought the seating arrangement was a little too big, but considering how casually friendly the place was during lunch, we decided to keep our tabs open The patio decor was also very nice. If we aren't able to visit at that time of year, this is a fine place to visit.

The Test Kitchen opened in July 2009. It definitely seems like a pretty good fit for food trucks and restaurants not really interested in trying out the food court business model. Restaurants in town want to open there and in my opinion this is a good place for that to happen; not only do they make quality food, they The concept behind the Test Kitchen is somewhat original since it caters to the whole "food indie movement." I tried one of the new "Lil Dumplings" this past Friday and it was great. It's also available for rent where the restaurants can cook on the tables, as a bar. This has been the most successful testing of some of the food trucks here in the last few months. There aren't a lot of things to consider, like crowd sizes, pricing, parking, or the cost of establishing location. There are 10 stores there but only 4 of them have a location. The place is verycrowded, there is also a lot of foot traffic, especially when you are there on Christmas and when there is a lot of tourists If it works for you, the upper level is nicer and has more space. The parking is easy to find. The restaurant parking will cost $20 for a day and they are charging $21 daily for a week. Somebody on the FoodVoice blog might have already posted their opinion of this place. I would recommend parking there instead of driving around & looking for a place in the parking lot. Looks like a win-win for everyone!

The shop is located at 79 East 5th Street, and is a unique place. The store has a nice selection of artwork to choose from, and it's also very easy to find everything you need. The store offers a variety of goods, including books on art and photography, as well as clothing and furniture. The shop itself is clean, spacious, and organized. The store has a little bit of everything specializing in antiques and collectibles. I really enjoyed looking through the items and shopping in a calm, friendly environment. I would have enjoyed more hours of shopping. The items are wonderful.

The Test Kitchen is an urban restaurant that is located in downtown Mesquite in West Mesquite. The restaurant opens on November 15th and we were seated about 15 minutes into our restaurant visit. We were able to find some really good looking tables, but I guess they are crowded. I stopped here a few weeks back for ice cream, as my husband loves to go out and eat ice cream in the area. The Coffee Shop at 313 North 7th Ave in Indianapolis is a bakery shop, small butcher stand, and coffee shop offering a variety of products After a week of nothing but delicious desserts, I can't say I was too pleased. This is an independent shop with the mission to provide high quality, locally sourced products in a casual, friendly environment. Inside of the shop is an industrial looking storefront that has a very cool feel about it. All the items are made to order and take about 5-10 minutes. There are two nice tasting windows. One is filled with pastries/baked goods. I was trying some coffee and salsa. My best friend brought us some chocolates from the Michigan Chocolate Company. I also picked up a bag of sundaes form Salvation Army and a bag of salsas from La Taina. It's not in a perfect location, but they are in a cute place. Most of the items come from local farmers. Their cakes were nice and well baked. I would have liked to sample the salsas and salsa, especially the green house seasoning. It is not a cheap place to find fresh flowers. This is more about the quality and making of the products and the price is what counts. You will not be disappointed!

This was my first opportunity to try a new restaurant in a new area, and all I can say is that Yolk exceeded my expectations! I was blown away by the large portions of food I ordered and took half a day off! and then found Yolk. Yolk & Cafe is located at 626 North University (on the east side of the North Campus). Yolk is located at 173 South Watkins Avenue in downtown Irving, not far from the airport or the University of Texas Medical Branch. It is small and there is not much space left for table seating. The bar area is very clean, I'd recommend. There are a few tables in the back that can only be taken up by the service staff as it takes up most of the space. We both ordered from the restaurant's "Spicy" menu (all savory if you will). I was impressed by the menu, but my wife, not realizing that it was a Sunday, had to wait for her entree. It looked like there was a lot more than that on the menu, but it consisted almost entirely of fresh corn and the sides were tasty. She really enjoyed the meat and loved the bread. She was also pleased with the variety of dishes on the menu. The hash was delicious and the meat melted in her mouth and my wife asked for more. I ordered the Eggs Benedict from the online menu (which I have never seen before), which came with a variety of sides. This was a delicious breakfast (i.e. a few additional toppings, egg, bacon mix, butter, etc.) and with the addition of fruit to my choice of berries (i chose the apple). The apple blintzes come with all the usual Apple Blintze toppings and are topped with a different fruit each day. The apple slices were perfect with the fruit. The Apple Blintzes were also very filling with a thin layer of fruit and the bacon and potatoes were fantastic as well. At our table, each person had an Apple Blintzes to go, which was nice since I don't eat too much for breakfast The Apple Blintzes were perfect for sipping with a drink on the patio under umbrellas. That included a small cup of coffee, a soda (free), a piece of fruit, and one of the apple blintze You would think that it took a little more patience to get the order taken but the food was definitely worth the wait and it left my belly feeling full. The salad was also good but a bit on edge with the over-fried pistachios - nice touch! This was my third visit here and I was pleased with both meals. They are also very generous with the portion sizes. It is a pretty big space for some brunch, it is a great place to eat and drink on Saturday mornings. Our meal was fairly successful on all accounts. Also, I liked that there were several options for fruit available throughout the menu (apples, blueberries, and kiwi). My daughter ordered the salmon/banana soup. It was delicious. The coffee and dessert menu had a variety of items from the savory side, including sweetened and cured bacon, fruits, and honeydew- I did get to touch the chicken on my plate and it was moist, tender and flavorful. I was looking for the apple butterblintzes in the past day and thought it would never fit on my plate since they aren't that big They also provided an apple cider for my wife for $5.00 after the meal. I added I was expecting more and tried to get the salad to go with our entrees but my wife wasn’t that picky. There are plenty of choices in the drinks and the draught beers are very affordable. I also tried a few others but was not impressed with the selection. To top it off, there were also slices of fruit including blueberries on the side. What a great spot to eat before the work day or Sunday mornings, and a good place to meet friends for good food and drinks! In addition to the egg, there are also apple, blueberry, mango, and orange slices. They were super large by most standards (like the ones that I had bought at Michaels and Sam's for a much cheaper price).

We had lunch for a group of 16 at a great place called "Galantisco's". We parked (it had been an hour since I had arrived and it was a surprisingly packed house) and ventured in to see what all the We went inside and was greeted by two female workers and greeted by three others who were all standing by the counter. In terms of salads, the ingredients are a bit more limited than those listed on the menus. The menu offered various options (it's not as if there were only 2 different choices). Most people order the chicken salad at this location, and I ordered the chicken salad and added bell pepper, apricot preserve, and honeycomb. When you place your order, you can choose from four selections: red, green, green, and yellow. Her salad was very satisfying. We ordered the "Fuji Onion Roll" which was a very simple, but tasty order with chicken, black olives, tomatoes, The wait times are about 45 minutes for two salads and 45 minutes in an order for more or less. To take an order, you need to go to the counter. The freshness and crispness did not detract from the flavor of the salad, so not too bad. I tried to ask the cashier for directions to get to the inside but didn't have any luck.) Just a touch more tart.) I expected there to be a bit of more dressing on my salad. I decided to add the chicken (the one from "The Forbidden Fruit") instead of an extra chunk of chicken. This was not the case, it was just a smaller piece (see photo). My wife didn't even see them because they weren't even half baked. My wife ordered a large green salad and while I was very happy with his portion (including the bacon pieces), he actually preferred the chicken. In my opinion, the whole environment in this restaurant is a good mixture of food and service and in my opinion the overall experience would have been fantastic had we Of course, it was more expensive if you ordered a burrito as a side dish as well as a regular salad. Just did not like the texture of the dressing. My husband had the pizza and salad that he made from scratch. We both ordered the same side of my salad. I should have given the chicken a higher rating, but the chicken was flavorful, my wife wanted some dressing added, and it was nice to break away While most of what I ate in Montreal was good, I got really disappointed with the portions that we ordered because we just didn't have space for leftover They were definitely an option because it's free to place an order in. I also enjoyed the atmosphere of the restaurant but was not particularly impressed with the food - nothing to say I would come back. There was more room for choice and variety by the way. We aren't usually the "high food" folks, and I guess this was a good thing for us.

I have done many trips to the outlet mall in Seattle and this shop is definitely on my short list for another visit. Today was my last visit to BurgerFuel in Oak Park. I thought about this place because of their name... it seemed very interesting and would be really close to the house I was staying at when I was there. I always enjoy going to BBQ places when I'm with my wife. If you like BBQ and have a southwestern theme, then you might like this place. I was incredibly surprised to find this place was still open. I called ahead to make sure there was a server and to make sure the menu appeared on offer. The menu is extensive with a lot of options. I ordered a margarita, but the sauce was quite salty so my wife ordered this spicy dish. It was hot, fresh, and very tasty. It also includes peppers, beans, squash, red onion, black beans, and chicken. Her husband ordered the pulled pork ribs with a side of corn on the side and he said it was fantastic. They do have vegan burgers and their sandwichs at this location are so-so. The meat was delicious, the buns were fresh, and the sides all were well seasoned, (to my knowledge only). I also had a sampler plate with what the kitchen described as a "banana shaped bun". We really enjoyed the combination of meat and sauces - I'm not really much of a BBQ snob so I would probably have The stale barbecue sauce on my sandwich was not at all spicy, but not really strong. I'll be back soon! There is also a large selection of sides and sides, so you can even try those for the first time. There is also a drive thru or a carryout window next to the outdoor patio. The menu is pretty standard which means they have plenty of sides and you can get just about anything you would want. I haven't been to a place more convenient to park than this one and I would definitely recommend dining here. I had a big party of 6 people and it was packed because they don't offer specials! My bill was $19. We did see some of the staff and the restaurant was busy so I don't think that it was much better than they'll have because of the small After all, even though I have lived in Broad Ripple for a pretty long time, I had no interest or desire to go anywhere else if I'm looking forward to going back soon! The sauces are not very authentic like the more expensive restaurant chains that have gone back to being fully smoked. The location is close to downtown, but we took the walk into the business first and if you want some fresh air then look down on the street to the Not as expensive as you might expect, but you will be sweating. There is a good amount of parking around the restaurant as well, so I feel you get the best of both worlds. It is good if you like spicy food. If you are looking for a nice place to find a good meal, look no further.

Several years ago, I checked Lava Express on my route to work every weekend. Have you ever wanted a quick lunch and wanted to try something new? Fortunately for me, Mediterranean Gyros & Smoothies is just such a restaurant! I was originally scheduled to make for a lunch in a cafeteria, but discovered Lava Express while I was in the area. The food comes out with a bit of a "busy" look to it and a big display of plates of Mediterranean food to pick up ( The food isn't in the open air kitchen, but they do have a small refrigerator which serves all of their food. I pulled up to a counter where they had a small menu with about half of their food. I waited until the door opened and then I went in to get my drink and browsed the menu inside to see what they were offering. The drinks were a large cup of giardiniera and a small bottle of fruit juice. I wasn't busy on the first day, so they were fast at busting down to the seating area. The employees were very friendly and the shop is really quiet and private - don't feel bad about not being able to speak in public due to not It looks like a small restaurant, but when it comes to their service, they are quick, friendly and efficient. The food came out within a few minutes. I ordered the potato and beef gyro combo which comes with a delicious filling of roasted Jerusalem artichoke hearts, olives It was well seasoned and consisted of several different types of meats, cheeses, and vegetables. It is served on a bun with a patty on each side. After eating, I quickly exited the restaurant and left. Lava offers a range of refreshing beverage, sweet tea, cold or hot coffee, and also a very fresh green smoothie. I ordered the mango and papaya smoothie and said it was one of the best I've had in a while before. You can also enjoy the refreshing drinks in a shaker as well. So, here's a quick round-up of the menu. Not much on the menu on a Monday, but there are some creative creative ideas on a Tuesday or Thursday. After a great meal, I will be back!

This was a very fun and very pleasant lunch lunch at the Northampton, New Hampshire sports stadium called the "Grand Army Inn/Jun This was my first trip to the restaurant and I was very excited to see it! I went to Harold's Steer-In one day after visiting a friend after shopping at the Smith Building. A sign appeared stating the restaurant was open all day (not just for lunch or dinner). In the dining room the TV was hung on one corner whereas the bar was standing to the right. It's close enough to my apartment to get easy access to the highway for getting to work, but far enough to get the rest of the menu. I selected the lunch specials. The menu came with a tenderloin which is made from 4 ounces of tenderloin and a side salad. When I got the sandwich, I was able to see that the cheese was actually really good. It seems the sauce on both were really finely sliced and the meat was quite moist. I could have finished it off in a little more than a minute. The meat was well browned and not too rare.
