The server wasn't there right away, but when we arrived, the table outside was filled and our table was just a few feet from the sidewalk. Although it seems like there is no limit when it comes to what people can eat, we still just didn't order anything. The scones at Rolling in the Dough were nice and flavorful; the whole table eats two or three every time they visit. So I decided to sample the cheesecake of my choice. While most of the menu choices on the list, with exception of the chocolate covered strawberry sandwich, don't have many items in the dessert area. A little taste of the Italian food will always be a plus. There is also a small food court (regardless of the menu). Despite the fact that I can't try their chocolate covered strawberries, the food at Rolling in the Dough was very good.

I'll admit that the bar is small, but there's a decent variety of beers on tap. There doesn't seem to be much of a reason to go to this place. The decor was plain, with just a few tables scattered throughout. There wasn't really much else to do inside, and there was no music on. I really didn't feel the vibe. The walls didn't even have a bar stools on top... only a bar stool. There was a bit of a wait as I was just about halfway through my beer, although I could see how it may have been because I found it The restaurant had some cool art on the fridges, but it didn't have any real charm. The beer selection is what it is and the service is fine even if it is a bit dated. I'd consider this a good place to sit. The food was decent, so I'll come back to that for more in a few months.

Review #14663. Although the store is open Mon-Fri 9-5 for flower delivery, which usually only comes in the evening. The store is an absolute treasure. I have lived in the South Side for quite a while, and can say that this place is one of the greatest shopping experiences ever. And not just flowers. They carry some truly exceptional decorative pieces. You rarely find something the size of a full size window a week. They have a beautiful Christmas display and live decorating, and during the show their Christmas Tree is made, and the display in the store is put on display along You never know just what you'll find, even if it is a store like this. It's a really good store. Have a look around the store. What a great place to stop! Love how great the decorations here are.

I received a great review from an awesome new neighbor of mine. My friend Wanda was the only person in my group to check out the restaurant, so I called her in to say I was coming. If you've never tasted Cajun, I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone that is looking for a new experience. I had to add something positive for my own safety without overtly introducing myself to someone. I had heard from my good friend that they provided several different meats and crawfish plates that were all delicious. I ordered: Jambalaya for my 1st meal on my 3rd visit. The Jambalaya is certainly thicker than you would expect. I noticed a huge difference in the texture of the Jambalaya. This creates a thin plate with a bit of a crust on the bottom, but it is still relatively light and flavorful. It had a distinct mellow taste, which I appreciated with the  smokey flavor. The crawfish included were large enough that any fish could easily be removed without having to cook in the rice. Crawfish is marinated in garlic, olive oil, and Worcestershire sauce until the shrimp are squished together. I added some shrimp to the dishes (I always am). On a side note, you can order the Steak, Clams, and Mushrooms & Grits on the sandwich menu. The food was clean and tasted great. The crab tasted even better, and since the crab was not really cooked, the texture was just a bit easier to swallow. The atmosphere was relaxed, yet cool enough that any food would be a pleasure. The decor was casual, but yet sophisticated. The vibe in the building is inviting. I would definitely be back! You will be happy! This restaurant just doesn't have the intensity or spice to make one too afraid to try Cajun dishes.

For my first visit to this new Hard Cidery I visited in the early morning. At the new location, Ash & Elm Cider, on Washington Street a couple of blocks away from the downtown area, I couldn't resist The store is very spacious and invigorating and I walked in on the very hot, sunny Saturday. This is a small space that looks mostly like a wine bar. The Ciderry is located on the left side of the corner with the coffee store. It reminds me of a country market. Aaron and his wife had been at the cider for two years and I chatted with them for a while as well. Andrea shared the story of the beginning of the establishment, having started a fruit ciderery in the mid 60s and selling hard cider in 2005. Initially, I really didn't feel formally welcome but that changed about a half hour later when I joined an employee discussion at the bar. The ciders were all excellent and the ciders were slightly more fruity-ish than regular apple cider, but with that being said, I was impressed by The first was a slightly sweeter cider Idle Summer. I thought it was a great balance of soft cidery to warm brittle characteristics. It had a few flavors that were similar/contrasting, but were all still interesting. The Half Summer Cider was just as sweet. I was pleasantly surprised by the added fruitier flavours too. I also ordered a Semi-Sweet. The cluster was a great way to finish. I have to say that I will not be dining there again, but, on my last visit, I found that it's well-attended and full This is another highly recommended ciderry, as well as the best one I've been to in East Lansing to be honest. Not a bad calorie punch!

I noticed that Three Carrot was on my short list. I came to this place a few weeks ago when I was driving on our way through the Golden Gate Parkway. Unfortunately, I couldn't find it. I didn't find the sign, but since I was at the corner of T Street and First Avenue, I figured I might try it since I did Luckily, I could find the sign from another location. I walked up to the door and waited for the staff. There is a line to place an order but it is quick. Despite the food being so simple, I still got a really good food experience. My only concern was that there was not enough protein in the sandwich. The sandwich was served on a vegan tortilla with a  Grilled Cheese and Veggie Platter. The main dish comes topped with Seitan Shredz, a little spicy, and a few vegetables. There are three sizes available and I got 3 or 5 gyros. (I had already been in line to buy some of the Shredz because this was the first time I had eaten them.) The sandwich was very flavorful and complemented one another. (Maybe they think we've hit the heat limit.) The wrap isn't a definite vegetarian dish since the only meat substitute on the menu is the seitan shredz. The Banh Mi costs about $15, but it definitely looks good for a good value. The dish came along with chips and salsa. This is a small joint and also pretty large so it wasn't great for me to share the other side because of the large size of my order. The sandwiches looked pretty reasonable on the outside and tasted a little rushed. I recommend Three Carrots to anyone looking for fresh, flavorful, and filling Vegetarian food at a low price. I'm happy I found it!

A wonderful place to get a nice little treat on a Saturday morning. I stopped in on a Saturday evening, and as a person who normally enjoys sweets, I was drawn to some of the pastries. The menu seems simple, but that's exactly what I'm looking for. There is a nice variety of cake flavors, not too many "silver" ones (a lot of the flavors were pretty standard or even really expensive It was my favorite! The pies were all good sized. Their prices are fair enough to justify an additional $19 per cupcake (I have found that they are almost as good as or cheaper than the typical grocery store cupcake The cupcakes were very moist and the cheesecake was very moist, but didn't dry out my mouth. They have a good selection of pastries and cupcakes, but the cupcakes are the more exciting options for the price. I would definately stop back here!

We stopped by and had dinner at the restaurant that is on the first floor of the Northside Mall. We called early and were able to snag a table because it was late on a Wednesday. We were seated at 7:30AM and it took us about 15 minutes to receive any of our food from the restaurant. There were no others in the restaurant, so our service was extremely slow and, inconvenient. We heard there was a sign outside for "dry heat" and found ourselves at a very poor place. Our server was nice enough that she kept us warm. The food was good. The fish was mostly white fish that had been rubbed in garlic with salt and pepper. Also, when we asked for a manager, he was absent. After the meal, the food was a little disappointing. Although the place was empty, we found that they were still busy on the restaurant floor. Even when the waitress got up and began to take orders the server seemed to let them down and there was only one person in the entire restaurant. They will not be using this restaurant with the new location that has opened. We may still check them out next time.

I recently visited Grindhouse Cafe for lunch about a week ago and it was excellent! Very good chicken burrito on top of a salad is on the menu. They were perfect, crisp, and flavorful. Oh and kuddos for the hot sauce. The bacon-choice was cooked to perfection using not one slice of bacon but two thinlysliced bacon pieces added to flavor the sandwich. My sister got the same sandwich since she loves BBQ; that was so much better than other places we went to. The sandwiches are served on a plate with a bowl of cold water and a piece of ice that helps to keep it together. But the sandwich was still super flavorful and I loved the way the sandwich was served. It was a bit dry, but it was really really good! I also had a great experience in the store! What I liked most about the restaurant is that they didn't need the menu to be repeated and reordered every time I came in. I didn't have any wait, the food was just right and the place was busy so it wasn't a large group dining area, but I as I had some left over hot dogs for lunch! I also appreciated that everything was served fast! Overall, great food, great service, great people! This place has a quaint feel to it. The interior isn't perfect yet, but it is a solid place to eat for lunch or dinner. Even though it was just a weekend, it's still a welcoming place and the food was good. The chairs look more like tables or stools for a less stodgy place. I think it could be better decorated to be more socially appropriate for the younger crowd. I will be back again soon! If you want more information on the place, check it out in a 'near you' video!

I grew up with a local Best Buy. They have an excellent selection of boxes to pack and label. There is plenty of space inside for you to package your box, as well as stapling of the box. They don't pressure you to buy anything until you have asked for it, but have great recommendations on things to get that done, whether it be on location At my home town an hour and a half drive, I would say that I have found a faster, less disorganized shipping place. Also, when I am at this location it is very noisy. They have a big pull in behind the back door, just before you get to the front door. There is some hood vents, but not much else. I would get the parking lot entrance closer to the entrance if you are using a credit card. A little pricey if you order more than one box but the selection and service is worth it.

On a recent visit to my brother inlaw's in Chicago, I wanted to check out a Chinese-based ice cream shop in the city At first I didn't take it seriously, since it seems very strange and even unusual to me. The ice cream shop was a suprise. It was hot outside, so many different options on the menu. There is an ice cream stand that you can purchase multiple flavors (both the sweet and sour version) and you can go up to a window There was a table and chairs open and I felt quite welcome because it was a small place. A lot of the products look or smell similar to what we have at California's own Costco. The only thing that stood out was the mango drink. The dessert features mango ice cream along with a shot of chili powder and a squirt of chamoy sauce! The jar of the drink had a glass of water placed in the top and I sampled it. There are many taste differences with this drink, but the combination did not really appeal to me. There are parts of it that dragged me out of bed. The main attraction was the sweet, but then some taste was lost. I was unable to sit still long enough to properly eat, and I felt the taste overpowering. There were bites where it was more of a flavorful mango but the heat from the sauce seemed to burn into the drink and make it too salty One of the things that stands out is the large amount of tamarind! This straw is basically made out of ripe mango with some added salt and sugar. We tried a few bites of the tamarind on the first try and it was very similar to mango, but the tamarind became a It's a difficult job to get the liquid out of the straw. The best strategy though is to drink on a clean day to avoid any bruising on the straw. I think it's possible to taste the water in the drink, but it's a bit too strong for my taste buds. The drinks are $4.75 plus tax. The mango was still good when dipped in lime juice. I got a small piece out of my tamarind without any problems but I would not go back and try something different. It's really not that bad. The flavor of the drink was quite unique from what you would usually find in a normal frozen dessert. The next time I go to this city/country, I will be going for a more adventurous ice cream, but I hope this post helps you out I also don't think this would be a good choice.

In San Francisco, NY, "Let's Do The Grocery" is a chain that has a large selection of pizzas,  There's an Enoteca, a Bakery, and a Deli. We were given the opportunity to tour the wine cellar and explore the menu. We bought both types of lunch items and they were great; both soups and sandwiches were surprisingly good, most of the time. The deli has lots of fresh ingredients and it made things exciting as we walked by. Even our table-mates enjoyed their lunches! We took a tour and saw that there were many different types of sandwiches on the menu. The sandwiches we got were the deli Batali and the goose (named after one of the owners, the Goose). The first was the Batali, which was a simple bread romaine wrap with fresh tomato topped with prosciutto, fresh mozzarella,  It was quite good, but this was the next highest price item we paid (it was $12.99). Both sandwiches were very flavorful and very good value! We decided to try two soups. The Chicken Broccoli Soup was served medium to thick, mainly cheese and chicken broth. The Chicken has a nice moist chicken flavor. We ordered it with a dollop of cheese. It was also nice to try the nuts and olives. I tried: the Chicken Platter, salad with the chicken, and the Sicilian Bruschetta Panzanella. These are also the place you find the frozen bananas and pecans. Definitely want to get the "Little Oysters". Our dinner was the last thing to make our day, but before our water came, we decided to try their Raspberry Float. I ordered it in a shot glass with a glass of their beer, and a glass of raspberry gelato. There is a dark taste of the ale incorporated into the float that makes things unique. A few bites and you will be satisfied! After a little trial, I would probably pick a whole load of the raspberry beer again. We were all very happy with this restaurant and we hope to go back again soon! Now that it's been poured, I really really liked it. We had a great time! If you are a fan of raspberry, definitely make this one. My friend liked it better. Everything they serve is made in-house, but they do get orders from local restaurants (I have a taste, but didn't stop there). A delicious float, which we shared with a friend with a half of a bowl of the new juice.

At approximately 200 acres you would expect this park to be a great place for children to play. It is a little more than a large area of park- mostly woods and a pond. Some of the features are large: a rock wall, small slides, a rock swam through the grass, and a broom The pavilion overlooks a pond for more peaceful pond swimming. The playground isn't in the middle of the park, so if you plan on walking between the park and the pavilion, be prepared to get out A small park, but perfect for children and the environment. There is something for everyone here, from young to old, ages 4-10 years old.

At lunchtime, this is my favored place to eat in New York City. I decided to order. They had a small menu with an Italian sausage (Italian Sausage). I saw what the menu was, but it appeared to be only the peppers and onions. But when called back, one of the employees informed me that they had run out of peppers and onions, so I decided on a chili sauce instead. Once I got there, I realize I would be ordering the combo and ordering one of the specialty items of Italian Spaghetti. The food truck was standing around the corner, so I waited for the order and then took my meal out and walked to the truck and waited  I just can't believe it. In other words, they didn't have peppers and onions. I also felt a bit screwed that they didn't get a refund. So that left me with the Italian Sausage combo and the chicken calzone. When I gave up and got home, the sausage I ordered tasted like a chicken kielbasa or hot dog. The outside was a bit brown, with a bit of seasoning there. It had some ground pork (not the classic Italian sausage). In truth, it tasted that way. This should not be considered a good meal. The sauce did take the edge off the meat while being a little thicker than I expected. Just not a good combo. At another local pizza joint, New York Side, a bit more salt may have been an improvement, but it was definitely not worth the price.

I got a review for The Phoenix Journal yesterday for 1205, the new Virginia Avenue wine bar in downtown Phoenix. I was in Charlotte for a wine tasting event and was a bit excited about 1205 tasting. The crowd was very friendly and the tour was pretty quick. :) It got us to spend an additional hour just to take a tour and get a sample of some great spirits. Parking meters close in the evening, so you can park close if you aren't in a hurry. I then went to 12.05 (who also sells some of the delicious house spirits). In any event, we came back from lunch to find that the tour was a bit short. I used the code YF for our scheduled tour. (I highly recommend their gin yuppie and rum diggers to add a shot of gin to their gin To avoid a wait time of about 45 minutes, we gave around 20 minutes to make our appointment.) Our hostess and tour guide were very knowledgeable about all the spirits and cocktails on its menu, and they gave us helpful advice on how to mix, I asked if I could sat in any seats at the bar, and they were very helpful in explaining the history, history of the restaurant, and what are your favourite cocktails and why? I liked the Orange Blooper brandies which are more complex, and the Grand Old rum (a 2% ABV) which was a bit I also really liked the gin (29 proof) which has a great balance between the alcohol and the fruitiness. At the end of our tour, I had the following cocktails: a Bloody Mary, Bloody Mary, a Pineapple Julep Martin While I was tasting the spirits, I found two glasses of bourbon, one of which was quite sweet and delicious. These establishments are some of the best I've ever seen in the West Coast. :) The tour/tasting portion of the visit was very nice, although I would have liked to have been able to see the bar outside Take a look. See their website for hours.

I can understand why Tahini is considered the city's finest take on Mediterranean food. The decor looks like a tea set was thrown into a desert garden filled with roses, like the one pictured in Aladdin. The staff is very friendly and always there helping out in other ways. It's probably a small business that was first opened because of the location, but it was still a great service and quick food. I ordered the Sahara Salad. All the vegetables were fresh and there was a bit of a flavor, but the dressing was very heavy handed and I found that the falafel was Probably a common thing in restaurants in Pittsburgh. I then ordered the Flatbread Sandwiches with sliced falafel and veggies on each side of it. When I opened the sandwich, I still felt like I was with a salad. Great sandwiches with a great portion and with great presentation. I left Sahara with only 4 bites of food and it was $17, but I was seated right away. It was an odd thing, and when I asked for one, the server directed me to go back to the counter on the side of the building. If I wasn't paying, he asked me to walk and wait. I ended up leaving, which seems like a pity, because there were so many other people on the counter who were waiting for me on the counter I just thought that I had left a trail of food, so I should have made it there first. You really enjoy the decor and food at Sahara, and it's an awesome place to watch the games, but if you would prefer to walk in I'll definitely be going back. I probably would not have gone out of my way to come back here today... maybe next time, but if you are in the area, I would definitely

Love the gyros at Greek Gyros, one of my favorite places to eat in Indianapolis, and as is usually the case here, I am I saw Mr Gyros on a Saturday night and was interested in seeing what it had to offer. At this location they are always open for the day and even have a drink special and a snack bar. It feels more upscale than other Greek restaurants, but doesn't feel as too crowded, which is a plus. Aside from the food, I think this will be a nice place to visit. They have a few options on the menus, but generally not that great. The best is the Greek Gyro. I was a little iffy about the burger but the meat itself was pretty good. It was nice to eat that way and had enough heat for me. I found that the Greek dressing made the gyro a little rubbery. They are quite generous and offer a lot of options such as pita bread sticks, pickled onions, and a few kinds of chicken. This is a meaty, cheesey and spicy topping. The sausage was a bit salty in texture. It comes with some meat, a slice of cheese, onion, and a bit of sauce. This was the first thing I noticed about the sausage. Had it in the refrigerator for a few minutes, and the taste was pretty pleasant, but I ain't seeing anything special about it. So I think I would pass on this one. As far as I'm concerned, the chicken wings and chicken shawarma are probably the best part. These are not included in the price. Nope, go to 'Mr. Gyros' in downtown. If you are looking for an authentic Greek dining experience that offers some variety, this location would be a great choice and I would definitely go back to order

My wife of 6 years and I came to Texaco at the beginning of September for an event showcasing restaurants right here in the downtown area of It was our last day in a Hilton and our friend was looking to eat at a restaurant but she had a big dinner planned and could have The first course came with a trio of cookies (which was the perfect compliment since they were so rich). I also had a side of chicken salad with an apple cider dressing and a generous dash of ricotta. The main course was the filet mignon. It was tender.. and was super moist as well! I ordered it mediumrare-rich. The sides were a selection of potatoes, a side of asparagus, and two sides of meat (prawn and shrimp). The shrimp was a little on the tough side, but still came with a nice side of flavor. They were tender but had a bit of a garlic smell. The asparagus was just soft and firm. The beef was tender and very well done. The filet was flavorful and the sides were very enough to keep it down too much for me. The side items included an enormous chocolate cake with buttercream, topped with cinnamon, red, dark and blueberries and a touch of chocolate syrup (which I would never have attempted to eat dessert without the whipped cream, as it was quite decadent. The restaurant itself was a little smaller than I think it would like to be, but I thought it was a nice enough addition. Prime 47 is located on the middle level of the Stacey Street Mall on U Street and was open. Food is good and excellent and the service is excellent, the environment is clean and comfortable. It gets busy during the evening hours and is only for a small group of people. The salad and desserts were also very flavorful and their menu was very extensive. The service at Prime 47 is top notch, as their staff are friendly and easy to talk to. Hopefully this restaurant will improve the quality of their food.

I was pleasantly surprised by the reviews about Little John pizza. I had been asked, why aren't they offering breakfast or dinner lunch specials any time of day? I thought that the sandwiches were a great option since I live less than five miles away. The sandwich wasn't that great, but it was still pretty good. It also comes with a bowl of ranch on it. At the cashier's, I paid for my soda and I got there within a few minutes to the restaurant. Several of their subs had the sauce mixed in with ranch or ranchero when they were made, which I felt was a great idea. I could tell the waitress was good, but just wasn't feeling it right. When the sandwich arrived, it was fresh, but that was actually the best part. The Chicken Bacon Ranch sandwich came very quickly and wasn't as bad as I hoped. I'm a big fan of the Buffalo Chicken Ranch style and this was very good to me (and I drank it a few hours later I would have preferred the chicken to be a bit tastier, but it was still good. The sandwich fell apart easily and I didn't find the hot bread to be tooggy (which is a positive for me). The sandwich was very good and I liked the addition of the BBQ sauce. It was just a bit too salty. It wasn't too bad, just a little not quite my favorite sauce. The pizzas were a bit too sweet and tasted like a microwave pizza. When they'd finished cooking them, they handed them out with a fresh breaded bun and a good helping of sauce. I am hoping the prices here will decrease and their food quality will improve. A great lunch special and a great place to go with great food.

A new place located on the corner of Pebble Beach Ave in the Old Town of Pebble Beach is Spring Gardens. The shop has a wide selection of flowers, candles, unique gifts, and more. I was super impressed with the shop and really enjoyed the selections in the store when I left. I particularly enjoyed the bouquets that include white roses and purple roses that are arranged on each shelf, all beautiful. The shop is open from 10 am to 3 pm, 7 days a week (except on weekends). If you're in the area at the next farmers' market of the week and looking to pick up a nice vase to fill with flowers for your home

I've seen the place a ton of times since moving to the area a few years ago. Although the menu is pretty extensive, it was too pricey for what I found. While I was at Bynum's, my son got very excited to see a new sign behind a booth in the back door before our meal. So, I called it a quits and returned. A good reason for the change of atmosphere was that it was their lunch special. A while back, I took a walk through the restaurant to see if it was as busy as it was. There was a nice, warm, modern interior. It's a comfortable place to dine. If not for the fact that the restaurant is small and has lots of little booths, then would be a pretty awkward place to dine, especially at I was greeted and seated in an booth, which was bright. At the table above me, the staff read the menu and the items before me. A person came and asked me to sit, I asked if I ordered anything, he was friendly, and the booth was empty-seated. This was actually very good! I finished with a large piece of fries. I was impressed by this particular burger and how it actually tasted. It's a great burger with a good balance of meat and cheese, just enough to keep it tender. The menu looks somewhat tired, but if you've been to Bynum's, the waiters are usually very friendly and the menu is always very It's possible that a lot of newbies are not paying attention, since they are quite educated about the menu and are also quick to judge We were hungry for a while at the time of our visit, so we ordered a couple of more beers, but he left us a This is a good place to take people to for lunch.

On Friday afternoon, we stopped in during their hours of 10-2, and enjoyed the variety of items they had for sale. The shop is very old in style with very large windows. They are located on the front porch of the Harrison location in Bel Air. They have a little gift shop inside the store which I highly recommend. All of the items here are unique and fun, and I really like that they have a wide variety of different kinds of items. I was happy to find several items that they didn't have in the market, and there were some wonderful pieces offered to us by local businesses that I can I was very pleased with our purchase, we'll have it at home for the evening, and it will be a great addition to our decor. You can order online through the store, and I did. Not too expensive at all; we thought it was pretty good value. So if you're in the area, do check this place out!

This was my first visit to this place. I have to say that the Chocolate Bakery is definitely worth a stop on your next breakfast visit here in Charlotte. Foods were diverse and the staff was very friendly and helpful. and were filled with fresh vanilla ice cream topped with chopped nuts and chocolate curls. The cookie was really hard and sweet with just the right texture to get you into the middle of the dessert. My friend had the Ice Cream Benedict, and hers had chocolate chunks! They were delicious!. I was ready for a glass of my favourite coffee, but had to wait for it to be ready, but the chocolate was great and my cup of coffee The only knock I would make is that the coffee (even though it was "hot") is made entirely from Arabica coffee, which has an overall bitter They also offer cold beverage options, which are really great for sipping hot coffee or sweet tea--one of my favorites when doing a quick quick visit (I've been a huge fan of the coffee in South Carolina) and, while I've sampled many other varieties, I usually stick to It was good!. I also liked their "Pets and Nuts" items that I am always ordering (coffee, cookies, ice cream). But let me just tell you that they have a variety of non-coffee items. I've been to Starbucks a handful of times, and this was the best experience yet. I am also glad they gave their hot coffee some room to cool before serving it on the table. by Sarah E. - Jun 22, 2014.

The staff was helpful and the restaurant was very clean. The restaurant was really a confusing experience for the two of us having only been there once to try out the food. We were glad we drove and made their acquaintance. The atmosphere was relaxed and not overly formal. They have large menus for an open bar and a good selection of dishes and drink/menu items. We went with a couple different dishes each of which I opted to eat in a separate box from my wife. My wife ordered a sourdough pizza and some beans and sour cream. A typical pizza is a half a plate and usually comes with a bowl of sauce and a serving of a small side of rice. I got one with chicken and rice, topped with guacamole, tortillas, and pickled vegetables. She asked if they would let her order the burrito or taco with chicken breasts plus rice, beans, beans, and cheese. So we went for it (it was in her to go box, but we shared and it was quite tasty.) She looked at the menu to decide what to get. I was not too fond of Mexican food, but it just wasn't my favorite in the bunch. This was a very simple, Mexican, but very tasty lunch. As I can see, they offered a large selection of vegetarian options, which was nice. I wasn't familiar with the sauce, but I don't usually like it when something smells garlic, and I was looking for an easier way to I also got an order of rice that had been made with black beans. My wife was happy to get a salad with chicken, rice and tomatoes, which she added to the plate. There was a little line to get in and it was a nice lunch, but not so much for sitting in acrowded restaurant. They are near Ditch and I would definitely say give them a try. The food was good, which is where we stayed last night, but I expect they will be making more and more food like this (with a little

Thai House is a foodie spot located in Sarasota, Florida. They provide a variety of cuisine that is cooked to order and has a nice selection of dishes to choose from. The restaurant has a cute little indoor-outdoor patio and we made our way in. My friend was taking a sip and noticed that the store was stocked with one of the best pilsner beers in the area. The beer had a clear color with dark reddish (ish) color. I also ordered the special, my first ever Thai dish from Thai Recipes. I was excited to have a refreshing drink without the burnt stomach that people receive when drinking pilsners. I ordered the burger with shrimp as well, but the waitress brought me some of the food right away. Some specials are offered, but I had to settle on the Lunch Specials with my lunch. Once you open the menu, you can find a table of 14 dishes, each topped with soup, salads, and desserts. Vegetarians can choose from the usual chicken entree, chicken pad see ew or veg pad see pad ew. For an extra fee, you also get a selection of fried Thai chicken and a selection of fried Thai rice and chicken Fried Rice with a The entrees come with an additional choice of Rice (no rice, but it can be made with noodles). There are also special plate of steamed rice and bowl of Jasmine rice included with each special. The selections are pretty good and the chef is very friendly. My friend ordered the #23 Black and Tan curry with Beef (medium heat). The Padd See Ew dish was served in a bowl of coconut milk, paddsee noodles (thick and tender), and beef (meat The egg added a great crunch too. The Padd See Ew came covered with a thick marinade of coconut milk, chicken stock, chicken stock reduction, sweet and sour sauce, The sauce was mild, but the flavor was tasty. I wish that the soup had added a little more "depth" to it, but that would be difficult to do for me. Having had a few Thai Diner specials this month in Indiana/Alabama, I decided to try a Thai cuisine special. For my second lunch special, my friend ordered the #3 Chicken Fried Rice from the menu and it came with coconut milk, Thai hot (mild), and It comes with a huge sauce that had a heavy spice feel to it with lots of basil. They tasted delicious with a hint of a coconut flavor. The chicken was in a bowl with shaved carrots and yellow onions. I really thought that the Chicken wasn't as moist as I thought it would be, and it took a long time. The soup came with large chunks of potatoes, a bit of egg, cashews thrown in, black pepper, carrots, peppers While ordering my lunch, we drank Thai tea and then chatted for a bit about the food in Thailand. This is a very flavorful, thick chicken soup and is served with rice or an addition to the order. As you can see, we were given a lot of rice, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. My friend ordered the pork egg roll (dried beef).

Authentic Burger Bar is an awesome location to stop in and check out, they are open Mon-Thurs, 9:30AM-5:00PM and Fri- The menu is a mixture of ethnic meats and an extensive dessert menu. The food is amazing and the food preparation has been noted by food critics online. I did two things a couple days ago - one was an item offered in store, and one was the house burger called the "Belmont The sprouts are dipped in a rich sauce of olive oil, garlic and a small amount of ranch. The ingredients were well-matched to one another. I finished with a delicious slice of sweet potato frittata with a side of hot sauce. The mustard sauce had no taste at all, which allowed for the dipping process. This is my third time that I have been there. The sandwich was ordered as an order of two, one to go, one for takeout. I chose the grilled option, which was good for a simple and fast lunch. I used the pepper jack and onion combo. The meat was seasoned well with salt and pepper, but had a thin layer of a somewhat salty batter that did not give a real season I could not taste any seasoning, so I gave it three stars out of five. So, after about 30 minutes, I asked for a more even bite and found the breading well done and flavorful. I would definitely recommend this place. I am going to have to try their kale and chicken salad for the chicken, as I still find some of the ingredients too salty. A good spot in Greenwood to find some good authentic American fare. The decor is modern looking, but the menu wasn't as much of a "modern place" as I remembered.

On my way to eat, I was so happy that I came across Jerk Poke in the center of downtown St. Claire! They offer 3 menus with a variety of options for each one. You simply sit and wait to choose your ingredients. Next, choose a filling (chop steak, shrimp, or fish.) It was very easy to pick up your ingredients and add them. You then choose an egg (or two) and choose two toppings. then the portion size. There are other options that you can ask, but not a mandatory order here. Then you can choose your drink or juice, and finally you can get on their WiFi network and order from the touchscreen on the left. As we were waiting for our order to be ready, it felt nice to notice the place was full of locals and family who were already eating. You can also pick it up for them to deliver right to your door. In the back there is a TV in the area that I found interesting and the staff were helpful enough to help me order my lunch. I was quite impressed with the variety and taste of the menu, which includes many different poke options. The wait time was good, the staff seemed super friendly, and it was good to have a restaurant that allows for two in one. The waitress was very helpful and provided me with a taste test to gauge the quality of the food. The menu options that were available (we had a few variations on the menu) were very well organized. The bowl came with an open end and was sliced in half. My wife got her bowl with meat and vegetable and was happy with that, but she thought that it would be easy to get if they sliced it along I ordered the bowl style, and I found that it was a good size and well placed. Food tasted great, my wife and I felt comfortable, the staff was friendly, and the pricing was very reasonable. I have yet to try anything quite as tasty as here (unless I am living in a similar neighborhood to myself, which would be a huge bonus).

The last time I went to a mushroom place was in 2007. I had heard that the food is really good and I had heard good things about the menu options. It is also a brand of the chain Avalon. It took me a bit of walking around to find the kitchen. My order arrived at about 8am on Monday, June 22, 2018. My party and I were seated right away, so they were all pretty close by in the kitchen. The menu consisted of a variety of wraps, which I thought was good. I settled on a salad with meat, salad, and some garden in a whole wheat bun. My salad arrived quick and I was rather impressed. The dressing was an herb vinaigrette with some organic vegetables. The Italian Hoagie was just as fast to arrive on the counter. There was a little bit of sauce or dressing on it but there wasn't a great taste at all. Both sides came with an assortment of sauces. The first bite of my sandwich tasted just fine. The lettuce was fresh and my second bite of meat was soggy. The meats were tender and the cheese was melted just right that I liked. Aside from their cuisine and atmosphere, The Chicken Salad was actually quite good, I would not come back. There is also a water fountain located nearby which is nice but not my first choice. I felt that there wasn't a long wait for any of our orders. It was a great experience and I look forward to going back. There is no way on the menu that you can order a salad from that plate; or ask for a bowl or two of salad instead. You can also purchase your own brews with their beer machine and wait time would be a bit longer in the future.

For the record, we may not have reviewed the full sycophants. I could say that the price was reasonable and there were lots of toppings offered. I need the time to do both so that's why I didn't feel like blogging at all. That is all I wanted to say about their food and what a great place to go. We're in a bit of a pickle over what I've tried at other restaurants and I'd like to think I came here because Thank you!.!. I hope I get to visit their location next year...I'll have to come visit it!

The City Market has been here in Charlotte for a long time. It is located in an historic building at 40 Market, part of the Mile Square Historic District in downtown Pittsburgh. I haven't seen much of this change after the recent collapse that had destroyed so many of the historic buildings erected in the area. Now, the City Market has evolved into a beautiful restaurant, bar, and food hall. The most popular, of course, is the old Food Hall which is packed to the brim with an array of eats (including ice cream Most of the businesses have very good food, and a huge variety, from deli to coffee shop--or coffee, and snacks--to fresh The downtown market is home to many popular restaurants and is an ideal place to meet people going downtown, as well as those looking for a quick meal that is The food hall is huge and there's a lot of seating. It is a beautiful building, one of the many buildings in the area that are used as a local landmark. Afterward, visit the redevelopment on the west corner that's going on right now, The City Farm, where there are several farmers shops and  I love it here. That alone could make the City Market a pretty popular place to hang out in downtown Indianapolis for a while! On an average, I never go to the market at night until the city does a little bit of planning for it to do that.

Review #1393 (It looks like it's still open though) I had an early reservation last night for 7:30pm and was seated right The place is very modern. I wasn't expecting Japanese food at the time, but the decor was a very neat mix of Asian and French. They also had some really nice rolls to choose from. At first I thought I decided on a Dragon roll, but was pleased that the fish and rice wasn't cold or overcooked. It came with 3 slices of sushi-paesu style, a bowl of egg-drop soup, and a thin slice of Spicy The egg drop soup came with 4 bowls. Very thick with no clumps at all. The chicken bit that was in the chicken was still a little spicy, but still wasn't too salty. I ordered the Salmon and it was a big meal for the size of the bowl! The salmon was slightly over cooked on the outside and was quite fresh. The tuna was cooked just right, the white meat was a bit dry, but still fresh. I also wanted to try their seaweed roll. If you are coming with a large group, the plate doesn't really look so attractive. The eel was a bit chewy, but was still very good. A nice variety of rolls. The fish seemed fresh enough, not over cooked or too spicy. The wait was very quick and they received my order without any problems. There was also a nice selection of tea, and I definitely could use a break from coffee after dinner. Nice overall experience with a great variety of options offered. I will definitely be back, I just wish there was more diversity in the menu. Happy New Year to everyone!

My first meal at Rize was very pleasant and enjoyable. I have no idea how many times I have gone to the same restaurant and it always becomes the same story, with the same staff and lack of quality food  However, today, I was not. I was there from 2:00p to1:00p. By the door, it was very busy, but the kitchen had a large space and we could not wait to order! I was very impressed with just how good the food was that I didn't even realize I was enjoying! After waiting for the "to go" menu, we ordered "Potato Chicken" and I have to tell you, it was absolutely delicious. The Roasted Chicken Salad was delicious and the texture was outstanding! I could totally eat this from scratch because it is delicious! The rice was cooked perfectly and it was perfectly seasoned with a nice salty flavor added to it. I also enjoyed the side item of the choice - the fresh fruit. I felt like I had been rewarded with a delicious lunch. Looks forward to a return as I am looking forward to the variety of menu options as well as our next visit!

My husband and I drove to Michigan Garden Center to pick out plants for the house and to get a better look at gardening supplies. It was a very pleasant experience, I highly recommend putting this Garden Center near me on your "must do" list!! They're located on a small campus next to the river. It has a clean, parking lot adjacent to the store. The entrance is open, and there are a couple nice booths in front as well. The center was clean. Unlike most other gardening stores, everything for customers is sorted in the greenhouse and then in the small shop. The staff was very helpful to me, especially from their knowledge of growing herbs. I'm on my way to my front yard! The staff gave me some great ideas and provided help with everything; I even got this super helpful green house to help water. :; I highly recommend this garden center to everyone! We'll be back for more!

One of my favorites in the Valley is Nobu. Service was great and the wait was short. Basically, you can have any of any one of these dishes to eat (as long as it's spicy). I made a reservation for 2 people. Because we had to get home after our lunch we were looking for a quick bite before going out for dinner. While our orders were being taken, I mentioned to our waiter that this time of year they might do lunch specials (I'm interested in trying other We ordered the egg drop soup and the eel roll. Had they added the egg drop to the lunch menu? Sadly, they could only give me Miso, but they could have offered the egg drop for an additional $9.95! The egg drop soup they had were not only good tasting but the server was nice too. The Miso soup was better overall but definitely not bad enough to make up for the egg dropped. The roll and wonton were just ok. Both of their wraps were large and had a nice wrap. It didn't get soggy as I anticipated in the morning after ordering, but the taste was fine overall. The cooked sashimi had an excellent flavor, the sashimi was not stuffed with any fish (I think I've tried the fish and was covered in the sauce. I would not go back. The chicken was cooked to temperature, but not very tender. The soup was actually pretty good, with plenty of flavor. My yaki was fine as well. I'm just not entirely satisfied with my meal. When we went to dine in, we were prettyseated at the dinner window which wasn't a particularly friendly place. The service at Tian Fu was excellent, and the food made it very memorable. We'll still order from their menu, but I think the pricing and food quality are better than other restaurants. My wife really liked the dish she ordered, but I think it isn't "very good yet" as I expected from a Chinese restaurant.

My coworkers and I were passing this place and I couldn't help but go there. It was easy to sit back and enjoy. We ordered a whole plate of stromboli and a side order. It's not very busy. I was disappointed to find out that their menu is mostly in English. The menu is limited that's why it took me almost an hour and half to place my order. I thought their strombolis were good, but not as good as most. There were 2 different size stromboli, one with ham and pepperoni, one small with pepperoni, and one large with pepperon A little bit more vegetables than meat, not too much either. The meat on one side had some vegetables on the other side. The ingredients were mixed well and the sauce was pretty standard, not too much sauce on the meat. I thought it was a bit dry, but despite the mildness, it was plenty dry. I liked the cheese. I would go back to this location any day for a quick meal and to try a new thing. I would love to visit for a lunch or dinner.

Plants at the Garden Center are one of the most inviting locations to visit in the mid-term. It is a small three-story building with a single parking lot (the others are separated by several large side alleys that can also be  The greenhouses are located near the south end of the campus in a large building near the front. Depending on how many times you have been, it is better to park at the south end of the front greenhouse and then go through the greenhouse doors. The greenhouses are set up with six of the same sized sheds to maximize the amount of room to pick up any type of plant you want. The checkout is located just outside of the greenhouse. There are ten sheds which are arranged one-by-one, with the first with veggies, the second with perennials, the third with pe The green house employees are always friendly and helpful. There is a large potted plant section just off of the front, and there are several other greenhouses nearby including the second greenhouse, the greenhouses and Still, there are two workers that usually will be working. The selection is really good and the plant prices are reasonable with the fact that it is a small business which means a lot of people will be purchasing from The plants are generally fairly priced at $2.50 per plant or less. I like the plant nurseries on this campus of UNC. So far so good. Thank you C&G Nursery!

We were in town for a friend's wedding party and decided to go visit the place on our last night in town. It was a great night. A couple of us had to wait a minute for our food to arrive. The first was the lack of staff. When we entered, we noticed that there was no staffed seating area. On the front of the restaurant, a host was standing at a counter to ask you if you wanted to seat yourself. Then there was an unstaffed service counter and we saw a woman and a man sitting opposite of us who sat themselves at the bar. From the outside, the food was excellent, and the service was pleasant. It took a couple minutes to get our drinks, but after a couple of minutes, we were seated in a nook next to the bar This was the first time I had a problem with a bartender getting a drink on me since the place was busy. When the waitress arrived, the same couple was seated opposite us and the waitress was just waiting. We have a table in one of the nooks across from the bar and the waitress never even appeared to welcome us. So it seemed like a lose- revenue opportunity for this restaurant. We were waiting as the waitress began bringing out the food. We were seated first, then one of the waitress, then our waitress, then the waitress and finally a male server. The restaurant does have a couple of tables that do not have waitresses, which felt pretty awkward to have. Why would just anyone at this point have to sit at the bar? By the time the waitress arrived, the bar at the back of the restaurant was empty. I feel like the host had lost his identity and was not paying attention to the others. After we had our drinks, there was a problem with the order that we didn't received, but the server figured out that it was something minor I got chicken soup and it was good. The soup was perfectly salted and the sauce complemented the soup. This wasn't a problem though, because I had a can of clam flavoring. Overall, we all thought the soup was very good, and not very pricey. We also had two sides: chicken Caesar salad and an omelet. The dinner entree was chicken fingers and veggies. I can't think of a better value and better customer experience in a lot of my trips to places because of all the negatives. It was a nice evening and a quick visit could be worth the drive. The sauce was great as well, but overall, the food was nothing compared to what would come out later. If you are looking for a good downtown restaurant that seems pretty empty and lacks the friendly server that you are used to, check this place out. All in all, a good meal and great value. So, overall, the food was delicious and a great place to visit if you're looking for a great place in downtown. I expected a softer bread and a more salty, flavorful soup. There is a really good line of food but there's nothing that would be bad here. I would give it a 7. Although it was dry at the time, it is not as dry in the morning after breakfast.

I have to admit my first time going to Kazuo Sushi was about 10 years ago. It was very nice, cosy, and comfortable. However, there are a variety of parking options available in the restaurant. A big crowd gets to the restaurant, especially during the weekends. I decided to have a full table for two, because the restaurant itself is fairly small (at least in the dining room). My meal began promptly with three of my favorite items. At my table, I ordered my "Lengthy Salad" which was a "Sesame Dressing with Spinach, Sea The recipe calls for soft-shell crab, whitefish, and seaweed. The green rice with marinated lemon jello was flavorful but not offensive. The fish had a nice balance between it and the vegetables. One of my favorite salads right there right here. The tuna has a slightly burnt flavor in the middle (always good when seasoned well), but is still quite flavorful. The sauce was hot and spicy with a distinct aroma. The tuna has an excellent meaty flavor. Now I had the eel roll. So I didn't expect the sushi to be very strong on flavor but it really delivered. It was well-seasoned, moist, and flavorful - the texture was just to die for. We shared this together for the whole meal and it was delicious. I also found the fish and roll to be fresh, but the spicy asian sauce would have made the sushi taste sweeter. Eel) I would also recommend the Tuna Sanrio, which was served with green goddess with a nice blend of garlic, salt, It was also somewhat expensive, which was actually very reasonable since you have only 30 minutes to get your sushi and the other items had been prepared ahead of time. Be careful going to this restaurant though. I would definitely recommend this place, if you are looking for a unique restaurant to dining out with friends or family to watch a movie.

My FAVORITE ice cream in all the shops! I did a taste test and the chocolate was good. Hence, the reason to give it five stars. I am so proud of it. I love the variety and the variety of flavors is always different.

This is an old school favorite in my neighborhood. One of the great restaurants in the area! I can't believe I was in my mid-20's when I stopped by. The waitress greeted me very warmly and took care of me quickly as she went around with her table and then continued her work. So, her greeting was warm and welcoming. Her supervisor was really quick to get my sub and I enjoyed it very much. The cheese is light on the hand and not as sweet as the others in the restaurant, but it was good. The sandwich tended to be a little thick and had a pretty much whole loaf of bread. The meats were very good, very tender. It was really tender without being too chewy. I don't have a lot of food experience but I would say it's ok. (We got both). So I just kept it simple after eating! In this section (and also in all other spaces located around the house) the cash register is the only point of contact for check out. However, on the way out of the restaurant, the waitress was on her way to the counter and was ready to take your check. When the food is brought out, they pull a few cards from the bar and then hand them to the staff. Then, the register lady gave me my check and I came back to the front dining room. I definitely recommend them to anyone! I don't have much to say about the prices (the restaurant is a little bit overpriced), not much else to say, and it

There were the usual items for sale at this store, but it had a very busy feel about it. Basically, this is an antique mall, and it contains a wide variety of objects. It took me about 10 minutes to find all the items I was looking for. The space was very clean with very good lighting though you would never know it from the outside. We ended up spending time at the top of the shop before leaving (the store's owner allowed one of us to leave early), and looking around on the This mall is more of a walk away from the antique shops. The interior is comfortable, though the doors do seem a bit sturdier at times. The store is open everyday.

After visiting a friend's restaurant several times, I finally went to Cafe Chimichanga. It was my second visit to Tacos 'n' Beer and I love their food. There were no signs out front. Across the entrance is a large bar area with two small booths, but it is not that big compared to other Mexican restaurant. I was initially told about the chimichanga and the lunch specials going with it, so I decided to eat there as a late lunch I walked in towards the entrance surrounded by booths. Waitress said I would see her there then sat with me in the booth for a few minutes. I then found the restaurant without menus (though they do have a little map of the restaurant with the menus) but I did see their coffee machine They didn't even mention the menu, so it was quite disorganized. The menu was pretty basic and easy to read. The waitress appeared to be a little overwhelmed, but she took care of me quickly. My chips arrived right away and were fresh-squeezed hot. (I am not sure what is called chip batter, but it is not hard to figure out it is actually ground flour in the oven, but I don' The salsa was excellent. I would not say that even the chips are bad, but the salsa was good. The chips were dry and had a nice crisp crispiness. I'm not really bothered by how soft they were as I find them a little chewy by comparison to other chips, but I also appreciate the Then the server brought a bowl of steak and a chimi on a plate. This makes for a large lunch plate. The Chimichanga was sized just enough to seat me. Next came the meatballs. The white sauce added a nice salty crunch to the chichimi. I was a bit iffy with the sauce, the whole order of chips being a little hard. The other items were really good. The chips and salsa are smothered with a light-cheese sauce and it was nice and easy to eat. They did have a good-sized lunch menu and had a full lunch, so the waitress was around pretty quickly. As I was leaving, I saw that they had a large amount of chips on the table but I didn’t see the waitress sitting there. Had a great lunch! I had the salsa bowl out on my way, so it worked out ok. Don't let the location fool you. The parking lot was not good to walk to even while they were running.

A week ago, I stopped by the Lal Kush restaurant on a Saturday morning and had lunch. The restaurant is extremely spacious with a nice open concept. The restaurant is located on a small corner lot opposite a gas station, so I walked in quickly. There are a number of menus, including chikong, cha pao, and naan (thin bread). This will help the restaurant staff to show you selections, so that you aren't having to ask for a drink! I ordered the two chapati (soup, rice, and flatbread) with garlic chutney and a cup of makh I received a medium hot filet mignon (one of two options made from beef) filled with a marinated and grilled beef sauce. The Beef Bahari is served with basmati rice. Most of the dishes offered in the menu are spicy/medium. We were told that they had a number of different cuts of beef and to get the best flavor selection, one would have to order the beef medium. I went for the mild and loved the taste. I received an 8 inch serving plate with the beef bahari and vegetables over rice. The beef was medium spicy, but still a tender but soft piece of meat. The wrap was served with the chutney on the side. They were piping hot and topped with lots of fresh fruit, some veggies, and a couple of Indian spices. It was a total of four pieces! The chutney was deliciously warm and the sauce tasted delicious. On the side were two pieces of rice. It was arranged in a large bowl and topped with the beef. The rice was coated with a sauce as well and I was pleased with its taste. I think the restaurant has a fun, fun feel to the place, which helped with the mood and feeling of being there. You can also order a meal to share to take home. A few days later, I had been out of town and had to make stops in Louisville for lunch, so I went back and ate at Chapati again While I don't see yourself eating at Chapati again, I can definitely recommend for some good BBQ! The spicy meat was perfect with the flavor and the basmati rice was moist to the touch. I think the food is delicious though, so I definitely plan to return. The rice and chapati was warm and filled with tender, vibrant flavor and just the right amount of heat to be perfect for me.

Zionsville Cafe takes you inside of a cool neighborhood coffee shop in Zionsville's Central Library District next to the Zionsville Art Museum. They are located on the lefthand side of the shopping center. A few employees are sitting around the counter and chatting while they make their beverages. There are some interesting displays with beautiful artwork. The drink selection was very appealing and the store was very clean. It's a bit of a dive at the entrance, but it was convenient. They also had a variety of fresh and hot coffees available. The coffees they have for sale are delicious! There is a "Seasonal" and a "Chocolate" specialty coffees available. The chocolate was a bit mushy and somewhat bitter, though didn't taste like chocolate at all. The coffee was delicious and full of flavor. It definitely tasted fresher than I expected (for the first time ever), and the hints of chocolate really added the perfect hint of fall flavor. I found my cup to be just brew worthy, but a little sweeter than I was expecting. There were about twenty other folks in the wait area. I was impressed with the coffee shop, but I didn't really notice the crowds. I'll be back. If I can't make it to a regular date time, I will certainly be coming back soon.

This was one of the earliest beer venues I explored - this place was really good. I went with my husband to Fork + Ale after seeing it as part of a craft beer artisanal food truck stop near the Grand Valley Market. Fork + Ale opened in late September, and I can tell from the exterior signage that it's on Washington Street. Unlike most other Breweries, there is a parking lot, but it looks like they are doing a little work to the parking structure. To find it, head out of the main gate on Veteran's Drive (It's about a walk along Veterans Drive). The plaza is under construction and is set to be completed very soon. Most of the building is lined with a large glass wall that provides excellent lighting. I walked by Fork + Ale for a second time on Sunday and was pleasantly surprised by their selection of beers and food. In the past, every time I did this, I'd run into the patio. The bar/diner was not so busy as I'd assumed. It's the bar side and there is a large bar area with a very large large TV. The bar also is equipped with an indoor/outdoor space. The kitchen area is full of booths with booth seats on the patio that is adjacent to the restaurant. The coffee is excellent and fresh served. The waiters are very professional and service was good! They are a bit expensive per beer too for a 4 oz flight. I was a bit dissapointed that you can only try their house beers as there are only three beers on the draft menu. Fortunately, most places will open to drink them and I'm pretty excited about sharing a beer with my friends and family when they open up. Of course, I decided to purchase their house brews and go from there. The first beer I ordered was a IPA from Miller Lite with a high alcohol content. The first one was the Imperial Stout (6.2% 77) which had a nice and warm finish. This would've been my second choice since I enjoyed the taste. Next was the I've Been There Red Ale (5.9%, 25 IBU) which was a little refreshing and had a nice tang All of these draft beers are made from beers which were brought in to be brewd by the new F+A Brewery which opened One of my first beers at Fork + Ale is the Hopped Beer with Cinnamon Jam. Fork + Ale was a great new addition to the midtown area! My flight of beers was a great lunch/dinner experience! I actually ordered one more glass of beer, but that's just for testing purposes. The restaurant and brewery are located next to Sun King Spirits and the plaza. I would recommend this place for any one looking for a beer/restaraunt in Carmel, Carmel-by-the-Sea This new location is located at 1002 Veteran's Drive in Carmel and it seems to be really quickly growing and moving rapidly. And the menu at Fork + Ale is very interesting and you can't help but be intracted to both the menu and the beer selections at the The food was excellent. Although the food did not have a lot of flavor, I would definitely return! I'm not going to lie, even though the wait was slightly longer than it was the first time I've ate there, it was worth it Overall, I really enjoyed my stay at F+A! I recommend giving them a try! I had to finish off my meal. The final drink was the Brut Ale (5% 28) which had a nice fruity/dry hopy profile, with some hints of alcohol I think I got more of a taste of the Hopping Around IPA than the Winking Cedar Brown Ale! The pizza was sooo good, I didn't even know it was made by Pizza Hut! The beer was served with a small side salad and was a good size for a quick snack! This is the last taproom of the day and they were running slow (stuck at about 12 on the hour)!! I was really happy with their selection of beers. Now, for the "food" item: sundried tomatoes and green beans, served with our selection of two sauces: cream & butter. I really enjoyed my visit. We finished up with a simple bowl of burgers and fries at a price of $11. They told me that the beers are named after the local restaurants.

I took a nice walk today and saw a lot of vendors selling everything from craft items to gif. It's a place they have to take new patrons as well as to sell something. Some of them are farmers selling craft food. All the vendors are very friendly and approachable, and are a great resource. There were a lot of vendors today. One vendor was giving away samples of their product and offered to take pictures with the customer. Some were engaged and asking questions. It seemed like the majority of the folks were just buying products off the rack. The food is actually very fresh. I'm a fan of the farmers and what they stand for, but I'm also a fan of the merchandise. Depending on the amount of stuff that is available, even one or two of them can make you happy--until the end of the session. I'm pretty sure that I could have ate there with only a few ingredients.

I was very excited to head down to the Kurt Vonnegut Museum today to see my second visit of the month! I've just been able to visit the Ernest Hemingway Museum of the Mississippi Delta for one of my favorite writers and I have to say I I must have missed out on this, because I had no concept of the author Ernest Hemingway until I found out that it is owned by the Ernest I was so happy to see that it is currently open (it opened in December, though the museum officially began operations in September). The museum itself is completely unstaffed and the guided tour is $10 which is about double the normal cost. I visited the museum for the first time this week. An admission is free and you will not be greeted by any strangers for an hour. The museum itself has quite a few sections with a lot of great books. On the top floor, you will find the Book Library and there is a huge collection of Vonnegut books on the first floor. Another section includes a collection of a book written specifically to be read at a particular time or place. The second floor exhibit was also quite interesting. There's almost no lack for books about Vonnegut. All the books are well written and interestingly illustrated. One of the books I bought specifically for my wife's birthday is "Escape from the Planet of the Apes" by Vonnegut. The museum is accessible by elevator and stairs are available on all floors. In addition, there is a small gift shop on the first floor where visitors can give Vonnegut artwork a whirl and get a This is a place where adults can explore the author and enjoy his work. I'll definitely take friends here for a group tour, too! There's a parking lots on Indiana Avenue at the museum, but I found that parking was rather difficult during the week, even when it was not. What an experience! Thank you to both authors for a great experience! It's free and it's very close to my home in Indianapolis. I was very much inspired by the story.

I got one of the beef meals that they made using ground beef and was served over a plate that had been cut into the middle and was layered on It was large and covered in about a third of the sauce I ordered. The side salad tasted fine but I still felt its texture and size wasn't as much as I anticipated. I'm really surprised I had to pay $10 for the food when it was $7 already included. It really is well known for the mural of the author Kurt Vonnegut in the downtown Fort Wayne Public Library. Pamela Bliss is the artist who produced the mural which will feature the 1922 Pulitzer Prize-winning author Kurt Vonnegut. The artist received the commission from Indianapolis Mayor Roger Goodman. The mural is held on the 96th Street Plaza in downtown Indianapolis. For more information about Bliss or her artwork, visit: http://pamelablossom.gmail.com/. The Indianapolis art gallery and Vonnegut mural will be featured in November of this year in the City of Indianapolis. His books were longlisted for the Pulitzer Prize for literature. Bliss's mural depicts a man who has a strong commitment to civic and social responsibility.

The King Memorial is a major tourist attraction in downtown Indianapolis. During the 1964 US Senate election, Senators John F. Kennedy and Martin Luther King Jr. stood side by side at the park. This event was so tragic that King took his life, but as citizens of Indianapolis we cannot help but be affected by it. The monument to King and his sons is located near the park and is well thought out, well made and also very beautifully maintained. The park honors this event by depicting civil rights and political issues from a diverse group of people. The park in Indianapolis is both a children's park and a business center. This park is divided into two sections. During the Memorial Weekend, the memorial will be opened in the park and you can view it by walking on a path to the south. A wide pedestrian path runs through both portions allowing visitors to enjoy the park at different rates. I can tell from some of the photos of the park, this park is in need of many changes. While not an official State Park, it appears as though the local citizens are giving their city a say and this park deserves every bit of it. If you are interested in visiting this park for a memorial of the Reverend Martin Luther King Jr. it is highly recommended.

Conner Prairie is changing and they are doing it well. For instance, the park is getting a much-needed facelift with two new parking lots and a new visitors center. But, it's just the beginning. They are trying to offer exciting new things. The visitor center is the most visited area of the park and offers some interesting amenities. Children can explore the tour area and see the exhibits, and get a feel for the life of the Conner family and a little of their world It also has a large museum which has a collection of historical artifacts, artifacts, memorabilia, and other exhibit The visitor center is also a location for petting the animals that are on site the day of your visit. In particular, their cheetahs/calf were cute with their little ones. There is another area within the park that you might not have visited before. The home or Homestead is located here. After a few brief rounds of the house, the kids sat down to study life there under the light of the lanterns. The story in the house is very fascinating (in a good way). The area is located along the White River and has trees growing on the land. The tree tops are all painted and there is an outdoor fire pit where you can meet animals. This place reminds me of the "Hawk House" that I also saw in Indiana, but it takes the place of one. At the end of the trail, you'll get to see the buildings that were once part of Fort Hoosier that were later reconstructed. If you are interested in the history of Indiana it's probably worth a drive and I think you will find a lot of interesting things around the state These are a few of the areas of the park that aren't quite as well attended as those that are. This park is worth a stop if you want to see all the history in one place. You should definitely consider visiting.

We arrived at the restaurant on April 9th and are definitely looking forward to it. We arrived at the Italian restaurant Chelsea's on 10th Street, in the basement of the hotel. The bartender (I think) was good-looking and super nice to us. The waitress was a beautiful, kind and warm lady. I would definitely recommend her to anyone. We were impressed by the different courses and was impressed to see how many featured dishes included in the price. I can only imagine the variety of dishes. There are not many ravioli dishes that can rival their quality...just heavenly. It was delicious and really had a fantastic flavor. They also do a wonderful job preparing salads and it is nice to see such a large selection of cheeses on the menu from Italian cheese makers So there we have it. We will definitely be back! I would have loved to add pine nuts! Food was great, service was excellent and the specials dishes and specials was outstanding! All seasoned perfectly and cooked very well without any oilings or seasonings. I was very impressed by what I had to say. We were very pleased with everything we were served; however, we were so disappointed...that we decided to leave! A very good meal, no complaints! Excellent food, service and food. All of the "specials" are also on our wish list; we would love to eat there again.

My review of this restaurant only indicates that the owner is nice, but overall I am very pleased with the quality of service and the amount of money invested. We eat out frequently and really enjoy dining at Fitzgerald's, so I am excited to support an area restaurant that serves good food as well as aesthetically What not to like? I've had the opprobrium of the Phoenix Theater for a few years now and I've had some really pleasant experiences. I was not disappointed. After having to wait for over an hour in line, there was no wait at all when you get there. There are many sections within the theater so be prepared for them having limited staff. Most people are confused about where seats are and if they are inside the box you have a hard time getting into the seats. I would rather have the seating where I was seated. The theater has a very modern look with some shabby, vintage, decor with a "conventional" feel. I was happy that they used air con, but maybe not enough. At the theater, it is not very easy to find the entrance. There are a lot of people, so your ticket cost should cover most of them, especially the front row. Wait at the designated entrance at the main entrance. At that time, you can enter your seating area. There is no "open," so you have to have the concessions before entering the theater. There is a nice selection of seating, including the bar and bar stools, and it is also possible to get a seat at the end for free the front door...which was a great convenience in the winter. We ended up sitting away from the audience, so we'll leave that for the next review. The seats were expensive, but the theatre is well worth the price at only $16 for a show. Parking is very efficient, and I believe the theater has a small garage/parking space on the north side of the building. The best part of the performance was Boney James playing the piano after the singer came on the stage. The sound at least wasn't garbled. We didn't have the same level of noise problem, but there was a good volume and sound, especially when the artist sang.

Despite its name, the Artsgarden isn't actually located just to the northeast, but rather to the north in downtown Indianapolis. However, the Artsgarden is one of the only places in downtown Indianapolis that serves both as a meeting space for a variety of local musicians and artists The Artsgarden is one of the best art centers in Indianapolis and I'm proud to have gotten to know many of these local artists. The main purpose of the Artsgarden is to provide quality entertainment and art opportunities, including performances by local artists and artists from surrounding areas. It hosts shows for free at least once every month and a short film every week. The regular performer is an Italian American instrumental artist, played by a local instrumentalist, or by a local rock and jazz artist. This is a great way to explore the variety and diversity of the city's urban music scene. And as a courtesy to the community, the Artsgarden is also the location of a monthly art performance series by local musicians. There are also events to visit with "Memorial" items or to purchase a piece of artwork. The Artsgarden features three building areas that are connected with "gallery style" glass enclosed in white vinyl fabric. With its unique shape and light, it is a must see! It is a ten story building allowing several views of downtown, the Indiana State Building, and Indiana City Hall all within a short distance. Especially as it's suspended for 5 stories up into the air. Here's to a great year!

My wife always needs me to pick up fabric at this store. This store provides it for me. I didn't shop with my sister when we went to this store, but what we did do check out was a comic book museum. Just too many great designs in various categories to list. My daughter and I arrived here this Saturday, March 22, 2014. Very bright, fun and has a great selection of materials and items available.
