The Book Barn is probably my favorite bookstore in the greater Seattle area. It's not just a book shop, not just a store, but a place that brings books to life. I had the chance to visit this store recently, and enjoyed this place to the point where we returned so quickly. The parking lot was organized for their customers so you don't have to be on a steepincline to get into the parking lot. They sold really great wrapping and a variety of Christmas trees and Christmas gifts. The store was clean and well organized. They even have the original book jackets on display and display cases for a pretty cheap price. They have good seating and an easy to visit cafe. This place is well worth a visit.

When I heard about M&J's ice cream store on 66th St., it was rumored that they were closed for  I recently visited.It was crowded, and the place was full. Upon entering the restaurant with my wife, we walked into a large, wooded shopping center with a brick wall and white carpets. We were directed to the bar area and walked into the dining room. In my experience, most restaurants can't get the staff to notice a guest is in, so this seemed to be a sign of people entering the The receptionist was very polite and asked us if we'd like to have drinks during the meal. A nice sized room. There is also a small bar on the front and a large patio, right in front of the restaurant. The dining room is located along side the river at the southwest end of the building. You can purchase chocolate chip cookies, a mini pumpkin pie, or apple pie. There is a small cafe, but I think that this would be more of an alternative. There are TV's, a piano, and dart board. To the left is a "tailor" shop (for the kitchen). We decided not to join the bar service, but instead ate in the dining room. I went with a chicken salad sandwich with kale, Romaine lettuce, tomato, and spinach cheese. It wasn't too salty since it was chicken, but no saltiness was needed. It was just moist, and was filled with everything I tasted on the menu. The sauce for the sandwich was prepared perfectly and the Pesto added another level of spice. It was a good combination that made a great sandwich. We also tried the potato chips. The sauce was very mild and wasn't overbearing. I was hungry after two sandwiches. My wife ordered the Pork Chop and the garlic dip with cheese. She really enjoyed her chicken sandwich and said it was very tasty, but she wasn't overly full. Very good chicken sandwich. Great place to have a quick lunch. Just another reason to make sure you visit this restaurant. They would have been happy to make it another day if the temperature warmed up a little. We both agreed.. I really enjoyed the sandwich and would do it again without question! To end, the atmosphere was pretty great. I also enjoyed the blue cheese sundae with chocolate chips. Food is quite good and the waitstaff seemed friendly.

I had just returned from a quick visit to the cafe with lunch before my visit to St Augustine. We were looking forward to going out for lunch with the 4 grandchildren and were not disappointed. I was pleased to see there wasn't a wait line, but was disappointed at the lack of the decor. There were other items available that I didn't mind, but they were clearly labeled to represent what kind of drink I'd be having. Food choices? No. My wife ordered the hot cheetah roll and thought it was good with a side of tomato sauce (that would serve as a dip I ordered a salad salad with a sliced avocado on top and a chicken sandwich with bacon ranch on the side. The cheese was decent and I expected more but overall the food was average. We ordered a Cuban Sandwich and the girl ordered a tomato and cheese horchata sandwich on a warm wheat bread. I decided to leave the chicken salad on the bun, because a few things were wrong with the bread. This did not seem to matter as it felt like I was eating just a piece of bread. The cafe is located near the State Museum, and it was clearly a small restaurant with one large booth and one small table. Unfortunately, it turned out that I wasn't even happy to eat it. I'm giving the cafe 2 stars for the sandwiches, but the salad was sorely lacking in flavor that the 2 stars could have been attributed to the We will not be returning. Besides that, the Cafe is a small restaurant with seating of just two people.

For their restaurants and dining experiences, the Public Greens in Salt Lake City, Utah, is one of the restaurants I'd recommend to any frequent visitor of I visited Panera today for the first time. The second stop on our visit to the mall was The Craft Shoppe. First off was a one of a kind shop, called "Amity and Liberty Artisans. I just came to this location to pick up breakfast for my niece while she was in town. After a short wait at the coffee place, I took advantage of a quick lunch special by getting an American to go. The place was very clean, and had an interesting concept for a breakfast bar. I loved their service and the atmosphere was fun. A really good coffee with a cool background. I also saw a lot of fruit available, but it was not picked out on the menu like I would like. It had a little bit of cream cheese over the muffin, which came with a bit of blueberries added. They also had a light cinnamon sprinkle sprinkled over the muffin. They are pretty good, but there are not many options and the menu is quite limited. An early morning brew at The Crabhouse. I arrived at Cornerstone Brewery from the airport about 10-12am (checking in was a great time). A pleasant receptionist was standing by while I waited. When I went into the bar, I asked about the menu and asked what beer was for this lunch. I liked their selection of organic beers which were all relatively mild. The selections had a nice balance! The selection was huge! I was very happy I chose the Koelsch! The beers were both really fresh, sour, and flavorful. Each was also rich, with medium-bodied flavor. Also, the restaurant is open until 4PM from Sunday to Thursday. We could have easily had our sandwiches (I had always wanted them), but we got in the mood for something else. This sandwich was delicious!!! This sandwich was very tasty. The sandwiches, as with all of my subs, went through a premade aioli/soy sauce mixture using an all natural sweet My favorite part of the sandwich was at the end what was definitely a bit too creamy for me. The sauces came out bright, flavorful, and fresh. The side of fruit, melons and berries, was made well. I noticed that the fruit was mixed in like a bag or jar, which was especially helpful because my bag of fruit was mostly melons and berries The fruit was fresh, vibrant and flavorful. They also brought out two large glasses of sweet tea. The sandwich definitely worked its way into the rotation for the next lunch-time customers. Thanks for all your efforts! This is my first brewing experience; I was very impressed and I will definitely be back. They worked with me on the portion sizes, keeping things pretty reasonable. And to finish off what he did right (and thnks to Taylor), he offered to take care of the rest of my lunch order

I recently joined the Scarlet Lane Brewery in Seattle where I always found their beers pretty strong. It's just north of downtown Tigard (not quite 2 miles away from the Tigard River at all) but there is some good character inside the bar The interior of Carvel's Cafe is fairly plain. The interior is clean and quite comfortable. There's free Wi-Fi and plenty of seating from the comfort of the bar. From the outside it's a cozy, laid back atmosphere, including an open fire pit, just before the bar opens. The Loiterers was the first of the three I had in mind, but the rest of the beers were fine. My first was a 2% White Ale which was very clean and smooth tasting. The beer was not a bad beers, but very salty. Nice flavor and I liked the salty flavor. The Blood Squash is a pretty solid IPA (4%) that isn't the most interesting because of the dark red color and pretty much an This would be a tasty addition to my favorites, but at only 4 percent, they really have a good balance. It's a lot sweeter on this one than most stouts, so I like it. Also, I didn't notice when I was finishing off this that I was a bit hungry, so it definitely tasted like I had drank I have to say I really enjoyed this pale ale and wasn't disappointed. I went on on to the Blissy Belgian Weed Ale (6.7%) which was a dry, malty, and dry Finally, The Rye, a 5% Rye Stout with Astringent Lime Flavors and a slight bite of Citra. This had a lot of fruity flavor in it which made for a great combination. I can tell that it could be a result of the rye being cooked off. My server was friendly and did a wonderful job and I look forward to returning. I like the idea that the beer is made from whole grain malts, and that is something that scarlets-lane might not be able to do There were only a few tables in the place when we visit, so it was one of the last places we visited.

On my way into town from Montreal I noticed some great restaurants nearby such as Sushi's, Panoramus, and Koh Koh. I was swayed by the taste of the Montreal Bistro sandwich I ate today. The order was delivered in about 20 to 25 minutes with a simple cutout on the bagels. The bacon was just a bit too nutty and the lettuce was very fresh but not so tangy. The Turkey and Bacon is delicious, served alongside a side salad just like a French toast. I liked the idea of it being wrapped in foil for a good portion of the day and not being a huge dish later. I also ordered a Mojito (chocolate & red velvet soda). It was sweet but wasn't nearly as sweet as some smoothies I've been having. Orders are always taken at the counter. Although the name does not match, that's not necessarily a bad thing given their popularity. I waited for only about 25 seconds before taking the order. The place is quick and convenient, but it does take a while to get there. This is an old place and although the food looks much better than the photos, I wasn't impressed. A good place for a quick lunch. As mentioned before, this is a late lunch location. I highly recommend this place for lunch and drinks! Great breakfast!.Bagels are always cooked well, but it was too cold for my taste!

Food Service Review: Lulula's Cafe was open in this area for lunch on Monday, Aug. 23, 2010. As you might have noticed, I am rarely at fast food restaurants in the neighborhood, and that was the first time it was on my list of places to try However, at least those early morning hours did serve lunch, so we decide to try a new favorite place. I was not on top of it at all - the bread had both the perfect texture I was looking for and the texture I was tired of. We decided upon the "Wrap" menu that consisted of four separate options including pizzas, queso dip, etc. The room is fairly small, but spacious and comfortable. As you walk in the cafe you enter the bakery where you are greeted at the counter with your name/number and then placed in someone's No waiting areas, and we are also not offered any seating when seated. I asked the staff if there was anything I could try since we were not looking for anything very sweet. We came over to get two slice of fresh baguette for our lunch option. The banana nut slices were quite good, having a lovely aroma with a soft center. I agreed and chose the zucchini bread slice. Initially, I was not interested in the banana nut bread as it had the same flour as most other breads. My wife ordered the French toast to share between two plates on a paper plate. It was perfectly fresh and tasty. I ordered a chicken wrap with avocado, tomato, and cheese on a toasted tortilla. This lunch option was my favorite. This was a thick chicken wrap with chunks of chicken and radicchio peppers that matched up perfectly with the ranch sauce. The chicken, cheese, and ranch was all very tangy and hot, and it remained in your mouth throughout lunch. I had a bite of the chicken, which had a nice texture and crisp exterior, but my wife really enjoyed the chicken as well. I would rate this restaurant 5 out of 5 stars. But I would still like to say we were very happy with our portions of their lunch, and I will return next time and definitely bring my lunch companions. They do have a drive-up window on this side of town where the menu display also shows a picture next to the building. For lunch items, I would recommend ordering with the cheese/guacamole.

Located in Midtown Chicago, the sandwich shop at the corner of the 2 and W, where I work has been doing business for a number of years and it opened today. You need to walk through a small tunnel from the curb to the front door and there is no wait. I arrived in the morning and was quickly treated to a friendly welcome by the staff. As you enter the restaurant, a simple front entrance provides a quick way into the place. A menu appears on the screen in front of me. There are also a few sandwiches available with a variety of meats. The wait was 15ish minutes for my chicken soup and about 40 minutes for my regular lunch sandwich. I'm not sure how good the soup was. It was good. My chicken was cooked perfectly. Nothing special about this soup. I was a little disappointed with its consistency. The Chicken Panini with fresh fruit came out in less than five minutes. Like many sandwiches on American menu, it needed to be re-heated. I had never heard of this before. How do you know?!) I ordered up a bowl of chips that had been thrown into the panini to make up for the time difference...I got the first two and The sandwich was served in a wrap with swiss cheese lettuce, tomato and mayo. The avocado slices were seasoned very well and the meat was moist and tender. The banana was very smooth and the savoy cabbage with the cheese was an awesome touch. This was followed by a plate of fresh fruit. The bread was thick so it felt like I was eating a sandwich that was not ripe enough. It's a casual restaurant with good food and good service for a reasonable price. The sandwiches are pretty standard, a chicken breast with avocado, mayo, and tomato. I'm glad Reme's did. It was not the worst dinner I've had though, for a small-ish joint....but not the best experience I've had in a

I like this place. It is big and filled with lots of good records. It was super clean and very well organized. There was a good selection of vinyl records; not too expensive at all. They have a full kitchen if you need to eat lunch or breakfast. They also have a place for special sale, and of course, you can order for free if you have online access - that's always  There was even nice seating for waiting.

At first I was a little unsure of how things work in this store because I thought it was a little run of the mill jewelry store. This place is actually from the 1920's and is now home to one of my favorite businesses in the area, The Shops Intown. The place itself is a little bit more dark outside than the outside, but it is worth it to take the short walk. There are really beautiful gifts available. I was able to find a place to eat after having had lunch today and I got food around 10 AM. Our waitress was helpful and the restaurant came out pretty quick. We left very quickly, and were greeted right away by a friendly waitress, who offered us a drink right away. All the staff were helpful, efficient and courteous. Very good.I ordered a burrito deluxe with beef, chicken, shrimp, and cheese.We ordered the chicken wings with onions and the We felt rather happy, especially since we weren't actually on their regular menu. Wild Ginger is a great option for fine sushi - they carry a variety to choose from (including Japanese and vegetarian options), which will give you variety They offer both traditional and specialty rolls. I recently visited and was greeted by the staff and was seated. I got to Wild Ginger last week to check out their lunch specials and reviews for a variety of specials. One would assume by now that the restaurant is a family-owned business. The room was cool (not crowded) and comfortable. The tables are all comfortable and the chairs look nice on my side of the restaurant. Orders were quick and I received my food on time, which I was happy about. Their manager was informative and helpful and answered any questions I had. I ordered three items to start my meal. I ordered their favorite: Tempura Roll. The Tempura was dry and not very good. I liked that the shrimp were fried to a crisp, golden brown then sliced into 3 pieces (so you have 2 pieces of shrimp in the I thought they were nice and flaky. The sauce was delicious and complemented the shrimp perfectly. Then we had the Salmon Roll and Salmon Omelet. When choosing a vegetable, I chose a long, thin cut, because they were very thin and we didn't want to pick out a lot The nigiri was a small piece of steamed fish and had few leaves (but the fish was so delicious, it was hard to I was ready to order the Dragon roll. It can be pre-loaded with a tuna roll (or two tuna rolls). This one was a dragon shape (the dragon is shaped like a butterfly, but the head and feathers resemble a panda). Rather than just using rice, chicken, and fish, they used a mixture of greens (including a yellow egg and a red egg) All the items on the dragon roll were arranged in an easy-to-detach manner on a lone square roll. They also sold me some seaweed. Review from Wild Ginger of Portland. The staff at Wild Ginger is very helpful,friendly,friendly and just a pleasant place to eat.

This place at 10801 2nd street in Lake Worth is worth a visit if you like baking cookies. Just inside a small, low-key office, what I feel is a shop with very few spaces to enter is covered in a small awning A side entrance leads to a smaller room in which our table and chairs were found. That’s where you buy the cookie dough, but that’s as far as I was concerned that the bakery is not that good. We were both told that they were so delicious that we were rushing back inside. The menu looked interesting but the cookies were all very unique, with a lot of options. I ordered the white chocolate chip cookie because they looked fresh and were very easy to make. She loved the cookie’s bite size and they also have an egg drop spread if you can’t go through the process of buying a cookie. The prices were reasonable. The price was right for the small bite sized cookies. I will definitely be back to try more of the recipes and perhaps buy some of the more unusual ones if available.

Here at Indiana Adventure, our favorite part of a visit to Nashville to visit a town is going to be looking around for a place to stop because We were talking about vanishing small towns. The Hero House also serves as a community-building tool as it shows that there's lots of potential for this kind of business to thrive. It's possible in Fountain Square. There needs to be at least one small shop to pull away all the chaos. I had the pleasure of visiting the Hero House earlier in the day. It was a nice shop and I am glad they did it this way. I had my dog with me and they put me next to a big brown kitty (not only did it keep me from hitting the dog several time And, of course, the pricing is fair. I went here with some friends today on a recommendation of my business associates and wanted to give it another shot. There are many delicious flavors and the menu is easily organized by theme, which makes it versatile and easy to search for a specific flavor. Featuring a variety of pieces from vintage to collectibles. Even better was the selection of vintage furniture at this place. I always want to try a new restaurant on South Lake Avenue before I head back to Chicago. We had an easy time in the lunch rush at Red Hot Ramen. While I was there, I thought the menu was quite good considering that there hasn't been much of a transition as far as their lunch items have I would not go back or purchase from YUJ, but I feel like the prices are fair and you have the option to get a bag of The food took a while to order (on & off hours) and took about half hour overall. This was my first dining experience, so I thought I'd check their other specials as well. I chose the "spinach dill pasta" which had tomato, pepperoni, pepperoni, onion, and mushroom. I ordered some fresh lettuce, followed by some tomato, onion, and a small Caesar salad with white wine and white cheese. I didn't like the salad because it felt like it was soggy, but it was still good. It was nice and fresh. The pizza arrived about 5 minutes later. The first slice was fairly small. My sandwich was good. I found all the ingredients to be pretty nice. I didn't notice a huge amount of sauce on my pizza, but it tasted good. Not that I'd avoid it, but you might want to add a bit more salt into the sauce after you get your plate off. I think it was a little thick on top of the pizza. They don't sell extra tomatoes but still give everything to you with your order if you wish. It was nice to be able to eat this in a casual restaurant environment rather than in a bar. We were both very happy with our lunch. After my salad was finished, I got there and the servers were taking pictures with my order. The food was fresh and the service was prompt. I'm not sure what the manager was thinking, but I was really glad I didn't leave hungry. I enjoyed my lunch, but I found that my mouth was burning, so I wasn't able to come back for dessert.

A few weeks ago, I came across the new beer establishment at Flat 12. Upon entering, you immediately get hung up and notice the huge spout of beer that flows down from one end of the bar to the other It's open 24/7 so you can come in any time and check it out. After you enter the restaurant, you'll be directed to a counter, where you can order a drink. The drinks list is huge and includes the likes of a craft beer flight and an alcoholic beverage. On the menu, you can choose from what they call "Southwestern inspired" breakfast meals, or you can order something savory, like Eggs Benedict, There are different options for toppings, so you could pick those up ahead of time for a really good meal. You can also order your chicken & waffles with hot or cold bacon. The Chicken & Waffles option is probably one of the best I've tried, and so long as you get an item that has chicken inside, My breakfast burrito was very large as opposed to what I normally get from the restaurant in general. I even noticed the cheese was slightly melted during the cooking process. You have your choice of chicken, beef, or sausage. My favorite part about the burrito was the crunch of the tortilla chips inside the burrito and the seasoned flavor. I've never tried the Breakfast Scramble, but I was very impressed with the meal and the way the food was rounded out. Not bad...the hot sauce and chili on top added some good flavor for this veal version, but I think the main ingredients did a lot of I loved how the ingredients together were served together to give it that bit of flavor. The burrito was made of chicken with a soft, nutty texture that was almost like chewy bread. There are other great breakfast options available throughout the day as well, but the menu might change for the better once the customer base grows. The restaurant is a little small, meaning they only have a limited number of tables available, but at least we can always come back to try another thing Not to mention the beer selection is quite good already but more choices to choose from. I'll probably make a special trip to downtown for them soon so I can stop by for a couple of dishes before I head off on my next

The department store is very nice and its easy to shop here. When you walk up the corner to the north end of the mall, across from the Red brick and neon sign for the Metro Center, turn right on to  They opened on April 8th, just two days before the official opening of the food court at just pop in! We had our first lunch here and it was beautiful. At first glance, we were a little shocked to see this quaint little cafe, but I think it is because I don't realize it's The facade is bright and cheerful. With a light breeze bouncing out from behind the patio, it was a wonderful place to sit to watch the kids play. There are two dining rooms down the north side of the building. The north dining area is a large private room with a couch and several cozy chairs. There are two chairs you can sit on and one table that can sit 3 people. The ceiling is covered with a mural that reads "Stop being a Slash" and it is in the center of the room under the arcade The seating is all about the coffee and the food quality is good! All the tables are in the area which they have called "Spot," while the north table is in the room on the west side. The whole place had a nice cool vibe! There are 14 different entrees with their choice of either fried or open faced cheeseburger, fries, or salad. There are two soups, two sandwiches, and seven sandwiches (all available as lunch specials) with different toppings. There are four cheeses, cream cheese and cheese, smoked salmon, pesto, and tuna. Food and drinks are really good at this location. There are four choices of beer, and four choices of wine. The chicken & chips and egg salad starters, served with cream cheese and a toasted bagel, are served with your choice of mashed potatoes (The service is served with the same cheeses too). And there is a small menu of "services" with chicken wrap, wings, wings, burgers, and sandwiches. They have the same bowl of tuna salad on their menu for $5.95, but I chose to add some of the tuna to the plate. The service came with a large salad with a bagged salad, a small dip, and two pops of hot sauce. I found some of the items on their menu too salty for my taste but then they added salt to the sauce, so nitrate free and not The staff was very pleasant, and I highly recommend this place. There is also an indoor picnic area with a big table and chairs, plus outdoor tables of sorts with picnic tables, and a cool little bench to sit They have a small selection of local beers including the "Double Dutch," "Friddland Ale." The waiter seemed to like popcorn when I ate, though I could tell he was enjoying his food. You can enjoy their pizza on the flat screen TV or get something to eat the next time you stop by. Just Pop In opens to the public on the first Monday in March 2018! They also have hot dogs and wings for breakfast. Even for my youngest he enjoyed the fries, which were just plain flavorless. The cafe is fairly tiny so you should expect it to go very quickly. Despite some minor minor blemishes, it was a great time and worth a visit.

I never really enjoy cupcakes. I've never been tempted like that by a Cupcake Bar in North Carolina. So no, it's not a good taste! I've seen cupcakes all over the place, but what a treat! I wasn't sure how many flavors or items they offered at their store in the Southside. Yes it was! And they did it as well as I could have hoped. One of my favorite places downtown! The store was empty. I was blown away. So I went in to browse and just ended up picking some up and putting them into a box. The cupcakes were delivered in a box that had holes all around so they would stay in an airtight sealed package. The boxes were designed very well: they come with a bag and are very dense and made really sturdy! The cupcake was rolled in a piece of paper with a little toothpick on each side and the tops of all three cupcakes. This saves you many dollars in the long run and they came out to be hot and yummy! I tried a small piece of each, but the taste was excellent! I opted for the vanilla cupcake as is one of my favorite cupcakes out of all the cupcakes they offered. I started with the red velvet. I would describe it as a butter cream cake and the icing was light and airy. I'd order from the store again if I wanted to. Pumpkin pecan is a lot more dense than the red velvet. I ate it immediately, and was just as surprised at the richness of the pumpkin-flavored flavoring. I got the pumpkin pecan flavor and absolutely loved it. The addition of the brown sugar in the icing tasted like cream cheese, but without the sugar. The red velvet was the same thing, but more sugary and the toppings were more reminiscent of the icing. The salted chocolate caramel was a tad dense in texture and flavor, but surprisingly the icing and the cakes tasted identical! Then there was the chocolate chip, but overall, not as good as the other two. I really enjoy their cupcakes, I will definitely be coming back to see if they still get these (the cupcakes will be coming back but I am They also made the tops from the vanilla shortcake. The store was so well maintained and clean that I had trouble deciding which ones to try. I was excited to try these and I can't wait to go back and try more out! They were a little pricey, but there were a lot of fun things going on.

I really enjoyed this lunch time at Hiko's. It was just so good I knew I had "a bowl" I had to try. The waiters were friendly and helpful. There was a small counter with no seating area, which is good since it offers a nice view of the beach. I had a small bit of trouble navigating during my first visit. You are asked to input your preferred meat/veggie combination: Turkey, Chicken, or Shrimp. You then eat your lunch. There are multiple options for the rice/sushi combination, so you are limited to the classics. I selected the "signature bowl", which is a mix of all the ingredients you might find on asian menu, but all in one bowl. I had it with some teriyaki chicken, yellowtail, pineapple, and mango. This bowl is more like a regular bowl, so I'll save room for the signature bowls. At checkout you can choose to have your signature bowl topped with shrimp shumai or yakitori shrimp. A bit of fresh lime, lime and grapefruit juice, one cup of mango and one cup of Thai basil adds a tropical twist to the traditional island I have no idea if they had to change the color of the dish because of that; it was very good. This was my first time eating inside a restaurant and I am glad I did! After the bowl was ordered, I noticed a lot of brown rice and crabmeat sticking in the bowl. After a minute or two, my order was done and the bowl was served to me. The flavor was definitely enough to hold my interest even ten minutes after adding more sauce to it. I love this bowl even though it's a regular bowl. The texture was really light and oh-so-sweet. The portions are huge, which is good for a place that is not big on portions. We came home to be full after 15 minutes, even though the restaurant was packed. Look for their food truck soon!

Nice venue.A great bar. This is the only St. Elmo's restaurant without a bar. They offer a nice view of the entire lake. They have good food, drinks, and service. Service was great too. Some things to note: The rooms are a little tiny at the restaurant or bar. I thought it was a little spooky when I was there because most of the customers are older and didn't even know what St. El It is also difficult to make a reservation, especially at peak hours. However, it seems like the drinks are rushed now and then so don't expect service to be fast or quick and the food is just average. Definitely worth a quick stop.

After attending a friend's wedding, I had to try out a breakfast at Blue Heart Cafe. Well, that is if you look for the name, "Family Diner", so in my case, you can always order from the "D So, I wasn't sure what to expect since the menu looked fairly standard for a hotel breakfast place with good Eggs Benedict, bacon, eggs Benedict and a lovely cafe design. The menu consisted of breakfast items like Eggs Benedict, pancakes, eggs and bacon (as seen with a hotdog or sausage roll), and However, upon walking down to the table in the bar area I noticed the menu (the one on the left) was a little different, with different items But I thought that was actually all I would ever order! It didn't look like everything was pretty standard, but there were a couple other options that I came to love. I have yet to find a good experience with it except last time. This was so good! The poached egg was the best you can find anywhere. So good!.Emphatic. I decided to try their Butter Fried Stew since it looked interesting and I thought it would really help bring the dish to life. That was the Romaine Roll. The potatoes were lightly seasoned with lavender and the pears were roasted and cooked with their liquids for a wonderful "cheddar" flavor that They were nicely seasoned with some kosher salt and pepper. These are truly some of the best items I've had at this place! The French toast was also very good on the side. It was just the right size & taste to share as an appetizer. I just expected the texture to be a little charred/burnt/toasted. I was told it would be a regular plain croissant (which would have made me hungry). But, to my surprise, I could tell there was a layered breakfast including bacon, eggs, and a fresh berry sauce. I just felt like a toasted cheesesteak and it was delicious. Felt like I was in a nice little place and the place felt like I had a pretty good breakfast. If you are looking for a great place to grab Sunday breakfast in this beautiful Chicago location, check out Lean In Kitchen, which is also close by. I think it is worth it. Although I thought it wasn't worth the price but it tasted so good! But it beats the usual fast food options! We are definitely going back for breakfast!

The front door led up from the parking lot and we were promptly seated. We were dining in and did not feel rushed. On a recent visit to this amazing facility, I was one of the first of the first to arrive in the area (we had arrived on Sunday evening, The seating is well thought out and overall comfortable for me. Stopped in late at lunch and was given a free refill on my soda - and it was a great deal! The food at the restaurant is fast and not at all over-the-top. The meal was very good at this location. The first park on the site is called Millpond Park. Initially called the National Cathedral, it was founded by Dr. Walter L. McConnell in 1881. To the west of the park, an obelisk tower lies over the street. His firm, based in New Canaan, was also responsible for the ornamentation. It is made of three layers of molded concrete with a height of 90 feet across. It marks the city of New York, which at the time of its deposition in 1940 was in control of the contiguous United States. The fountain is surrounded by various sculptures indicating the founding values of the current "laws", laws, and institutions of the nation. The fountain is curved as it is above the obelisk. The first two fountains were built in 1936, one of which was designed by the architect Henry Hering. In the middle of the park, a bronze sculpture with a fountain fills the lower part. The park has two lanes on all sides with a fountain in the center. The park is open daily from 8:00-9:00 p.m. This location is one of the most beautiful parks in Indianapolis. There are numerous park buses running throughout the area.

What isn't to like? Roku Sushi & Pho has been open since March of this year, and you can order any kind of food you want, including the menu items It's called Sushi Cafe and has a tiny interior, but everything else is fresh and delicious. It's difficult to find because the entrance is in the middle of an open lot. The interior is really simple and pretty sleek. If you're looking to avoid getting smelly, be aware the windows can have the shades on (and the doors) and your food (including drinks) As you can see, there is very little decor inside. If you are in that area, there's a small table with a couple of Chinese tea sets on it. The menus have a bunch of options that were made available to me. The chairs are comfy though. There are no tables in the middle of the room, but at most tables, you won't see it. Then, despite the relatively large sign, it turns out the bar is a low alcohol venue. They have a variety of options and are definitely worth the wait. On to the food. You can get the menu in Vietnamese instead of English. There are 5 salmon choices: tuna, salmon, salmon sashimi and roll. Then I ordered 1 of their popular Pho (poké) dishes (yum). I'm not a big fan of having a roundball of rice on top of your meal and being exposed to all the flavor that goes along with On TV, I often see people eat two or three as part of their party, and then a third to finish off a big portion! It was really good. I could only get about half. Not bad, but a little overcooked and the salmon wasn't as fresh as I had expected. Their nigiri are sliced, with no pieces stuck together (see pic). I ordered this with lemon grass-flavored nitrate-based sauce which was really good. I also ordered a Chicken Panang (whole chicken) which was very good. I wish that it would be a little longer, since they will only serve it in a bowl. The fish tasted great, too! My wife had the beef (noodles) and seafood (beef tofu) rolls. If you are looking to get a bit of Sushi, I've been putting it on my wish list to try again! I've learned to appreciate a little variety! For the sake of completeness, I don't know where the other reviewers at this restaurant got all the delicious things that they do, but I think Roku is open daily, but not always. I like Thai, and Roku makes me happy with its authentic cuisine. I'm not sure that would be for everyone, but I'm glad I tried it and was impressed. It's a little small and it's very a bit pricey on menu items. That's right, the fish has to be whole instead of just cut up. They even added on additional Thai sauce for the nigiri. The rice plate was delicious. I'm glad I did. If you haven't had it in a while, the rice is cooked longer than usual. We had this dish again, but I have to say, it was quite rich and tasteful! I really enjoyed it and think Roku is just as good as the first. This is the first Pho restaurant I have ever had, and they do a great job! There are 3 or 4 different options of pho in the menu, but I didn't try one of the 3 options. The rice was good (no fish), and the salmon was flavorful. The salmon was very tender, with flavor. You can make your own frog roll (so it really sounded like a frog roll), a bowl of pho ( Just like that!, for the next time! I am sure their customer service can be better. (I believe they are now open later evenings.) My husband and I decided to split a bowl of eggrolls for fried chicken. This is a very low key restaurant with great menu items and service.

My wife and I were in town for dinner on Saturday evening. The room was very clean and the seating area was also extremely nice. She said they only provide water in the burger area and there was no beer on tap and no service. My wife was quite excited about having dinner here and told me that it was the best Thai restaurant we’d ever been to, and that the food and service They had a very interesting selection of sandwiches and starters for us. I ordered the Shrimp and Slaw with Turkey and Tomatoes. We had the food delivered to our table right away when she arrived. There were plenty of shrimp and not too crowded. The shrimp itself were well prepared and just the right amount of seasonings. The shrimp were not seasoned at all and had a nice, tender seasoning. I ordered a burger on a Kaiser bun. A lot of cheese was melted while the bun was still warm. This was a big, juicy burger. This was not a very complicated order but the burger was very tender and the bun was very soft and didn't crack. The burger and sides came in a paper cone and were made by thigh-high heat. That probably would have been less salty though, but the fries were tasteless. However, they were still quite delicious and you could probably do without the fries. My wife and I will definitely return again because she loved it but I really think her favorite food was the Flashback Shrimp. We were very pleased with our experience at Buffalo and would definitely recommend it if you want great and fresh food.

I found the place on Washington Street in the Eastside after a long drive. I know they are still owned by Ben as he is the owner, which brings a sense of stability to the bakery. For the owner, many items in the bakery come about because she is a passionate baker. This is a store that is owned and operated by a local woman. Located at 325 Washington St., it took a while for me to find this place, since I drive to the bakery from my house. If you know a lot about Irvington, maybe you won't know the little nuances like this. Luckily, it was no trouble! You won't drive near the bakery unless you are in good driving weather. The entrance to the building is small and low. Afterwards, it's a nice walk through to the kitchen. The front entrance is a cafe style space and while you enter, you receive a warm welcome from the owner and the staff. There is a bar which is available for your take-out orders. Of course, the items in the baked goods section are all made with fresh dough. You might want just one item. Maybe you'll find a piece of chocolate. Sometimes you want some soup. Don't be afraid to try anything. Yes, there is more than just baked goods. I even felt as though I was back to eating on the island with my favorite calzone or something. BitterSweet is open everyday 9-12 ish, so on some days you can get a "light bite" and get your food for I had several items I tried – not to mention that they are all homemade. I'll be back!

Sometimes it's just about running the whole way out west. Sometimes it was walking along the main road and capturing a stunning picture of the city. It is a two-block drive west of the downtown area. It is a two story building, with all of the beer making equipment in one room. I think this is very easy to find. Just past the train tracks is their restaurant and bar at the other end of the street. Outside there is a food court with patio and outdoor grill. There are also plenty of bar and restaurant items in the bar area. And on the left side is a bar area. The kitchen area has the typical burgers and salads you would expect at most bars. The menu is quite generous and the brewery menu is on the next page. My wife and I stopped by on Christmas Eve and had a fantastic time with our friends. It is a bar type restaurant (which is a welcome change from the previous pub called Flat 12). RAD is the most comprehensive list of craft beer in the area and has a bartender to help you figure it all out. A few of these beers are a bit stronger than other choices so a try is the best way to test. They have been selling their beers since at least the summer of 2011. For lunch I ordered the Nachos with a side of fried onions and pick There are a few beers that I don't actually remember the names of, but I've been on the lookout for them now. The burgers were very good, however, at $20+ a burger the quality of the meat did not seem very good - one burger All in all, the food was good but I'd suggest the beer be a first timer. In the new kitchen area, rad is offering more than just beers to drink and food. I like the fact that the bartenders are really friendly and will make a point to make you feel welcomed. On this visit, they had only served beer so far. The owners of this new brewery (and brewery) is all very cool and kind and I will definitely be coming back and visiting at RAD soon There is a free (though small) parking lot on the other side of town (be sure to bring your bike!). I think they are still learning how to do their bartendering. It was well prepared and good beer served in a fun looking place. It takes a long time to order (at least four) and the food is good. Most importantly, they have a delicious menu which is clearly written out and makes all the choices clear. I would certainly eat at RAD again!

New York Italian is a small pizza restaurant featuring local ingredients and a full menu of Italian favorites. The bread was a bit chewy, but overall the flavor was good. King Dough is located at 8407 Michigan Place in Glen Rock, MI but you will feel a bit of a bit of congestion heading out of The restaurant is inside the new office building which is a bit difficult to find as you'll notice it on the front facade. However, the crust was undercooked for the whole pie but not soggy. Maybe a couple extra layers of ham or peppers would have saved a whole lot of work. This means that I will not get my order again. While the Horchata was good, I won't buy it again. It was probably the best Mexican ice cream I had tried at an event. Danny's Ice cream is a store owned by a Mexican man who owns and serves his own ice cream shop! and he offers a great amount of choices and it is a fun atmosphere and a great place to be after a fun event. There are all kinds of different varieties of ice cream, so be prepared to try other flavors. So, if you go with an empty heart, you may not find yourself lingering on it. It's a fun, relaxing atmosphere where you can come with a group of friends, or as the owner, you can come out when everything is Let the ice cream be the talking point!

Arrived at the restaurant shortly after 5:00 p.m. (we were getting ready for a dinner party) and were seated around 7. We were seated at the bar and enjoyed the food and drinks. Theambiance was a contrasting blue and green. I got the Chimi wrap with chicken, white rice, and Mexican rice. The serving were plenty but they were all pretty big. She also added that she enjoyed the guacamole-based margaritas. The Margarita was delicious and light with a very sweet, sweet taste. The tacos were fresh and large for the cost. The tacos were very mildly spicy and just right for sharing. It was an extra step on the side because the chicken wasn't really cooked enough in my mouth and the rice was still a bit dry. It's been a while since I went to Don Cuervo's and I really wish I could say I really enjoyed eating at this location. as our dinners often do, which is a plus for me. Definately worth the drive!! It is located at Fishers Center at 96th st and Hague with free Wi-Fi and a wonderful environment for dining and nightly My wife and I came to lunch for a company dinner. We were not sure when it was going to take about 45 minutes to get there (thank you! ), our reservation was cancelled (after waiting at their website) because my wife had made a reservation at another restaurant when we got there. While the crabcake was pretty good I think the other dishes were just as good. This was the best meal we have had in Fishers. We liked both of our orders, but were disappointed with the lobster bisque. We got a big hit for the price of this evening’s dinner. I recommend this restaurant to anybody. (You better see it to believe it!). I highly recommend Peterson's! It made me hungry! This might not necessarily be the best steakhouse to go for if you are in a rush. It tasted good and had very little chicken (and had nothing like it being served with bone marrow). We finished up with lots of glasses of beer. The food was good! Some fresh garlic, scallions and a touch of parsley. If you are heading there, go up the hill to the corner of Hague and 96th Street. I decided to stop in from work one afternoon to check out the new brewery in Downtown Chicago (the place that I bought my beer from), and I got the I was initially excited to try the house brews. I think that any zoo should have an annual day. I am usually pleasantly surprised. People don't tell me that. I am a little more of a "theme park" fan than that. But it is still not too bad. If I'm in need of a place that is free, I go on any time of the day. There is never any question that the animals at the zoo live in natural habitats and in cages. For those of you that read this, you may remember what it was like back in 1974. It was more of a waste of money and didn't have enough options to display. At one point, the zoo was putting in more animals than the city needed. Now, about 15 years later, the zoo has been completely renovated. It gets a little busy sometimes. But, I have to admit that the zamzoo isn't the only one with great scenery. Of course, it doesn't have a lot of animals. We see that animals aren't kept purely captive so that humans can't take them away. The animals are well loved here and I see them enjoying it, while still getting some attention. And although there are some animals that we no longer see, it seems that more and more people are recognizing that a zoo is a I'm sure that you will too. I'm going to keep trying to protect them.

On a Saturday during Memorial Day weekend, I was on the hunt for a new "fast food" bar I wasn't familiar with. The cafe is located in the heart of downtown at 244 Cruze Street. The menu is incredibly simple with an interesting combination of flavor, texture, and presentation; and it is just as easy to get there as it is outside. The menu is a bit limited, but I got the garlic chicken and a Cuban sandwich with a side of fries. Moto can be found on the northwest corner of Washington and Elm and is next door to the Grizzly Coffee. The directions to the place are in the below map. Turn right onto Washington Street then turn right on the first light that is off, and go across to the east over the bridge. On the second bridge, make a U turn to the left of your stop sign. Enter this light.. you go into Cruze and turn back left. Turn right and the cafe is located on the right side. Turn left onto Cruze and the Cafe is immediately on your right. When you are there, just find the main door and turn left. On your return, if you're looking for something different, you should stop at the restaurant on your right (the entrance is on the right side of I found a plate of sandwiches with red sauce on it and decided the biggest I wanted would be the one, which is a large bun. I got the chicken salad which comes with a choice of a red sauce or a plain hot sauce on white bread. The menu also listed items for takeout (and if you want, they ship out to your car.) The sandwich was quite good. When I was done ordering, the menu said "Urban cuisine" and there was a sign on the back door for parking on the 2nd floor There's plenty of indoor seating on the first floor. The kitchen is small with a few shelves, but everything is very clean (except for the food). Once inside the stairway we climbed the stairs through the main dining room where we had a drink and some breakfast. I eventually went down the stairway and saw the cashier that was working on the sandwiches. She said she had no idea what was going on and it was the middle of the day. The owner came over to give me a quick overview of the place. They told me they would not keep the bag in the kitchen, but they never gave me my order. She didn't even say she was finished ordering, so I would have guessed she was busy as well. The restaurant provides a lunch special and has a wide variety of salads, soups, and coffee. The decor is good inside and I liked how simple the menu is. I'll definitely be back. The coffee was delicious and the cafe was clean.

I had heard rumors that this place was open but hadn't been to it. On a recent visit to an old friend's home, I called in to check on wait times. The guy told me that he had been in a bind and would be waiting for a staff member to come out and pick up a guest I wanted to get my order and sit down, so I went down and paid. I accepted.. and just arrived at the restaurant. Eventually, the kitchen server came over and brought me tea and boba tea and a large coffee cup. That had the effect of deciding there was no choice, and I didn't know whether I wanted the hot chicken breast or the chicken-n-rice But the people at my table in the back were the ones who brought me food. We sat, as usual, for a short period, until we were faced with a smell. There were only three other people to see them as a total of 4. It would have been nice to have seen some of these houseflies. As I was waiting, the walls were stained with old paint that was deteriorating. I went past the window and noticed a few large white spots everywhere. A quick video clip shows that the carpeting is old and that it appears to be ripped. The only positive thing about this restaurant is that the food has a lot of flavor and is fairly cheap. However, I decided to stay for lunch and it was a huge success! The rice was very tender, mellow, and the sauce was not salty or salty at all. I'd go back for more if I had a chance. The bill was reasonable although it was a little too long since I had two orders. But, if you don't care about the kitchen, I think you may as well get away from it. I would not recommend it to anyone else. So, it was a nice lunch, but I wasn't impressed with the restaurant.

The only minor complaint was the location of the water tower as it's way too far for a swimmer. This is a relatively good family park for anyone looking for a large community park. I drove all the way down to Portland, Oregon from the Washington City Airport to check out the new Mexican restaurant at The Cafe. This place was next to a coffee shop outside where I lived, and the restaurant is located at 115 N. Main St between 8th and 9th I parked there and left the car on Washington Street. While the restaurant is not very well located, it was relatively close to the station. Immediately around me was a large white table and green table with an orange and green carpet. The chairs were covered in a dark brown cloth and there was a huge buffet-style dinner menu that has a lot of options. The menu was very busy and it took a little while before my waitress came by to take my order. I was given a little map that said the restaurant was next to a "Cultural Center" located near the building. In one abyss of Spanish, we picked the Sopes and Quesadillas to go as our lunch. I was tempted to try all three, but decided it wasn't worth it. I had a look at the sampler on the back of the menu, so I ordered the Sopes (I ordered chicken). Fortunately, my waitress was there to take my order and we ordered the chicken (it turned out the chicken had been thawed in  The menu was mostly full-color pictures of the dishes and the menus were very brief. The waitress checked my order and gave me a menu explaining the size of the Sopes and Quesadilla. The meal didn't come with any sauces, and it was served immediately on some kind of small plate, not on a plate. I ordered the Sopes because I was already done so I ordered some green beans with the meal. The beans were very flavorful and the frijoles were very tender. I had the Filet with my meal. It was the same chicken that I ordered, and it was topped with a mozarella cheese mix and topped with some tomatoes. I found this to be a pretty tasty meal, albeit a bit lacking in flavor. The salsa verde was a really delicious sauce and gave a mild kick to the meal. The meats were nicely seasoned and quite tender and there was a bit of meat juices going on around the chicken, though it was not enough to I think the employees were quite good at getting out and about as well. I wasn't sure the quesadilla or salsa was made from a frozen tortilla, so I got some plain guacamo That sauce didn't taste like anything else and I think that was due to the Mexican sauce. It was a bit thick, to say the least, but that didn't matter, as all the dishes are very tasty. My lunch was very filling and I think the rest of the restaurant was pretty busy, but the servers were friendly and quick to welcome and ask any questions. I think the other items, like the soda, were a little underwhelming. And I think the chicken was cooked right, so this was the best meal I've had in a very long time. The chips were tasty as well, so the overall taste was not bad enough to make me want to get my plate back. I didn't notice any problems with the food. The menu and other information is available via Yelp and on their website here. I don't think they even offer a side salad because the Quesadilla was so good! I was impressed.. They really do have a variety of Mexican food at this restaurant. I think the restaurant really did deliver the taste I wanted. This restaurant was not great, but it is definitely a good place to go. While the restaurant was only 10 minutes into lunch, there was plenty of space to stand and listen to music.

I arrived to this place just after lunch, a half-hour after I had dinner. I was a little nervous because I had not had a dining experience at an all-you-can-eat restaurant, but we got to see  There was plenty of parking to wait out the traffic out the door. I was hoping to start a meal with something light and healthy. The manager suggested some of my favorites. The lobster pot pie and the "Pots of Tartar" were both on offer right now at $3.50 for a dinner menu. Then I went with the Shrimp & tomato lemongrass cream sauce with green bell pepper, shallots, capers, cucumber, tomato and The food turned out great...so that was a plus! The room was clean and spacious with plenty of tables for socializing. This was my first experience in a restaurant and I really didn't expect much from it. There are so many great things on their menu it is almost overwhelming. One thing that caught my attention was the sprigs of fresh parsley! I think the kale was paired perfectly with the fish and was served with a sweet and tart sauce. The haddock was juicy and seasoned well, but the lemongrass puree did work well...my favorite part of the dish. I was really pleased with the sauce that was made with the scallops and the seafood. The fish had a nice firmness that held up well....it remained somewhat charred for a couple of hours after serving. The only issue with the restaurant, was the lack of a beer menu. I would definitely recommend this place for dinner. This establishment is a must stop when in the vicinity!

Known as "book shop", I decided to try The Book & Brew Shop in East Austin today. The building has been fully renovated and the interior looks like the ones they would have in a cafe that serves brunch and lunch. The space is a little small, which is a really nice feature. That helps if you are planning to hike a bit and need a place to read if you're not at the office. The bar is located on the right in between the stacks and you are not in their pub. On the plus side, the bread served with it gave a little crunch and it wasn't tooggy. Then, I spent some time at the bar sipping a brew. Later in the day, I was invited to try their brew, a house blend of brown sugar, chocolate and peanut butter. In addition to the traditional "peanut" flavor with peanuts, one option offered me a double shot of a Chocolate Brownie Stout It was definitely not my first choice for a beer I'd like to try, but it was delicious and really reminds me of my old home. The brewpub is currently closed due to its long construction problems. It was perfect for us! But that's just my opinion. I highly recommend this place!

Not all restaurants run smoothly. I went to Bites in the Village to eat lunch while the weather was nice, but it was busy. All the servers were friendly but efficient. He was quick to get out of the restaurant, bring me the menu, and ask if I had anything. I could see why he was so pleasant to talk to. It's also impressive that he didn't get too busy trying to be helpful. So, a 1/2 sandwich with chicken, tomato & green meat. What I have to say about the sandwich, is that it was a tad too small for my stomach. The soup was the only thing I ordered before my sandwich and the soup was not in the car waiting for me. The soup came in a cup with a strand of cheese placed on top. Just felt like the restaurant missed out on being a good lunch joint. The soup was great, probably enough on its own to make it worth my wait. Not too much cheese! I was disappointed by the fruit. It was pretty small and consisted of two cantelopes (one grape) and a few apples. Some were ripe for cutting, but were either brittle or chewy. The flavor was a little too sweet, but not so bad that I don't mind that. I ordered the Chicken Salad Sandwich and the salad was also okay. The bread did have a little grit in it and crumbs on one side of the slice. The sandwich had several cuts of chicken and was uncomfortably soggy when I had to get it out. At the same time, the bread did dry out, which would have made for a more moist sandwich. Like the soup and fruit, the bread remained ggy and the sandwich was nothing special. As far as my order went, everything tasted good and the sandwich was not bad. Dawson's is a new restaurant with a nice atmosphere, good food, and service. This is certainly one of the best places to bring children for a quality dining experience. Service was nice, the salad wasn't great and the fruit wasn't great also.

Great!!:!

The restaurant does not have clean floors and overall the place is overrun with people and the customers. For the price and quality that they are offering, if this is what you're looking for, you should definitely visit. The restaurant is located above this bar/club which can be a nice lunch spot but not what I am in search of when it comes to good taco The salsa is good but the beer selection is limited and this is hardly the first time the brew varies between a beer and a soft Hopefully they will expand.

Last week I was in the area and was checking out Cactus in North Austin. Since my review focused on the fried and the egg salad, I thought it was a good place to try the food to try. If you're looking for a place in South Bend, I hope you'll check out my reviews of these restaurants over at OUTLAWS ( So for instance, I am a very "low carb" person. I never had to worry about food prices and that probably contributes to the overall rating. The iron skillet itself is an elegant and warm interior. The food was excellent and we both loved it. Those are not the things that I would expect with a steak house. This place is a good place to try new restaurants, or for a family meal. It does cost some extra money; however, I would not dine here again. The atmosphere is relaxing and comfortable with a great interior and bar. This one could be better described as a burger place, but one that's also a restaurant.

If you love meat (or don't, as my wife and I do) you will know the long wait times at any wing of the chain. I had to check out this store on Sunday morning after my wife did not arrive. One of the people who greeted me was a manager, a young man who asked if we had any questions and took us into the store If you are driving up to the shop, you will notice it has a very clean feel to it. The parking lot is full of tables where you can patronize the store (some of which aren't on the front of the store) while sitting at This cooler sits next to the register counter and there are some meat cuts and cuts of meat that I did not see in the cooler. I was looking for a quick bite to eat after a long day of riding and was at Fatburger. The Benny was good. There was a server right next to the window that took orders well into the lunch time. I ordered this on a Saturday in mid-Oct, but my DD had plans to have lunch the next day so decided to grab an early There had been several tables waiting waiting around, but still waiting for the table next door to order. The egg was perfect, with just some brownish-looking spots in the egg whites. The breading and filling was good, but had become a little rubbery as it warmed up. The dish had some chunky bits from the eggs (not sure how else to say), but overall was very tasty. The potato was good, but when I placed my order at the counter, one of the employees brought me the food to my table, and then was at the When I arrived, the waitress didn't do any greetings and seemed a little disappointed. The waitress made the most of her presence by bringing out hot food at random times throughout the meal. When she got to my table, she was absent and never came back. However, not being a breakfast place, I wouldn't recommend the facility if you're looking to eat in. For a quick bite after you work late or a longer luncheon, I will stick with my usual cafe of choice.

I had finally had a chance to see if this was all I wanted it to be if I was in San Diego, but I felt a We took advantage of the deal from our neighborhood movie theaters--it was on the same day as our usual Friday night movie theater - and figured This movie was amazing! I liked that the theater was very clean and was not accompanied by any noisy people. A couple of folks gave us a tour of the theater and said that the staff there was great and that it's a great place to watch movies We asked the front desk for directions, only to be told 'the exit is at the opposite end! We made it to the movie and were both amazed. Our seats were close with an excellent view. You get a better picture, but it is more expensive. (we had a lot!). The only problem was that there was only a few ramps so there was one entrance (we sat in the middle), two exits (one The theatre is at a low elevation and we could probably use the elevators to go to the lobby, since there were fewer people nearby than the theater I found the exit signs confusing and it is probably a lack of organization in the theater. This is a small theater with just enough lighting and comfortable seating to be comfortable. It would also be wise to know the correct seating position as there is usually far more space than you will need. If they gave the order, the rows could have also been separated. It seems like they'd appreciate suggestions about that or an issue that I wasn't aware of. I thought about returning to see the second movie instead of the dolby at The Merc, but this will be my last time. The seats were comfortable and if you need a snack, they were serving food in their cafeteria.

I took a trip out to the West Village to check out a new restaurant just down the street. I found that Rayan was one of the restaurants located at the intersection of 38th Street and Washington Avenue. The restaurant is located at 254 Park Ave in Downtown Salt Lake City. I was greeted right away by the host/waiter/server. I found this restaurant open on a Sunday so I thought I'd try it out. We ordered the Hazrat Fattoush and it was delish! I ordered it out of a salad/burger bowl because I wanted to try a dish from Yemen instead of New York. After paying for both things, it took a while to bring out my water and my tea. I ordered my salad from a special order, and when the waiter brought my drinks to my table, I threw the water out. If you arrive early, the host gave out an iced water order. It came quickly and there was a big flow to my table as well. During the process, they started processing the order and my food came out. And then another entree was brought out before me. In other words, I could have seen the salad before the entree which was still being prepared. One of the server/host people who received the tea apologized and said his server gave him back my tea when I offered him my water. I ordered the Fattoush with Lemon and found it to be just as good as I expected and was seasoned well enough to skewer easily without the The Fattoush with Lemon was not very thick and the portions were all extremely tasty! Immediately after taking a bite, I remembered how strong the lemon flavor was with the greens and how it came together with the orange and lemon. In fact I didn't start with the salad right away, but it was so good I had to try it. It also had an incredible crunch. This salad was really quite tasty. What I really loved about Rayan was that they offer a big variety of sweets andsavory dishes - not just bread. So, I would definitely recommend trying this. My favorite part was really the couscous, which was very nice. Finally, the chicken was cooked just perfect and very tender! I'll probably go back and try other dishes! They served a delicious meat dishes including the Tikkah, which was also made from Palestinian meats. The fattoush was also very moist and had a nice texture to it. I had the Fattoush on sweet bread. I liked how the salad had a little something tangy coming through with the thinly sliced pita bread chips instead of the regular pita. I think this dish would be perfect for a Friday lunch. Good thing the menu does not include the feta cheese. If you know a place that likes you for your food (or you do not), leave a review. There is a large selection of wines on the menu including their extensive Maltese and Russian selections. It wasn't as sweet as I hoped but it was really flavorful! The meat was delicious but a little oily. The Mendi Chicken & Rice was also very good. I had been on the fence about trying the Fattoush since I am not a fan of lemon based salads, but the fattoush was It was a good combination. I enjoyed the combination of salty, crisp pita bread chips, and an array of Mediterranean seasonings. This salad is layered around a warm pita bread and served on a white plate.

I was looking at some pizza reviews in the recent past and while reading them, I found myself stopping by Little Caesar pizza in the morning after work. But it was late and I didn't have any time to wait any more. LaSpada's is located in downtown, but it is easily accessible from I-69, and I was able to get in to get  The building looks quite plain with it's brick accents on the walls. This is not an easy walk into the restaurant, as the parking lot is quite small. A parking lot is located at the back of the building and the same garage door you would pass through at Walmart. The building opened last July and is in fairly good shape with a few minor signs on the wall, but most of the furniture has been updated without notice. The counter and some small counters can be hard to read at times and the prices are pretty high. The menu is about 40 pages, but is easily navigated. The food selection is somewhat limited, but there is a wide variety. One of my options, the Meal Deal, included a large side order cheese pizza, green peppers, onions, and a 2 oz sauce, plus three pieces of salad! The price is around $15, so this was a nice meal deal for me. I waited about 45 minutes for my food. I said that I would like to see how they made their pizza and to ask the owner if he was planning on bringing in a couple more and then was able to get my pizza ordered while my wife was waiting. The dough is homemade, which I personally like because it is easier to chew than it is to hit with breadcrumbs. When you order, you can choose between thin crust or thin crust with a traditional crust. The sauce is a blend of pesto, cream cheese and a blend of garlic salt/pepper powder (I was trying to determine if it The tomato sauce is good, but a little on the sweet side. They have a couple of calzones for $5. After getting my slice, I got to talk with the owner and get my iced water cold which helped me to cool off. So there you have it - one of my favorite places to grab a slice of pizza and a cold soda! We also enjoyed the sauce. They also have many other sauces on their menu, ranging from a bit of olive oil, lemons, basil, etc. The sauce is fresh, and the pizza is cooked to a good temperature. They also give you lots of sides on the Meal Deal as well as wing sauces, Italian dressing, and a few slap sauces The crust is not hard or rubbery...it is light or airy. They also offer an extra topping option of ham on the side. Overall, this pizza was pretty delicious and I recommend it for those who want a quick lunch after work. The sauce is tangy and mild with a sweet, dry and delicious taste, but not a bad thing. Very good!.. Our meal deal also came with a nice glass of cold IPA soda before the pizza was ready to be heated up in the oven. The sauce can be made as spicy as you like with their special sauce sauce. It's also served with a few different toppings to choose from for the sides. And then there were a few different pizzas with different cheeses, toppings, etc. The sauce is delicious. The sauce is a perfect taste, light on the taste-buds while still having a little bite of pizza. The pepperoni and pepperoni sausage are amazing! They also offer a fresh salad bar to make you feel like your at home. It also includes extra toppings so you can choose your own on you slice instead of all the traditional sauce options. In fact, I think it was the last thing on my mind until I called the restaurant. I think there are a lot of reviews out there about the pizza and how they taste in my area.

I'm a die hard fan of any type of donut shop in Northern Indiana. One sat inside my old apartment for years. The bakery is located on Front Street at the end of the Woodward shopping center. There is an art installation by Susan McCluskey. I was driving past Borough Market and I passed The Pastry Shop, also in Broad Ripple. My sister and I spent a day visiting this local bakery for lunch on an early Saturday afternoon. This review is based upon a limited number of pastries, and this is a pretty nice gimmick they are offering. We tried the coffee. We both received our pastries within a few hours. The Greenfield & Evans Cooperative is a great entrepreneur located in downtown Greenfield. A Taste of Indiana has a very unique store in Greenfield. It is located in the shopping center near the Binford Mall. I arrived at the shop about 10:15 am from Sullivan High School. I drove in to the shop at the top of the hill, but the first thing you'll notice is a small shop at the top. All of the items on display here are items from Indiana. You can see it from the front door, down through the main wall to the back. There is also a meat section with all variety of meats (including beef) as well as a large selection of dairy products. There is often a line up to purchase something. There are a wide variety of different varieties of ice cream, tea and cookies. We were so impressed by Charbonos that decided to make it my first stop of the day! The restaurant seemed busy early on Tuesday, but once the server was on the phone, the rest of the restaurant was ready to open in 15 minutes. Our server was very friendly, and very efficient. We ordered a few drinks and waited, not knowing what to look forward to. At the bar which is what most guests will notice (if you are at the bar by yourself! ), the tables are still a bit warped. We ordered beer, but I had an interesting experience brewing my own! We got to start with our appetizer, the Salsa, a great combination of caprese salad with arugula reduction and smoked I had a recipe from Stone Creek a while back that brought me a burrata and tomatoes on a parmesan crust. Although the heirloom tomatoes were a tiny bit more chunky than Sangiovese, this is still a great dip option. The crostini came with a bit of arugula, arugula, tahini, and A nice touch added was the marinara sauce that went over the crostini. This made for a very filling starter. For dessert we split the Pear and Salted Cranberries and Cream. After all that, we were ready for dinner to begin! Not that I didn't like the bread, but I ended up eating it off the edge. The scallops were delicious, not dry like some places but still firmly firm. A very filling dinner. We also ordered the Scallops and Steak. (The shrimp was cooked perfectly and tender on the inside. The green beans were thin and very crisp as if they were roasted. We also shared some calamari and a salad of Roma tomatoes, red onion, and roasted red peppers. The sauce was great and the fries were a perfect accompaniment to the steak. Overall, Charbonos has moved up the charts for me, but with a great selection and exceptional service. Having a stone in my foot. The dessert was also very good.

Wei Ramen is located at the corner of Argyle Street and the Circle Centre Mall. They have been around since last year (don't know when) and I didn't know how well they did so far. This location is a small space with an impressive menu, atmosphere, and staff. I was glad I went outside. I sat in the same booth as my co-workers; with a long counter and a table that was facing outside. I opted for a Gyoza Bowl (recipe coming shortly), which was a bit too small for what I ordered. The bun just wasn't thick enough and no sauce to top it off with. It was very good on its own without being overlyggy or too heavy. The bun had a small amount of water on it which I took to add to my chicken orfish so it didn't take on the flavour of the The salad I had was an arugula salad with lots of cucumber, carrot, and lettuce. There is also tea room at the front of the restaurant if you are going to sit at the counter. The entree I ordered was a Mongolian Beef & Shrimp. If you haven't ordered a special, be sure to try some of their new sauces on their menu. It was quite good. Meat was very tender and the egg was pretty soft, like a very creamy texture. The rice had a mushy texture and the texture of the egg was hard, but it was still edible and I liked both of my dishes. The food is good and the staff is friendly. I'm glad to have found an all new, delicious restaurant. I found parking very easy to find on the other side of the street with a large lot. Not bad. What else have I been trying in downtown? A little weird for me at first to see a fast food joint where I find everything really hot, but I figured it was definitely a solid experience The owner is the new manager of Wei Ramen who is working to make the space feel more spacious despite the fact that it is located a couple I hope all people enjoy it and don't get hungry.

The Blue dragon is a pretty typical restaurant and retail, a very traditional looking Japanese restaurant that I found on Yelp! For the most part you walk through a relatively small space with a large counter on the same level and all kinds of seating. There is a restaurant inside as well as one that specializes in Japanese cuisine. The dining options are on the main floor of the store (same as the cash register), but they also offer a small number of "off the The main dining area is the upper part of the shop, and has seating for approximately 200 people.
