Before I went in to place my order, I had my Yelp discount and they were giving me 10% off when they opened in November. If you wait more than five minutes, the cashier will hand you over to another person. I noted my name on the menu as my order was being prepared, which was an added plus. Then I was escorted to my spot. While I was there, I waited for my food to be prepared. Just outside the cooler, a small counter serves most of the food ordered. They make the food fresh and you can pick up your order to take home. Just be careful and be friendly to those around you while you're there. The interior of One World Market doesn't take a lot of effort to maintain or clean, making it one of the more comfortable restaurants in the Valley. I was sat in a lovely atmosphere with some great vibe and a fun atmosphere overall. I was a bit suspicious of the soup for a Japanese lunch due to its nastier texture. The sushi sat on some rice which was wrapped in a rice paper and topped with seaweed. The dragon came face down and swung like a bull in a cage. A giant crab tail with the top strewn with avocado and rice, and a sprinkling of tuna on top. There was also an entree that included a piece of salmon fillet and salmon sashimi, also not included on the lunch menu. A huge thank you to Yelp for their service and assistance. The rolls were hot and fresh and could only be ordered by the time my lunch was finished, since the only lunch menu item on the menu I received was the There is so much more to the menu, but I cannot remember what I had while I was there. One of the things that made me go oh-so-ha is that this was the first time I had tried eating in-house and I You can view my review of the dragon roll by clicking here. They also bring out a nice selection of teas/hot water (with the usual drink selection), drinks, and specialty sauces to help everyone. Probably the best of the lot! I ordered a bowl of Miso soup to match and even had a taste of the soup. If you want to make a special request or use their online reservations tool, they are extremely helpful. I had the opportunity to try the Tuna tartar which was VERY delicious, and the Miso soup which came with a piece of meatball. I'd say it was much closer to a "monster roll" as there were a few fillets within the roll. I thought it was great because it was one of the best lunches I have had in a long time! For my entree, I went with the "Eel Roll" which came with an egg egg roll, azui tofu, and This is a very unique place to dine. My dinner was also amazing with some great veal dish. And a couple of fresh limes...yes they did. For my entree, I wanted to try their Pan Seared Tuna Roll. So you get the impression on the quality of the ingredients, the presentation, and the creativity behind the presentation, and the ingredients are certainly not going to last  To top it off, you can order extra salad or any kind of side dish on request. While it was the most wonderful experience of my restaurant visit, despite some dissatisfaction with the quality, I am glad I went to a But the overall experience was very good and all of the menu items that I had were mouth watering. You know, just looking at these photos, I didn't even appreciate it, but I'm glad I did! With all my food, I had a chance to sit with the food processor and the cashiers. This sushi is so unique that I would definitely visit again! The entire roll was really amazing and was full of flavor, and very light so it went well with my lunch. This was just a little too much on my palette for me, but then again, it was much more than the average restaurant would need! The whole thing was fantastic and one that I would definitely eat again! The sauce was tangy and flavorful.

We visited the Detroit Furniture and Home Furnishings Museum on Lake Michigan on Saturday, 3/1/22. Our first visit was on Tuesday, October 2, 2019 in Indianapolis. We exited the restaurant on Michigan and drive to the building. This way you should see an address on the left and access in through a side entranceway. This building is huge and well worth it. This is two floors, not the first. The first floor is open to the general public (Sep 2019). The second floor offers a lot of different goods, including old furniture, furniture fittings (both furniture and fixtures), and some decorative items for home or office It is a huge warehouse with over 3,000 items. There are a few small corridors throughout that work together. Instead, just go through the shops in either direction so you can find the one that interest you. The second floor is much more organized with furniture and fixtures for the home and garden. Luckily, there are quite a few vendors selling antiques and items for a reasonable price. They seem to have been here for months before some other antique stores were closed. The "Little Shop of Treasures" was particularly cute. The second floor has a very eclectic collection of furniture and accessories. There are lots of antique glass doors, cabinets, and other miscellaneous items as well. Some were very bright, but you could see that there were a few of these pieces that were pretty old (not too old and not very new) and There was a very good, modern bathroom. The second floor also has some more classic antique furniture from the day when the warehouse became famous. However, the doors to the second floor still open. I would definitely recommend checking this place out. It is really, really worth a visit and I would suggest that you schedule a visit at least two weeks in advance.

We called in to work on Wednesday and were all excited that we were getting a 20% discount that night and not having to pay a ton for lunch The price was great, and theambiance was nice. We had the choice of dining inside or outside on the patio. We dined in Hyde Park from 9:30 to dinner to take advantage of the promotion while still enjoying the excellent food. We were presented by the server and suggested that we start with the "cheap" meal package. We were pleasantly surprised that the portions were large and the portion sizes were good for this pricepoint. With lunch comes appetizers. The starter was just as good as the filet mignon, but the capers brought more flavor to it to balance out one of these two courses. After that was all done, our waiter came out and took a second look at the menu. Now to the meat. Immediately, he brought out three amuse bouches (fish à dolce) just for us. Yes, we all wanted that. Our tummies loved them, however we all thought the fish was too salty, and they really weren't. The bar-side portion of the entree was great until a bite came out of the patty which had a lot of meat. It was a good matchup with the bbq / Mediterranean offerings at the restaurant. A couple of salads were ordered. Just like our first course, our pizza came out excellent. Just to add note: the fish flavor at the tail end was also a bit too salty for me; otherwise, it was good and the flavor of Regardless we still enjoyed the ambiance and the staff was very helpful, which I think is something more likely to happen in the future. It was a meal well worth your money. What a great experience - definitely coming back here again but if it's on their buffet menu...that's a winner! The staff had been patiently serving us and extending our time to give us a good experience, but we had to make a decision. When our waiter reached out to us and told us that we were free to pick up and deliver, we were a bit surprised. So, I ate all of it. Best of the best! We enjoyed our meals with our friends and enjoyed our conversation about the food. We all felt that the waiter didn't take the time to talk with our group on this one...we wanted to be able to talk about the On to the main course. It's still a 5 star restaurant, but doesn't have the same level of service as most of the other Chicago restaurants. My wife actually was more than happy with the soup. I hope this review does not inspire you to avoid Hyde Park. The last course of the evening is the prawn linguine. The atmosphere was also great as it had beautiful ceilings and beautiful ceiling fans...it just pushed you towards the restaurant floor (not necessarily a bad thing They also had "Champion Fish" which I actually thought had the good flavor of a fish from a lobster bisque. We would not suggest a more expensive dinner at Hyde Park! I really enjoyed it. The final course of the evening was a seafood plate, which was very good. Good to know! Thank you. So I think the server has a bit more control over the presentation of her entrees and our time.

When I came in to McNamara's floral shop in St. Charles this past week, I was pleasantly surprised that they had the option to But this week McNamara acquired one of their smaller stores in the Southport neighborhood of Toronto. I was able to enjoy a fine dinner and three wineries at Papa's before our wedding. They all commented on theambiance and the food! Neither of us enjoyed the cocktails, but that was a good thing. We had a romantic evening summing up our experience after checking in. We ordered a couple of starters! This entailed the Grilled Mozzarella Sandwich and our new favorite, the Fresh Mozzarella Patties. The egg and the breadcrumbs combined to create a very unique and exotic texture. The Italian Turkey (I tried the Italian Turkey) was served with parmesan-pizza, prosciutto, carrots, and cheese. In a delicious citrus marinade, they were both very good. Those came in my opinion to be a great option to eat right away as they are fairly quick to prepare. We ordered different pasta selections for the main course. The whitefish dish was outstanding. This is a rich flavored sauce with whitefish and nuts. My husband ordered the prawn and mushroom tempura and was very pleased with both the texture and taste. The whitefish also came with marinated diced tomatoes, parmesan, capers, and a sauce based on the original Italian cocktail I ordered The ladies tried the shrimp linguine chowder with vegetables, basil and capers. She loved the crusted shrimp. Very crisp and just the right amount of skin left on the chicken. It was fantastic. Another quick stop here was enough to fill my appetite for the remainder of the evening. This served with a salad and a garlic sauce was very good too. Our other entree, the Crabcakes with shrimp and a creamy sauce was made with a light lemon, honey, and cream sauce and  We came home with lots of chocolate with whipped cream and fresh berries! If you're looking for a great restaurant with friendly servers, come early. We tried a couple of other dishes but didn't fall in love with any of them until we asked one of the waitresses why. The restaurant is very well kept and clean, and the staff is pleasant and helpful. Loved going to Mama's as well. The garden is a large area for people to relax. Despite the slightly overrated decor, this place was so charming and well maintained that it was a perfect stop before or after our family dinner at my house

Good news!..This is the very first review I've made from the Artesian Well. It's free. This park has a small stone shelter to sit by. A nice park with a nice shaded area to sit and enjoy the water and a path for people to browse the vendors if they wish. The trail begins in a small open space near an attractive bridge with a raised boardwalk where wheelchairs can cross. The path passes through several smaller trees that are in a cluster around the creek. The path continues on through the woods then leaves the woods and ends at a small shelter (with a few tables) where you can park. During the next couple of weeks, you can expect the change to be visible as Chateau Thomas' new location begins to open. But once the changes were complete, I had to go back another two doors to get inside. Over at the storefront, I had the pleasure of shopping the old-fashioned way, checking out some of the old cajun-style dishes and getting  But despite the fact that I was hungry in there and I was in the middle of my order in the gift shop, I wasn't surprised. They also were saying that they might try to have me revert to their current pricing. he just said that the company won't be getting any more wines. I bought three reds and two whites from a variety of flavors including several different styles of roses and pears and peaches. So, if you've visited Chateau Thomas, I think next time you are in the area, try a bottle! You can find it on their website. I bet that even those of you who aren't local to Chateau Thomas, they wouldn't mind trying it out. I really was hoping that they would have some left in the barrel and not be discontinued. Located down the road from The W Hotel, Red Bee Cafe is a casual, neighborhood food establishment in the Las Vegas area. This low-income family owned business has a somewhat disorganized menu, which includes the basics. I had the red jerk chicken with white rice on white rice and red plantains with rice and beans. The onion rings were sliced, but they were really good because it was a bit tougher to cut because of it's shape. The chicken arrived ready to be served before we knew when it was ready. The flavours were very distinct, with a hint of Caribbean flavor that is not overpowering. Although it's definitely Jamaican food, the beans were too hot for me. The chicken was extremely tender and meaty. The beans, while a little watery, had a smoky and sweet flavor. It all seemed to taste just fine. They went well with my chicken, which I will be ordering again. The service here is fast at this location, but I think it's more of an off-site restaurant and it may get busy during peak hours. This place was a good place to stop on my last long day in NYC. It wasn't too difficult to find, just as I was on the way. I stayed after waiting for the last couple minutes before going up the backstreets, and found the front door open. A solid starter for mealtime or for a quick lunch with friends. I always try my best to go for familiar and familiar if I can. I just love when a food truck or restaurant makes me feel special. The very first restaurant to do that was Russian-American restaurant EatingRussia. The restaurant was fairly new, opening in late November. I had heard the kitchen was very busy already, but I had been waiting the last one to come out of the store. I took the time to look into their menu. I was pleasantly surprised by Gregory's. And after all, they just opened a couple of weeks ago! One of my favorite dishes was the gushing buttery Russian olive oil with sour cream. The beer was very smooth and refreshing, with a sweet and tart flavor that I enjoyed. The beer made the perfect pairing with the light pastries. I ordered the pork fillet and onion sauce, which was light and crispy on the outside, but had great flavor inside. They were topped with butter, which was great because it added a nice rich, buttery texture. It was mildly moist, so the main flavor was the filling. The food came out completely cooked, which wasn't too bad since the meat did feel extremely moist. The meat had tons of flavor while the pork was very tender and tender. The overall presentation was very well done with the flavors clearly showing. For entrees, I ordered the goulash. Originally I wasn't sure what to expect. At Gregory's, every single flavor of beef was perfectly balanced and had a nice texture. From start to finish, I couldn't take my eyes of the deliciousness. When I bite into a bite, it was utterly delicious! I got my second piece of beef. My entree of Vegetarian Vegetarian Skulls and carrots (the one I had been ozing past) arrived. I immediately tried to bite through a piece of the vegetables which was cooked a bit too fast and I almost had a small pan burn at the end And, as with the vegetable plates, the crust on the veggies, onion, mushrooms, and tomatoes was flavorful. I had to try the cake, too! We had our own large group, so it was not a lot of work. Just a few weeks ago I visited a restaurant called "Boryati" in Los Angeles that was more Russian than it was American. Although I did have to ask for fresh fruit juice to go with my entree, the sides and salads were delicious to the point of being excellent! I'm certain the Russians ate it too! After all the desserts, I'll be returning for more Russian fare in the future. There are plenty of options available to choose from, so there's really something for everyone! When I finished my entrees, a nice dessert was waiting. For a meal that was relatively inexpensive, it was certainly worth the money to pay less than five dollars. The entire place was completely clean and smelled of fresh herbs. The vegetables were cooked through and the flavors in the sauce were perfect. The meal was definitely something exceptional. They gave me the last slice of pizza you ordered a couple minutes before your food was served.

The NCAA Historic Campus Center is a beautiful outdoor space spanning one level of State Hall and one level of Eiteljorg building. The HoC is located at 8431 Brown Street (MLS# 68976) and they opened on April 12, 2008. There is parking on the grounds for a short amount of time, but is not permitted in my opinion. It is located at 513 Central Main Street, White River, SD 47252 and is open daily 1pm-3pm. The HoC is located on the North State Street Exhibit Building. First floor is about 80 feet long and features the NCAA and other sporting programs. Although in the first level, you will find a display displaying all the sports, each includes a brief biographical statement, photo and written history. The first floor features a large display of some notable sports athletes (which depicts athletes in their prime in football's old "reverse " formation ( The Flying Wedge is an embroidered wing, featuring a football player trying to defy his opponents. An image of the wedge of a player laying in a row is also featured and the phrase, "The Wedge is Made of Solid You then walk through three floors, including a main Hall of Champions and a second main Hall with a theater show in one location. Some of the more commonly chosen sports are wrestling, diving, and track & field. This is a bit overwhelming and the exhibits are very lengthy with some movies. The show was short but entertaining. This section is where kids can participate in the real stuff. However, I found it difficult to get the hang of the equipment and to interact on certain parts of the equipment. When the floor gets warm, the "ghost figures" are gone. As a result, the interactive section was quite interesting. This level is a little off the beaten path, so don't expect too much in the way of training. There are also multiple exhibits focusing on NCAA sports, from the sphere of influence and sphere of influence to the NCAA's role in developing and The HoC focuses on the physical and emotional aspects of sport and there are many opportunities, not least because of the price. A short walking trail runs between the two buildings. There are many great activities to see during your stay in White River.
