I made the pie by combining limes with cream cheese, then topped with a layer of graham cracker crust. It had a very smooth and sweet crust, with plenty of sauce for sauce dipping and an ice cream filling that was so rich it almost taste The key lime pie was too sweet for my taste. It was a really good lunch. I got a smile and a nice smile, which was very appreciated, not a loud laugh! We had some discussion about what lunch items we wanted to try. At lunch, it was a busy spot with 2 tables occupied. I could have used some more variety when I had ordered the full size salad for lunch. The salad arrived, I picked it up and had to check before the server could serve my lunch - I didn't know the size. The lunch price was $7. I thought the lunch size salad was really good, but it just wasn't worth that much. I was pretty pleased after the service was good. It was a good meal for a reasonable price, but was not as good as many places I've been to for lunch.

Today, on the way from the airport a group of girlfriends, sister, and I ventured toward The Cafe on the 3rd floor of Circle The food was outstanding. The service was excellent, the portions were generous and I really enjoyed the steak. The restaurant felt very modern (I was really excited to say the least about how fresh food was, especially considering a few other nearby restaurants were less comfortable). We were seated close enough for me to sit at the bar so I opted to order from the outside bar area because it was the smallest part of It was quiet, and they put great attention into serving us. I wasn't sure that this would be a popular restaurant in this area but I was very happy we chose this restaurant based on that. In the end I gave this restaurant a three and left. My waiter asked about my drink order and then suggested a selection from the menu, including a drink. This bread course provided a great selection of options to start and end the meal with a couple of the more popular selections. One of the main entrees that we had was the roasted pulled pork and egg sandwich. I think this dish is on the hot side because it has a nice spicy kick to it. The gumbo was fantastic. I served the gumbo bowl with my favorite sauce (chilaquiles?) ), onion, and sauteed celery. This could be served with the side of a rice crisper to take home. My friend ordered the Braised Salmon and Fried Salmon. Both were very good. I opted for the Prime Rib filet, medium rare. It was a pretty large plate with 3 slice of filet and 2 slices of steak. One of us ordered on request with the sauce on the side, which makes me glad we got the sauce as it made for a nice bite. When I saw this sauce, I knew I was going to want it! There was a nice smoky tomato sauce which was just right, but I found that the sauce on the plate had the right amount of heat I was very happy with the steak slices, too. This will be my second trip to this "not just another steakhouse" before moving to the East side. They also served the steakhouse sauce on the side. The wait staff was really good as well. Good food, but I really enjoyed the desserts. For me the flavor was a little salty, but I didn't find it to be as bad as I thought it would be. We could have ordered more courses and it would not have been nearly as filling. We finished with a nice bottle of wine (after tasting) and finished with desserts and coffee. I was a little disappointed by the short stack of fries they offered on the table with my steak. The chicken was actually good, fresh and seasoned very well, which trumps anything I can put out myself. I would definately go back. (Before I could get the cheese he told me it was cheese roux topped with blue cheese and cranberry sauce.) The menu is very extensive (as expected) and the servers were always friendly. We were able to stop in early on a weekday at lunch to try the "Boneless Chicken" which was really good - a I think any filet is a hit with any party, though. There are several specials on weekdays (everything is half off on weekends and on Tuesdays/Thursdays) and you can take We had a nice meal and enjoyed chatting with the staff in the dining room. I would come back here for some more food. We had a fantastic experience at Gaps with George Reese and had a lot of fun. The menu has something new for the menu. If you are in Indy and it's open, you should check it out. It is possible that the food was too salty so you got a little bit of a smoky flavor. I would like to see more 'not just another steakhouse' options in Indianapolis.

I was in Edinburgh on Tuesday to check out the Dunedin Brewing Company at the intersection of Kentucky Avenue and Morris Street. You can hear them on one of the speakers next to each of the brew stations. This isn't a super long tour to get to but it still made me want to take a moment to let everyone know that it's The beer selection was good, most items were fairly new but some were familiar and not too well known. They have a big bar area with high ceilings, two small tables where you can sit, and two outdoor seats. The bar is on the upper level and there is a outdoor patio as you make your way up the stairs. The food there is quite basic, but they have several choices on tap, but a couple of their beers don't appear to be limited editions The prices have been dropping recently, but I was hoping that would be a sign that a different location/beer selection would be out soon. Each flight contains a 5-5-1/2 ounce selection of beer. They had a lot of their own beers, but I wouldn't call them their best beers. I requested the four options. and a few craft pales. The Ice Cream Ale gave it a nice smooth flavor. The Ale was a bit dry, but this was more IPA as the flavors combined, which was nice. I also ordered the Mountain Creek Double Malt (8.5% 26 IBU) which arrived as a gift in a package with the four Ales I I thought it was just underwhelming...it was dry, dry and sweet. The last selection was their Cascade, which I liked, but I don't think I'll go back. If you are looking to grab a cheap craft beer, I'd stick to their pale ale, which a beer like this should be. I'm glad I took the opportunity. Take Tennessee Avenue through the center of town over the River, turn right, and then left. You'll find the brewery on the left.

The restaurant is located on 22nd Street and Delaware in downtown Fort Worth. My friends and I were heading on out to the North side from downtown and found this location on 22nd Street. I found the restaurant nice and clean from the inside out. We also stopped at Baron on our way from the river (or in my car). The bar area is mostly located in the back of the restaurant. The room was bright and spacious and clean. The main floor is dark wooden with modern decor. You can see from the bottom of the pictures that there are more than a few tables that were occupied, but there were still more in the dining area Some other decor included a TV that projected video of a couple of videos, a kitchen counter, etc. It was very tasty and I was full by the time I left for lunch. The beer I ordered was the Shibuya. Generally, these dishes are comprised mostly of vegetables and an assortment of fresh beans. This soup is hot and flavorful. Overall, this soup has a strong flavor that had a strong fish component to it. A very filling, delicious broth with a lot of veggies zinging. I recommend this soup especially if you love Thai soup while you're in San Francisco. I went with the monkfish roll. They were sliced thin, fried, and dipped in garlic broth. The rolls were topped with a delicious cream sauce and served a few minutes after arriving in the truck. A quick lunch after a long day of travel. I was happy to find that they also stock this special dish at the same time. On my last night out, I decided to go with the Pork Ribeye. This small piece of tenderloin is deep fried and then dipped in a crisp golden brown breading that adds just a touch And yes you can eat it raw! It was moist, tender and served with green onions with a bit of red onion for an added kick. Although it was tough, I liked it. The sauce is on the thick side with the Tonkatsu paired with the rice and soy sauce. Their bbq has a nice tang, but if you like your bbq spicy, it can turn a little strong. I also added some chicken and pork dumplings that were a little on the saltier side and were a great addition to the dish. The rice is not cooked and is tender. We ate with friends and had quite a few great conversations during our meal. The sauces were very simple, but it didn't seem to overpower the meat as much as I thought it might have, so I would definitely be I would recommend this place! I will definitely be back again soon! I think it will be a favorite addition to the bar to enhance the area for many years to come! The Tonkatsu was very good with a bit of spice in the flavor. Then we got my way to dessert. The food was excellent, definitely a new addition to the area! The burger was awesome! So, if you are looking across the street from the new 'Hotel Marriot' restaurant, it's definitely worth checking out. They also have a small kitchen on 22nd street that is a nice way to check out the food! For dessert, I had the Caramel Coconut Ice cream with toasted caramel and butter.

Pogue's Run Park (near Center St., between 2nd and 3rd Avenues) is always a favorite area of residents for There is a growing restaurant culture along the trail along with bike paths. The Pogue's Run Public Park is the largest of the Greenwood Parks in North County. The park is a tangled series of colorful paintings on the walls to the east of the path. There are now three accessible picnic areas on this stretch of park. It's easy to see why the park is an ideal spot for residents and visitors to this part of town.

This is my second time cooking at Mesh. All I can say is it is very flavorful, but it often takes a little too long to go down the way I would like. Mesh is affiliated with Culinary Institute of America. We have stayed there a few times, but we decided to try this Sunday because it was a Sunday afternoon brunch. The food was delicious, although the coffee was hot. We went on a Sunday morning at 12:12 to catch up with some friends at one of Cunningham's other restaurants, Pappas. Mesh has a private patio that is a little tight, but there is plenty of space to have lunch and dinner while you eat. The place is sized for a party of 4. We were seated quickly at the bar and had an amazing variety of food choices. I am not a huge fan of honeycomb, so I was happy without it, but the lemon curd really was an interesting flavor. They were served with a side of maple syrup, sweet and sour, and a side of hollandaise. The chicken seasoned well and came with a side of waffle flour, a side of honeycomb, and a side of ham. If you are more of a meat lover, I recommend a few pieces of fresh ground chicken instead of the thicker bone-in breasts. Some people had complained about the seasoning and the flavor of the Waffle. My wife and I shared two eggs served with a side of hollandaise, a side of blue cheese, and a side of bacon. She loved the eggs, but was not too happy with the potatoes. It has seasoned chicken, ham, and bacon, not a bad mix. It could have been a bit more thick cut, but it was delicious. We were also able to take advantage of the Clubhouse special: We had to buy the meal and purchase the Clubhouse points at Mesh. The points are valid for any meal, only from 3:00 to 7:15PM and all items are non-returnable. This was a nice find. On this occasion, we received our card with a bonus of free meals from the restaurant! I also gave that the 'Meat Lovers Plate' for an extra $10. Both things you mentioned, the bacon at the French Toast, and the biscuit and jam at the chicken & waffles were delish, so I Although their online order system seems to be fine, their website has some weird bugs and/or things that aren't listed on their website. That is a great savings.

My wife and I had lunch at La Bs de Luca in the Midtown area of San Antonio, TX. It was a Saturday, so for lunchtime, I had to pay the $15.00 entry fee. Once you have the ingredients in your bowls, they will give you a bowl to go to go with the ingredients. After almost an hour waiting, the order arrived. The food is fresh, and the meat was just the right thickness and quality. I have to have a bite of this to feel the full flavor and the taste of the mayo mixture. I ordered my next favorite item, the Ramen Bowl. It was served on a soft fried rice in a bowl. I put a small amount of the fresh ground pork (don't use the thicker kind) and added some Chinese salad leaves. I began serving it to my wife after filling it with a generous amount of the spicy iekei broth & miso (we were Most of my ingredients were very tender (about 4 minutes). There were some things I appreciated about the bowl. The egg was a perfect texture but the broth wasn't as tender as it was the seasoning. My sandwich was also pretty salty. I had to let it sit out for even a moment in order for it to taste as good as the broth. The food looked great (and you don't pay a little extra for the extra bread and meat), and I would recommend trying their sandwiches and bowls This is the first time that their food was not available to sit down and drink. However, I had an issue with my bag snagging under the counter and it was very difficult to get to the counter. I have to say I would give the ramen bowl a 5! A perfect park place to be for dinner if you need quick access for your vehicle.

My only negative experience at Moose was the noise. On the way to the restaurant, the employees were friendly, and the place looked very modern. The place was very clean, but the server really had to talk me through every menu item as they were very loudly playing the music to get my attention. I watched the music playing on the wall in the bar section. I was more worried as a bit of an impatient person. I asked the waitress who recommended me what I wanted. The server was friendly, which helped decide if I wanted to eat it. I ordered the name given to both the burger and the egg. (I know that a burger is a burger.) I was greeted warmly by a female server, that was extremely friendly and gave me a name of the Burger. The burger was a little tough to eat as well..the egg on top was much stronger than the bacon on the regular-size burger It was a very delicious burger but the bun was too salty, so I wouldn't actually go back for a second burger. However, the inside of the burger still had bacon and the egg was still on the bun, so that was fine, but if I wasn't I'm not sure the other choices are much better and I found myself ordering the sweet potato fries.  Overall, I think I was just disappointed. The food is better but it definitely has better than other diners. I do like the atmosphere outside in the parking lot and the music.

I arrived at R.N.E.S. in a mid-morning rush to meet a friend and order a few bites Although this is a new cafe, they have been serving their food for less than a year so I was concerned it was going to be a bit The menu consisted of two sandwiches to choose from: the basic burger or the burger fix! topped with fresh pineapple, barbecue sauce, ranch dressing and pickled tomatoes on a whole wheat bread. Several places to eat and shops to check out were nearby, but I decided to stay for lunch and eat aburger. The interior was cute, open, and clean with a lot of signs. The wait staff was friendly and responsive, and the bar was on point with beer, wine, and hot food. If you love food & dogs, I would highly suggest calling in and giving them a call. I hope it still gets it's own place soon!

The restaurant is located at 1131 Woodlawn Ave.Walnut Grove. If you want a great Mexican place located within a short walk from some of the best Mexican restaurants in the city, La Margarita is it. You can turn left and this restaurant is about the corner on both Virginia and Woodlawn. The main dining areas were open, so it was quickly setup and the tables were setup all the way down to the bar. There is no line in the restaurant. The restaurant is on a small sized enclosed patio that includes a covered table and chairs and no outside seating. The courtyard is a large room with a fire pit, bocce ball-playing areas, and a small fire pit. The patio was busy with patrons, but we did not have problems. We ordered the traditional bowl of pico de gallo, refried beans, Mexican rice, and a baguette if you are looking to We ordered a cup of hot salsa and a cup of pico, both came out shaped like tiny bowls with just about equal amounts of food Ours was hot. My first bowl had a little extra avocado that added to the flavor. She said it wasn't that hot though, so was probably a bit too hot for her. Also, she liked the taste of the Mexican salsa. I ordered the Pork Chopa, but I think my wife went with the Tenderloin, so I opted for the Chicken Chop The tortilla chips offered was a nice blend of hot and sour. On the plate was a whole pieces of pork cooked in the oven, seasoned with salt and pepper, with a little of all the usual fixings with a side of guacamole dressing on top and a plate of pork. I ordered mine medium rare since I was a bit grossed out. However, I wasn't sure how it fit into my mouth, but it was very tangy. The meat was medium rare, and I could still feel the fat in the meat. The beans tasted great as they had a great consistency and the taste was great. This would make a great dinner or dinner-party entree with just the right amount of meat and an abundance of salsa. The meal came out in 15-18 minutes, so we had to wait a few minutes after getting the plates and tables to finish the meal. There was a bit of hot sauce on top. The carnitos were really good, and if you are looking for a good option in Mexico City, La Margarita has a I got a good amount though, about half a liter. My apologies for not remembering more about the sides of our dishes, but we wanted refried beans. The food was delicious. On our second night we ordered burritos on the patio.

On Monday morning I headed by my own recommendation and found the "Larry's Diner" on my way to Downtown SF to try out  This is a great fast food restaurant inside the mall of downtown Dallas; it is just north of the Old Mill Street Mall. There are two dining areas, one inside the dining room, The Grill & Bar and The patio. A cool, dark and modern atmosphere that seemed to have a very "Burger" feel. I ordered the Mac Salad. The Mac was already cooked and the cheese was a good texture, but the Mac wasn't slathered in a sauce. I was also pleased to see that they included chicken breast rubbed in the sauce just before you put it on top. This made sense as it always seems to be a slightly soft ball. This was probably the first time I bought their a la carte appetizer bar (it's a really nice change from the restaurant that the regular menu has I also liked trying to add some sauce on my plate of fried pasta with the roasted cashews. A little too sweet, but also too salty (like a salad), so I liked that I could taste the pasta and cheese to know even more about The lunch portions are medium-sized burgers, but the portions of their burgers were big enough that I could eat a lot. I had been wanting to try a burger this week and hadn't had any special options at a burger place. I love all things strawberry and do not like meat. And this one was too simple with little food beyond the chicken breast and tzatziki sauce. After a couple bites, I understood exactly why. The flavors are a bit extreme, but still good. It was a very good burger that didn't have any strange twists or flavors. It was a little bit too hot but the taste was well balanced. The meat was moist and the flavors worked well together. I actually liked the color on the burger compared to some I've had. That was a nice change for me. I think the server was a pretty sweet person and the place was clean, not too busy. The burger was definitely a step up from my typical "burger for a night", but I will have to try this one again and try to get It was more than overpowering, but it was also memorable and interesting. The burger wasn't as good on its own as it were with the sweet dipping sauce (the white wine reduction wasn't particularly great, but This might be another sign to sign off on 317 Burger. We'll be back. Great flavor!, I could just about describe it in terms of texture and flavor. I love the burger because it is truly one of a kind and a great burger!

Amelia's Bistro was on the list of places I wanted to try in Montreal when I found it. I went to this store, which is one of several that are located in a neighborhood adjacent to my house, and was very impressed with the quality of their The interior is large and well-appointed with plenty of seating. A few tables were available and were pretty good. It was very relaxing to sit down at a casual dining location. A Wine Flight was available to me and my girlfriend who opted to order my cheese and meat. The wine flights are priced at $10 each and come with a selection of three wines (Arctic White, Burgundy, and Rioja). I had to add a glass of water or two wine glasses as I was trying to enjoy myself as the wine didn't taste great. The white wine sampler consisted of three varieties, ranging from an 8-10 bottle selection to paired with a variety of cheeses. Each wine is paired with a variety of meats. The meats from the board ranged between 1.5-10.5oz and 2-2oz. The meats offered in this board were well seasoned and well-groomed. I also opted for a layer of the Brie cheese. They were extremely rich, but not too melted! For the spread, I chose the Greek Jam. The meats were finely sliced and made my sandwich very good. To finish, I went with the Blackened Sea Salt and Blackened Garlic Cream. We were told by the server from the wine flight that we could make various choices, such as the traditional charcuterie board, paired with a The decor was nice, and the ambiance was well-suited for a wine bar. I would have liked the wine to be a slightly higher alcohol content. I'd certainly check it out! Can you guys give us any more details on their wine flight and the charcuterie?

If you've ventured to the strip or the hills on your GPS, I'd recommend checking it out. Two friends and I went to I-Mart to celebrate the holidays. But with a little extra effort we got to our table and got seated. Our reservation was for lunch, which started around 11:30am. The interior was not well lit. While we waited, our waiter came around our table and introduced himself as "Mr. B." He brought out some asian tapas I ordered the Pork Strips (3); a combo of pulled pork and chips. We used the side of chips and it was enough to share on a plate; my sister and wife both finished it off, as did we... (and She even mentioned after the meal that she had to eat the whole thing! It was a nice change from the usual "scrambled eggs and cream" food we try these days. The chicken on my bun was tender, had no sauce, and included a side of potato chips. At first it came out a bit of a wee bit dry, but they were well seasoned and they were just enough crunch and a Just a little bit salty, but that was not an issue, with a few fresh herbs that added a lot to the flavor that was good Their menu includes some great burgers which did not go over well with me! The Sliders were thin and only a little squishy which I admired. They were so so soggy that I had to re-dunk. I ordered the "Kool Aid" (which was a medley of beer and wine) with side of chips. There was plenty of wine on the menu, notably a selection of Irish beers and a very nice pitcher of red. I would return for dinner and maybe the drinks as well. I'd probably return later. I would probably recommend parking away.

I was just passing through the city and decided to have Chinese while I was in San Diego. As a regular customer I can't get enough of the chicken, fish, and salad. The restaurant is right outside of the Palazzo. If you are looking for lunch, this is a well deserved choice. When I got my food fried, the kitchen was pretty empty, but I couldn't seem to stand there waiting for them to serve me. I will keep looking to see what happens if my experience there has improved. If you have a waiter on speed dial, do your homework about who is your waiter, how much your food is and how long you wait to However, I may visit again before I leave. Don't give up on your experience, but don't expect top dollar on the table.

I recently came across a Greek restaurant called Myrtle Hill in New England. It was a glimmer of hope, as I had heard about the same restaurant on the Boston Pizza Group's website for a while. The place is near the corner of North and South St-Anonymous in the area of I-70 and I-64. This little establishment is quite small - not like even a big restaurant. I think that is because a lot of the restaurants you pass by don't want me to be there. Here you see a small sign stating, "We are here for all your Greek cooking". It was full at 3:25pm. There is also an open kitchen that is very small and bright. The waiter took a few minutes before taking my order and did a nice job of getting my order. All the seats are occupied by a kitchen that is only one table away from the kitchen. The cashier, a guy with a big stick in his hand, went to the back, took his order, and then got back to helping customers I got my order to the cashier outside and he immediately started making his food. We could almost hear him coming through the door and I'm pretty sure he'd be rushing from place to place. The cashier was super fast delivering the food and you never know when they'll get their food (I've never been a fast food person That explains why I got the fries quickly, but not all the other food. Especially when it's my turn. I ordered a "Karabaske" Shawarma sandwich and two pieces of fries. All the ingredients were fresh, including the chicken and sauce, and it was quite tasty. I had a little problem when I bit into it though. If you lift too quickly, something may get in your neck and it will stow. As far as I know though, all I had on my shirt was the chicken, so that's the only way I managed to put on a bit The chicken was flavorful, though not huge. On the side were a side of potato salad which I didn't really like. The sauce was mild (as you can see below). They had some red-color sauce on the side for the fries and there was a bit of a green pepper taste to the chicken, but I liked The whole waloo was pretty good. It's going to be a while before I come back for some of their food. I really want to try the chicken burrito.

As far as I'm concerned, the McNamara's store on Main St. in Greenwood was gone when I last went in, and For now, I have picked just a few of my favorites. It is very busy between Tuesday and Saturday (the Monday sales are already gone), so they get very busy at times. It is an old neighborhood/commercial center with a few new business building that will likely open soon. We had the opportunity to explore the store in a couple of hours, so we thought we would try to explore the rest of it. My favorite thing about this McNamara's is that they are open late, so even if you're late to work, the store is They were helpful and friendly as I browsed and I am looking forward to getting around all the things that are featured on the store display in the fall. I wish that their other stores had this attitude.

I am still on a Mexican food hiatus. It is the same business which is now open another location which has good food. It was a great day, the weather felt like a perfect day to sit outside on the patio and drink water while waiting for our meal. I have to admit that although the parking was a bitcrowded, the location was still quite convenient to get to. There are two sets of chairs that sit on the table each and they are the opposite of the booths. And there is plenty of space in between. There were three tables (including one that was facing the front door) seating 10-20. I was a bit disappointed in the texture of the tacos but overall I liked it. I ordered the chicken taquitos with rice, pico de gallo, and sour cream. The food was extremely hot and it was difficult to order from the side, but eventually got an excellent meal without complaints. It came with guacamole and guacamole chips on the side. I was so excited to hear that my wife chose the Chimi to go with the Chimichanga. She had a bit of lettuce with it and like the one I ordered, she was expecting it to have a slightly crispy exterior and meaty inside. Our experience at Agave was so different than our usual Mexican joint. She thought they had a pretty good chicken, but the shell really wasn't crisp enough. All of the ingredients were thyme and chile peppers and she couldn't finish her lunch. After a couple more bites, we moved on to the dinner menu and ordered our main dish. The Nachos came with the meat insides, cheese on the outside, and a bit of rice and refried beans on the side. The service was a little too slow, but also not as bad as you would expect from a busy restaurant where you aren't going to know I believe the menu is a little pricey, but my wife and I did try it for the first time (we had the Chimichanga). So, while the food and drinks were good, the customer service was... a bit slow and the staff lost their way when I tried to get some feedback We ended up sharing a few bites as we left and we went through the food. Overall, food was still pretty good and if we had more time, I would definitely go back. I think if you had to buy meat, they will still be willing to cut it for you. Not sure if there was nothing I was missing to my meal, but it was worth the drive back to work.

This is one of my favorite bars in Indianapolis. It is within walking distance to many nearby sites, including the Indianapolis Museum of Art (DMA), and numerous theatres and restaurants in the Old Town Downtown area Amelia's is usually occupied, but not often, but it is not uncommon to see their staff walking around on Friday afternoons. I would say to go there when you are in the district and plan to stop in there. Today, I was able to sample a slice of wheat bread with pears. Meat, like that of the steakhouses, was tender and tasted fresh. You get to see what the product is made of, and it is good to not forget the garlic flavor, however it is a bit lacking in flavour and All sandwiches also come with salad, and some of the sandwiches contain sauce. Many of these items are very reasonably priced. The salad and tomato sauce accompanied the bread perfectly. I will be back.

Pi Pizza opened on the second floor of a new food truck in downtown Indianapolis. Pi opened in May of 2012 as a new take on the familiar Carmel Valley pizza place, Pi on Main St. There are two options for pizza: Pi is more casual than the street food truck you will often see and their pizzas are fairly priced at $10.95. Pizza options range from three sauces (spinach pesto, red sauce, and sauce, with garlic and herb), to five Italian cheeses, or two Most of the ingredients are fresh sourced and the pizza itself is small. (which I did). The pizzas take about 40 minutes to cook. There are five booths and a counter. You can pay by check or card and there are several cash machines for that. You can also have your drink in a small tall glass bottle. The building is still in construction, but I am sure many other pizza places have opened there. The menu includes wine by the Glass and a selection of draft beers. Pi is located next to Sun King Distillery on the corner of Monon Trail and Parker Street. The parking deck in parking lot has the Sun King Distillery logo on it and is a great place to get a coffee/drink on the Pi pizza is a must take here! It's just like the ghetto-like Pi that closed down a few years ago! Would never go elsewhere!

The park consists of two very attractive trails, named 'Say Goodbye to the Trees' and 'Stop the Rain' The loop is overgrown, but there are some beautiful redwood trees and some large stone walls to help you through. There is also a playground for children (on the south side), but no showers. I think this is an excellent place to spend some of your first Saturday morning and then spend some time as a family. You can also look for a large picnic table near the lake.

Very comfortable for a quick shopping session. I feel there is a lot more left to be done. There was only one aisle in 2008 and that was the one I'd most like. Been shopping here since early 2007 so there are good products available, but you can sometimes get a little lost in the unorganized aisles that you have It is hard to find the product you need right when you enter the store.

My second visit to Kuma, Inc. has been an excellent experience as I always do. Heavier burgers are usually my favorite and I can't think of a better place to hit up on a Friday night. My first visit was for the Taco Tuesday Special. Very happy! This is the first review that I've done on the restaurant and I can't believe how much I liked it! The portions for lunch were plenty and I wouldn't hesitate to go back. The interior has a great variety of food and drink options to choose from. I started off with the Caramelized Smoked Bacon Burger. (This is a blend of a green salad and some kind of green dressing). Headed by a very nice young man, the burger came with this tangy heat as well as the traditional bacon. It was delicious!We also ordered some hot sauce. I really like the combo and definitely recommend it. I would highly recommend this burger. I also went with a side salad that included arugula, kale and tomato. I also had the Led Zeppelin combo which cost $9. My husband had it at a restaurant near him and I liked it also. It had a bun that was fried right side up and the burger was quite heavy. We also served the burger with their fresh fruit for less than $2. I think the sauce was a little too thick for my liking, but my husband really loved the meat and the sauce. My friend went with the breakfast burger combo. The side dishes were a great mix. She loves the meat and cheese with the burger that she ordered. This is definitely a combo that you have to try since she loves the flavor of bacon and eggs! The service, although a little slow, was good and quick. For what you get you might think that the food was expensive, but I'm surprised at the size of the plates. This area has a lot of business coming from the north and they're pretty busy on weekdays. But the restaurant is very clean and the staff is friendly. So, if you want a nice meal, this way to work! You don't have to be that close to the place to get any parking. There is no drive through and no amenities so you have to step outside of the building to find your way out if you can't park. Great lunch! Almost my favorite burger joint on the North Side!

This restaurant was on our top 10 list of the best restaurants in Portland. The food was great. It was fun and comfortable for us to sit outside in the large patio with heaters and we were able to take in the view of the lake. My wife ordered the Ribeye and our son ordered the Turkey wrap which seemed to have the right mix of protein and flavor. The steaks were cooked well and the chips and salsa were flavorful enough that the kids wanted to order the cheese quesadillas. The tacos were good, but I think it was a bit too much sauce. Our meats..(no shrimp) my wife ordered a Thai Chicken Roll (I ordered the prawns) and this was  As soon as it arrived, I noticed a texture that I suspect was not as nice as other places. I could eat the shrimp and chicken without feeling like it was tasteless. The steak was very tender but not overly so as usual, and with sauces that didn't have much kick to them, it was tough and chew It was definitely not my favorite dish, but I really like the fish that goes with it. We ordered from the lunch menu and even though the restaurant was busy, all of our food came out in a timely manner. The service at this restaurant was good. And I wish they would have offered more free items while we were there. This is a nice hotel or dining room. We'll be back!

The City of Indianapolis is proud to announce the installation of 'Mari Evans'. Mari Evans of Indianapolis passed away this past December. She was an accomplished poet of the post war United States in the late 1930's and early 1940's (for which she is noted). Evans is known as a black woman who often goes by the title of "Miss Evans Black Woman" and even the title of the "Black Lady The "Mari Evans" painting was painted by Jim Jordan. On January 2, 2015, Jordan was invited to take part in a 'Race to the Memorial' event. The name of the mural on Mass Ave was taken from Evans' poem The Awakening, originally published in "The Indianpolis Star" on October 22, Several pieces can be seen at the corner of Indiana Street and South Park Avenue.

Review #415 This place is one of the few independent breweries that has any kind of beer on tap at its bar. I love a good beer, and I love this place. The golden ale did not pass the test which was good because it tasted pretty like a fruitier IPA. For prices, that is not as good as some other beer breweries, but it's what can really set this place apart. I also liked the stout, which went in just slightly darker than the golden ale, having just a little hint of tan, which But, I had a lot of great food to share with my coworkers and I didn't mind it at all. I ordered the egg crepe taco (pistachio) to go with my IPA. It was served with hardboiled-eggs (which were very tender with a slight crunch that seemed to go along with the beet juice ), pickled onions, tangy green tomato puree, and guava pieces for a hearty taste. The taco was definitely in the sauce, not in the egg. There was a strong hint of salt which was paired well with the slightly sweet hot sauce. But I wanted to try something different, and the panini, which had been made crammed full of vegetables was nice and thin. The panini was made with peppered turkey, cheese, and a tangy blueberry preserve dressing. The sides were the iced Greek dressing, dill, and pickled salad. We found a great spot next door to the restaurant so we figured we'd share! If you like Mexican food, this brewery is a really cool place to visit. Aside from the small selection of brews, the bar is pretty modern. With a little work, it would make a great place to stop by during the warmer months. On a bright day, the glass windows give it a very clean look and are very clear. It has a patio area that looks out over the street next to the bar. For an easy downtown experience, you could easily recommend this bar even if you know the surrounding area very well. It's a very nice spot for a quick bite before heading out, and I'll definitely be back.

This is a very late review. My tumor is currently undergoing treatment from the Neuroscience Center of South Texas, where we recently went and got some testing done. That does sound a bit like a long road to recovery, but I have a feeling that I am making progress and the doctors think you will win While it is a lot of work, the staff is very friendly and I can now handle the day-to-day operations to get me through my treatment You know the lady who will be in charge of my care? They also did not want to talk to me about how I am feeling in the aftermath of the surgery. I greatly enjoy my visit to this wonderful office and I look forward to many more days in the future. I am grateful to my patients, staff and doctors. Thank you again.P.S.

On the plus side, it was a nice place to get a pizza. A huge selection of pizzas, a ton of toppings, and prices that are reasonable. Overall, I had a really good experience with the store and the food. The pizza was baked with an oven ring and a thermometer to make sure it was at least 190F degrees. I was able to tell by the center of my slice that it has been baked for an extra 15 minutes. I would have preferred it to have a little crispier crust on top and a crisp/smooth bottom. The sauce was soggy and had no flavor. I didn't do that. Besides the sausage, there was no other meat. The only positive about the pizza was the garlic bread. On the upside, they had a side of French knots. They had a nice garlicy taste, but the garlic flavor was not in abundance because the entire flavor was not in them. The garlic was flavorful thanks to the butter soggy on the outside of the pizza. Well, they were cooked well enough, but the dipping sauce took a while to sink to the outside. Using the spatula and brushing it across the knot was a lot easier and the garlic sauce was very flavorful. So I added some goat cheese and roasted garlic seasoning and some olive oil and ate a zing of garlic that doesn't get sweeter The price was too good to pass up. At times, the menu is a little unclear or unorganized so I had to ask. The only online option is the web menu which is just a short video presentation about the menu. They made the order without displaying a lot of ad, so it's hard to determine the ingredients of the slices. It may be worth a look for the flavor. If the staff is friendly and helpful, I think it would help out with ensuring quality. Even if it took a fewtries to find my order, they were very friendly!

Located in the old theater complex, the menu is a nice mix of the usual Mexican fare. We had a great experience. Although the interior is rather old, the service was friendly. The rooms tend to get pretty crowded during the dinner hours. You can get a free menu online, a few options, but the menu is not as extensive as other Mexican restaurants. The menus are not easy to follow. The menu provides several choices, but the selection of entrees, entree salads, and tortillas are a little limited to just one or two Also, I went with a Torta. All three items were served on deep fried rice. The restaurant offers a "comfort drink" called La Salsa and a "juice" or "fruit Juice" which is just I had the Salsa dip, which was very unique in flavor. The salsa was very spicy so I expected it to be too intense. It was very tasty and easy to drink. It was also very tasty. I had also sampled the corn on chips. I could taste more of the heat in the salsa and that helped too. My wife ordered a burrito (sans wrap) with taco and beef. It was moist and delicious with a nice flavor profile. The guajillo sauce was wonderful too. The inside texture was fresh. I did find the sauce slightly tart to my tongue, not something I'd typically order, but the sandwich held up well. At the end of the meal, we had a dish we had been eyeing for quite some time. When she received her order, she was expecting a very large, thin torta, but was also disappointed that the shell stayed soggy. Although it was still nice and well-seasoned, it did not have the same flavor as something I would prefer. She felt it absorbed a lot of the sauce and tasted like it was going to burn inside. Second, the ingredients were undercooked. Second, the sauce was a little too salty for my wife's taste. They also don't offer guacamole, so it might have been just a few small drops of that. It was an average lunch. I would not hesitate to say that they should consider making their menu a little wider as they seemed in need of more variety. The salsa was a pretty good match for the chips, but the bowl got too liquidy. It was a little too chewy and was hard to cut off.

The store was organized with ease and with ease. The staff was very good. The store is also well organized and there were many other things that I was interested in but I didn't purchase. I decided to visit with my wife when she was shopping and I asked her what types of stitches were available. She went to the Quilters Center who had a large section of asymmetrical shapes and designs. She could use these for both decorative and everyday quilts. I took a friend to this store before we had our wedding. They also showed us how to make the quilts we had in mind.

I stopped here on a rainy day at about 11:30am and ate lunch at the bar. The chicken was on the tender side and not dry at all. The chicken strips were thick and juicy and the buns were cooked perfectly. Very good sauce, but not too much, so that the chicken was notggy and too salty. The food was great quality. Orders are served daily, so you are not left waiting in line; they come out at a convenient time. The servers were friendly too! Will definitely be back!

This is a great local park that has many trees and a small pond. The pond is small and deep, but it does appear to be popular for swimming. There's a lot of greenery in the form of grass and a little trees and flora. There is a cafe and it was very quiet during the time I was there. The patios are set amidst a green space. I've never really gotten a chance to sit there, but I will definitely visit again next time I visit Japan.

This is one of my favorite restaurants in the area as well as the best Mexican food in the country! It is in a large building just off Main Street (tonight) and has a very large patio area that covers half of the restaurant. I really like the way the restaurant is laid out, it's bright, and you can clearly see what's going on in the bar area. There is a separate bar tucked away in the corner. A few days ago we walked through their large open space and ended up being ushered down a small level area to the bar. There are 2 large white booths towards the bar, one above the other on the main floor. I understand the small steps, but when you're looking this way, even in this crazy town, it can be a bit difficult to keep your attention The seating is a little too low, and you must park at the bar. He ordered my food and said it was waiting for him. (If the bar was a big room, at least that would be more appropriate.) The menu was very varied and the burritos appeared slightly different than most in Phoenix. (See below) My burrito wasn't bad, but not one of my favorites. Sometime, they add a side of chips, salsa and cheese. The burrito wasn't too greasy and everything went fine. It almost felt as if I was eating salty food. (Or else you may get skin burning while eating it.) Not too hot, but very hot. They have a bar, but the counter is not open. The meal was very worth the wait, we all got it! It took around 35 minutes to walk out.

"There's a little bit of everything at NEXT" My family and I stopped by NEXT last night to browse the selection They are big and have a good selection of items. It is a beautiful store as well, full of wonderful holiday items. The Christmas trees and Christmas ornaments are always pretty great - there are even cards for Santa Claus to hold! Although I think the store is pricey (it was about $11 from the time they opened), the items and prices are well worth the price. The store is open 7 days a week, but only while the Holidays are in session. After being there a bit... you drive to the shop, where the main entrance is on the right-hand side of the highway. There is a lot of parking available near the store but there is no street parking available. The store can be quite busy at times as soon as you enter the drive, so plan accordingly.

It always surprises me when a restaurant offers a free lunch special. I went to Chun Sing on a Thursday to try their Padd Seuw as part of a new menu I was looking to try. This time around, I opted for Padd Siuw at the Hotel Indigo, and what a great choice it was! I arrived on my first Sunday after going out to dinner that night, hoping to find a good Thai restaurant near my house. Be sure to turn right after a few steps if you enter the parking lot. The food and service was amazing. Service was good as well. The lunch specials are priced at $4-15 depending on the combination of vegetable choice and the meat option. We received a linguine noodles, steamed egg rolls, fried chicken, and lemongrass soup. Across the table, there is a side of green tea & basil. I ordered a bowl for my wife and we each shared the same padd sesuw, mixed with hot spicy sauce and noodles. A little water was added for an added flavor. I was very impressed with this dish and definitely recommend the menu. The tangy flavor is very unique and it makes food go down smoothly. I was happy to split this with my wife and we all finished it off. The padd was just ok, but it was very tasty with a few bites to spare. My wife enjoyed it, as did my husband. The soup is another great Thai dish and the menu had many options to choose from. I wasn't really sure what they were supposed to be so the restaurant offered them in a soup, spring roll, and a salad combination. The soup was good and we both enjoyed it. I felt a little bit hot coming out of the soup. It was warm and very thick on the bottom, but had enough flavor to hold it together. The ingredients were mixed and paired to produce a very spicy bowl of soup. It had a bit of a kick and did not taste too much like the lemon grass I usually find at my favorite restaurants, but I could find myself I also ordered the spring roll. It was very good, and was packed with fresh ingredients. Luckily, the spring roll had some vegetables included and I was also able to have a taste of most of the vegetables in the spring roll and was The decor was in a great area of the restaurant. I don't have a photo of it but I have been a consistent customer all my life and had an easy time. Well prepared food.I would highly recommend this restaurant. I think I would give it a try even if there was no special to it. I want to visit this restaurant often! One word of warning: be very aware of the server, because they may not be familiar with Thai.

This was our first experience with the restaurant where my wife and I went. I had a fairly standard restaurant experience here with a couple of complaints that were just a little out of my usual league. The diner was fairly new and there was no sign on the door. I was told it's a dive and that they are actually working to get the business to move to the larger space next door with better service. ;).. But it was a nice diner and it showed us that i liked it. I sat in the breakfast station with my wife, and she enjoyed a bowl of soup ranging from egg salad to egg Benedict. The waitress took a lot of notes when we ordered dishes and brought us our order after giving us a few minutes. My wife and I both ordered the Tomato Bisque and I ordered the Millionaire's Bacon. She chose the chicken salad Melt. Like most chicken burritos, it tasted delicious, but was kind of bland andggy. Her husband thought the dish had a "bit of a kick" and said that he also loved the bread. They even had a resaurant which is very fun since you get to order what you want from there. I ordered the Tomato Burrata. The presentation was very nice and they added a nice little tucker to the sides. The burrata was topped with fresh parmesan cheese and was sliced in sections. I just had to have some of the sauce on the plate. I also liked that the portions were plenty. I also ordered the Salty Bacon Bacon Sandwich to eat as a snack. The bacon was just baked when we got it. They were wrapped so that their sides came out in between. The bacon was layered on a light blue cheese burger wrap. The bacon had a lovely crunch to it and was nice and moist with a light smokey flavor. The bacon was crispy and tasted very good. It wasn't very good after a while and I noticed the ingredients layered together but didn't seem as sweet. It wasn't too bad really but it wasn't spectacular either. The flavor did end up not that good to me either. Definitely not my favorite breakfast at the diner. Good place. Thanks for the review. Foodie's note: The restaurant is a little run down, but it's well worth it! They did refund credit and even returned it to the waitress.

In My Eyes is a relatively new concept! The place is quite spacious and well maintained. A very spacious, well decorated inside, a bit on the dark side. I found the seating layout unusual. I was not seated as it was lunchtime and my waitress was busy entertaining many patrons at the bar. The hostess was nice and friendly, and I did not mind a bit of chatter, so if she was busy, she probably would When I got there, she asked what kind of salmon I ordered, and I asked to see if I could try something new. So I ordered a plate of the Mediterranean Salad. After we discussed what to expect, I opted for a Plate of Salmon Blackened Salmon Salad. The restaurant had over 100 plates in its front area. Not too large... but still huge! At only $5, it could have been a lot cheaper at a local place, but it was actually very affordable at lunch time. It wasn't bad at all. The egg had no flavor and the lettuce wasn’t wilted after a few minutes – the texture was a bit frozen. I have made a few salads from this location, but this did not live up to the expectations. For me, I didn't believe that the blackening would add anything special to the salad, so that was probably the reason... Not sure if we will continue coming here. If you are looking for a little something different then you should definitely check out Le Guin at 6358 Washington Rd.

The winery is located in a parking lot on Main just north of the YMC Arenas (which is primarily used for baseball) off of The outdoor seating area is in the front of the office complex and has nice natural lighting. The wine is free to try, and no charge is charged at the ordering counter. In the wine department is a beautiful showroom that contains over 30 wineries. In fact, the wine was quite good, so I opted to order a bottle of the 2004 vintage. I bought one by the pitcher at the restaurant, but I'm not sure if I'll ever try other wines. We sat at several table-style tables that were set about 30 inches apart for people to mingle to the music playing. There are tables and chairs at the back, so there is plenty of seating to relax. I ordered a wine at the door on the small side of the building. The owner and manager, Dan, smiled and seemed to understand what it was about the wine. The owner is a good-looking guy who has experience as a bartender. Inside, there are several glass cases with wines ranging from $15-$30/glass. It is a fairly small store, but with a nice patio, it was worth it for this particular winery. They are all good, and are priced well. This guy is quite talented, and I could hear the sound for some time. This is where to get your wine or beer fix during the Spring/Summer season! A must try.'.

I stopped in today to get a look at the adobe antique shop in my neighborhood. It was worth it, especially because it isn't always the case that you see something you like at an antique mall, but if you travel this So much to explore! This place is large enough that it looks almost like a warehouse. There are several categories of products. This is a great spot if you are looking for a treasure trove of old items. Some items are in good to pretty good condition, like the tea set. So there is something for every type of person. Maybe you have a room remodeled that needs some decorative items. Maybe you are an antiques fanatic and want to find that perfect piece that you have been looking for! Or maybe you are looking for a vintage sign that will brighten up your home. Maybe you are a big collector of antiques and want a unique desk for a museum or for an office that isn't quite what you Whether its something that reminds you of a time or someone involved with the antique business, if their pieces still interest you, you should take it They have a great selection of furniture, artwork and architectural items. Or if you are just looking for unique furniture, you can find just about anything here. All of the pieces are handcrafted by the shop owners. Also for those of you that like to spend extra time looking, they have a great gift shop there. I'd love to take you to this place, but sometimes a quick stop to see what they have is a must. And the price was very reasonable. I've been to other antique markets before and I have yet to find something like this here (but it looks so good).

This was my first dining experience at The Cafe. We were there around lunchtime, so we were expecting lots of traffic. Our family visited the cafe with a large group of friends (and it was quite busy) and was seated at the bar area, which was at the The parking lot was a little crowded and as much of the parking space as we could find, some of the seating had been assigned to customers only as It was a busy lunch when we arrived and the place was fairly empty by about 10:15. The sound of the bar was so loud I had to take my ears to a nearby store and retrace my steps the entire time. We were escorted back to our parking space and the food came out as quickly as possible.The prices are higher than in the nearby restaurants but  Our first meal was our regular lunch combo of soup and salad. We started with a soup, which was huge!! She thought the soup had the typical soup flavor of soup with an acidic side. Her soup was solid and she enjoyed it very much! It also contained some organic whole wheat pasta, rice, and the fresh basil. What can I say about the soup/salad? She thought it was a bit more flavorful than she thought. She still liked the soup. The bread was crisp and was baked and then smothered with the pickled onion, lemon, and arugula (as  The Bistro sauce tasted just as fresh and the chicken was tender. The sauce was incredibly strong and the chicken was tender. I could have easily added more salt, pepper, or onions than what was on the menu (I prefer the whole grain bread and extra seasonings if The sandwich took a couple of bites to start and wasn't very oily in the mouth. With my sandwich, I felt like I was home cooked! With that said, the wait times are pretty long because they have a huge number of tables on the second floor. If it isn't busy, I'd go back next time!

I was in the area looking for somewhere quick to go to try out the new restaurant that is open in downtown Chicago. I came across Duos while searching online and decided to check it out. The menu is fairly basic, with things like soups, salads, and a variety of dishes. I chose the chicken bowl and ordered a rice bowl. Orders are taking less than 10 minutes to arrive. My meal arrived at the table in under 24 minutes. The lunch consisted of hot dog buns (my favorite), tofu, and a bowl of mixed grains, veggies and grains. The flavor combination combined well with the greens and the chicken was just enough to give it a nice flavor balance. It's a good thing that they did not have any white meat and I found that it brought the meal together nicely enough. I do like that there are a few other options near where I live so I can try other spots if I don't have enough time to try I would definitely come back to Duos. I am not a big fan of the "Vegetable Bowl Specials" they are actually very limited when it comes to the quality and options that go Great place to order and enjoy your meal!

I had heard about Avalon Brewery all my life from some of my friends and family. Will the place be a place where kids can chill out? HELL NO!!! It turns out the beers were okay from what I'm telling you. Would all beer be at about 18 OZ? Would the buildings fit with the interior? Would it be in the old school building that used to be the high school? The brewery is located out on Third Street just off of West Main Street. The inside of the "Gym" is the old school gym which was also used for a basketball game between the teams. I love this place, it's just a stone building with a bar on the south side and a parking area just before the front entrance. The front of the building and the basement are open to the west. A stone wall was then hung to serve as a bar before the brewery was officially launched. It is a nice restaurant open all day with a great beer selection. In the center is the bar with its three taps as you would expect in any type of bar with a full bar. The food bar is located on the left. A tall bar serves as a bar area, and tables are available over the bar with one or two booths for dining. If you are in the area, I highly suggest visiting for a delicious beer and good food. I was glad I did because the beers and food were good and it was nice to sit outside. I didn't try theIPA, but the Belgian Stout "Red Rooster" (4.5%) with malty chocolate, coffee and The other beer in the flight was an IPA, "Lexicon", which came with a stout base, and "The Lion I would definitely recommend the "Into the Void" for an IPA. There are many more beers on draft and on tap than you will find in any other brewery. I ordered pulled pork, served with a tomato sauce dip, served with pickles, with pickled green onions and fresh green bell peppers. The pizza did not hit the mark for me, but the toppings were a solid choice! I also had a medium-sized serving of smoked corn. The corn was tender and flavorful and not too watery. It's actually very good!! The beer and food are definitely worth trying! The flatbreads came with a burger that was actually better than a dog's burger. The wait time can be a bit too long though to order by the slice.

I asked a few friends to rate restaurants locally they have visited during their visits to my area and they all rated their food. It was not a problem. No surprise given these were the two restaurants I frequented. It was fairly easy to see and the parking was free. After walking through this spacious space, I entered into a warm, welcoming environment. So it would have been ideal for a casual lunch or midday meal, and I felt the atmosphere was welcoming. I found myself immediately enjoying my lunch at a place that offered some sort of "vacation atmosphere" (the bar and the outdoor terrace are a bit I would recommend this place.) The menu listed a variety of breakfast, hot and cold items for around $10-14 and a healthy choice for around $5-12. Not something you would expect from a cafe of this kind. Then they brought out the Tropical Smoothie. As the name implies, a strawberry-based smoothie with a cup of frozen fruit. This wasn't sweet or processed, but the fruit was fresh and tasted great. So, the flavor was good but didn't have enough of that fruity sweetness. After that, I sipped on some tasty frozen popsicles and enjoyed a delicious, healthy wrap. This was one item I normally get from this cafe - the wrap. And I was really pleased with the food experience and prices. Their pricing is fair for the quality of the wrap as well! The wrap had a great flavor paired with the fruity juices, that came with it, and was well worth the price. The wrap was pretty good. However, the wrap didn't really deliver on the jerk flavor or wacky salad. I like sweet, savory/tangy Jamaican jerk chicken. I understand what people are saying: you can't take the salt out and taste it all. I did like the flavor. I'm not a salt and pepper expert, and the spices did not match with the chicken breast flavor. The chicken itself was pretty good; I like Caribbean chicken. I'll have to try that to see if they succeed. As mentioned before, this is a place I will return to and hope to do some more experimenting with my recipe. Well, as it turned out, it ended up being a fairly good bowl for the meal. It was a pretty typical Americanized chicken wrap. We shared our meals since it was such an afternoon, and with the other three meals we all had a good quality of food. So, I had a pretty solid lunch to compare to.

I was excited to visit a new restaurant near my house. Not sure what I was doing, I walked up from where I worked after work and walked past the Korean/Japanese restaurant. The entryway to the restaurant is just too narrow and I took a little while to get used to navigating the long driveway. There was a parked car park right outside the venue, but this is very unlikely to happen any time soon. I stopped by to ask if they would allow me to sit on the front patio. All of the people at the restaurant were very friendly and seemed to enjoy the food. This seems like it would be a good spot for an Indian lunch since it's located on both sides of the counter. The waiters aren't necessarily very knowledgeable about their dishes and the items are limited to a few options. My plate was a little small and I think I did have a large portion of soup, but the waitress told me it is better to order on There are three main entrees on the menu (soup, soup, and chicken). This is a pretty common item with a few different versions for varying prices. The Egg Rolls are the aforementioned. The egg rolls were served with a sauce of sweet and sour mixed with sweet and sour sauce. The chicken wing wraps (the other chicken option) are stuffed with a meatball mixture, carrots, and mushrooms. The egg rolls were served immediately with the dipping sauce. At first bite, I noticed that they were fairly crisp and not too chewy looking, but I thought that their chicken pieces were a bit greasy. The interior was pretty good for a restaurant in this price bracket. A minor gripe was that the dipping sauce was thin and very runny. Also, the dipping sauce was so good that I just about had to eat it all and the dipping sauce was enough to just sit on top. The chicken was well seasoned and had a nice chewy taste. The chicken was a little moist with a taste of watery sauce, but it tasted like it wasn't cooked enough and wasn't It was flavorful and my mouth was satisfied. The sauce on both dishes was very flavorful and tasty, but I feel like a few more flavors needed to be added to get it to an appropriate thickness Although it wasn't a huge dumpling, the dish was very good and I would definitely suggest it. The restaurant also has a drive-thru window, so I really didn't mind that. I think I could have cooked it more or mashed the egg rolls more though rather than eating them individually. I found this one of my least favorite Chinese restaurants in the area and I would be glad to give it another chance. The egg rolls were served hot, but a little mushy, so I didn't really enjoy the flavor of it. The chicken pieces were not salty and the sauce was tasty. Aside from the chicken and rice, all of my food choices were good.

I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised with this location (very familiar with them). We arrived around 12 p.m. after driving in from the north at 12,000 square feet. After checking in, we noticed that our seats were not accessible for an older patron outside of the bar area. My wife and I walked in, took seat as the bartender was busy making drinks, and walked to the back of the restaurant. The bar staff seemed very friendly and kindly took our orders. In addition, the restaurant had two different options for food at the table. We walked in and ordered: My wife ordered the hummus wrap and her salad was nice and lightly seasoned. She really didn't miss a single bite when she got it because the wrap was extremely dense! She did not like the sauce because it was just soggy with the meat. My neighborhood Mall.. It's just not worth spending money here. What's up with this place it has such a bad vibe, you'll hear all manner of people yell at you for parking, and I got here, and it was still pretty shady at this point.

Today I was browsing on Pet Smart to see what was on sale for next week. I looked around and the first item I found was the fountain bowl. I usually don't really like the company, so I was pleasantly surprised with its selection. The reptiles were really nice, but the one that really affected me. I often visit Countryside Dillards in the Spring, and it is an amazing store. They have the nicest clothes but not the worst! Earlier this week I got to check out this new restaurant located downtown called the Craft Steak House. Before coming to the shop, unless you're very close to work, the wait was well worth it. Looks like it has a hipster theme going on in the place. The place has a very casual feel and is a lot smaller than most locations.. but that doesn't mean it's less friendly! The food is wonderful, made from different types of fish, and they also offer many unique drinks and apps on the menu. We ate at Xoodoo after walking across the street to make reservations for the place. We were offered a few different starters and salads. They had some original and trending items on the menu. Although we wanted something different than traditional summer fare at home, we decided to try something a little different. We had the Baby Brats. They were both really good. The burger looked like a very tasty piece of meat, I ate it in about 30 seconds and it wasn't really gross. The pork belly was smothered in sauce that was very rich and flavourful. Besides the burger they were both really good. My husband ordered the vanilla ice-cream soda, super sweet and delicious. We tried so many different items I didn't feel like they were really that bad. Theirs was the State fair puffs with chocolate cake with peanut butter ice cream and they were amazing! The place was clean and welcoming, with a great view of the river. Have you been or have you been inspired? :) The location is close to our house and we plan on launching a sever in the near future.

I really like Target's location on South Creek in Mesquite. I like that the majority of the things in the store are available in a couple aisles of the store. I will definitely make this my go to location with my dog.

Pi is my personal favorite pastry shop, and I find that they are able to meet my expectations. It's a good place, and Lindsey just loves desserts, especially the ones made here. I had the Mocha ice cream, and it was awesome. They mixed this all in the morning. It was good, I could have tasted a glass of this cold brew later, it was really quite smooth. It was super smooth. My chocolate vanilla mousse cake was the perfect consistency, soft and rich, with a delicious flaky bottom. Unfortunately, it's so damn gross that the food delivery lady sounded like she was not washing her hands, and it was obvious she had nothing on she threw up her food when she was being served, after we left the restaurant, she would become absolutely irritated and utterly smell What a surprise.
